# THE BOOK OF EXODUS

## CHAPTER THE THIRTEENTH.

### THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY.

**8033.** We must now define what Charity is and what Faith is in relation to man. Charity is an internal affection <note>In this context, "affection" refers to a deep-seated emotional state or a "ruling love" that drives a person's actions.</note> consisting of a heartfelt desire to do good for one's neighbor. This desire becomes the very delight of one's life, and it is performed without any expectation of reward.

**8034.** On the other hand, Faith is an internal affection consisting of a heartfelt desire to know what is true and what is good. This is not sought for the sake of simply knowing doctrine as an end in itself, but for the sake of living it. This affection of faith joins itself with the affection of charity through the desire to act according to the truth—thus, to put the truth into practice.

**8035.** Those who possess the genuine affection of charity and faith believe that they do not desire anything good or understand anything true from their own power; instead, they acknowledge that the will to do good and the understanding of truth come from the Lord.

**8036.** This, then, is the essence of charity and faith. Those who live in these states have the kingdom of the Lord and heaven within them, and the church exists within them. These are the individuals who have been <term>regenerated: the process of spiritual rebirth where a person’s selfish nature is replaced by a new nature guided by the Divine</term> by the Lord, receiving from Him a new will and a new understanding.

**8037.** Those who hold the love of self or the love of the world as their primary goal cannot possibly live in charity and faith. Those immersed in these selfish loves do not even know what charity and faith are. They cannot comprehend that willing good to one's neighbor without seeking a reward constitutes "heaven" within a person. They do not realize that within this affection lies a happiness as vast as that of the angels—a joy that is unutterable; for they believe...

<note>original: "Exodus, Charity, Faith, internal affection, Lord, genuine affection, regenerated, kingdom of the Lord, love of self, love of the world"</note>

<summary>This page defines the spiritual concepts of Charity and Faith as internal drives focused on selfless service and the pursuit of truth for the sake of life. It emphasizes that these qualities are gifts from the Divine and constitute the presence of heaven within an individual.</summary>
<keywords>Exodus, Charity, Faith, Regeneration, Self-love, Kingdom of God, Divine Influence, Altruism</keywords>

...replaced by a spiritual nature from God. **8037.** Such individuals often believe that if they are deprived of the joy arising from the glory of worldly honors and wealth, all joy would cease to be possible; yet it is only then that heavenly joy, which infinitely transcends every other joy, truly begins to be felt.

## CHAPTER XIII.

1. And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
2. Sanctify to Me all the firstborn <note>In the internal sense, the "firstborn" refers to the primary essentials of faith and the beginning of spiritual life.</note>, that which openeth every womb among the sons of Israel, in man and in beast; it is Mine.
3. And Moses said unto the people, Remember thou this day, in which ye went out from Egypt, out of the house of servants <note>original: "domo servorum." This refers to the state of spiritual captivity or being enslaved to sensory desires.</note>; because in strength of hand Jehovah led you forth from hence; and what is leavened shall not be eaten.
4. This day ye go forth, in the month Abib <note>Abib: The first month of the Hebrew year, corresponding to the start of spring, symbolizing a new spiritual beginning.</note>.
5. And it shall be when Jehovah shall have brought thee unto the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite <note>These various tribes symbolize different types of internal evils and falsities that must be cleared away to make room for the church.</note>, which He sware to thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey <note>Milk and honey: Symbols of the abundance of spiritual and natural truths and the delights that come with them.</note>, that thou shalt serve this service in this month.
6. Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened things, and in the seventh day is a feast to Jehovah.
7. Unleavened things shall be eaten seven days; and that which is leavened shall not be seen with thee, leaven shall not be seen with thee in all thy border <note>Leaven: Symbolizes falsity or corrupted thinking that "ferments" and disturbs the mind.</note>.
8. And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying, It is because of that which Jehovah did for me, in my going forth out of Egypt.
9. And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes <note>Between thine eyes: Signifies that these truths should be constantly in the person's will and understanding.</note>, that the law of Jehovah may be in thy mouth; because with a strong hand hath Jehovah led thee forth out of Egypt.
10. And thou shalt keep this statute at the set time from year to year.
11. And it shall be when Jehovah shall have brought thee in to the land of the Canaanite, as He sware to thee and to thy fathers, and shall have given it thee:

### NUMBER 8037] CHAPTER XIII. 3

**12.** That thou shalt cause to pass over to Jehovah all that openeth the womb; and all that openeth of the offspring of a beast, which shall be to thee males, shall be for Jehovah <note>original: "transire facies" (thou shalt cause to pass over). This ritual of "passing over" signifies the dedication of one’s primary spiritual intentions to the Divine.</note>.
**13.** And all that openeth of an ass thou shalt redeem with one of the flock; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck; and every firstborn of man among thy sons shalt thou redeem <note>The "ass" symbolizes the natural or everyday intellect; if it is not "redeemed" by the spiritual innocence represented by the "flock," it remains unusable for spiritual life.</note>.
**14.** And it shall be when thy son shall ask thee to-morrow, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, In strength of hand Jehovah led us forth from Egypt, from the house of servants.
**15.** And it was that Pharaoh hardened himself against letting us go, and Jehovah slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man and even to the firstborn of beast; therefore I sacrifice to Jehovah all that openeth the womb, being males; and all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.
**16.** And it shall be for a sign upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes; because in strength of hand Jehovah led us forth out of Egypt <note>The "sign upon the hand" symbolizes action and power, while "frontlets between the eyes" signifies the understanding and the will.</note>.
**17.** And it was in Pharaoh's letting the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, because that was near; for God said, Perchance the people will repent when they see war, and will return to Egypt.
**18.** And God led the people about, by the way of the wilderness, the sea Suph <note>original: "mare Suph." Commonly known as the Red Sea. In a spiritual sense, this represents the boundary where one undergoes trials or temptations.</note>; and the sons of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.
**19.** And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him; for swearing he had caused the sons of Israel to swear, saying, Visiting God will visit you <note>original: "Visitando visitabit." A Hebrew idiom emphasizing the certainty of God's eventual intervention and care.</note>; and ye shall bring up my bones with you from hence.
**20.** And they journeyed from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, at the end of the wilderness.
**21.** And Jehovah went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them in the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and by night.
**22.** The pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, departed not from before the people <note>The "pillar of cloud" represents Divine truth as it appears in the light of the world, while the "pillar of fire" represents the warmth of Divine love as it appears during times of spiritual darkness.</note>.

<header>EXODUS</header>

# THE CONTENTS.

**8038.** In this chapter, the subject treated in the internal sense <note>The "internal sense" refers to the hidden spiritual meaning within the literal words of the Bible.</note> is faith in the Lord, and the perpetual remembrance of having been liberated by Him from damnation. Faith in the Lord is signified by the sanctification of the firstborn, and the perpetual remembrance of liberation by the Lord is signified by the celebration of the passover.

**8039.** In the latter portion of the chapter and thereafter, the subject treated is the further preparation of those who belonged to the spiritual church <note>The "spiritual church" refers to people who are guided by their conscience and intellectual understanding of truth, rather than by direct perception of love.</note> and who, before the coming of the Lord, were detained in the lower earth <note>The "lower earth" is described in this tradition as a transitional state or place in the spiritual world where people were kept in safety until they could be raised into heaven.</note> until they could be introduced into heaven. For this purpose, they were first sent through the midst of damnation in safety, and after this underwent temptations, while the Lord was continually present. Transmission through the midst of damnation is signified by the passage through the Sea Suph <note>Original: "Mare Suph," commonly known as the Red Sea. In the spiritual sense, it represents the boundary of a state of spiritual danger or "damnation."</note>; temptations are signified by that life in the wilderness to which they were led; and the presence of the Lord is signified by the pillar of cloud by day, and of fire by night.

---

# THE INTERNAL SENSE.

**8040.** Verses 1, 2. *And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying, Sanctify to Me all the firstborn, that which openeth every womb among the sons of Israel, in man and in beast; it is Mine.* "And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying," signifies an informing by the Divine; "Sanctify to Me all the firstborn," signifies faith, that it is from the Lord; "that which openeth every womb," signifies which is from charity <note>In this context, "charity" refers to the love of one’s neighbor.</note>; "among the sons of Israel," signifies the spiritual church; "in man and in beast," signifies the good of faith interior and exterior; "it is Mine," signifies that it is the Lord's.

**8041.** *And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying.* That this signifies an informing by the Divine, is evident from the signification of "speaking" and "saying," when by Jehovah about <note>The entry ends mid-sentence here as it transitions to the next point of the spiritual explanation.</note>

### [N. 8041] CHAPTER XIII. VERSES 1, 2

The things of the church which are to be observed, as being an informing <note>Informing here means the process of being shaped or instructed by spiritual truth (see references to sections 7769, 7793, 7825).</note>, and because it is by Jehovah, it denotes an informing by the Divine; and from the representation of Moses, as being truth Divine (sections 6771, 7014, 7382). Hence by “Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying” is signified an informing by the Divine through Divine truth.

**8042.** *Sanctify to Me all the firstborn.* That this signifies faith, and that it comes from the Lord, is evident from the signification of “sanctifying to Jehovah” or the Lord, as being to ascribe to Him—that is, to confess and acknowledge that it is from Him; and from the signification of “the firstborn,” as being <term>faith</term> <note>In this context, faith is defined as the first and most essential realization of spiritual life.</note> (see sections 352, 2435, 6344, 7035). 

When it is said “faith,” there is meant all the truth that belongs to the <term>spiritual church</term> <note>The "spiritual church" refers to people who find their way to God through the intellect and the study of truth, rather than through direct, intuitive love.</note>; and as there is meant all the truth of the church, the spiritual church itself is also meant, for truth is the essential foundation of this church. 

Good is indeed the essential of the church, and is actually the firstborn (sections 2435, 3325, 4925, 4926, 4928, 4930); but the <term>good</term> <note>In Swedenborgian thought, "Good" refers to the quality of the heart and will, while "Truth" refers to the quality of the mind and understanding.</note> which those have who belong to the spiritual church is in itself truth; for when they act according to the truth which is of their doctrine, then the truth is called "good," having then passed from the understanding into the will and from the will into act; and that which is done from the will is called "good." That in itself and in its essence this good is nevertheless truth, is because to them the doctrinal things of the church are truths, and the doctrinal things in churches differ, consequently so do the truths; and yet although they are so various, by willing them and doing them they become goods, as just now said. 

[2] While a man is being <term>regenerated</term> <note>Regeneration is the process of spiritual rebirth or transformation into a heavenly person.</note>, he is led by means of faith in the understanding (or in doctrine) to faith in the will (or life)—that is, by means of the truth of faith to the good of charity. When a man is in the good of charity, he has then been regenerated, and then from this good he produces truths, which are called the "truths of good." These are the truths which are the most essential truths of faith, and which are meant by “the firstborn;” for it is with the begettings or births of truths from good, as it is with the begettings or births of sons and daughters from a parent, and afterward of grandsons and granddaughters, and thereafter of great-grandsons and great-granddaughters; and so on. The first or...

<summary>This page explains that the biblical command to "sanctify the firstborn" spiritually represents acknowledging that all true faith comes from the Lord. It details the process of regeneration, where religious doctrine (truth) is moved from the intellect into the heart (will) to become a life of charity (good).</summary>

<meta>This page continues the spiritual interpretation of the Book of Exodus, specifically the conclusion of section 8042 and the beginning of 8043. It transitions from defining the "firstborn" as the primary essence of faith to explaining the spiritual symbolism of the "womb" as the site of spiritual rebirth or regeneration.</meta>

<page-num>6</page-num>
<header>EXODUS [N. 8042]</header>

...immediate begetting or birth—which refers to the birth of sons and daughters—is what is signified by "the firstborn," regardless of how many there may be. However, this does not refer to the second and third generations of births, except in relation to their own parents. The reason why these are sanctified to Jehovah (the Lord) is that all derivative or descending truths and goods derive their essential nature from these primary ones. On this spiritual principle is founded the "right of the firstborn" that is spoken of in the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used here for the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>.

**8043.** *That which openeth every womb.* That this signifies what comes from <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is not merely almsgiving, but the active, spiritual love for one's neighbor that flows from a renewed heart.</note>, is evident from the meaning of "that which opens the womb" as being that which is born immediately from a <term>regenerate</term> person <note>A "regenerate" person is one who has undergone a spiritual rebirth, moving from a self-centered life to a God-centered life.</note>. Thus, it refers to that which comes from charity (according to what was said just above in section 8042). 

For he who is conceived anew comes, as it were, into the womb again; and he who is born anew goes forth, as it were, again from the womb. However, that which is conceived in the womb and born from the womb in this sense is not man *as a physical human*, but is the faith of charity. It is this faith that constitutes the spiritual part of man—essentially making the man himself anew—for from this point forward, his life is derived from this spiritual source. 

From all this, it can be seen what is meant in the spiritual sense by "that which opens the womb." The angels, who think in spiritual ideas alone, understand nothing else by this expression. (For further reading on what is meant by the "womb," "being in the womb," and "going forth from the womb," see sections 3293e, 3294, 3967, 4904, 4918, 4931, 5052, 5054, and 6433.) [2] Because such spiritual things are signified by the "womb," the Lord is called in the Word "the Former from the womb"—that is, the Regenerator—as seen in *Isaiah:*

> Thus said Jehovah, your Maker, and your Former from the womb; He helps you: Fear not, Jacob My servant, and Jeshurun whom I have chosen, because I will pour out water upon him that is thirsty, and rivulets upon the dry ground; I will pour out My spirit upon your seed, and My blessing upon your children (Isaiah 44:2, 3);

The Lord is called "the Maker and Former from the womb" because He regenerates man, changing him from a natural being into a spiritual one. And as regeneration is achieved by means of truth and good, it is said that He "will pour out water upon him that is thirsty, and His spirit upon his seed"; for by "water" is signified the truth which belongs to faith (see section 2702).

<summary>This page explains that the "firstborn" represents the primary truths of faith and that "opening the womb" symbolizes the beginning of a life led by charity. It describes spiritual regeneration as a second birth where the Lord acts as the "Former from the womb," transforming a person's nature through Divine truth.</summary>

> Jesus said unto Nicodemus, Verily, verily, I say to thee, Except any one be begotten anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus said unto Him, How can a man be begotten when he is old? > Thus said Jehovah thy Redeemer, and thy Former from the womb: I am Jehovah, that doeth all things; that spreadeth out the heavens alone; and that stretcheth out the earth by Myself (xliv. 24);

> Upon Thee, O Lord Jehovih, have I been laid from the womb; Thou art my Bringer-forth out of my mother's bowels; Thou art my praise continually (*Ps*. lxxi. 6).

**8044.** *Among the sons of Israel.* That this signifies "in the spiritual church," is evident from the symbolic representation of the "sons of Israel" as the spiritual church (see n. 4286, 6426, 6637, 6862, 6868, 7035, 7062, 7198, 7201, 7215, 7223).

# CHAPTER XIII. VERSES 3–10

[...appro]priate (see numbers 3168, 3513, 3596, 4745 <note>These references point to earlier explanations of how spiritual qualities become a permanent part of a person's character.</note>); and from the symbolic meaning of "leaven," as being <term>falsity</term> <note>original Latin: "falsum"; refers to errors in thinking or incorrect religious concepts</note> (n. 2342, 7906); consequently "what is leavened" denotes what is falsified. 

Regarding the appropriation of *falsity* and that which is falsified, it should be understood that *falsity* cannot be truly appropriated—meaning, it does not become a permanent part of the soul—in anyone who lives in "good" <note>A state of living characterized by kindness, charity, and unselfishness.</note> and who, from that state, desires to find the truth. It can only be appropriated by one who lives in evil and has no desire for truth. 

The reason *falsity* is not appropriated *as falsity* to one who is in a state of good is because they think well regarding God, the kingdom of God, and spiritual life. Consequently, they interpret and apply any errors or *falsities* they encounter so that they do not contradict these core values, but rather harmonize with them. In this way, the person softens the error; its harshness and rigid nature do not enter into their mind or intention. 

If this were not the case, hardly anyone could be saved, because <term>falsities</term> are more common in the world than truths. However, those who are in a state of "good" also possess a love for the truth. Therefore, in the next life, when they are instructed by angels, they reject these errors and accept truths, according to the level of love for truth they held while in the world.

**8052.** ***This day ye go forth.*** That this signifies liberation to eternity, is evident from the symbolic meaning of "this day," as being eternity (see n. 2838, 3998, 4304, 6165, 6984); and from the meaning of "going forth," as being to be liberated (n. 8049).

**8053.** ***In the month Abib.*** That this signifies the beginning of a new state, is evident from the meaning of a "month," as being the end of a former state and the beginning of a subsequent one—thus, a new state (see n. 3814). That "the *month Abib*" denotes the beginning from which all following states arise is clear from what was said of this month in the previous chapter: "*This month shall be unto you the head of the months; this is the first to you in the months of the year*" (see n. 7827, 7828).

**8054.** ***And it shall be when Jehovah shall have brought thee unto the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.*** That this signifies the region of heaven occupied by those who are in evil and falsity, is evident from the symbolic meaning of "the land of the Canaanite, and [the other nations]" <note>In this symbolic system, the various tribes inhabiting the Promised Land before the Israelites represent different types of negative spiritual influences or "evils" that occupy the "region of heaven" (the human mind or the spiritual world) and must be displaced for spiritual growth.</note>.

The **spiritual heaven** was not yet formed. The region where the spiritual heaven was to be, was occupied by those who were in falsity and evil, but who could be kept in some truth and good by external means, especially by means of ideas of eminence and dignity, just as is the case in the world, where they who are in evil and falsity are nevertheless obliged to as it were think and speak truths, and as it were will and do goods, by external means, which are honors and gains. 

The reason why this region of heaven was then occupied by such spirits, was that good ones were lacking, and they who were of the spiritual church had not as yet been prepared, and yet every place had to be filled by spirits, in order that there might be <term>continuity</term> <note>The spiritual connection or "chain of being" necessary for Divine influence to reach the human race.</note> from the Lord down to man, for without continuity man would have perished. At this day also there are some regions of heaven occupied by such; but they who are there are withheld by a strong force from the doing of evils. Immediately above the head are they who deceive and seduce by means of innocence; but above them the celestial from the **Most Ancient Church** <note>The first symbolic era of humanity, characterized by a direct, intuitive love for the Divine.</note>, who keep them in bonds with such force that they cannot possibly occasion what is evil to any one.

# CHAPTER XIII. VERSES 3–10 [N. 8054]

Even today, there is a region behind the back of the head which was once a region of heaven, but is now occupied by those who are evil; there is another such region in front, toward the left. [3] There is also a constant effort on the part of the evil to invade the places where the good reside, and they actually do invade them as soon as those places are not filled by the good. I have often been permitted to notice this ongoing struggle.

These spiritual regions are occupied in this way whenever evil increases and goodness diminishes in the world; for in such cases, evil spirits draw closer to humanity, and good spirits withdraw. To the extent that the good withdraw, the regions nearest to a person are taken over by the evil. When this condition becomes widespread, the inhabitants of these spiritual regions are completely changed. This occurs when a <term>church</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s terminology, a "church" refers not just to an institution, but to the overall spiritual state of humanity during a specific era.</note> is nearing its end, for then evil and falsity begin to prevail. However, at the end of the church, the evil are cast down, and the regions they occupied are given to the good, who have meanwhile been prepared for heaven. This is the meaning of these words in *John*:

> There was war in heaven; Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels; but they prevailed not, neither was their place found any more in heaven (*Revelation 12:7, 8*). <note>original: "Michael et angeli ejus pugnaverunt cum dracone..." Michael represents those who defend the Lord's divinity, while the dragon represents those who separate faith from a life of love.</note>

This state of heaven was represented by the land of Canaan, specifically in how the various nations occupied it, and how the sons of Israel eventually cast those nations out. This is because the "land of Canaan" signifies the Lord’s kingdom—meaning both heaven and the church—as can be seen from the passages cited previously.

**8055.** *Which He sware to thy fathers to give thee.* That this signifies what was promised by the Divine to those who are in goodness and truth, is evident from the meaning of "swearing." When this is done by <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The name for God emphasizing His Divine Love and unchangeable nature.</note>, it signifies an irrevocable confirmation by the Divine (see n. 2842, 3375); thus, "to swear to give" denotes a promise. This is also evident from the meaning of "fathers," as being those who are in goodness and truth; for when the church is the subject, "fathers" signifies the ancients, or the <term>ancient churches</term>, which were established in goodness and truth (n. 6050, 6075, 6589, 6876, 6884, 7649).

...be wholly done; and from the <term>signification</term> <note>In this system of interpretation, "signification" refers to the specific spiritual concept represented by a physical word or object in the Bible.</note> of “seven days,” as being what is holy, and also a full state (n. 8058).

**8061. *And that which is leavened shall not be seen with thee.*** That this signifies that what is <term>falsified</term> <note>To "falsify" a truth means to take something that is true and twist it to justify a wrong or evil intention.</note> must not be admitted at all—that is to say, so as to be <term>appropriated</term> <note>To "appropriate" something spiritually means to take it into one’s heart and life so that it becomes part of who they are.</note>—is evident from what was unfolded above (n. 8051); that this must not be done at all is signified by the words being repeated.

**8062. *And leaven shall not be seen with thee.*** That this signifies that neither must any <term>falsity</term> <note>Swedenborg distinguishes between "leavened" things (distorted truths) and "leaven" itself (the underlying false principles).</note> be admitted, is evident from the signification of “leaven,” as being falsity (see n. 7906). That which is falsified, which is signified by “what is leavened,” and falsity, which is signified by “leaven,” differ in this way: what is falsified is truth applied to confirm evil, and falsity is everything that is contrary to truth.

**8063. *In all thy border.*** That this signifies so far as the truth which is from good extends itself, is evident from the signification of “border,” as being the extension of truth from good; for all truth has its extension, which is sometimes manifested by a <term>sphere</term>; <note>A "sphere" is like an invisible aura or field of influence that radiates from a person based on their inner character.</note> and because it has extension, it has its borders. The sphere of the extension of truth is according to the quality and the amount of good; for good is like flame, and truth is like light. The sphere of extension in the spiritual world is to the societies which are round about; and so far as the sphere extends into them, so far there is communication (see n. 6598–6613). In heaven every one has intelligence and wisdom, and has happiness, according to the sphere of extension; that is, according to its amount and at the same time its quality. From all this it can be seen what is signified in the spiritual sense by “in all thy border,” here, that in good there must not be any falsity; for falsities are outside of the sphere, because they begin where truths leave off; whereas if they enter the sphere, they are appropriated. That they must not enter is signified by its being said “there shall no leavened thing, or leaven, be seen with thee in all thy border.”

**8064. *And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying.*** That this signifies the interior perception which is of conscience, is evident from what was unfolded above (see n. 7935), where there are similar words.

# N. 8078] CHAPTER XIII. VERSES 11-16

"To cause to pass over to Jehovah" <note>The Latin phrase "transire facere" refers to the ritual act of setting aside or dedicating the firstborn to God.</note> denotes to ascribe to the Lord, in the same way as "to sanctify" and "to sacrifice" were shown just above (in section 8074). Thus, "not to cause to pass over, but to redeem" signifies that we should not ascribe something directly to the Lord, but rather give something else in its place. This is based on the symbolic meaning of "one of the flock" as the truth of innocence. 

The reason "one of the flock" signifies the truth of innocence is that the term refers to a lamb or a kid, both of which symbolize innocence (sections 3519, 3994, 7840). In this specific context, it refers to the *truth* of innocence because the text does not name a specific "lamb" or "kid," but uses the more general category of "one of the flock." From all this, it is evident that the phrase "every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with one of the flock" signifies that faith which is merely natural must not be ascribed to the Lord; instead, it is the truth of innocence within that faith that must be recognized as belonging to Him.

**[3]** Faith that is merely natural is a belief that is introduced through an external path rather than an internal one. This includes **sensuous faith**, which consists of believing something is true only because the eye has seen it and the hand has touched it. This is the kind of faith the Lord spoke of to Thomas when He said, "Because thou hast seen, Thomas, thou hast believed; blessed are they who do not see, and yet believe" (*John* 20:29). It is also similar to the "faith of miracles," which consists in believing something is true solely because of a miracle (see section 7290), and the "faith of authority," which consists in believing something just because someone else—in whom one has confidence—has said it.

**[4]** In contrast, **spiritual faith** is that which is introduced through an internal path and an external path at the same time. The introduction through the internal path causes the person to believe, and then what is introduced through the external path serves to confirm that belief. The "spiritual" part of faith is the affection of charity <note>Original: "charitas." In this system, charity is not just giving to the poor, but an active, internal love for doing what is good and helpful.</note>, and from this arises an affection for truth for the sake of useful service and for the sake of one's life. These are the qualities that make faith spiritual. This internal introduction of faith is accomplished through the reading of the <term>Word: the Sacred Scriptures or Bible</term>, combined with <term>enlightenment: a spiritual clarity or "light" given to the mind</term> from the Lord. This light is granted according to the quality of a person's affection—that is, why they are seeking to know the truth.

**[5]** From all this, it can now be seen what "merely natural faith" is. Because this faith is not spiritual, it cannot be ascribed to the Lord—meaning it cannot be acknowledged and believed to originate from the Lord. For the Lord flows in through...

**8089.** *But all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.* This signifies that the truths of faith are not to be attributed to the Lord, but rather the "goods" of faith <term>goods of faith: the practical expression of faith through love, kindness, and useful service, rather than just intellectual belief</term>. This is clear from the explanation provided earlier in entry number 8080, where the same phrasing appears.

**8090.** *And it shall be for a sign upon your hand.* This signifies that these principles must be constantly present in the will <term>will: the part of the mind associated with desire, intention, and action</term>. The phrase *for frontlets between your eyes* signifies that they must also be constantly present in the understanding <term>understanding: the cognitive part of the mind that perceives and analyzes truth</term>. Finally, the phrase *because in strength of hand Jehovah led us forth out of Egypt* signifies that they were liberated by the Lord’s Divine power. This interpretation is based on the analysis of verse nine of this chapter (see entries 8066, 8067, and 8069).

**8091.** Verses 17, 18. *And it was in Pharaoh’s letting the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, because that was near; for God said, Perchance the people will repent when they see war, and return to Egypt. *   “And it was in Pharaoh’s letting the people go” signifies the moment when those who were causing infestations <term>infestations: in a spiritual sense, the harassment of the soul by deceptive thoughts or negative influences</term> finally left those belonging to the spiritual church <term>spiritual church: a state of being where a person is guided by an enlightened intellect toward what is good</term>.
*   “That God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines” signifies that Divine providence ensured they would not transition immediately to a "truth of faith" that does not come from "good" <note>The "Philistines" here represent those who have religious knowledge but lack a life of charity; the text suggests that jumping straight to this state is spiritually dangerous</note>.
*   “Because that was near” signifies that this is the first state or path that presents itself.
*   “For God said” signifies Divine foresight.
*   “Perchance the people will repent when they see war” signifies the danger that they might turn away from the truth when faced with spiritual assaults or conflicts.
*   “And will return to Egypt” signifies that such a turning away would lead to a fall back into falsities <term>falsities: distorted ideas used to justify selfish behavior</term>, which are the complete opposite of the truths and goods of faith.
*   “And God led the people about, by the way of the wilderness” signifies that, under Divine guidance, they were brought to a state where they could strengthen their faith through temptations <term>temptations: internal struggles or trials that test a person's character and spiritual resolve</term>.
*   “The sea Suph” <note>original: *mare Suph*; traditionally known as the Red Sea or Sea of Reeds</note> signifies a state of "damnation" or spiritual crisis that they had to pass through first.
*   “And the sons of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt” signifies that they were removed from their state of being harassed and were thus prepared to face their upcoming spiritual trials.

# CHAPTER XIII. VERSES 17, 18

**8092.** *And it was in Pharaoh's letting the people go.* This signifies the moment when those who had been harassing others with falsehoods finally left those who belonged to the spiritual church <term>spiritual church: a community of people who are led by the Lord through truths and the practice of charity, rather than direct perception of good</term>. This is evident from the meaning of "to let go" as leaving; from the representation of Pharaoh as those who harassed others by means of falsities (see entries 7107, 7110, 7126, 7142, 7220, 7228, 7317); and from the meaning of the sons of Israel—who are called "the people" here—as those who were of the spiritual church (as discussed above in entry 8044).

**8093.** *That God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines.* This signifies that it was provided by the Divine that they should not move toward a "truth of faith" that does not come from "good" <term>good: the inner motivation of love and kindness that gives life to religious beliefs</term>. This is clear from the meaning of "God led them not by the way," as being provided by the Divine that they should not pass that way; for "leading," when done by God, signifies Providence, and a "way" signifies truth (see entries 627, 2333), and in this context, it means passing toward truth.

This is also clear from the representation of the Philistines as those who possess "memory-knowledge" <term>memory-knowledge: factual or intellectual information about faith that is stored in the memory but has not yet changed a person’s character</term> regarding the concepts of faith, but do not live a life of charity <term>charity: the active love of neighbor expressed through useful service</term> (entries 1197, 1198, 3412, 3413). Thus, the Philistines represent those who hold truths of faith which are not rooted in good. That this is what is meant by the "Philistines and their land" can be seen from the passages in the Word where they are mentioned—especially in Jeremiah 47, where they are described, and in Joel 3:5, 6—and also from the historical accounts in the Word describing the wars between the sons of Israel and the Philistines. In these stories, the Philistines represent those who believe in "faith alone" <note>the theological doctrine that salvation is achieved through intellectual belief or "faith" without the necessity of performing good works or living a moral life</note>, or those for whom the intellectual knowledge of faith is the most important thing, rather than a life lived according to that faith.

[2] This opinion concerning "faith alone" (faith separated from charity) is not new, nor does it belong only to this current time. It existed in the ancient churches and came into use whenever people began to live lives of evil. This concept is described throughout the Word, but under different names: first by "Cain," when he killed his brother Abel (see entries 337, 340, 1179). In the internal representative sense, "Cain" signifies this kind of faith, while "Abel" signifies charity. It is also described by "Ham," when he was cursed by his father (entries 1062, 1063); and afterward by "Reuben," in that he went up on... <note>original Latin: "quod ascenderit super," referring to the biblical account of Reuben dishonoring his father's bed, signifying faith without the primary position of charity</note>

**8094.** *Because that was near.* That this signifies that it first comes up, is evident from the meaning of "near," when said of faith separate <term>faith separate: the theological error of believing that one can be saved by correct belief alone, without a life of active love or "charity"</term>, as being that it first comes up. How it is to be understood that the opinion concerning faith separate or alone first comes up, shall be briefly told. 

An evil life is attended by its own specific falsity <term>falsity: a distorted idea or lie that justifies a person's wrong actions</term>. This falsity lies hidden in a person who is in an evil state of life, and sometimes he is not even aware that it is in him. But as soon as he thinks about the truths of the church, and especially when he thinks about salvation, then this falsity comes forth and clearly shows itself. If it cannot outright deny the truth in its general statement, it explains it in a way that favors its own evil, and thus falsifies it. 

Consequently, when he is thinking about faith and charity <term>charity: the internal affection of doing good and acting with justice and kindness</term>—which are the essentials of the church and of salvation—faith at once comes up, but not charity, because charity is the direct opposite of an evil life. Therefore, he also sets charity aside and chooses "faith alone." From all this it is evident that the truths of faith are "near," but not the goods of faith <term>goods of faith: the practical, lived-out results of belief, such as kindness and integrity</term>; that is, the former come up first, and not the latter. **8104.** *At the end of the wilderness.* That this signifies the first state of temptations, is evident from the signification of a "wilderness," as being a state for the undergoing of temptations (of which above, section 8098); and as this state began at the end of the wilderness, therefore by "the end of the wilderness" is signified the first state.

### CHAPTER XIII. VERSES 20–22

**8105.** *And Jehovah went before them.* That this signifies the continuous presence of the Lord, is evident without further explanation. (That “Jehovah” refers to the Lord, see above, section 8046.)

**8106.** *By day in a pillar of cloud.* That this signifies that when there was a state of enlightenment <note>Enlightenment refers to a clear understanding of spiritual truth.</note> it was tempered by an obscurity of truth, is evident from the meaning of “by day,” or “in the day,” as being in a state of enlightenment; for the times of day, such as morning, noon, evening, and night, correspond to the various degrees of light belonging to intelligence and wisdom in the spiritual life (see sections 5672, 5962, 6110). Because of this, “day” signifies a state of enlightenment or clear perception, and “night” signifies a state of no enlightenment, or of obscure perception (section 7680). 

The meaning also comes from the word “cloud,” which signifies an obscurity of truth <term>obscurity of truth: a shaded or veiled state of understanding where the full light of truth is softened.</term>, because a cloud takes away the brightness of light from the sun and tempers it. [2] Throughout the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> it is said that Jehovah appeared “in a cloud,” and that He was “girded with a cloud,” and also that “beneath His feet was a cloud.” In these passages, “cloud” means the obscurity of truth. Specifically, it refers to the literal sense of the Word, because compared to the internal sense <note>The internal sense is the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the surface stories.</note>, the literal sense is an obscurity of truth (see the preface to *Genesis* 18; also sections 4391, 5922, 6343, 6752). 

This was symbolized by the “cloud” when the Lord was seen in glory by Peter, James, and John (*Luke* 9:34); when He appeared from Mount Sinai to the people; and when Moses entered into His presence there (*Exodus* 19:9; 20:18; 24:15–18; 34:5). It is also shown by the fact that the Lord often said He “would come in the clouds of heaven” (*Matthew* 24:30; 26:63, 64; *Mark* 13:26; 14:61, 62; *Luke* 21:27). [3] The literal sense of the Word is called a “cloud” because the internal sense, which is called “glory,” cannot be understood by a human being unless they are regenerated <term>regenerated: the process of being spiritually reborn and made new by living according to Divine truths.</term> and enlightened. 

If the internal sense of the Word—Divine truth in its full glory—were to appear before a person who is not regenerated, it would seem like thick darkness. They would see nothing at all and would even be blinded by it; that is, they would be unable to believe anything. From all this, it can be seen what is signified by a “cloud by day,” namely, an obscurity of truth; and when discussing the Word, it refers to the literal sense. [4] It is said “in a pillar of cloud and of fire,” because a “pillar” signifies a prop <note>A prop is a support or a foundation that holds something up.</note>...

In general these variations and changes are like the changes of times in the world; namely, the changes of the times of the year—spring, summer, autumn, winter, and again spring; and the changes of the times of the day—morning, noon, evening, night, and again morning.

These are the things which were represented by the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night with the sons of Israel in the wilderness.

**8111.** By long continued intercourse with the spirits of the earth Jupiter, it became evident that they are better disposed than the spirits of some other earths. Their approach when they came, their stay, and their <term>influx: the spiritual process where influence or energy flows from one being or state into another</term> at the time, were inexpressibly gentle and sweet. In the other life, goodness manifests itself by gentleness and sweetness. These qualities could be very clearly distinguished from the gentleness and sweetness of the good spirits of our earth.

**8112.** When any slight disagreement arises among them, there appears to them as it were a slender ray of white light, such as usually is that of lightning; or a little band in which are sparkling stars. These are signs of disagreement; but the disagreement among them is quickly repaired. When the stars sparkle and at the same time wander, the sign is not good; but when the sparkling stars are fixed, the sign is good.

**8113.** I was able to recognize the presence of the spirits of Jupiter, not only from the gentleness and sweetness of their approach and influx, but also from the fact that they inflowed most especially into the face, and that they disposed it to be smiling and cheerful, and continually so while they were present. It was said that they so dispose the faces of the inhabitants of their earth, for they wish to inspire them with tranquillity and delight of heart. This tranquillity and delight with which they inspired me sensibly filled my chest and heart. # SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF JUPITER

**8116.** The spirits reported that the region of their world where they had lived is very densely populated—as many people as the planet can possibly sustain. They described the land as incredibly fertile, overflowing with everything needed for life. Because the inhabitants desire nothing more than what is necessary for survival, the planet is able to support such a vast number of people.

**8117.** They further explained that their society is organized into nations, families, and households. Everyone lives separately with their own kin, and their social life is almost entirely centered around their relatives. No one ever covets the possessions of another; the idea of claiming someone else's property—let alone attacking or plundering it—never even enters their minds. They view such behavior as a crime that is both horrible and contrary to human nature. When I tried to tell them that our Earth experiences wars, looting, and massacres, they turned away and were deeply unwilling to listen.

**8118.** I have been told by the angels that the most ancient people on our own Earth lived in a similar way—organized into nations, families, and households. <note>Swedenborg refers here to the "Most Ancient Church," a symbolic era of humanity before the fall into selfishness.</note> In those times, people were satisfied with what they had. The concepts of growing rich at another’s expense or exercising power over others were completely unknown. Because of this, those early times were more pleasing to the Lord than the ages that followed. In that state, a spirit of innocence reigned, and with that innocence came true wisdom. 

Back then, everyone did good simply because it was good, and acted justly because it was just. They did not do good deeds for the sake of personal honor or profit. They spoke nothing but the truth—not because they were following a rule of logic, but because the truth flowed from a good heart. In other words, their words did not come from an intellectual process separate from their feelings, but from a <term>will: the seat of a person's love and intentions</term> that was perfectly united with their understanding. 

Because of this harmony, angels were able to interact closely with people in those times. They could lead human minds toward heaven in a state almost entirely detached from physical concerns, showing them the magnificent and happy realities of the spiritual world and sharing their own heavenly joy. These times were well-known to ancient writers, who called them the "Golden Age" and also the "Saturnian Age." <note>original: "Saturnia saecula." In classical mythology, this was a legendary era of peace and abundance when the god Saturn ruled.</note> [2] Those times were of such a nature because, as previously mentioned, people lived divided into

# THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY

[N. 8120]
...if he provides help, he confirms that person in evil and supplies him with the means to do harm to others. It is quite different for one who gives assistance to those who are good.

8121. But <term>charity</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s Latin, "caritas" refers to a selfless, spiritual love for others rather than mere financial almsgiving.</note> toward the <term>neighbor</term> <note>The word "neighbor" (proximus) here refers to anyone or anything we are called to love and serve, extending from individuals to the entire human race.</note> extends much more widely than just to the poor and needy. Charity toward the neighbor consists in doing what is right in every task, and performing one's duty in every office or role. If a judge acts justly for the sake of justice, he is practicing charity toward his neighbor. If he punishes the guilty and acquits the innocent, he is practicing charity toward the welfare of his fellow citizens, his country, and also the Lord's kingdom. By doing what is just for the sake of justice, he cares for the welfare of the Lord’s kingdom; by acquitting the innocent, he cares for his fellow citizen; and by punishing the guilty, he cares for his country. The priest who teaches truth and leads people toward what is good, doing so for the sake of truth and goodness, practices charity; but he who does such things for the sake of himself and his reputation in the world does not practice charity, because he does not love his neighbor, but only himself.

8122. The case is the same in all other instances, whether people are in a specific profession or not. This applies to children toward their parents, and parents toward their children; to servants toward their masters, and masters toward their servants; to subjects toward their king, and the king toward his subjects. In these cases, whoever performs their duty from a sense of duty, and does what is just from a sense of justice, is practicing charity.

8123. These actions belong to charity toward the neighbor because every person is "the neighbor," though in various ways (see <note>original: "n. 6818"</note>). A society, whether small or large, is "the neighbor" to a greater degree (n. 6819, 6820); our country is even more so (n. 6819, 6821); the church more still (n. 6819, 6822); the Lord's kingdom even more (n. 6819, 6823); and the Lord above all (n. 6819, 6824). In the most universal sense, the "good" which comes from the Lord is the neighbor (n. 6706, 6711), and consequently, so are justice and right. Therefore, whoever does any good thing for the sake of goodness, and anything just for the sake of justice, loves the neighbor and practices charity; for he acts from a love of what is good and a love of what is just.

<summary>This page redefines charity as the faithful performance of one's professional and social duties for the sake of justice and truth. It outlines a hierarchy of "the neighbor," moving from the individual to society, the country, the church, and ultimately the Lord.</summary>

**8124.** He who acts with <term>charity</term> <note>original: "caritas"; in this context, it refers to a selfless, spiritual love that seeks the welfare of others as its primary goal.</note> toward the <term>neighbor</term> <note>original: "proximus"; Swedenborg defines the "neighbor" not just as a person, but as the "good" within a person or a community.</note> from an internal affection is an embodiment of charity in everything which he thinks and speaks, and in everything which he wills and does. It can be said that, as to his inner being, a man or an angel is a "charity" when goodness is to him the neighbor. So widely does charity toward the neighbor extend.

# EXODUS

<meta>[N. 8137</meta>

...by **being glorified**, <note>In this context, "glorification" refers to the manifestation of Divine power and the revelation of truth that occurs when the Lord is present.</note> but here there is signified that they who had infested the well-disposed should be cast into hell, and there encompassed about with **falsities** as with waters of a sea, and this as a Divine effect from the mere presence of the Lord.

[2] To show how the case herein is, it shall be further unfolded. There are as many hells as there are *genera* and *species* <note>categories and types</note> of evils, each hell being separated from others as it were by rain-storms, clouds, or waters. In the other life evils and **falsities** appear before the eyes of spirits as rain-storms and clouds, and also as waters; the **falsities** from evils of those who have been of the <term>spiritual church: a state of being where people are led by intellectual truths and a developed conscience</term> and have lived evilly, appear as waters; but the **falsities** from evils of those who have been of the <term>celestial church: a state of being where people are led by direct love and perception of what is good</term>, appear as rain-storms. 

They who are in the hells appear to be thus encompassed, with a difference everywhere in respect to amount and kind, density and rarity, thick darkness and dimness, according to the genus and species of the **falsity** from evil. The hell where they are who have lived in **faith separate from charity** <note>This refers to the belief that one can be saved by religious doctrine alone without practicing kindness or a good life.</note> and in a life of evil, is encompassed as by the waters of a sea; the **falsities** of evil do not indeed appear as waters to those who are there, but to those who look from without. 

Above that sea, where these are, are the hells of **adulterers**; these are above, because in the <term>internal sense: the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Word hidden beneath the literal story</term> adulteries denote **adulterations of good** and the consequent perversions of truth, thus they denote evils from which come **falsities** contrary to the truths and goods of faith (n. 2466, 2729, 3399), being such **falsities** as are with those who are in the hell beneath, and who have lived contrary to the truth of the church, and have made its good of no account, and therefore have also adulterated and perverted everything that is said in the Word about good, that is, about charity toward the neighbor and about love to God. 

[3] As regards the **glorification in Pharaoh and in his army**, this here denotes immersion in this hell and being encompassed by waters as of a sea at the mere presence of the Lord, as was said above. For the evil flee from the presence of the Lord, that is, the presence of the good and truth that are from Him, feeling horror and torment at their mere approach; and also by reason of this presence they become encompassed about with their own evils and **falsities**, for these then burst forth from them;

**Persuasive faith** <term>persuasive faith: a conviction in religious doctrines based on personal gain rather than a love for truth</term> can exist alongside an evil life, but **saving faith** <term>saving faith: a heartfelt belief that leads to a life of kindness and service</term> cannot. This is because persuasive faith is a conviction that the church’s doctrines are true, not for the sake of the truth itself, nor for the sake of a better life, nor even for the sake of salvation (which such people hardly believe in), but rather for the sake of **self-advantage**—to gain status, wealth, or a good reputation. 

Such people learn religious teachings only to acquire these worldly benefits. Their goal is not to serve the church or the salvation of souls, but to serve themselves and their own circle. Consequently, it makes no difference to them whether these teachings are actually true or false; they do not care about the truth and certainly do not investigate it, for they have no genuine affection for truth for its own sake. Whatever their doctrines may be, they simply confirm them. Once they have "proven" them to themselves, they become convinced they are true, failing to realize that a lie can be argued for and "confirmed" just as easily as a truth (see references: n. 4741, 5033, 6865, 7012, 7680, 7950) <note>These numbers refer to other sections in the author's work, *Arcana Coelestia*, providing deeper cross-references for the reader.</note>.

Only faith joined to a life of good is **saving faith**. 

Saving faith is a gift from the Lord, while persuasive faith comes from the person themselves. The one lasts for eternity; the other is swept away in the afterlife, and even disappears in this world if it no longer provides any personal profit. However, as long as people benefit from it, they will fight for this faith as if they were fighting for heaven itself. In reality, they are not fighting for faith, but for themselves; the teachings of their faith are merely tools to reach an end: namely, power and wealth. ## 8149. *And all the chariots of Egypt.* 

This signifies the **doctrinal things** <term>doctrinal things: the specific teachings or organized beliefs of a religion</term> of falsity that serve their interests. This is clear from the meaning of **“Pharaoh’s chariots,”** which represent the primary false teachings upon which everything else depends. Consequently, **“the chariots of Egypt”** signify the secondary false teachings that support them. 

In the symbolic language of scripture, a king and his personal chariots represent primary or "leading" principles, while the common people (the Egyptians) and their chariots represent secondary or "supporting" principles. 

The teachings of a church, when held by those who live an evil life, are called "doctrines of falsity"—even if parts of those teachings are actually true. The reason for this is that for someone living an evil life, truths are not truly "truths" at all. Because they are applied to justify an evil lifestyle, they lose the essence of truth and take on the nature of a lie. These truths look toward evil and join themselves to it. 

Truths cannot be joined with evil unless they are **falsified** <term>falsified: the process of twisting a true idea to support a wrong or selfish conclusion</term>, which is done through wrong interpretations and perversions. This is why, for such people, even the established teachings of the church are considered doctrines of falsity, even if they were originally true. For it is a spiritual law that for those who are...

**8150.** ***And tertian captains*** <note>original: "tertiani"</note> ***upon all of them.*** This signifies that these forces were organized under general categories. This is clear from the meaning of **“tertian captains,”** which refers to the governing principles <term>generals: broad, overarching categories or principles that organize smaller details</term> under which specific details are arranged. 

“Tertian captains” carry this meaning because the number **“three”** (from which the word "tertian" is derived) signifies something that is complete and perfect (see sections 2788, 4495, 7715). The word **“captains”** refers to essential or leading things. When combined, they represent "generals," because every single element in a series must be organized under a general category to function as a unified whole and to have a distinct character. 

<note>In this philosophical system, everything is organized in a hierarchy: "Generals" are the broad categories, "particulars" are the groups within them, and "singulars" are the individual components. For more on this structure, see sections 920, 2384, 3739, 4325, 4329, 4345, 4383, 5208, 5339, 6115, 6146.</note>

**8151.** ***And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh.*** This signifies stubbornness arising from false beliefs that are rooted in evil. This is clear from the meaning of **“hardening the heart,”** which is to be determined or obstinate (see sections 7272, 7300, 7305, 7616). 

While the text says that **“Jehovah hardened Pharaoh’s heart,”** the internal sense <term>internal sense: the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories</term> reveals that it is actually the people who are in evil and falsity who harden themselves. In other words, their own evil and false ideas cause this reaction (see sections 2447, 6071, 6991, 6997, 7533, 7643, 7877, 7926). 

**8152.** ***And he pursued after the sons of Israel.*** This signifies an attempt to dominate those who live in faith combined with charity. This is clear from the meaning of **“pursuing,”** which refers to an attempt at subjugation (section 8136), and from the representation of the **“sons of Israel.”** 

As established previously, the sons of Israel represent those who belong to the **spiritual church** <term>spiritual church: a community defined by people who prioritize neighborly love and live according to their religious convictions</term>. These are people who live out their faith in both their teachings and their daily lives. For a member of the genuine spiritual church, the "good of faith"—or charity—is the most essential thing and always comes first.

# CHAPTER XIV. VERSES 5–9

**8152.** [continued] ...whereas with those for whom faith is separate from the good they do—both in what they believe and how they live—the "truth" of faith, or faith itself, is seen as the most essential thing. These individuals do not truly belong to the church, for it is the life one leads that makes the church, not a set of doctrines, except in so far as those doctrines are actually lived out. 

For this reason, it is plain that the Lord’s church is not found only in this place or that, but is everywhere—both within the nations where the church is established and outside of them—wherever people live according to the rules of charity <term>charity: here meaning active love and kindness toward others, rather than just giving money</term>. Because of this, the Lord’s church is scattered throughout the whole world, and yet it is a single whole. When the way one lives is what makes the church, rather than a doctrine separated from life, then the church is unified; but when doctrine alone makes the church, then the church is divided into many.

**8153.** ***And the sons of Israel went out with a lofty hand.*** This signifies that they were released by Divine power from the attempt to enslave them. This is clear from the representation of the **“sons of Israel,”** who represent those of the "spiritual church" <note>the "spiritual church" refers to people who are guided by a conscience based on faith and love</note>, or those whose faith is joined with charity (as mentioned just above in section 8152). 

It is also clear from the meaning of **“to go out,”** which means to be liberated—that is, to be released from the attempt to conquer or "subjugate" them, which is what is meant by the word “pursue” (section 8152). Finally, it is clear from the meaning of a **“lofty hand,”** which refers to Divine power, because the **“hand”** in sacred symbolism signifies power (see sections 878, 3387, 4931—4937, 5327, 5328, 5544, 6292, 6947, 7011, 7188, 7189, 7518, 7673, 8050, 8069). 

The word **“lofty”** signifies what is Divine. "Lofty" refers to the Divine because it points toward heaven where the Divine dwells. Therefore, in the Word <note>the "Word" refers to the Bible</note> it is said of Jehovah, or the Lord, that He “dwells on high,” and He Himself is called “the Most High,” as in these passages:

> Jehovah is exalted; for He dwelleth on high (*Isaiah 33:5*).
> Thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, and whose name is Holy: I dwell in the holy and high place (*Isaiah 57:15*).
> Jehovah sent from on high, and He rescued me (*Psalm 18:16*).

Because of this, Jehovah is frequently called **“the Most High”** (*Deuteronomy 32:8; Daniel 4:17, 32, 34; 7:18, 22, 25; Psalm 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 46:4; 50:14; 57:2; 82:6*). **8155.** ***And they overtook them encamping by the sea.*** That this signifies communication around the region of hell where are falsities from evils, is evident from the signification of “overtaking,” as being communication—for in the spiritual sense “to overtake” or come in contact with denotes influx <term>influx: the spiritual process by which thoughts and feelings flow from the spiritual world into a person's mind</term>, by which there is communication, here of the falsities from evil of those who are signified by “the Egyptians” with those who are signified by “Israel.”

# EXODUS 14:10–14

**8158.** [The biblical text continues:] **“And the children of Israel were sore afraid,”** represents a state of overwhelming spiritual dread; **“and the sons of Israel cried out to Jehovah,”** represents a humble plea for help from the Divine; **“and they said to Moses,”** represents the peak of a spiritual trial <term>temptation: a period of inner conflict where one’s faith is tested by doubt or despair</term> when one feels hopeless; **“Because there were no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in the wilderness?”** represents the thought that if one is to be spiritually lost, it matters little whether it happens through the lies of their oppressors or during the difficult process of spiritual transformation; **“Why have you dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt?”** represents the feeling that being freed from old, harmful habits was pointless; **“Is not this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying,”** represents a recurring doubt that was present even before their liberation; **“Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians,”** represents a desire to give up the struggle and return to one's old, selfish ways; **“For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than that we should die in the wilderness,”** represents the belief that living in spiritual bondage is preferable to the pain of inner change; **“and Moses said to the people,”** represents a lifting of the spirit through Divine Truth; **“Fear not,”** represents the command to cast off despair; **“stand still and see the salvation of Jehovah,”** represents the realization that salvation comes from the Lord alone and not from human effort; **“which He will work for you today,”** represents a salvation that is eternal; **“for the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you shall see them again no more for ever,”** represents the promise that once these specific spiritual errors are removed, they are gone for eternity; **“Jehovah shall fight for you,”** represents the truth that the Lord alone carries us through our spiritual battles; **“and you shall hold your peace,”** represents the understanding that human strength alone can achieve nothing in these matters.

**8159.** ***And Pharaoh drew near.*** This signifies that the spiritual influence <term>influx: the way spiritual energy or thoughts flow from the spiritual world into the human mind</term> of lies stemming from evil was becoming intense. This is clear from the representation of **Pharaoh**, who embodies those who live in falsehoods rooted in an evil heart; and from the meaning of **"drawing near,"** which refers to this spiritual "flowing in." 

In the internal sense <note>the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories</note>, this passage describes the very first trial faced by those who have been liberated from a life of pure materialism. All spiritual trials are caused by an influence from the "hells" <note>the collective state of selfishness and falsehood</note>, as the spirits from those realms stir up and draw out every latent evil or negative thought within a person.

Horror arises from the mere influx of falsity and evil with those who have conscience, for conscience is from the truth and good of faith, thus from those things which make the spiritual life. Falsities and evils are destructive of that life, and thus endeavor to inflict death, that is, **damnation** <term>damnation: a state of being completely ruled by selfish desires and false beliefs, shutting out the divine</term>; and from this comes the horrible dread.

There are **spiritual temptations**, and there are **natural temptations**. Spiritual temptations belong to the **internal man** <term>internal man: the inner, spiritual part of a person that is capable of connecting with the Divine</term>, but natural ones to the **external man** <term>external man: the outward, physical self that interacts with the material world and is driven by worldly desires</term>. Spiritual temptations sometimes arise without natural temptations, sometimes with them. Natural temptations exist when a man suffers as to the body, as to honors, as to wealth, in a word, as to the natural life, as is the case in diseases, misfortunes, persecutions, punishments, and the like. The anxieties which then arise, are what are meant by "natural temptations." But these temptations effect nothing whatever toward man's spiritual life, neither can they be called temptations, but griefs; for they arise from the wounding of the natural life, which is that of the love of self and of the world. The wicked are sometimes in these griefs, and they grieve and are tormented in proportion to the extent of their love of self and of the world, and the life they have from this source.

[2] But spiritual temptations belong to the internal man, and assault his spiritual life. In this case the anxieties are not on account of any loss of natural life, but on account of the loss of **faith** and **charity** <term>charity: here meaning active, selfless love for others rather than just financial giving</term>, and consequently of salvation. These temptations are frequently induced by means of natural temptations, for if when a man is in these—that is, in disease, grief, the loss of wealth or honor, and the like—he begins to think about the Lord's aid, His providence, the state of the evil in that they glory and exult when the good suffer and undergo various griefs and various losses, then spiritual temptation is conjoined with natural temptation. Such was the last temptation of the Lord in **Gethsemane** <note>original: "Gethsemane" — referring to the garden where Jesus experienced intense spiritual agony before his arrest</note>, and when He suffered the cross, which was the most frightful of all. **8165.** *Were there no graves in Egypt, that thou hast taken us to die in the wilderness?* That this signifies that if there is **damnation** <term>damnation: in this spiritual context, a state of being completely overtaken by false beliefs and selfish desires, resulting in a separation from the Divine</term> it would be all the same whether it came through the **falsities** <term>falsities: distorted ideas or spiritual lies that cloud a person’s judgment and lead them away from what is true</term> of the **infesters** <term>infesters: spiritual influences or "spirits" that surround a person's mind with troubling thoughts and doubts to test their faith</term>, or through a state of **temptations** in which they would yield, is evident from the **signification** <term>signification: the deeper, symbolic meaning that lies beneath the literal words of the Bible</term> of “graves,” as being damnation (see n. 2916, 4564); from the signification of “Egypt,” as being **infestations** (n. 7278), for by the Egyptians and Pharaoh are represented those who in the **other life** <term>other life: the spiritual realm or world of spirits experienced after physical death</term> infest by means of falsities (n. 7097, 7107, 7110, 7126, 7142, 7317); from the signification of “dying,” as also being damnation (n. 5407, 6119, 7494); and from the signification of “the wilderness,” as being a state of undergoing temptations (n. 8098); whence “to die in the wilderness” denotes to yield in temptation, and consequently to be damned. 

From all this it is evident that by “Were there no graves in Egypt, that thou hast taken us to die in the wilderness?” is signified that if there is damnation it would be all the same whether it came through the falsities of the infesters (thus in the state in which they were before), or through temptations in which they would yield (thus in the state into which they come afterward). 

[2] That these words are words of **despair** is evident. Moreover those who are in despair, which is the last stage of temptation, think such things, and then they are as it were on the slope, or are as it were sinking down toward hell. But at this time such thought does no harm whatever, nor do the angels pay any attention to it, for every man’s power is limited, and when the temptation arrives at the furthest limit of his power, the man cannot sustain anything more, but sinks down. But then, when he is on the downhill course, he is raised by the Lord and thus liberated from despair; and is then for the most part brought into a clear state of hope and of the consequent consolation, and also into good fortune. It is said “damnation through a state of temptations in which they would yield,” because they who yield in temptations come into a state of damnation; for temptations are to the end <note>The phrase "to the end that" here means "for the purpose of."</note> that truths and goods may be confirmed, and may be conjoined...

These two forces act reciprocally against each other. **8170.** *And Moses said to the people.* This signifies being lifted up from a state of hopelessness through **Divine Truth** <term>Divine Truth: the spiritual light and wisdom proceeding from God that provides clarity during mental or spiritual confusion</term>. This is evident from the words Moses speaks next, which describe rising out of despair. The text specifies "through Divine Truth" because all progress or "elevation" during spiritual trials is achieved by means of this truth. (For the internal symbolic sense where **Moses** represents Divine Truth, see sections 6752, 7010, 7014, and 7089.)

**8171.** *Fear not.* This means that they must not lose hope. In this context, "fearing" signifies a sense of horror (see section 8162) that leads to despair. In spiritual trials, fear begins as a deep dread and eventually settles into hopelessness. **Spiritual fear** <term>spiritual fear: an inner anxiety not of physical danger, but regarding the potential loss of one's spiritual life or goodness</term> is specifically the dread of being overcome by evil or falsity.

**8172.** *Stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah.* This signifies that salvation comes from the **Lord** <note>original: "Dominus"</note> alone, and not at all from the person themselves. This is shown by the meaning of "standing still and seeing," which signifies having **faith** <term>faith: in this sense, the act of understanding, acknowledging, and trusting in the truth</term> (to "see" denotes understanding and acknowledging, see sections 897, 2150, 2325, 2807, 3863, 3869, 4403—4421, 5400). The "salvation of Jehovah" refers to the rescue provided by the Lord. Here, where the topic is liberation from spiritual trials, the emphasis is that the Lord is the only savior. (That the name **Jehovah** in the Word refers to the Lord, see sections 1343, 1736, 2921, 3023, 3035, 5041, 5663, 6281, 6303, 6905, 6945, 6957.) It is taught here that one must believe salvation is from the Lord alone, as this is the most important part of faith during a trial. Anyone who believes they can resist a spiritual trial through their own strength will fail. This happens because they are operating under a false premise and are claiming **merit** <term>merit: the mistaken belief that one's own good deeds or strength earn them salvation</term> for themselves. By doing so, they block the **Divine influx** <term>Divine influx: the constant flow of life and power from God into the human soul</term>. However, those who believe the Lord alone fights the battle will conquer, because they are in the truth and give the credit to the Lord. A person who lives in the faith of **charity** <term>charity: the active love for one's neighbor</term> attributes all salvation to the Lord and nothing to themselves.

**8173.** *Which He will do for you today.* This signifies that which is **to eternity** <note>In the internal sense of the Word, "today" does not refer to a 24-hour period, but to a perpetual state or something that is eternally present</note>, as is evident from the meaning of "to—"
