### EXODUS [N. 8423]

...from the meaning of "gathering," as being to receive (n. 8418); and from the meaning of "day by day," that is, on each day, as being continually (also n. 8418). The reason why "two" denotes <term>conjunction</term><note>A technical term for the spiritual "joining together" or marriage of two different but complementary elements, like heart and mind.</note>, is because there are two things to which all things in the universe bear relation—namely, **good** and **truth**, or what is the same, **love** and **faith**; for good belongs to love, and truth belongs to faith. 

Hence also there are two things in man which make up his life, namely, **will** and **understanding**. The will in man has been formed to receive good or love, and the understanding to receive truth or faith. The joining of these two is called a "marriage," for when these two are joined, they are in a similar situation as a married pair: they love each other; they conceive and bring forth; and the resulting offspring is called "fruit." From this it is now plain why "two" or "double" signifies conjunction, for without the joining of these two, nothing is ever born or produced. It may be added that from all this it can be plainly seen that without love or <term>charity</term><note>In this context, charity refers to the active expression of love toward others, not just giving to the poor.</note>, faith can produce no fruit; rather, fruit must come from the two joined together.

**8424.** *Verses 6-8. And Moses and Aaron said unto all the sons of Israel, In the evening, then ye shall know that Jehovah hath brought you out from the land of Egypt. And in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of Jehovah, in that He heareth your murmurings against Jehovah; and what are we, that ye murmur against us? And Moses said, In that Jehovah shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to satiety; in that Jehovah heareth your murmurings with which ye murmur against Him: what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against Jehovah.* 

"And Moses and Aaron said unto all the sons of Israel," signifies information from <term>truth Divine</term><note>God’s truth as it is communicated to humanity.</note>; "In the evening, then ye shall know that Jehovah hath brought you out from the land of Egypt," signifies that in the end of the former state there shall be a revelation that they are liberated; "and in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of Jehovah," signifies that in the beginning of a new state there will be the <term>advent of the Lord</term><note>The "coming" or presence of the Divine within a person's perception.</note>; "in that He heareth your murmurings," signifies that complaints will cease; "against Jehovah, and what are we, that ye murmur against us?" signifies that the complaints were against the Divine, and not against those who represented it.

In this context, “the glory of God” clearly signifies light from the Lord, which is the <term>Divine truth</term><note>In this theological framework, "Divine truth" is not just a concept, but a spiritual light or energy that radiates from God and allows the human mind to perceive reality.</note> proceeding from Him. > The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth. (*John* 1:14).
> These things said **Isaiah** when he saw His glory and spoke of Him. (*John* 12:41).

In these instances, “glory” refers to the Lord. In the same way, in the books of **Moses**:

> As I live, the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of Jehovah. (*Numbers* 14:21).

In this context, “the glory of Jehovah” signifies the arrival of the Lord and the enlightenment provided by the <term>Divine truth</term><note>In this theological system, Divine truth is described as a spiritual light that emanates from God, enabling the human mind to perceive reality and goodness.</note> which comes from Him. > When the Son of man comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels (*Mark 8:38*).

Just as “the glory of Jehovah” signifies the Lord in the form of Divine truth, so also “glory” signifies Divine wisdom and intelligence, which are the results of the Divine truth coming from the Lord. Wisdom and intelligence from the Divine are meant by “glory” in the book of **Ezekiel** (1:28; 8:4; 9:3; 10:4, 18, 19; 11:22, 23), where it was represented by a rainbow such as one sees in a cloud.

**8428.** *In that He hears your murmurings.* That this signifies that complaints will cease is evident from the meaning of “hearing.” When the word “hearing” is used in reference to Jehovah, it means to show mercy and to bring help; consequently, it means that complaints will cease. Furthermore, “murmurings” signify the suffering caused by the bitterness of spiritual <term>temptation</term><note>Temptation here refers to a state of inner conflict or crisis where a person's faith is tested by their own selfish or worldly desires.</note> and the complaints that result from it (as seen in section 8351).

**8429.** *Against Jehovah, and what are we that you murmur against us?* That this signifies that the complaints were directed against the Divine and not against those who represented it is evident from the fact that “Jehovah” refers to the Divine—specifically, the Divine truth which Moses and Aaron represented. It is also evident from the meaning of “murmuring” as a complaint (as just mentioned in section 8428). Because it is said that “they murmured against Jehovah and not against Moses and Aaron,” it signifies that they murmured against the Divine truth represented by Moses and Aaron (see section 8425), rather than against the men themselves. This is why the following verse also says, “What are we? Your murmurings are not against us”; for a person who represents the Divine is, by comparison, nothing at all. Moreover, those who complain against a person who represents the Divine when that person speaks from a Divine source are not complaining against the individual, but against the Divine itself.

**8430.** *And Moses said*, signifies information (just as it did previously in section 8425).

**8431.** *In that Jehovah shall give you in the evening flesh to eat.* That this signifies that at the end of a <term>state</term><note>In this work, a "state" refers to a person's inner spiritual condition or mood, which is constantly changing, much like the weather or the time of day.</note>, goodness will be <term>appropriated</term><note>To "appropriate" something spiritually means to make it a permanent part of one's own character or life.</note> by means of delight, is evident from the meaning of “evening,” as being the end of a state (see section 8426); and from the meaning of “flesh,” as being that which is truly one's own but has been made alive—the "heavenly self" that a person receives from the Lord. Thus, it represents the good of love (as seen in sections 148, 149, 780, 3813, 7850, 8409). 

However, in this specific instance, "flesh" signifies the good of faith, because it refers to the meat of a bird or "flying thing" called a “quail.” In spiritual symbolism, a flying creature signifies things that are spiritual or related to faith; consequently, its “flesh” signifies goodness of that particular quality—specifically the goodness experienced by the <term>natural man</term><note>The "natural man" refers to the part of the human personality that deals with the physical world, external senses, and basic emotions.</note>, which is called "delight." 

It should be understood that “manna” signifies the goodness of the <term>internal or spiritual man</term><note>The "spiritual man" is the higher part of the human mind that is open to heaven and concerned with eternal truths.</note>, while the “quail” signifies the goodness of the external or natural man, which we experience as delight. The reason for this distinction is that the manna was given in the morning, while the quail was given in the evening. In the spiritual world, the "morning" is a state where spiritual goodness (the internal) is clear and bright, while natural goodness (the external) is in the shadows. Conversely, the "evening" is a state where natural goodness and delight are clear, while spiritual goodness is obscured. These cycles or "alternations" follow one another so that a person may be perfected, specifically so that goodness can be fully integrated into their life, which happens during the "evening" state through the experience of delight.

**8432.** *And in the morning bread to satiety.* That this signifies that in the beginning of a new state they shall have as much good as they can receive, is evident from the meaning of “bread,” as being the good of love (sections 2165, 2177, 3464, 3478, 3735, 3813, 4211, 4217, 4735, 4976, 5915, 8410). In this context, however, it specifically means the "good of truth," which is the spiritual nourishment for the church, because "bread" here refers to the manna (which will be discussed further on). This is also evident from the meaning of “the morning,” as—

# EXODUS

### CHAPTER XVI. VERSES 9-12

**8439.** *Come ye near before Jehovah.* That this signifies a state of reception and the application to it, is evident from the meaning of "coming near before Jehovah," as being <term>influx</term><note>Influx refers to the constant flow of life, love, and wisdom from God into the human soul.</note> (see n. 8159), and therefore also reception; for reception is the reciprocal or matching response to influx, because they correspond to each other. In so far as a person receives the Divine influx, so far they are said to "come near before Him." In the spiritual sense, coming near before Jehovah is nothing else; for coming near to Him is achieved by means of faith and love. Since both faith and love come from Jehovah (that is, from the Lord), "coming near to Him" also signifies the reception of the good and truth that flow in from Him. 

That it also signifies application is because reception is meaningless unless there is also application—specifically, application to "use" or service. For the influx from the Divine passes first into the perception, which belongs to a person's understanding; from there it passes into the will, and next into act—that is, into good work, which is use—and there it reaches its completion. When the influx of good and truth from the Lord follows this path, then that good and truth are <term>appropriated</term><note>In this context, to "appropriate" means to make something a part of one's own character or life.</note> to the person. This is because the influx goes down into the <term>ultimate of order</term><note>The "ultimate of order" refers to the final, physical level of existence where spiritual intentions become physical actions.</note>, which is the final stage of nature, where all Divine influx aims to arrive. A person in whom Divine influx advances in this way may be called "a way of heaven." From all this it can now be seen that by "coming near before Jehovah" is signified a state of reception and its application; in this specific case, it refers to a state of receiving the "good" signified by the <term>manna</term><note>Manna represents spiritual nourishment or the "bread of heaven" that sustains the soul.</note> and the "delight" signified by the <term>quail</term><note>The quail represents a more natural or worldly level of satisfaction that is still provided by the Divine.</note>.

**8440.** *For He hath heard your murmurings.* That this signifies that He may bring aid on account of the suffering in the <term>temptation</term><note>Temptation here describes an internal struggle or a crisis of faith rather than a simple desire to do wrong.</note>, is evident from the meaning of "hearing," when said of Jehovah, as being to have compassion and to bring aid, and consequently to cause the suffering to cease (see above, n. 8428); and from the meaning of "murmurings," as being the suffering and complaint experienced during a spiritual trial (n. 8351, 8428, 8433).

**8451.** *And it was in the evening.* That this signifies the end of a state is evident from the meaning of “evening,” which refers to the conclusion of one spiritual phase before another begins (as seen previously in section 8426).

**8452.** *That the quail came up.* This signifies a <term>natural delight</term> through which spiritual good is introduced. This is clear from the meaning of “quail” as a symbol for natural pleasure. The reason a “quail” represents natural delight is that it was a bird of the sea; in the language of symbols, sea birds represent natural things, and their flesh—which the people craved—represents the feeling of delight (see section 8431). 

This delight is described as the means “through which good is given” because the quail appeared in the evening. In the spiritual world, when a person (or an angel) is in a state corresponding to "evening," they are allowed to return to the natural affections and pleasures they experienced in the world. This is done so that "good" can be drawn out of those experiences; in other words, so they can be perfected (section 8426). 

Everyone is perfected by having faith and charity planted in their <term>external or natural man</term><note>The "natural man" is the part of our personality that interacts with the physical world and experiences earthly desires, as opposed to the "spiritual man" which looks toward heaven.</note>. Unless these qualities are rooted there, spiritual truth and goodness cannot flow in from the <term>internal man</term> (the soul), because there is no "receptacle" to catch them. If there is no reception, this <term>influx</term><note>The constant spiritual "flow" of life and light from the Divine into the human mind.</note> is blocked and lost. Therefore, the natural part of a person must be brought into a "state of accommodation"—it must be made ready. This is achieved through delights, because the things that feel good to our natural selves are the only things we truly "feel" and notice. 

[2] That the “quail” represents this natural delight is also confirmed by the fact that it was carried from the sea, as written in the Book of Numbers:

> A wind went forth from Jehovah, and carried off the quail from the sea, and let it down upon the camp (*Numbers* 11:31).

In this sense, a “bird of the sea” and its “flesh” signify natural delight, though in a negative context, they can signify the delight of <term>concupiscence</term><note>Original Latin: *concupiscentia*. This refers to selfish or obsessive cravings that pull a person away from spiritual health.</note>.

# EXODUS

This is signified by "the quail" in the following passage from the books of Moses:—

> The rabble that was in the midst of the people lusted with a great craving, and desired to have flesh; they said, "Now our soul is dried up, and our eyes see nothing except this manna." Then a wind went out from Jehovah and brought quails from the sea, letting them fall beside the camp. The people stayed up all that day, all night, and all the next day gathering the quails; even those who gathered the least reached ten <term>homers</term><note>A 'homer' was an ancient Hebrew unit of dry measurement, roughly equal to 220 liters or about 6 bushels.</note>, which they spread out for themselves all around the camp. But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was even swallowed, the anger of Jehovah burned against the people, and Jehovah struck them with a very great plague. Therefore, that place was named the "Graves of Lust," because there they buried the people who had given in to their cravings. (*Numbers 11:4, 6, 31-34*)

In this context, "the quail" represents the delight of <term>concupiscence</term><note>In this theological context, 'concupiscence' refers to an intense, selfish desire or lust for worldly and physical pleasures that outweighs spiritual concerns.</note>. We call it the delight of concupiscence when the pleasure of any physical or worldly love takes total control over a person, even to the point of extinguishing the goodness and truth of faith within them. This specific type of pleasure is described as the cause of the great plague. 

However, the "natural delight" symbolized by the quail given to the people in the evening in this chapter of *Exodus* is different. It is not the delight of concupiscence, but rather the pleasure of the <term>natural man</term><note>The 'natural man' refers to our external self—our physical senses, basic emotions, and worldly logic—as opposed to the 'spiritual man' or the inner soul.</note> that aligns with the goodness of the inner, spiritual self. This healthy delight contains spiritual goodness within it, whereas the lustful delight described in the book of *Numbers* contains hellish evil within it. 

Both are called "delight," and both are felt as pleasure, but there is the greatest possible difference between them; for one has heaven inside it, and the other has hell. Furthermore, when the external body is eventually set aside, the first becomes a person’s "heaven," and the second becomes their "hell." 

[3] The situation is like that of two women who, on the outside, appear equally beautiful in face and pleasant in company. However, their inner characters are completely different: one is faithful and healthy of spirit, while the other is unfaithful and corrupt. Thus, in spirit, one lives among the angels, while the other lives among the malevolent. What they truly are does not appear on the surface; it is only revealed when the external layer is pulled back and the internal reality is shown. These points have been made so that we may distinguish the "natural delight" that contains good—which is what the quail represents here—from mere selfish craving.

When a man is in this faith, he is in peace, for he then fears nothing, and no solicitude about things to come disquiets him. A man comes into this state in proportion as he comes into love to the Lord. 

[2] All evil, especially self-confidence, takes away a state of peace. It is believed that an evil person is at peace when he is in gladness and tranquillity because all things succeed with him. But this is not peace; it is the delight of lusts, which counterfeits a state of peace.

### [N. 8458]

As truth, this divine influence builds the <term>intellectual part</term><note>The faculty of the mind responsible for thought, logic, and understanding.</note> of the mind; as good, it builds the <term>new will part</term><note>The part of the mind transformed by the Lord to feel love and kindness instead of selfish desires.</note>. In a human being, the intellect is distinct from the will because the intellect presents things to itself as forms or images—allowing us to see them as if they were in the light. In contrast, the will is affected by these things emotionally, feeling them as a sense of delight or "good." The specific quality of the form determines the quality of that delight. 

The reason "smallness" is associated with truth and "roundness" is associated with good is rooted in how truth and good actually appear in the <term>other life</term><note>The spiritual world or heaven, where inner qualities take on visible, outward appearances.</note>. When truths and goods are shown in a visible form—as they are openly seen by the eyes of spirits and angels—truth appears in a <term>discrete quantity</term><note>Individual, separate units that can be measured or counted, like grains of sand.</note>. This means truth is seen as more or less in quantity, often has an angular shape, and appears white. 

However, good is seen there in a <term>continuous quantity</term><note>A seamless, flowing whole that cannot be easily divided into separate parts, like a stream of water.</note>; therefore, it is not viewed as "much" or "little" in a countable sense. Good also appears as a round shape—which is a continuous form—and shows itself in colors like blue, yellow, and red. These visual differences exist because the inner quality of truth and good expresses itself naturally when it becomes visible. Indeed, there is nothing in the entire universe that does not relate back to either good or truth in some way.

**8459.** *Small as the hoar frost upon the earth.* This signifies that truth has taken the form of good, becoming consistent and flowing. We know this because "small" refers to truth (as explained just above), and "hoar frost" refers to being in the form of good.

### [Entry No. 8468] EXODUS

Many houses shall be in devastation, even great and beautiful, that there be no inhabitant, for ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah (*Isaiah* 5:9, 10);

In this passage, "ten acres" signifies that which is full and abundant; "a homer" carries the same meaning. Conversely, "a bath" and "an ephah" signify a very small amount. This is because when "ten" represents plenty, a "tenth part" (as these measures are in relation to the larger units) represents a meager amount. In the books of Moses:

**8469.** *According to the number of your souls.* This signifies that there is enough for everyone in the society—specifically, enough of the "good of truth" which is symbolized by the "**manna**." This is evident from the phrase "according to the number of the souls," which means a sufficient supply for everyone in the community. Since the measure of "an omer per head" signifies enough for each individual, the phrase "according to the number of souls" signifies enough for the entire group. 

The subject here is the "good" enjoyed by those in the Lord’s spiritual kingdom. This goodness is represented by the manna, and the text explains that it is given in a measure sufficient for every individual and for the community as a whole. Each "house" of the Israelites represented a specific <term>society</term><note>Swedenborg uses 'society' to describe communities of angels in heaven who are grouped together based on their shared character and type of goodness.</note> in heaven (see Entry Nos. 7836, 7891, 7996, 7997). 

Regarding these heavenly societies, the situation is this: Heaven is composed of countless societies, each distinct from the others. Every society has a "general good" that differs from that of other societies. Furthermore, every individual within a society has a "particular good" that is unique and different from everyone else in that same group. These distinct, varied, yet harmonious qualities of goodness combine to create a structure called the "**heavenly form**." The entire expanse of heaven is made up of such forms. When we speak of these connections in terms of the "goodness" involved, we call them "**forms**"; when we speak of them in terms of the people involved, we call them "**societies**." This spiritual reality was represented on earth by the way the Israelites were divided into tribes, families, and houses.

**8470.** **Take ye every one for him who is in his tent.** This signifies communication with others, which leads to the "general good." This helps clarify what is meant by "communication" and the "general good" resulting from everyone "taking for those in their tent." 

In a heavenly society, every individual shares their own personal goodness with everyone else in that society. In return, the entire community shares its collective goodness with each individual. From this exchange arises the **general good** <note>Also known as the "common good" or "collective well-being."</note>. This local good is then shared with the general good of other societies, creating an even broader circle of goodness, ultimately reaching a "most general" state. This is how heaven becomes a single, unified whole—much like how the different organs and internal parts of a human body, though distinct and various, form one single person through their constant communication and cooperation. Such a sharing of "goods" is only possible through love, which acts as a <term>spiritual conjunction</term> <note>A spiritual connection or bonding that links separate entities into a whole.</note>. The universal force that organizes and brings every detail into order is the Divine Good of Divine Love flowing from the Lord.

**8471.** **And the sons of Israel did so.** This signifies the actual effect or the carrying out of the instruction, which is clear without further explanation.

With such there universally reigns **solicitude** <note>Anxious or excessive concern.</note> about things to come, and a desire to possess all things and to dominate over all, which is kindled and grows according to the additions thus made, and finally does so beyond all measure. They grieve if they do not obtain the objects of their desire, and feel anguish at the loss of them; and they have no consolation, because of the anger they feel against the Divine, which they reject together with everything of faith, and curse themselves. Such are they who have care for the morrow.

[3] Very different is the case with those who trust in the Divine. These, notwithstanding they have care for the morrow, still have it not, because they do not think of the morrow with solicitude, still less with anxiety. If they become rich, they do not set their hearts on riches; if they are raised to honors, they do not regard themselves as more worthy than others; if they become poor, they are not made sad; if their circumstances are mean <note>Common, lowly, or humble.</note>, they are not dejected. They know that for those who trust in the Divine all things advance toward a happy state to eternity, and that whatever befalls them in time is still conducive thereto.

[4] Be it known that **Divine Providence** <note>God's constant, governing care over the universe and every individual life.</note> is universal, that is, in things the most minute; and that they who are in the **stream of Providence** <note>A metaphor for living in harmony with God’s guidance, allowing one’s life to be carried toward spiritual well-being.</note> are all the time carried along toward everything that is happy, whatever may be the appearance of the means; and that those are in the stream of Providence who put their trust in the Divine and attribute all things to Him; and that those are not in the stream of Providence who trust in themselves alone and attribute all things to themselves, because they are in the opposite, for they take away providence from the Divine, and...

**8481.** *And it bred worms.* This signifies that, consequently, the state became filthy. This is evident from the meaning of “breeding worms,” which is to produce something foul; for worms are produced from things that are rotting and stinking. The **falsity of evil** <note>In this context, "falsity of evil" refers to distorted or wrong ideas that a person uses to justify selfish or harmful behavior.</note>—which exists within the "good" that we claim as our own—is compared to a “worm” because the effect is similar: falsity gnaws at the spirit and causes torment. 

There are two things that make up hell, just as there are two things that make up heaven. The two that make heaven are **good** and **truth**, and the two that make hell are **evil** and **falsity**. Consequently, it is these two in heaven that create the happiness there, and it is the two in hell that create the torment there. The torment in hell arising from falsity is compared to a “worm,” and the torment from evil is compared to “fire.” As it is written in *Isaiah*:

> As the new heavens and the new earth which I will make shall stand before Me, so shall your seed and your name stand: at last it shall come to pass from month to month, and from sabbath to its sabbath, that they shall stand before Me: then they shall go forth, and shall see the carcasses of the men that have transgressed against Me, for **their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched**; and they shall be a loathing to all flesh (*Isaiah 66:22–24*).

In the same way, the Lord says in *Mark*:

> Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched (*Mark 9:44, 46, 48*);

speaking of **Gehenna** <term>Gehenna: A Greek term for the Valley of Hinnom, which was used as a metaphor for hell or a state of spiritual destruction because it was a place where fires burned continuously to consume waste.</term> or hell. The filthiness of falsity is also compared to a “worm” in the books of *Moses*:

> Thou shalt plant vineyards, and till them, but thou shalt neither drink of the wine, neither shalt thou gather, because the worm shall devour it (*Deuteronomy 28:39*);

In this passage, “wine” represents **truth from good** <note>The refreshing spiritual insight that flows from a heart full of love and kindness.</note>, and in the opposite sense, it represents falsity from evil (see section 6377).

### CHAPTER XVI. VERSES 21-24

**8484.** "...and it grew hot and it melted," signifies that it vanishes away according to the degree of the increase of **concupiscence** <note>original: *concupiscentia*; in this context, it refers to intense worldly or selfish desires that consume spiritual life</note>; "and it was on the sixth day," signifies at the end of every state; "they gathered bread double," signifies a joining together (conjunction) from the good they have received; "two omers for each one," signifies the power or capacity they have at that time; "and all the princes of the assemblage came and told Moses," signifies a reflection based on primary truths; "and he said unto them," signifies instruction; "This is what **Jehovah** <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, representing Divine Love</note> spake," signifies **influx** <note>original: *influxus*; the spiritual process by which life and truth flow from the Divine into the human mind</note> from the Divine; "a rest," signifies a state of peace when there is no temptation; "a **sabbath** <note>original: *sabbatum*; meaning a day of rest, symbolizing the union of the Divine and the Human</note> holy to Jehovah is the morrow," signifies the joining together of good and truth for all eternity; "what ye will bake, bake ye," signifies preparation for the joining of good; "and what ye will boil, boil ye," signifies preparation for the joining of truth; "and all that is left over, this lay ye by for you to keep until the morning," signifies the enjoyment of all good and truth then as if it were their own; "and they laid it by till the morning," signifies the enjoyment that is to come; "as Moses commanded," signifies according to instruction from Divine truth; "and it did not stink, and the worm was not in it," signifies that there was nothing filthy within it, because in this way it was made their own by the Lord.

**8485.** *And they gathered it morning by morning.* This signifies the reception of good from the Lord continually. For "morning by morning" signifies every "morrow," and the "morrow" signifies that which is eternal (section 3998), and thus also that which is perpetual and continual.

**8486.** *Every man according to the mouth of his eating.* This signifies that it is received by everyone according to their power of **appropriation** <note>original: *appropriatio*; the process of making spiritual qualities part of one's own nature through living according to them</note>. **8487.** *And the sun grew hot, and it melted.* This signifies that it vanishes away according to the degree of the increase of concupiscence. This is evident from the meaning of "the sun growing hot," which refers to increasing concupiscence (which we will discuss further below), and from the meaning of "melting," which is to vanish away.

# EXODUS

**8487.** ...vanishing, as being to vanish away. That "the sun grew hot" denotes increasing **concupiscence** <term>concupiscence: from the Latin *concupiscentia*, referring to intense, burning desires for worldly or selfish things that consume spiritual life</term>, is because "the sun," in a positive sense, signifies heavenly love. This is because the Lord is the Sun in the afterlife; the heat radiating from Him is the good of love, and the light is the truth of faith. <note>The author provides an extensive list of references to earlier sections of his work (n. 1053 to 7270) to support this specific symbolism of the Lord as the Sun.</note>

Consequently, in the opposite or negative sense, "the sun" denotes the love of self and of the world, and "the heat" or "growing hot of the sun" denotes in this sense concupiscence.

[2] We must briefly explain how the "good of truth" (signified by **manna** <note>manna: the "bread from heaven" which represents spiritual nourishment</note>) vanished as **concupiscence** increased (signified by its "melting when the sun grew hot"). Spiritual good is indeed given to those in the spiritual church when they are being **regenerated** <term>regenerated: the process of spiritual rebirth and character transformation</term>. However, since the delights of self-love and world-love—which previously made up their entire life—extinguish this spiritual good (because they are opposites), pure spiritual good cannot stay with a person for long. Instead, the Lord tempers this good using the delights of the person’s previous natural loves. If the good were not tempered in this way, it would feel unpleasant to the person and would eventually be loathed. This is how heavenly good first appears to those undergoing spiritual change. Therefore, as the delights of self-love and worldly love rise up, the good of heavenly love vanishes, for as stated, they are opposites; the reverse is also true.

[3] This is why there are "alternations of states" in heaven, which correspond to the changing seasons and times of day in our world (see n. 8426). Through these shifts, inhabitants are occasionally released back into the delights of natural pleasures. Without these changes of state, the good of heavenly love would become "dry" and lose its value to them. It is different when it is balanced by natural delights, either at the same time or in succession. This is why, when the manna was first given to the Israelites every morning, the **quail** <note>original: *coturnix*; here representing natural or sensory delights that satisfy the external mind</note> was also given in the evening; for the "quail" signifies natural delight, as well as the delight of concupiscence (n. 8452).

<summary>This page explains that the "heat of the sun" represents worldly desires that can dissolve spiritual goodness (manna). It details how the Lord balances high spiritual states with natural delights to ensure that spiritual life remains attractive and sustainable for the individual.</summary>

### CHAPTER XVI. VERSES 21–24

8452). [4] It should be understood that the **concupiscences** <term>concupiscences: from the Latin *concupiscentia*, referring to intense, often selfish, worldly cravings or desires</term> into which those in heaven are occasionally released when they experience an "evening" state <note>The author describes spiritual life as a cycle of day and night; "evening" is a state of diminished joy or clarity</note> are not desires that oppose heavenly goodness. Instead, they are desires that agree with it to some extent. They also include the pleasure taken in the splendor of a beautiful home or fine clothing.

Such delights do not destroy the essence of heavenly love, though they do temporarily obscure it. Eventually, as a person is **regenerated** <term>regenerated: the process of being spiritually reborn and reformed by God</term>, these desires become the "outer layers" or foundations of heavenly goodness. At that stage, they are no longer called "cravings," but simply "delights." 

Without being tempered by these natural human pleasures, heavenly love would feel "dry" to us; it would eventually be rejected as something worthless. This is symbolized in the Bible when the children of Israel called the **manna** <note>manna: the miraculous food provided by God in the desert, representing spiritual nourishment</note> "dry food" and "worthless food" once the meat of the quail was no longer provided. > The mixed multitude among them felt a deep craving, and the children of Israel also wept again and said, "Who will give us meat to eat? Now our soul is parched; our eyes see nothing at all but this manna." (*Numbers 11:4, 6*)

> The people spoke against God and against Moses: "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water; and our soul loathes this worthless bread." (*Numbers 21:5*)

> Jehovah humbled you and let you hunger, then fed you with manna which you did not know, nor did your fathers know; so that He might teach you that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that comes from the mouth of Jehovah. (*Deuteronomy 8:3*)

[5] Just like the "manna," the "unleavened bread" also signifies goodness that is pure and free from falsehood. For the same reason, this bread is called the "bread of affliction" (*Deuteronomy 16:3*). From all this, we can see why the "good of truth" vanishes as worldly cravings increase—this is what is meant by the manna "melting when the sun grew hot."

This meaning is clear from the symbolism of the "sixth day," which represents the conclusion of a spiritual cycle.

# EXODUS [N. 8489]

**8489.** *They gathered a double portion of bread.* This signifies a **conjunction** <term>conjunction: a spiritual joining or union, here between the individual and divine goodness</term> arising from the goodness received. This is clear from the meaning of "gathering the manna" as the reception of good (see previous explanations in n. 8467, 8472; and that **manna** <note>original Hebrew: *man*, a miraculous food provided to the Israelites, symbolizing spiritual nourishment</note> represents the "good of truth," n. 8464); and from the meaning of "double," which represents this joining together (n. 8423).

**8490.** *Two omers for each person.* This signifies the spiritual power present at that time. An **omer** <term>omer: an ancient Hebrew unit of dry measure, roughly two liters</term> signifies having "enough," and therefore the capacity or power to receive what is needed (see n. 8468, 8473). In this context, it refers to having sufficient power for union with the Divine; for the "seventh day" or the **Sabbath** <note>original: *shabbath*, meaning to cease or rest from labor</note> signifies the union of goodness and truth within a person.

**8491.** *And all the leaders of the community came and told Moses.* This signifies **reflection** <term>reflection: the act of the mind turning inward to consider spiritual truths</term> based on primary or foundational truths. This is shown by the "leaders of the community" representing these primary truths (see n. 1482, 2089, 5044), and "telling" representing the process of reflection (n. 2862, 5508).

**8492.** *And he said to them.* This signifies instruction. The act of "saying" here introduces the directions that follow regarding how the people were to gather manna on the day before the Sabbath. (That "saying" often indicates spiritual instruction in the Bible, see n. 6879, 6881, 6883, 6891, 7186, 7267, 7304, 7380.)

**8493.** *This is what Jehovah said.* This signifies **influx** <term>influx: the steady "flowing in" of divine energy, life, or wisdom from God into the human soul</term> from the Divine. This is because **Jehovah** <note>The Hebrew name for God, often translated as LORD</note> (the Lord) instructs people through this inner flowing of wisdom. In the historical narratives of the Bible, this internal process is described outwardly as "saying" or "speaking." (For other instances where "speaking" represents this divine influx, see n. 2951, 5481, 5797, 7270, 8128.)

**8495.** *A sabbath holy to Jehovah is the morrow.* That this signifies the conjunction of good and truth to eternity, is evident from the signification of "the sabbath," as being the conjunction of good and truth (of which below); and from the signification of "the morrow," as being to eternity (see n. 3998). He who does not know what the sabbath represented, and thus what it signified, cannot know why it was accounted the most holy of all things. 

But the reason why it was accounted most holy was that in the supreme sense it represented the union of the **Divine** and the **Divine Human** <note>The 'Divine Human' is a central concept referring to God as He made Himself accessible and visible to humanity</note> in the Lord; and in the relative sense the conjunction of the Divine Human of the Lord with the human race. Consequently the sabbath was most holy. And because it represented these things, it also represented heaven in respect to the conjunction of good and truth, which conjunction is called "the **heavenly marriage**." 

And as the conjunction of good and truth is effected by the Lord alone, and nothing of it by man, and as it is effected in a state of peace, therefore it was most severely forbidden that man should then do any work, insomuch that the soul which did this was to be cut off, as we read in *Moses*:—

> Ye shall keep the sabbath, because it is holy to you, he that profaneth it, dying shall die; for whosoever doeth work therein, that soul shall be cut off from the midst of his people (*Exod. xxxi. 14*).

Therefore one was stoned who merely picked up sticks on that day (*Num. xv. 32–36*). Therefore also the commandment concerning the sabbath is the third commandment in the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, immediately following the two concerning the holy worship of Jehovah (*Exod. xx. 8; Deut. v. 12*). And therefore the sabbath is called "an **eternal covenant**" <note>original: *berit olam*, a permanent and binding spiritual agreement</note> (*Exod. xxxi. 16*), for by "covenant" is signified conjunction (n. 665, 666, 1023, 1038, 1864, 1996, 2003, 2021, 6804).

### CHAPTER XVI. VERSES 21-24

#### [8495 continued]

...entering in chariots and on horses, they and their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city shall be inhabited forever (*Jeremiah 17:24, 25*);

By "work on the sabbath" is signified everything that comes from **our own** <term>our own: translated from the Latin 'proprium,' referring to the human self-will, ego, or the belief that we act entirely by our own power</term>. The state of those who are not led by their own self-will, but by the Lord, is described by the image of "kings and princes sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, entering through the gates of the city." 

In this spiritual symbolism:
* **Kings** signify the truths of faith.
* **Princes** signify the primary or most important aspects of those truths.
* **Sitting upon the throne of David** signifies that these truths originate from the Lord.
* **Chariots and horses** signify the doctrinal and intellectual systems of faith.

It should be understood that everything originating from a person’s own selfhood is inherently flawed, while everything originating from the Lord is good. (For those led by the Lord, every detail of life—both in the intellect and the will—is influenced by Divine flow; for further evidence on how faith and charity flow into every part of life, see references: 2886–2888, 6053–6058, 6189–6215, 6307–6327, 6466–6495, 6598–6626, 6982, 6985, 6996, 7004, 7055, 7056, 7058, 7147, 7270.)

[5] That the sabbath served as a **representative** <note>representative: a physical ritual or object that mirrors a deeper, spiritual reality</note> of the union between the Lord and the human race is clear in *Ezekiel*:

> I gave them My sabbaths to be a sign between Me and them, so they would acknowledge that I, Jehovah, am the one who makes them holy (*Ezekiel 20:12; see also Exodus 31:13*).

This is also why it was forbidden to light a fire on the sabbath day (*Exodus 35:3*). In this context, **fire** signifies the vital energy of life itself; "kindling a fire" represents generating that life-energy from one's own ego rather than receiving it from the Divine. From these points, it is clear why the Lord is called the "Lord of the sabbath" (*Matthew 12:1–8*). It also explains why the Lord performed many healings on the sabbath (*Matthew 12:10–13; Mark 3:1–8; Luke 6:6–11; 13:10–17; 14:1–6; John 5:9–18; 7:22, 23; 9:14, 16*); the physical diseases He cured represented spiritual diseases caused by internal evils (see references 7337, 8364).

This is how the union of heaven—that is, of those who are in heaven—with the Lord works. It is described as being "as if from their own" because the goods of faith and charity cannot be given to a human or an angel so that they truly belong to them as their own property. This is because humans and angels are only **recipients**, or forms designed to receive life—and therefore good and truth—from the Lord. Life itself comes from no other source. ## 8512. 

**And Jehovah said unto Moses.** That this signifies the appearing of the Divine obscured, is evident from the meaning of the phrase "Jehovah said," as involving what follows—in this case, that they did not keep His commandments and laws, and thus the appearing of the Divine among them was clouded. For this happens when any one does not live according to the Divine commandments; because when a person *does* live according to them, they live according to Divine order, since the Divine commandments are truths and goods in conformity with that order. When a person lives according to order, they then live in the Lord, because the Lord is order itself. From this it follows that he who does not live according to the commandments and laws of Divine order, does not live in the Lord, and consequently the Divine appears obscured to them.

To live in a way that is not yet according to order is to be guided by truth alone. When a person is guided only by what they know to be true (rather than what they love as good), the Lord does not appear clearly to them. They walk in a kind of darkness where goodness is hard to see. It is different when a person is led by goodness; they then see clearly in the light.

**8513.** *How long do ye refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?*

This signifies that they are not acting according to Divine order, as was explained just above (in section 8512). To understand what it means to act according to Divine order versus acting against it, we should consider this further: everything done according to Divine order is open on the inside all the way to the Lord, and thus contains heaven within it. However, everything not done according to Divine order is closed on the inside and lacks the presence of heaven. 

[2] Divine order consists in the Lord flowing through a person’s <term>interiors<note>The inner levels of the human mind, including the will and deeper intentions.</note></term> into their <term>exteriors<note>The outer levels of the mind and the physical body, where actions and speech take place.</note></term>—essentially, flowing through a person's will into their actions. This happens when a person is "in good"—meaning they desire to do good for its own sake, not for personal gain. When someone does good for selfish reasons, their inner self is closed. They cannot be led by the Lord through heaven; instead, they lead themselves. A person's love determines who leads them: whoever loves themselves more than their neighbor leads themselves, but whoever loves what is good is led by that good, and therefore by the Lord, who is the source of all good. 

[3] This shows the difference between living according to order and not doing so. The Word <note>original: "Verbum"; referring here to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> and the teachings of faith derived from it show how one must live to be in order. Those who only look at external, physical things cannot understand this; they do not know what the "internal" is, or even that it exists, let alone that it can be opened to allow heaven to enter. **8514.** *See ye.* This signifies that they should pay attention and reflect. This is clear from the meaning of "seeing" as understanding (see sections 2325, 3863, 4403—4421, 5114); consequently, it also means to perceive (sections 2150, 3764, 4567, 4723, 5400) and to reflect (sections 6836, 6839).

**8515.** *Because Jehovah hath given you the sabbath.* This signifies the <term>conjunction<note>A spiritual union or "marriage" where a person’s knowledge of what is right (truth) finally merges with their heartfelt desire to do what is right (good).</note></term> of good and truth brought about by the Lord. This is evident from the meaning of "the sabbath" as the union of good and truth (see n. 8495). That this is done by the Lord is shown by the phrase "Jehovah hath given," for in the Word, "Jehovah" refers to the Lord.

**8516.** *Therefore He giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days.* This signifies that, for this reason, the Lord provides enough "good through truth" at the end of a person's initial spiritual state to eventually bring about this union. This is shown by:
1. The "sixth day" meaning the end of a previous state (see n. 8421).
2. The "manna" (called "bread" here) meaning the <term>good of truth<note>A stage of development where a person does good things because they are following the rules/truths they have learned, rather than yet acting from a spontaneous love of goodness itself.</note></term> (sections 8462, 8464).
3. The "sabbath," for which the double portion was given, meaning the union of good and truth (n. 8495). 

It was shown earlier that because the "sabbath" represents this union, the fact that "no manna was found on the seventh day" signifies that when a person reaches this union, they act from a place of goodness, and no longer merely from a place of following rules/truth. In fact, they *must* no longer act from truth alone (n. 8510). 

**[2]** Since this might seem like a <term>paradox<note>The idea that one should eventually stop "acting from truth" can be confusing; the author explains that we move from "learning the rules" to "loving the life."</note></term>, it can be explained briefly. Everyone must be led to Christian goodness—which is called "charity"—by way of the truths of faith. The truths of faith teach us not only what <term>charity<note>Spiritual love for the neighbor.</note></term> is, but also what its nature must be. Unless a person first learns this from the teachings of their church (since it is impossible to know this instinctively), they cannot be prepared or adapted to receive this goodness. For example, a person must know from their faith that it is not true charity to do good for the sake of oneself or for a reward.

...internal Divine truth, which is represented by Moses, to the external truth Divine, which is represented by Aaron, as being influx; <note>The author uses "influx" to describe the way spiritual energy or information flows from a higher, internal level to a lower, external one.</note> for Divine influx takes place through the truth which proceeds immediately from the Lord into the truth which proceeds mediately. **8530.** ***Take an urn.*** That this signifies truth, is evident from the signification of "an urn," as here being truth. That "an urn" denotes truth, is because it was the vessel which received the manna, by which is signified good, and all truth is as a vessel for good; hence also by <term>vessels</term> <note>In this context, a "vessel" is any mental or spiritual structure that "holds" or contains life and love.</note> in general are signified truths (n. 3068, 3079, 3316, 3318), and consequently by "vessels" in particular, and here by "an urn." That truths are recipient vessels for good may be illustrated by various things in nature—as by light, which is recipient of the heat from the sun, the light signifying truth, and the heat in the light signifying good. So it is with truth and good. It is similar with a garment in respect to the body, and with the body in respect to the soul; also with a blood-vessel and a fiber in respect to the blood and <term>animal spirit</term> <note>This refers to an 18th-century physiological concept of a subtle fluid that carried life through the nerves.</note> enclosed therein; so also with the lungs in respect to the heart, consequently with the respiration of the lungs in respect to the pulse of the heart; in a word, with every organic form of the body in respect to the life which is therein. From these comparisons it can be seen what is the quality of truth without good, or what is the quality of faith without charity, namely, that it is like the organic forms of the body without life; that it is like the respiration of the lungs without the pulse of the heart, or like the lungs without the heart; and that it is like a blood-vessel and a fiber without blood and animal spirit; also like a body without a soul; consequently that it is like something inanimate; and if evil instead of good be therein it is like a <term>carcase</term>. <note>original: "cadaver" (a corpse or dead body)</note>

**8531.** ***And put the omerful of manna therein.*** That this signifies good therein as much as it will hold, is evident from the signification of "the omerful," namely, as much as it will hold; and from the signification of "the manna," as being spiritual good, or the good of truth (see n. 8462, 8464).

**8532.** ***And lay it up before Jehovah.*** That this signifies that it may be in the Divine presence, is evident without explication.

**8533.** *To be kept for your generations.* This signifies that it serves as a measure for those who belong to the spiritual church <note>The "spiritual church" refers to a state of being where people are led to what is good through the understanding of truths, rather than by direct intuition or celestial love.</note>. As previously discussed, this represents having "as much as is sufficient" (see n. 8468), and thus acts as a measure for the amount of "good" <note>In this theological framework, "good" refers to the specific quality of love and charity an individual possesses.</note> that this church held. (The phrase "your generations" refers to the members of this spiritual church; see n. 8526.)

Regarding the measure or degree of "good" belonging to a church, one should know that in the afterlife, these spiritual qualities vary in both quality and quantity. These are determined for every person during their life in this world based on the depth of their faith and the extent of their charity. When the Lord allows it, the specific quality and quantity of a person's goodness is made visible to the angels; it can be seen clearly in the light of heaven, though not in the light of the world. This same principle applies to the church as a whole. In the Word <note>The "Word" here refers to Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, the quantity and quality of goodness belonging to individuals and the church are represented by weights and measures. In this specific passage, the amount of goodness in the spiritual church (represented by the children of Israel) is symbolized by the "omer of manna" stored before Jehovah to be kept.

**8534.** *As Jehovah commanded Moses.* This signifies that it was done according to the Divine mandate, which is clear from the meaning of "commanding"—when it comes from Jehovah—as a direct instruction (see above, n. 8466, 8524).

**8535.** *And Aaron laid it up before the Testimony to be kept.* This signifies that it was placed in the presence of the Divine. This is evident from the meaning of "laying up to be kept," which signifies creating a memorial (see above n. 8526, 8533), and from the meaning of "before the Testimony," which refers to being in the presence of the Divine. That "the Testimony" <term>the Testimony</term> <note>Usually referring to the Decalogue or the Ten Commandments, which "testify" to the covenant between the Divine and humanity.</note> represents the Divine is clear from the preceding text; Moses told Aaron to store it "before Jehovah" (see n. 8532), which means before the Divine. "The Testimony" signifies the Divine because, in a universal sense, it refers to the Word; and because the Word is Divine Truth, it is the Lord Himself. That the Lord is "the Word" is made clear in the Gospel of *John*:—

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word: and the Word was made flesh, and dwelt in us <note>John 1:1, 14. In this context, "the Word" represents the Divine Truth coming into the world.</note>.

That "the Testimony" denotes the Lord in the form of Divine truth is evident from the ark where the Law published from Sinai was kept, which is called "the Testimony." From this, the tabernacle derived all its holiness. The Testimony was the holy Divine itself; this is clear because above it was the <term>propitiatory</term> <note>Also known as the "Mercy Seat," the gold lid of the Ark of the Covenant, representing the place where the Divine presence met humanity.</note> with the cherubs. **8536.** *Verses 35, 36. And the sons of Israel did eat the manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat the manna until they came unto the border of the land of Canaan. "Until they came to a land inhabited" signifies before they came to heaven, where goodness is found everywhere. "They did eat the manna until they came unto the border of the land of Canaan" signifies that they continued to take in goodness from truth until they reached the region of heaven. "And an omer is the tenth part of an ephah" signifies the specific amount of goodness present at that time.

**8537.** *And the sons of Israel did eat the manna forty years.* That this signifies the appropriation of the good of truth in the state of all temptations is evident from several symbolic representations:
*   The **sons of Israel** represent those who belong to the <term>spiritual church</term> <note>A community of people who are led toward what is good by learning and understanding spiritual truths.</note> (see n. 6426, 6637, 6862, 6868, 7035, 7062, 7198).
*   **Eating** signifies the act of appropriation, or making something one's own (n. 3168, 3513, 3596, 4745).
*   The **manna** represents the "good of truth" <note>This refers to the quality of goodness that is born from living according to spiritual truths.</note> (n. 8464).
*   **Forty years** signifies states of temptation. (In spiritual symbolism, "years" denote internal states, see n. 482, 487, 488, 493, 893; and the number "forty" specifically denotes trials and temptations, n. 730, 862, 2272, 2273, 8098.)

**8538.** *Until they came to a land inhabited.* That this signifies before they came to heaven where good is everywhere, is evident from the meaning of "land"—in this context the land of Canaan—as being the Lord’s kingdom, and thus heaven <note>Swedenborg frequently references his previous points (n. 1607, 3038, etc.) to show that "Canaan" consistently symbolizes the spiritual state of heaven.</note>. Heaven is called "a land inhabited" from the presence of good, for "inhabited" signifies that which is made alive by goodness.

**8539.** *They did eat the manna until they came unto the border of the land of Canaan.* That this signifies that there was an <term>appropriation</term> <note>The process of making spiritual values a permanent part of one’s own character.</note> of the "good of truth" by them until they reached the region of heaven, is evident from:
* The meaning of "the manna," as being the good of truth; 
* The meaning of "eating," as being appropriation; 
* And the meaning of "the land of Canaan," as being heaven. 

Therefore, the "border of the land of Canaan" represents the entrance to heaven, or the region where the heavenly state begins. From all this, it is clear that their "eating the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan" signifies that they made the <term>good of truth</term> <note>A state where a person does what is right because they understand it to be true, rather than doing it from a spontaneous love of goodness.</note> their own right up until they reached the threshold of heaven. 

[2] The nature of this process is shown by what was said earlier regarding how we acquire goodness through truth. Specifically, before a person undergoes <term>regeneration</term> <note>The spiritual process of being "reborn" or transformed from a worldly person into a spiritual one.</note>, all goodness is obtained through the study and application of truth. However, after regeneration, the person is led by the Lord through goodness itself. 

The first state—learning and practicing truth—is symbolized by the "six days" of work that come before the seventh. The second state—living from love and goodness—is symbolized by the "seventh day" or the "Sabbath." This is also why the first state was represented by the sons of Israel wandering in the wilderness for forty years, and the second state by their entry into the land of Canaan. 

The reality is this: a person remains "outside" of heaven as long as they act primarily from a sense of duty to truth rather than from a heart of goodness. They truly enter heaven only when they act from goodness, for then they are moved by the Lord according to the "order of heaven." One cannot enter heaven, where this perfect order exists, until they have been prepared; and this preparation involves using truth to reach a state of goodness.

<summary>This page explains that the Israelites eating manna until reaching Canaan symbolizes the spiritual journey of using learned truths to reach a state of genuine goodness (heaven). It distinguishes between the state of spiritual struggle/learning and the state of living in heavenly order.</summary>

# CHAPTER XVI. VERSES 35, 36

**8540.** *And an <term>omer</term> <note>A dry measure of volume, approximately 2 liters.</note> is the tenth part of an <term>ephah</term>.* That this signifies the amount of the good then, is evident from the meaning of "an <term>omer</term> is the tenth part of an <term>ephah</term>," as being as much as is sufficient. This is because the number "ten" signifies a state of fullness (see n. 3107), and therefore a "tenth part" signifies a portion that is exactly enough for the purpose (n. 8468). It is also evident from the meaning of an <term>ephah</term> as representing "good." The <term>ephah</term> denotes good because it and the <term>omer</term> were used to measure dry goods used for food—such as wheat, barley, and fine flour—and in spiritual symbolism, things used for food represent different types of goodness. Conversely, the <term>bath</term> and the <term>hin</term> were used to measure liquids used for drink; consequently, those measures represent different types of truth. In the language of symbols, the container takes on the meaning of what it is designed to hold. 

[2] That the <term>ephah</term> was a standard measure is clear from these passages:

> You shall have a just <term>ephah</term> and a just <term>hin</term> (*Leviticus 19:36*).
> The <term>ephah</term> and the <term>bath</term> <note>A liquid measure roughly equal to 22 liters.</note> shall be of one measure, so that the <term>ephah</term> contains the tenth part of a <term>homer</term> <note>A 'homer' was a large bulk measure, not to be confused with the 'omer' discussed above.</note> (*Ezekiel 45:11*).
> You shall have just balances, and a just <term>ephah</term>, and a just <term>bath</term> (verse 10).
> It is mentioned as a standard measure in the same way in *Amos 8:5*.

[3] That "an <term>ephah</term>" represents goodness is evident from the passages concerning the <term>meat-offering</term> <note>original: "minchah." In historical English, "meat" meant food in general; this refers to a "grain offering" made of fine flour.</note>. For these offerings, the flour or meal was measured by the <term>ephah</term> (*Leviticus 5:11; Numbers 5:15; 28:5; Ezekiel 45:24; 46:7, 11*). The grain offering itself represents goodness. This is also shown in this passage from the prophet *Zechariah*:

> The angel who spoke with me said, "Lift up your eyes and see, what is this that goes forth?" and I said, "What is it?" He said, "This is the <term>ephah</term> that goes forth." He said moreover, "This is their eye in all the earth." And behold, a leaden weight was lifted up, and there sat a woman in the midst of the <term>ephah</term>. Then he said, "This is Wickedness," and he threw her into the midst of the <term>ephah</term>, and he threw the leaden weight upon its mouth. Then I lifted up my eyes and saw two women coming forth, with the wind in their wings; they had wings like the wings of a stork; and they lifted up the <term>ephah</term> between the earth and the heaven. And I said to the angel, "Where are they carrying the <term>ephah</term>?" He said to me, "To build it a house in the land of <term>Shinar</term> <note>Ancient Babylonia; spiritually, it represents a state of external worship that hides internal evils.</note>; and when it is prepared, she shall be set there on her own base" (5:5–11).

[4] No one can understand what these things signify except through the **internal sense** <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note>, and unless he thereby...

### CONTINUATION ABOUT THE SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH JUPITER.

**8541.** As regards their Divine worship, the chief point is that they acknowledge our Lord as the Most High, who rules heaven and earth; they call Him, "The One Only Lord." And because they acknowledge and worship Him during their bodily life, they accordingly seek Him after death, and find that He is the same as our Lord. <note>The author identifies the "One Only Lord" of the Jovians as Jesus Christ.</note> They were asked whether they know that the One Only Lord is a Man? They answered that they all know that He is a Man, because on their earth He has been seen by many as a Man, and because He instructs them in the truth, preserves them, and gives eternal life to those who believe in Him. They said further that He has revealed to them how they should live, and how they should believe; and that what has been revealed is handed down by the parents to their children, and that thus the teaching spreads to all the families, and thus throughout the whole nation that is descended from one father.

# N. 8541] SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF JUPITER

**8542.** The greatest care is taken that no one should fall into wrong opinions about the One Only Lord; and if they observe that anyone begins to think wrongly about Him, they first admonish him, then deter him by means of threats, and finally by means of punishments. They said that they have observed that if any such thing has crept into any family, that family is taken from among them—not by any death penalties inflicted by their companions, but by deprivation of breathing and consequently of life by spirits, after they have first been threatened with death. <note>Swedenborg often describes the inhabitants of other planets as being under the direct, visible supervision of the spirit world to maintain their moral order.</note> For on that earth, spirits speak with the people and chastise them if they have done evil, and also if they have intended to do evil (see n. 7801–7812); consequently, if they think badly about the One Only Lord, they are threatened with death unless they repent. In this way the worship of the Lord, who to them is the supreme Divine, is preserved there.

**8543.** They do not know that their One Only Lord was born a man on this earth. And because a doubt was injected by the spirits of our earth—whether their One Only Lord is the same as our Lord—they removed the doubt by recalling that they had seen Him in the Sun, and that they recognized that it was He whom they had seen on their earth. (On this subject see n. 7173; and that our Lord is the Sun of heaven <term>Sun of heaven</term>, <note>In Swedenborg’s vision, the Lord appears in the spiritual world as a Sun that provides light (wisdom) and heat (love) to angels.</note> n. 1053, 3636, 3643, 4060, 4321, 5097, 7078, 7083, 7171, 7173.)

# EXODUS

### THE SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF THE PLANET JUPITER (continued)

[**8544.**] ...but this doubt, which flowed in for a moment, was also cleared away in an instant. It had originated from certain spirits belonging to our earth. To my surprise, the spirits of Jupiter felt such deep shame for doubting even for a moment that they asked me not to publish this account on our earth. They were afraid they might be accused of a lack of faith, even though they now understand these truths better than most others.

**8545.** While I was reading the seventeenth chapter of the Gospel of *John*—which speaks of the Lord’s love and His "glorification" <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "glorification" refers to the process by which Jesus made His human nature Divine.</note>—spirits from the planet Jupiter were present with me. As they heard the words, a holy influence came over them, and they confessed that everything written there is Divine. 

However, spirits from our own earth who were skeptics continually raised objections. They pointed out that He was born as an infant, lived as an ordinary man, appeared like anyone else, and was crucified. The spirits of Jupiter paid no attention to these arguments. They remarked that such skeptics are like their own "devils" whom they despise. They added that nothing from heaven can find a place in the minds of such spirits from our earth; instead, they are filled only with material, worldly things, which the Jupiter spirits call "dross." <note>The term "dross" (Latin: *scoriae*) refers to the waste matter or impurities left after refining metal; here it signifies thoughts focused solely on the physical world without spiritual insight.</note> 

The spirits of Jupiter confirmed this assessment when they noticed the reaction of the Earth-spirits to another fact: when the Earth-spirits heard that the inhabitants of Jupiter walk about naked, their thoughts were immediately filled with obscenity. They ignored the description of the Jupiter inhabitants' heavenly life, which was being described at the same time (see n. 8375). <note>To the inhabitants of Jupiter, nakedness symbolizes innocence and a state of being "clothed" by the Divine, whereas spirits from Earth associate it with shame or lust due to their more material focus.</note>

**8546.** On another occasion, I spoke with the spirits of Jupiter about the Lord. I explained that no one can do anything good from themselves, but only from the Lord, who is Goodness itself and the source of all that is good. They replied modestly that they had always supposed they could do good of their own accord and didn't know any other way to think about it. 

But when it was demonstrated to them that all good comes solely from the Lord, they admitted they had been speaking in a "human" way, whereas the idea that all good is Divine is the "heavenly" way of speaking. They noted that their angels think this way, and they themselves do as well, as they become more like angels. They added that it is simply easier or more natural to speak the way they first did. In response, I was led to tell them that the Lord allows those who live in simplicity and innocence to speak that way, as long as they acknowledge in their hearts that no good originates in themselves, but everything comes from the Lord.

## CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

### THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY

**8548.** Anyone who does not receive spiritual life—that is, anyone who is not begotten anew by the Lord—cannot enter into heaven. This is what the Lord teaches in the Gospel of *John*:
> “Truly, truly, I say to you, Unless a man be begotten anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God” (3:3). <note>The phrase "begotten anew" (original Latin: *denuo generatus*) is often translated in modern Bibles as being "born again."</note>

**8549.** A person is not born of their parents into spiritual life, but only into natural life. Spiritual life consists of loving God above all things and loving one’s neighbor as oneself, according to the commandments of faith which the Lord has taught in His Word. However, natural life is to love oneself and the world more than the neighbor—and even more than God Himself.

**8550.** Every person is born of their parents into the evils of the love of self and of the world. Every evil which has become a habit and a second nature is passed down to the offspring. Thus, it is inherited successively from parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents in a long series stretching backward. Because of this, the accumulation of inherited evil has eventually become so great that a person’s own inherent life is nothing but evil. This continuous, inherited nature cannot be broken or changed except by the Lord through a life of faith and charity.

**8551.** A person continually leans toward and slips back into what they have inherited. By doing this, they reinforce this evil in themselves and also add even more evils of their own making.

**8552.** These evils are utterly opposed to spiritual life; they destroy it. Therefore, unless a person, in respect to his spiritual...

<summary>This page explains that true humanity is found in reflecting the Lord's love and introduces the "Doctrine of Charity," which argues that spiritual rebirth is necessary to overcome inherited selfish and worldly tendencies.</summary>

## CHAPTER XVII.

1. And all the assemblage of the sons of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys according to the mouth of Jehovah, and they encamped in Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink.
2. And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said, Give ye us water and we will drink. And Moses said to them, Why quarrel ye with me? why do ye tempt Jehovah?
3. And the people thirsted there for waters, and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this, that thou hast made us come up out of Egypt, to make me die, and my sons, and my cattle, with thirst?
4. And Moses cried unto Jehovah, saying, What shall I do to this people? a little more and they stone me.
5. And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pass on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go.
6. Behold, I stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come waters out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Israel.
7. And he called the name of the place <term>Massah</term> <note>original Hebrew: *Massāh*, meaning "Temptation" or "Testing."</note> and <term>Meribah</term> <note>original Hebrew: *Merībāh*, meaning "Quarreling" or "Strife."</note>, because of the quarreling of the sons of Israel, and because of their tempting Jehovah, saying, Is Jehovah in the midst of us, or not?
8. And Amalek came, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

10. And Joshua did as Moses had said to him, in fighting against Amalek; and Moses, and Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

12. 13. And Joshua weakened Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

16. And he said, Because there is a hand against the throne of Jah <note>original: "Jah," a poetic shortened form of the name Jehovah or Yahweh</note>, Jehovah shall have war against Amalek from generation to generation.

### THE CONTENTS.

**8554.** In the preceding chapter, in the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The deeper spiritual or symbolic meaning that Swedenborg believed was hidden beneath the literal stories of the Bible.</note>, the third temptation was treated of—that there was a lack of good. This having been given them, in the internal sense in this chapter the fourth temptation is treated of—that there was a lack of truth. This temptation is signified by "the murmuring of the sons of Israel because they had no water;" and therefore the truth of faith was given them by the Lord, which is signified by "the water out of the rock of Horeb."

## THE INTERNAL SENSE.

**8556.** Verses 1—3. *And all the assemblage of the sons of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys according to the mouth of Jehovah, and they encamped in Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink. And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said, Give ye us water and we will drink. And Moses said to them, Why quarrel ye with me? why do ye tempt Jehovah? And the people thirsted there for the waters; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this, that thou hast made us come up out of Egypt, to make me die, and my sons, and my cattle, with thirst?*

“And all the assemblage of the sons of Israel journeyed,” signifies the progression of spiritual life; “from the wilderness of Sin,” <note>original: "a deserto Sin." In this context, Sin is a geographical location, not a moral failing; spiritually, it represents a specific stage of testing.</note> signifies a transition from a state of <term>temptation</term> <note>In this spiritual philosophy, "temptation" refers to an internal struggle where a person's faith or character is tested.</note> regarding what is good; “after their journeys,” signifies according to the order of life required for receiving the life of heaven; “according to the mouth of Jehovah,” <note>original: "ad os Jehovae." This refers to following the Divine command or guidance.</note> signifies by the providence of the Lord; “and they encamped in Rephidim,” signifies the arrangement of the inner self for undergoing temptation regarding truth—the specific nature of which is signified by the name “Rephidim;” “and there was no water for the people to drink,” signifies a lack of truth and the refreshment that comes from it; “and the people quarreled with Moses,” signifies a severe complaint directed against Divine truth; “and they said, Give ye us water, and we will drink,” signifies a deep and burning desire for truth; “and Moses said to them,” signifies a response provided by <term>influx</term> <note>The process by which the Divine flows into a person's thoughts and perceptions.</note> into their thoughts; “Why quarrel ye with me?” signifies that they should be more moderate in their complaints; “why do ye tempt Jehovah?” signifies that their complaint was actually against the Divine, whose help they had begun to doubt; “and the people thirsted there for the waters,” signifies an intensification of the longing for truth; “and the people murmured against Moses,” signifies a...
