greater degree of suffering; “and said, Wherefore is this, that thou hast made us come up out of Egypt,” signifies why have we been liberated from <term>infestations</term> <note>In this context, "infestations" refers to being overwhelmed by negative thoughts or spiritual pressures that hold a person back from growth.</note>; “to make me die, and my sons, and my cattle, with thirst,” signifies that from the lack of truth everything of spiritual life is expiring.

**8557.** *And all the assemblage of the sons of Israel journeyed.* That this signifies what is progressive of spiritual life, is evident from the signification of “journeying,” as being what is successive and continuous of life (see n. 4375, 4554, 4585, 5996, 8181, 8345, 8397), here what is successive or progressive of spiritual life, that is, its growth, which takes place continuously by means of <term>temptations</term> <note>The author uses "temptations" to mean inner struggles or crises of faith that test and ultimately strengthen a person's character.</note>. That spiritual life grows by means of temptations is because by means of them the truths which are of faith are confirmed, and are conjoined with the good which is of <term>charity</term> <note>Charity here refers to the active love and desire to do good for others.</note>. (That “the assemblage of the sons of Israel” denotes those who are of the spiritual church, see n. 7830, 7843.)

**8558.** *From the wilderness of Sin.* That this signifies from a state of temptation as to good, is evident from the signification of a “wilderness,” as being a state of undergoing temptations (see n. 6828, 8098); and from the signification of “Sin,” as being the quality and state of temptation as to good (n. 8398) <note>original: "Sin." Though it sounds like the English word for wrongdoing, in the original Hebrew this is a specific geographic location; the author interprets it here as representing a specific stage of testing the heart's intentions.</note>.

**8559.** *After their journeys.* That this signifies according to the order of life for receiving the life of heaven, is evident from the signification of “journeys,” as being what is progressive of spiritual life (of which just above, n. 8557), thus the order of that life (n. 1293). That it denotes for receiving the life of heaven, is because that life is a gift of the Lord to man by means of the temptations that are described by the journeys of the sons of Israel in the wilderness. The life of heaven is to be led of the Lord by means of good. In order that a man may come to that life, good must be implanted by means of truth; that is, charity by means of faith. So long as this is being done, the man is in the way to heaven, but is not yet in heaven. And in order that at that time the truths which are of faith may be confirmed, and may also be conjoined with good, the man is let into temptations, for these are the means of the conjunction of good and truth. <header>EXODUS [N. 8559</header>

A person who lives in good—that is, who has the affection of doing good for its own sake and for the sake of their neighbor—is uplifted into heaven. This is because they are aligned with the order of heaven and are led by the Lord through that goodness. From all this, one can see what is meant by "the life of heaven."

**8560.** *According to the mouth of Jehovah.* This signifies that they were led by the <term>providence</term> <note>Providence refers to the Lord's continuous and careful guidance of every detail of a person's life toward their eternal well-being.</note> of the Lord. This is evident from the meaning of "the mouth of Jehovah" as the Divine Truth according to which they were led; for "the mouth of Jehovah" is used here to mean a Divine utterance, and being led according to it is what we call Providence. Divine Providence differs from all other forms of leading or guidance because Providence constantly looks toward what is eternal. It continually leads a person toward <term>salvation</term> <note>In this context, salvation is the process of being healed from selfish tendencies and prepared for a life of love in heaven.</note>, and it does this through various states—sometimes joyful, sometimes sorrowful. A person cannot possibly understand why these states occur, yet they are all beneficial to their eternal life. These are the things signified by "journeys according to the mouth of Jehovah." (On the fact that "Jehovah" in the Word <note>original: "Verbo"; Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> denotes the Lord, see references: n. 1343, 1736, 2004, 2005, 2018, 2025, 2156, 2329, 2447, 2921, 3023, 3035, 5041, 5663, 6281, 6303, 6905.)

**8561.** *And they encamped in Rephidim.* This signifies the arrangement of the <term>interiors</term> <note>Interiors refers to the deeper levels of the human mind and spirit where thoughts and feelings originate.</note> for undergoing a <term>temptation</term> <note>A "temptation" here is not an impulse to do something bad, but a spiritual crisis or trial that tests and strengthens a person's faith and character.</note> regarding truth. The specific nature of this trial is signified by the name "Rephidim." This is clear from the meaning of "encamping" as the setting in order of truth and good for undergoing trials (see n. 8130, 8131, 8155); in this case, a trial regarding truth, which is represented by their "having no water" (which is discussed below). We speak of "the setting in order of the interiors" because truth and good constitute the inner life of a person in the church. The reason "Rephidim" signifies the nature of this trial is that place names in the Bible signify the quality or state of the subject at hand—here, the specific quality of a state of spiritual trial concerning truth.

**8562.** *And there was no water for the people to drink.* This signifies a lack of truth and the resulting lack of refreshment. This is evident from the meaning of "water" as the truth of <term>faith</term> <note>Faith is defined here not just as belief, but as the internal understanding of spiritual truths.</note> (see n. 2702, 3058, 3424, 4976, 5668); and from the meaning of "drinking" as being instructed in the truths of faith and receiving them (n. 3069, 3772, 4017, 4018).

here, to be refreshed; for just as water and drink refresh our natural life, so truths and the <term>knowledges of truth</term> <note>These are the specific facts and concepts learned from sacred texts that provide the framework for spiritual understanding.</note> refresh our spiritual life. For a person who is in spiritual life longs for the sustenance of that life from things called heavenly food and drink, which are the <term>goods and truths of faith</term> <note>In this context, "good" refers to the impulse of love and charity, while "truth" refers to the wisdom or ideas that guide that love.</note>; in the same way that a person in natural life longs for sustenance from natural food and drink. 

[2] The reason that <term>temptation</term> <note>Swedenborg defines "temptation" not just as a move toward sin, but as an inner spiritual struggle or crisis where one's beliefs and values are tested.</note> concerning truth is now being discussed is because the temptation concerning "good" was treated just before it. After that trial, the people received the manna, which signifies good. For when a person is gifted with "good" by the Lord, they begin to long for "truth." This longing is intensified by a lack of truth, because goodness is constantly striving to find truth. All genuine affection for truth originates from goodness. This is similar to physical food, which cannot nourish our natural life without drink; food naturally "longs" for drink so they can be joined together to be of use to the body. This is why a trial concerning truth follows immediately after a trial concerning goodness. Temptation always attacks that which a person loves and longs for (see references: n. 4274, 4299).

**8563.** *And the people quarreled with Moses.* That this signifies a grievous complaining against <term>truth Divine</term> <note>Divine Truth represents the laws and wisdom that proceed from God; in the story of the Exodus, Moses represents this Divine Truth acting as a guide.</note>, is evident from the meaning of "to quarrel," which is a grievous complaining (since anyone who "quarrels" while in the midst of a spiritual trial is complaining bitterly); and from the representation of Moses, who stands for truth Divine (see references: n. 6723, 6752, 6771, 6827, 7010, 7014, 7089, 7382).

**8564.** *And they said, Give ye us water and we will drink.* That this signifies an ardent longing for truth, is evident from what was shown just above (n. 8562) regarding the meaning of "water" and "drinking."

**8565.** *And Moses said to them.* That this signifies an answer by <term>influx</term> <note>Influx is the spiritual process by which Divine life and thought flow into the human mind, often appearing to us as our own spontaneous thoughts.</note> into the thought, is evident from the meaning of "saying" when it comes from the Divine Truth (represented by Moses). In this context, it signifies an answer; and since every answer from the Divine is experienced as an influx into one's thoughts, this is the internal meaning.

**8567.** *Why do ye tempt Jehovah?* That this signifies that it was against the Divine, of whose aid they despair, is evident from the signification of "tempting <term>Jehovah</term>," <note>original: "Jehovah." In this context, it refers to the Divine Being or the Lord. To "tempt" Him signifies a state of doubt or complaint against God's providence.</note> as being to complain against the Divine; that it denotes even to despairing of His aid, is because complaints in <term>temptations</term> <note>In Swedenborg's thought, a "temptation" is not just a lure to sin, but an intense inner spiritual struggle or crisis that tests a person's character and faith.</note> involve such despair. For temptations are continual despairings of salvation, in the beginning slight, but in course of time grievous, until at last there is doubt, almost denial, of the presence of the Divine and of His aid. 

In temptations the spiritual life is for the most part brought to this extremity; for in this way the <term>natural life</term> <note>The "natural life" refers to the self-centered ego and worldly desires, which must be "extinguished" or quieted so the spiritual self can emerge.</note> is extinguished, because then, in the midst of the despair, the inmost is kept by the Lord in combat against falsity; and therefore this despair is soon dissipated by comfortings that are in the next place insinuated by the Lord; for after every spiritual temptation there is consolation, and as it were newness of life. (That temptations are carried even to despair, see n. 1787, 2694, 5279, 5280, 7147, 7155, 7166, 8165, and that after temptations there is consolation, n. 3696, 4572, 5246, 6829, 8367, 8370.)

**8568.** *And the people thirsted there for the waters.* That this signifies an increase of longing for truth, is evident from the signification of "thirsting," as being to strive after and long for, and as being predicated of truth, as "hungering" is predicated of <term>good</term>; <note>In this system of thought, "Good" relates to the will and love, while "Truth" relates to the intellect and faith.</note> and from the signification of "water," as being the truth of faith (see n. 8562). That "to thirst" denotes to strive after and long for the truth which is signified by "water," is very plain from many passages in the Word, as in *Amos*:—

> Behold the days come wherein I will send a famine into the land, not a famine for bread, nor a thirst for waters, but for hearing the words of Jehovah; and they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they shall run to and fro to seek the word of Jehovah, and shall not find it; in that day shall the beautiful virgins and the young men faint with thirst (viii. 11-13);

a longing to know truth is here described by "thirsting;" the longing for truth is signified by "I will not send a thirst for...

here "water" plainly denotes the truth of faith from the Word, thus from the Lord; "never thirsting" here denotes that truth shall no longer fail him.

To "drink" spiritually is to take in knowledge and allow it to become part of one's internal life.</note>; "streams of living water" denote the divine truths which come from the Lord.

### EXODUS [N. 8568]

> Bring ye waters to meet him that is thirsty; O ye inhabitants of the land of Tema, come before the wanderer with his bread (xxi. 14);

where “bringing waters to meet him that is thirsty” denotes instructing in truths him who longs for them, and thus refreshing the life of his soul. <note>The land of Tema refers to an Arabian region; spiritually, it represents those who possess a simple kind of goodness and are ready to be taught deeper truths.</note> In the same:—

“the hungry one” denotes him who longs for good; and “he that thirsteth for drink,” him who longs for truth. <note>In this symbolic system, "hunger" relates to the heart's desire for love and goodness, while "thirst" relates to the mind's desire for wisdom and truth.</note> [6] Again:—

> The poor and needy seek water but there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst; I will open rivers upon the hillsides, and I will put fountains in the midst of the valleys, the wilderness for a pool of waters, and the dry land for springs of waters (*Isa.* xli. 17, 18);

every one can plainly see that “seeking water” denotes seeking truth; that “failing for thirst” denotes being deprived of spiritual life from a lack of truth; that “rivers,” “fountains,” “a pool,” and “springs of waters” denote the truths of faith in which they were to be instructed. [7] Again:—

> Say ye, Jehovah hath redeemed his servant Jacob; then shall they not thirst, He shall lead them in the wastes; He shall cause the waters to flow out of the rock for them, and He will cleave the rock that the waters may flow out (*Isa.* xlviii. 20, 21);

“they shall not thirst” denotes that truths shall not fail them; “waters” here manifestly denote the truths of faith. Again:—

> They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor the sun smite them; for He that hath mercy on them shall lead them, so that even upon the springs of waters He will lead them (*Isa.* xlix. 10);

“they shall not hunger” denotes that good shall not fail them; “they shall not thirst” denotes that truth shall not fail them; “springs of waters” denote the knowledges of truth from the <term>Word</term>. <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures, which are seen here as a source of living water or divine instruction.</note> [8] In like manner in *Moses*:—

> Jehovah leadeth thee through the great and fearful wilderness, of the serpent, of the fire-serpent, and of the scorpion, and of thirst, where... <note>The "fire-serpent" and "scorpion" represent the dangerous persuasions and deceits that threaten the soul when it lacks the protection of spiritual truth.</note>

### [N. 8568] CHAPTER XVII. VERSES 1–3 281

...there are no waters; who bringeth forth for thee waters out of the stone of the crag (*Deuteronomy* viii. 15). <note>The "stone of the crag" or "flinty rock" represents the hardened state of the natural mind before it is opened to receive spiritual truth.</note>

Again in *Isaiah*:—

> Behold your God will come; then in the wilderness shall waters break out, and rivers in the plain of the desert; and the dry place shall become a pool, and the thirsty one for springs of waters (xxxv. 4, 6, 7);

“the waters in the wilderness that shall break out,” “rivers,” “a pool,” and “springs of waters,” plainly denote the truths of faith and the knowledges of them, which would be given from the Lord when He should come into the world. [9] In *David*:—

> O God, my God, in the morning do I seek Thee; my soul thirsteth for Thee, my flesh longeth for Thee, in a land of drought, and weary without waters (*Psalm* lxiii. 1);

where “thirsting” is predicated of truth; “weary without waters” denotes that there are no truths. <note>In the symbolic language of this manuscript, "thirst" refers specifically to the intellect's desire for truth, while "hunger" refers to the heart's desire for goodness.</note> “Thirst” denotes a lack of truth and the consequent privation of spiritual life, as seen in *Isaiah*:—

> Therefore My people will go into exile, for not acknowledging, and their glory are men of famine, and their multitude are parched with thirst (v. 13).

> I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh because there is no water, and dieth for thirst (l. 2). <note>Original: *dieth for thirst*. In the spiritual sense, "fish" represent scientific facts or basic knowledge; when there is no living truth (water), these facts lose their life and purpose.</note>

[10] From these passages it can now be seen what is signified in this chapter by there being “no water for the people to drink” (verse 1); by their saying, “Give us water and we will drink” (verse 2); by “the people thirsting there for waters” (verse 3); and by the fact “that there shall come waters out of the rock” (verse 6). Consequently, by their murmuring on account of the lack of water is signified temptation arising from the lack of truth; for when a person comes into <term>temptation</term> <note>Temptation here refers to a spiritual trial or crisis of faith where the individual feels lost or lacking direction.</note> from the lack of truth, they are kept in a vehement longing for it, and at the same time in despair of eternal salvation on this account: these things then cause suffering and complaint.

**8569.** *And the people murmured against Moses.* That this signifies a greater degree of suffering, is evident from the signification of “murmuring,” as being suffering from the bitterness of the temptation (see n. 8351); that it denotes a greater degree of suffering is indicated by the context.

<summary>This page explains the symbolic meaning of water and thirst in the Bible, identifying them as representations of spiritual truth and the soul's longing for it during times of trial. It concludes that the Israelites' "murmuring" in the desert represents the intense suffering and despair a person feels when they lack the spiritual guidance necessary for salvation.</summary>

Such an idea have very many about the intercession spoken of in the Word, where it is said that the Lord will entreat His Father for them. There is intercession in all love, consequently in all mercy; for mercy is of love. That he who loves, or who feels compassion, continually intercedes, can be seen from examples. A husband who loves his wife, wishes her to be kindly received by others, and to be well treated; he does not say this in express terms, but continually thinks it, consequently is in silence continually entreating it, and interceding for her. Parents act in like manner in favor of their children whom they love. In like manner do those also who are in **charity** for their neighbor; and they who are in friendship for their friends. 

From all this it can be seen that there is constant intercession in all love. It is the same in respect to the Lord’s intercession for the human race, and in especial for those who are in the good and truth of faith; for toward them there is Divine, that is, **infinite love**; and there is Divine, that is, **infinite mercy**. He does not pray the Father for them, and in this way intercede, for this would be to act altogether after a human manner; but He continually excuses, and continually forgives, for He continually feels compassion; and this is done on the part of the Lord Himself, for the Lord and the Father are one (*John 14:8–12*).

**8578.** *And take with thee of the elders of Israel.* This signifies that these actions should proceed from primary truths. This is clear from the meaning of "the elders of Israel," who represent the fundamental elements of wisdom and intelligence that are in harmony with what is good and true (see n. 6524, 6525, 6890, 7912). **8579.** *And thy rod wherewith thou smotest the river.* This signifies the Divine power by which falsehoods were cleared away. This is why Jehovah (the Lord) says, "Behold I stand upon the rock." Consequently, these words signify the Lord in the context of the truths of faith that arise from His Law, or the Word. Through the Lord’s Providence, a means of communication between the angels of heaven and humanity was provided through these physical things. There must always be a church, or at least a "representative" of a church, somewhere on earth so that heaven can remain connected to the human race. Since that nation, more than any other, could focus their entire worship on external objects—and thus act out the representation of a church—that nation was chosen for this purpose.

# CHAPTER XVII. VERSES 8, 9

### [No. 8592]

*“...choose men for us, and go out, fight against Amalek: tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand.”* 

“And Amalek came” signifies falsity stemming from deep, internal evil. “And he fought with Israel in Rephidim” signifies that these forces attacked when a person was enduring a heavy spiritual <term>temptation</term><note>In this theology, a temptation is not just an urge to do wrong, but an intense inner struggle where a person’s faith and character are tested by spiritual trial.</note>. “And Moses said to Joshua” signifies the way Divine influence flows into the specific truths used in spiritual combat. “Choose us out men” signifies the process of selecting and arranging those truths for the fight. “And go out, fight against Amalek” signifies taking action against the falsities that arise from hidden, inner evil. “Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill” signifies the joining together of Divine Truth with the quality of <term>charity</term><note>The "good of charity" refers to the active, heartfelt desire to do good for others, which acts as a foundation for higher truth.</note> and the spiritual energy that flows from that union. “With the rod of God in my hand” signifies that the power for this struggle comes from that Divine connection.

### 8593.

**And Amalek came.** This signifies falsity arising from interior evil. This is clear from the symbolic meaning of “Amalek,” which represents a specific kind of deceptive thinking that comes from a person’s hidden, inner malice (which we will describe below). 

First, we must explain who these people are and what it means to be in “interior evil.” Interior evil is a type of malice that lies buried deep within a person, hidden in their secret will and their private thoughts. No trace of it shows in their outward behavior—it doesn't appear in their actions, their speech, or their facial expressions. Those who possess this kind of evil use every possible trick and method to hide it. They mask their true nature under a disguise of honor, justice, and even a pretended love for their neighbor. 

Yet, inside themselves, they are constantly plotting how to cause harm. Whenever possible, they inflict this harm through others, making sure it never looks like they were the ones responsible. They are experts at “coloring over” their actions so that the evil does not look like evil at all. The greatest joy of their life is to meditate on these plots and try to carry them out in total secrecy. This is what is meant by **interior evil**. 

In the spiritual world, those who are defined by this evil are called **evil genii**. They are kept completely separate from those who are in “exterior evil” (who are simply called “spirits”). These <term>evil genii</term><note>Distinct from "spirits," genii are more dangerous because they attack the will and the subconscious feelings rather than just the intellect or outward ideas.</note> occupy a space "behind" a person—at their back—living in various deep caverns. In contrast, ordinary evil spirits occupy the space in front of or to the sides of a person. 

Within the concept of the <term>Grand Man</term><note>A symbolic framework where the entire spiritual universe and heaven are seen as a single human form, with different groups of souls corresponding to different biological organs or functions.</note>, these genii correspond to the area of the **cerebellum** and that part of the spinal cord that controls involuntary functions. 

[2] Regarding the "falsity" that comes from this kind of evil: it is different from the false ideas held by ordinary evil spirits. This is because this falsity is not just an error of the mind; it is, in its very essence, evil itself.

# EXODUS [No. 8593 continued]

Those who are stuck in this specific type of evil do not attack the truths of faith, but rather the goodness that springs from faith. They operate through distorted emotions, which they use to twist a person's good thoughts in a way that is almost impossible to perceive. Because their nature is so destructive, their "hells" <note>In this context, "hells" refer to specific spiritual states or communities characterized by distinct types of malice.</note> are completely isolated from the hells of other evil spirits. In fact, they have almost no contact with others, specifically to keep them separated from the people of the <term>spiritual church</term><note>The "spiritual church" refers to people who are guided by their conscience and by truths they have learned, rather than by direct divine perception.</note>. If these spirits were allowed to influence people from their hells, it would be the end of the spiritual person; they would work in the most secret ways to attack and corrupt the person’s conscience by breathing in these distorted desires.

These <term>infernal genii</term><note>The term "genii" refers to a specific class of harmful spirits who attack a person's will and hidden desires, rather than their logic or thoughts.</note> never attack a person openly, nor do they strike when someone is strong enough to resist them. Instead, they wait until it appears that a person is already stumbling or ready to give up; in that moment, they suddenly appear and push the person toward a total spiritual fall. 

This behavior is represented by the way Amalek attacked Israel in the desert. It is also seen later, when the children of Israel turned against Jehovah and were afraid of the nations in the land of Canaan:

[3] From all of this, we can see the true character of those represented by Amalek. This is described in the final verse of this chapter:

> Because the hand of the evil is against the throne of Jah <note>The "throne of Jah" represents the Divine Truth and the spiritual kingdom.</note>, there shall be war for Jehovah against Amalek from generation to generation.

And in *Deuteronomy*:

> Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, when you came out of Egypt; how he met you on the road and attacked your rear ranks, striking all who were weak and lagging behind, when you were faint and weary; and he did not fear God. Therefore, when Jehovah your God has given you rest, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven; you must not forget (*xxv. 17–19*).

The same theme is found in the first book of *Samuel*, where Jehovah speaks through Samuel to Saul:

### CHAPTER XVII. VERSES 8, 9 [No. 8593 continued]

I have resolved to punish what Amalek did to Israel, how he set an ambush for him on the way as he was coming up out of Egypt. Therefore, go and strike Amalek, and devote everything he has to the curse; do not spare them, but kill both man and woman, infant and nursing child, ox and sheep, camel and donkey. But Saul spared King Agag, along with the best of the sheep, the oxen, the fatlings, the lambs, and everything that was of high quality.

Because of this, it was declared to Saul that he would no longer be king over Israel (1 Samuel 15:1–3, 9, 23, 26). The command that “the memory of Amalek was to be blotted out” and that “everything belonging to him was to be devoted to the curse” signified that <term>evil genii</term><note>As noted previously, "genii" are a specific class of malicious spirits who attack a person's emotions and secret desires rather than their logical thoughts.</note> should have no connection whatsoever with those who belong to the <term>spiritual church</term><note>The "spiritual church" refers to people who are guided by their conscience and the truths they have learned.</note>. These genii only find a connection with people who do not live in the truth, but instead prefer false ideas because of their own selfish desires. 

[4] Anyone can see that without a deeply hidden reason, <term>Jehovah</term><note>The personal name for God in the Hebrew Bible.</note> would never have declared a “perpetual war against Amalek,” or commanded that their “memory be blotted out from under heaven,” or that everything they owned be destroyed—especially considering that, historically, this total destruction never actually happened. The deeply hidden reason behind these commands and actions is revealed in the words Samuel spoke to Agag, the king of the Amalekites, whom Saul had spared:

> Agag the king of Amalek came to Samuel with a charming manner; but Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women." And Samuel hacked him to pieces before Jehovah (1 *Samuel 15:32, 33*).

“To come with a charming manner” <note>Original Latin: *delicate*, often translated as "delicately" or "cheerfully."</note> signifies the outward politeness or deceptive friendliness that these types of spirits use when they are around others. The phrase “your sword has made women childless” signifies that the false ideas of these spirits do violence to a person's good affections. “Your mother shall be childless among women” signifies that within these spirits, a corrupted will—rather than just a corrupted intellect—is what prevails. Finally, “Samuel hacked him to pieces before Jehovah” signifies that these genii were completely separated from those who are in a state of falsity originating from the intellect. In other words, the <term>genii</term> (who attack the heart) were separated from the ordinary <term>spirits</term> (who attack the mind). (For more on how “women” represent affections, see n. 568, 6014, 8337; and how a “sword” represents the combat and destruction caused by false ideas, see n. 2799, 4499, 7102.)

# EXODUS [N. 8594]

**8594.** *And fought with Israel in Rephidim.* This signifies that they attacked while a person was enduring a heavy spiritual trial. This is clear from the meaning of "fighting," which signifies attacking through false ideas stemming from deep-seated evil; and from the meaning of "Rephidim," which represents the specific nature of a trial regarding truth (see note 8561). The meaning here is explained by what was said just before (note 8593): in the spiritual world, those represented by Amalek attack people undergoing <term>temptation</term><note>In this context, "temptation" refers to an internal spiritual struggle or crisis of faith, rather than a simple urge to do something wrong.</note> precisely when they are at their weakest and nearly ready to give up.

**8595.** *And Moses said unto Joshua.* This signifies Divine <term>influx</term><note>A technical term in this theology meaning the "flowing in" of life, light, or power from God into the human mind.</note> into "fighting truth." This is clear from the meaning of "saying," which here refers to this flowing-in (influx), because it is directed toward the truth that is currently in combat, represented here by Joshua. 

This is a Divine influx because Moses represents Divine truth—that is, the truth that comes directly from the Lord. Because this truth is purely Divine, it flows into every kind of faith and gives them their reality as truths. Joshua, however, represents "fighting truth." We know Joshua represents fighting truth because he was the one commanded to fight against Amalek (who represents the lies born from internal evil). 

This spiritual war must be waged by truth that has been "empowered for battle" through the influence of the Divine. The Divine truth itself, as it comes directly from the Lord, does not fight; it is peaceful. It is peace itself because it flows from the Divine good of the Lord’s Divine love. However, to become "fighting truth," it flows into angels who have a passionate zeal for what is true and good. Moved by this zeal, they engage in the struggle. This is the origin of the "fighting truth" represented by Joshua.

[2] Because Joshua represented this fighting truth, he was appointed the leader of the people of Israel after Moses. He was the one who led them into the land of Canaan and fought the nations there. A "drawn sword in the hand" symbolizes the power of Divine truth in its role of spiritual combat. **8597.** *And go out, fight against Amalek.* This signifies a struggle against the false ideas that spring from deep-seated, interior evil. This is evident from what Amalek represents (see above, note 8593).

**8598.** *To-morrow I stand on the top of the hill.* This signifies the joining together of Divine truth with the <term>good of charity</term><note>A technical term for the state of being where a person's actions are motivated by a genuine love for others and for what is right.</note>, and the spiritual influence (<term>influx</term>) that results. 

This is shown by the role of Moses, who represents "Divine truth." His "standing" on the hill represents being connected and exerting influence. In this context, "standing" means to be connected because he was positioned at the top of the hill, and a "hill" symbolizes the good of charity (note 6435). It also represents "influx" (spiritual influence) because from that height he watched and determined the outcome of the battle: the text says Israel prevailed when he lifted his hand, and Amalek prevailed when he lowered it. 

[2] A brief explanation of how "goodness" (the good of charity) flows into "truth" during a struggle: As previously mentioned, the Divine becomes a "fighting truth" when it is joined with those who act out of <term>zeal</term><note>In this context, zeal is a holy passion for what is good, whereas anger is a selfish passion for revenge.</note>. People who act from zeal do fight, but they do not do so out of personal hatred or hostility; rather, they act out of love. Zeal differs from anger because zeal contains the inner quality of charity. Therefore, when zeal "fights," it simply aims to remove those who are caught in lies and evil to prevent them from hurting others who are trying to live rightly. Anger, on the other hand, does not just want to stop the harm; it pursues others with hatred and a desire for revenge.

# EXODUS [N. 8603]

...in <term>successive order</term><note>A structure where things follow one another in a specific hierarchy, from the highest/innermost to the lowest/outermost, rather than just being a flat sequence.</note> shall be briefly told. Each and all things in universal nature come forth from interior things in order, being <term>derivations</term><note>Things that originate or "flow out" from a primary source.</note> and successions. But interior things do not cohere with exterior things by continuity <note>Meaning they are not just a thinner or thicker version of the same thing, but are entirely different "levels" or "degrees" of reality.</note>, but they are distinct, and are conjoined by means of protrusions like fibers, through which there are communications. 

An idea of the nature of these derivations and consequent successions in general, may be obtained from fruits, as from citrons, apples, and the like. The most external things are the skins which encompass them; the interior things are the pulp which is enclosed; the still more interior things are the seeds, which are encompassed with cases outwardly, and next themselves with membranes; beneath which is the inner pulp, containing the first form, as a soul; from which again come new trees and new fruits. 

[3] All these things are in successive order, and are distinct from one another, and are also joined together. The communication of the interior things with the exterior is effected in a wonderful way by means of passings over that are as it were fibrous. At first, while forming, they almost cohere, but in course of time they are separated; for before the first form, which is the inmost in the seed, can be expanded into forms like its parents, it must be successively opened; and when it is being opened and begins to grow, the pulps with which it is encompassed adapt themselves, serving first as soil, next as fertilizing sap; after this period, which is its period in the womb, it is born, and is then left to the soil of the earth, wherein it has been sown in the form of seed. 

[4] From all this an idea can be formed how the case is with derivatives in successive order. As it is in the vegetable kingdom, so also it is in the <term>animal kingdom</term><note>In this context, the 'animal kingdom' refers to all sentient life, including the biological and psychological structures of human beings.</note>, but in this much more perfectly. There are in the animal kingdom exterior, and interior, and inmost things, in like manner in successive order, which are distinct from one another, and are also joined together; but they differ in the fact that the forms in the animal kingdom have been created to receive life. Consequently, as the forms <term>recipient of life</term><note>The idea that living things do not have life of their own, but are biological 'vessels' designed to receive life from a Divine source.</note> are in successive order, so also are the lives which result therefrom; for the forms or substances recipient of life are the subjects, and the things that result from their changes and modifications are the forces, which are to be called "lives," because they are...

This is evident from the symbolic meaning of a "stone" as truth <note>See paragraphs 643, 1298, 3720, 3769, 3771, 3789, 6426</note>. The nature of "truth in the ultimate of order" can be understood from what was discussed earlier regarding how truths are arranged in a specific sequence, from the most internal and spiritual to the most external and literal.

**8610.** *And put it under him, and he sat upon it.* This signifies <term>correspondence</term><note>A central concept in this philosophy, where physical things (like a stone) act as a mirror or container for spiritual things (like Divine truth).</note> with truth in the highest level of order. This is shown by the fact that the stone supported Moses. In this narrative, Moses represents <term>truth in the first of order</term><note>The "first of order" refers to pure Divine truth as it first flows from the Lord, before it is adapted for human understanding.</note>, which is the Divine truth proceeding directly from the Lord. When the truth at the lowest level (the stone) matches or "corresponds" to this high truth (Moses), then the high truth is supported because the two levels act as one. Interior things are joined to exterior things, and finally to the lowest level, through these correspondences. When this happens, the "first" or highest truth gains its power through the "last" or lowest truth, because it lives within it and acts through it. However, if there is no correspondence, they are disconnected, and the highest truth has no power at the lowest level.

[2] Every person who reflects can see that the things which are related in these verses contain arcana <note>original: "arcana" — This Latin term refers to the hidden, sacred mysteries or spiritual secrets contained within the literal words of Scripture.</note> which do not appear in the letter — as that Moses stood on a hill, and had a rod in his hand; that Joshua conquered when Moses lifted up his hands, and Amalek conquered when Moses let down his hands; that they put a stone under him upon which he sat; and that Aaron and Hur held up his hands, and this until the setting of the sun. [3] Correspondences <note>A core concept in this work: the belief that every physical thing or action in the world is a direct reflection of a spiritual reality in heaven.</note> have all power, insomuch that what is done on earth according to correspondences avails in heaven, because correspondences are from the Divine. All the miracles recorded in the Word <note>The author uses "The Word" to refer to the Bible, emphasizing its status as a living, divine communication.</note> were done by means of correspondences. This is effected by means of the correspondences of all the several expressions in the Word.

Every person carries the memory of all their acts with them into the other life; this constitutes the "book" of their life (see section 2474). However, no one except the Lord alone can judge a person according to their acts. This is because all acts proceed from <term>final causes</term> <note>The inner intentions, goals, or "ends" that motivate an action. In this theological view, the morality of an act is defined by the intention behind it, rather than the outward deed alone.</note>, which lie deeply concealed within. A person is judged according to these causes, and no one knows them but the Lord. Therefore, judgment belongs to Him alone, which is also meant by these words in the Gospel of *John*:

> I saw upon the right hand of Him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals. Thereafter I saw a strong angel crying with a great voice, "Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof?" And He took the book, and they sang a new song, "Worthy art Thou who takest the book, and openest the seals thereof" (*Revelation 5:1, 2, 5, 8, 9*).

**8622.** *That in blotting I will blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens.* That this signifies that this falsity must be completely removed so that it may fight no longer, is evident from the meaning of "blotting out the memory," as being to remove (discussed further below); and from the representation of Amalek, as being those who are in falsity from interior evil (see n. 8593). 

[2] The reason "blotting out the memory of Amalek" denotes removing the falsity which is from interior evil is because this can be removed, but cannot be entirely "blotted out" <note>In this spiritual sense, "blotting out" does not mean the person or spirit ceases to exist, but that they are separated and moved away so they can no longer cause harm.</note>, for this falsity exists with the <term>infernal genii</term> <note>A specific class of the most dangerous hellish spirits who do not attack a person’s thoughts, but instead secretly influence their deepest feelings and desires.</note> who live to eternity (n. 8593). The reason for this is that they do not flow into the thoughts which belong to the understanding—and thus not into what belongs to faith, as ordinary infernal spirits do—but rather into the affections which belong to the will, and consequently into the things of charity. They do this so secretly that there never appears a trace that it comes from them. Therefore, if they were permitted to flow in, the person of the spiritual church could not possibly be saved, because they would pervert and utterly corrupt the affections for truth and good. Hence it is that these infernal genii are removed, so that they may not communicate with those who belong to the Lord’s spiritual kingdom.

In the original language <note>Referring to Hebrew</note>, "Jehovah-nissi" means "Jehovah my banner," or "ensign," and by "an ensign," or "banner," in the Word <note>The Word: A term used here for the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note> is signified a calling together for war; and as it is said that "Jehovah shall have war," protection by Him is also signified.

> Declare in Judah, and make it heard in Jerusalem, and say, and blow the trumpet in the land; proclaim, fill full, say, "Gather yourselves together, and let us enter into the fortified cities." Set up a banner toward Zion; assemble yourselves, stay not (*Jeremiah* iv. 5, 6).

### CONTINUATION ABOUT THE INHABITANTS AND SPIRITS OF THE PLANET JUPITER.

**8627.** The inhabitants of the planet Jupiter define wisdom as thinking well and justly about the occurrences in life. They receive this wisdom from their parents starting in infancy, and it is transmitted by succession to their descendants, increasing as it passes down. They know nothing at all of the <term>sciences</term> <note>In the 18th-century context of this writing, 'sciences' refers to formal academic disciplines, logic, and technical school-learning.</note> as they are practiced on our earth, and they have no desire to know them. They call such studies "shades" and compare them to clouds that block the sun. They formed this negative view of academic science from certain spirits belonging to our earth who, in their presence, boasted that they were wise because of their scientific learning.

They see only through technical terms, which in the spiritual world appear like dust or thick clouds obstructing their intellectual sight. Those who have become conceited because of this learning have even less perception. Furthermore, those who have used the sciences as a means to dismantle the things of faith have totally destroyed their understanding; they see in thick darkness, like owls—mistaking falsity for truth and evil for good.

[2] From their interactions with such people, the spirits of Jupiter had concluded that the sciences <term>sciences (Latin: scientiae)</term> <note>In this 18th-century context, 'sciences' refers to any structured academic or sensory knowledge, including the humanities and natural philosophy, rather than just modern laboratory science.</note> bring about shadows and cause blindness. However, they were told that on our Earth, the sciences are actually the means of opening one's mental vision. This vision exists in the light of heaven and provides instruction in matters of spiritual life. But because the love of self and the love of the world are so dominant here—and with them, the things of a merely natural and sensory life—the sciences become a means for such people to become "insane." That is, they use their knowledge to confirm their belief in nature over the Divine, and in the physical world over heaven.

[3] They were told further that, in themselves, the sciences are "spiritual riches." Those who possess them are like those who possess worldly riches: both are tools for performing useful services for oneself, one's neighbor, and one's country. Yet, they can also be used to do evil. They are also like garments, which serve for practical use and adornment, but can also be used for pride, as seen in those who wish to be honored for their clothing alone. The spirits of the planet Jupiter understood these points well, but they marveled that any humans should have placed the tools that lead to wisdom above wisdom itself. They were surprised that people could not see that burying the mind in such things, without elevating it beyond them, is to darken and blind the soul.

**8629.** A certain spirit ascending from the lower earth <note>A region in the spiritual world where spirits often undergo a process of preparation or clarification of their state.</note> came to me and said that he had heard my conversation with the other spirits, but that he had understood scarcely anything that had been said about spiritual life and light. I asked him...

<summary>This page contrasts genuine wisdom with mere academic learning, explaining that scientific knowledge is a tool that can either open the mind to heaven or, if fueled by pride, lead to spiritual blindness. It records a dialogue where spirits from Jupiter express shock that Earthly scholars often value the "means" of knowledge more than the "end" of wisdom.</summary>

...whether he wished to learn these things. He said he had not come with that intention; from which it might be inferred that he was unwilling. He was very stupid. The angels said that this man, during his life in the world, had been one of those who are celebrated for their learning. He was cold, as was plainly felt from his breath <note>original Latin: *afflatus*; a spiritual "aura" or influence that emanates from a person's presence.</note>, which was a sign of merely natural light and of no spiritual light; thus, that by means of the sciences <note>In this context, "sciences" refers to any structured academic learning or external knowledge.</note> he had not opened, but had closed for himself, the way to the light of heaven.

**8630.** As the inhabitants of the earth Jupiter acquire intelligence by another way than do the inhabitants of our earth, and besides are from their life of a different disposition, they cannot be together; but if they approach, they either shun or repel them. There are spheres that are to be called spiritual spheres, which continually emanate—nay, pour forth—from every society. These spheres are from the activity of the affections and of the derivative thoughts; thus they are of the life itself (concerning spheres, see n. 1048, 1053, 1316, 1504, 1505, 1507, 1508, 1510-1519, 2401, 4464, 5179, 6206, 7454, 6598–6613, 8063). **[2]** All the consociations <note>Spiritual associations or communities.</note> in the other life are effected in accordance with the spheres; those which agree together are conjoined according to their agreement; those which do not agree are repelled according to their disagreement. Every province in the <term>Grand Man</term> <note>original Latin: *Maximus Homo*; the concept that heaven and the spiritual world function together as a single, coordinated human organism.</note> (to which some member or organ in the human body corresponds), has its own sphere distinct from the sphere of any other province; hence the mutual conjunction of those who belong to the same province, and the disjunction of those who belong to some other. The spirits and angels who are from the earth Jupiter bear relation in the <term>Grand Man</term> to the <term>IMAGINATIVE OF THOUGHT</term> <note>This refers to the internal process of conceptualizing or visualizing ideas before they are expressed or acted upon.</note>, and thus to an active state of the interior parts. But the spirits of our earth bear relation to the various functions of the exterior parts of the body, into which, when they desire to rule, the <term>Imaginative of Thought</term> cannot flow; hence the oppositions between the spheres.

**8631.** In what clear perception the spirits of Jupiter are with respect to spiritual things, was made evident to me from their representation of how the Lord, whom they call their <term>One Only Lord</term> <note>The specific title the inhabitants of Jupiter use for God, emphasizing His absolute unity.</note>, converts depraved affections <note>Disordered or harmful desires and impulses.</note> into good affections.

# EXODUS [N. 8631

**8631.** They represented the **intellectual mind** as a beautiful form, and gave it an activity of form that was suited to its inner affection. They then showed how the Lord bends what is depraved within that form toward what is good. This was done in a way that no words can describe, and so skillfully that they received praise from the angels. At that time, there were learned individuals present from our own earth. These people had immersed their intellectual capacity in <term>memory-knowledges<note>original Latin: *scientifica*; these are external facts or academic data stored in the memory, which Swedenborg distinguishes from deeper, spiritual understanding.</note></term>, and had argued extensively about "form," "substance," and what is "material" or "immaterial" without ever applying these concepts to any useful purpose. Because of this, they were unable to comprehend even this visual representation.

**8632.** I have spoken with spirits from the earth Jupiter about the Lord—specifically, that He does evil to no one, and certainly never punishes anyone. These spirits, being among the more simple-hearted ones, at first did not want to accept this, as they believed that punishments come directly from the Lord. However, they were told that when their own angels are with a person on their earth, those angels do not punish or even speak harshly; they merely permit the <note>punishing spirits: in Swedenborg's theology, these are spirits whose nature leads them to inflict discipline, though they are overseen by the Lord to ensure even this serves an eventually good purpose.</note> who are also present to do so. Since the angels themselves do not punish, it was explained that the Lord—who is goodness itself and who guides the angels—could do so even less. Upon hearing this, they acknowledged the truth and affirmed clearly that the Lord punishes no one, does evil to no one, and never speaks harshly to anyone. (For more on the angels and the punishing spirits associated with the inhabitants of Jupiter, see sections 7802–7805 and 7810.)

**8633.** Regarding the further details of life on that earth, I have been instructed by their spirits that because they do not value **memory-knowledges**, they also do not care for things made by human art or craftsmanship. Furthermore, they have no specific holidays; instead, every morning at sunrise and every evening at sunset, they perform holy worship to the **One Only Lord** in their tents, during which they also sing.

**8634.** The subject of the inhabitants and spirits of the earth Jupiter will be continued at the end of the following chapter.

# THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY

## CHAPTER THE EIGHTEENTH.

### THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY.

**8635.** No one can be <term>regenerated<note>The process of spiritual rebirth or renewal where a person’s inner nature is transformed by God.</note></term> unless he knows the things belonging to the new life, that is, the spiritual life; for a person is introduced into this life through the process of regeneration. The things belonging to the new life, or spiritual life, are truths which must be believed and goods which must be done; the former belong to faith, while the latter belong to <term>charity<note>In this context, charity refers to the active love for one's neighbor and the performance of good deeds from a spiritual motive.</note></term>.

**8636.** No one can know these things by himself, for a person only grasps what has been obvious to his physical senses. From these senses, he has acquired for himself a light called **natural light**, by which he sees nothing else except what belongs to the world and to himself, and not what belongs to heaven and to God. These higher things he must learn through revelation.

**8637.** For example, he must learn: that the Lord, who was God from eternity, came into the world to save the human race; that He has all power in heaven and on earth; that every element of faith and every element of charity—and thus every truth and every good—comes from Him; that there is a heaven and there is a hell; and that man will live for eternity, in heaven if he has done well, or in hell if he has done evil.

**8638.** These things and more belong to faith, and they must be known by the person who is to be regenerated; for he who knows them can think about them, then will them, and finally do them, and in this way possess new life.

**8639.** On the other hand, he who does not know that the Lord is the Savior of the human race cannot have faith in Him, worship Him, love Him, or do good for His sake. He who does not know that all good comes from Him cannot think that his own <note>original Latin: *justitia* (justice/righteousness)</note> and his own salvation are from Him; even less can he wish it to be so, and thus he cannot live from Him. He who does not know that there is a hell and a heaven, nor that there is an eternal life, cannot even think about the life of heaven, nor apply himself to receiving it. The same is true for all other spiritual matters.

<summary>This page introduces the necessity of spiritual knowledge for the process of regeneration, arguing that human reason alone (natural light) cannot discover divine truths. It lists the core concepts—such as the divinity of the Lord and the reality of heaven and hell—that are required to live a life of faith and charity.</summary>

<keywords>regeneration, spiritual life, faith, charity, natural light, revelation, Lord, salvation, heaven, hell, eternal life, divine truth</keywords>

We can also see that this life cannot be granted to anyone until they reach a state where they are able to acknowledge the truths of faith and, in acknowledging them, truly desire to live according to them.

23. If thou do this thing, and God have commanded thee, then thou shalt be able to stand, and also all this people shall come upon its place in peace.

### THE CONTENTS.

**8641.** The subject explored in the internal sense <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper, spiritual meaning hidden behind the literal words of the Bible.</note> of this chapter is the way truths are organized in a specific order, from the highest levels down to the lowest. These truths are set in order by "Divine Good" <note>Divine Good represents the active love and power of God that organizes spiritual life.</note>. In this symbolic arrangement, truth in its highest degree is represented by Moses. The truths that flow from that height in a descending order are represented by the leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. Finally, the Divine Good that carries out this organization is represented by Jethro, Moses' father-in-law.

And Jethro Moses' father-in-law came, and his sons, and his wife, unto Moses, unto the wilderness where he was encamped at the mount of God.* <note>The "mount of God" refers to Mount Horeb or Sinai, signifying a state of high spiritual holiness where divine revelation occurs.</note>

### [N. 8642] CHAPTER XVIII. VERSES 1–5

**8642.** “Jethro the priest of Midian” signifies **Divine good**; “Moses’ father-in-law” signifies the source from which comes the good joined with **Divine truth**; “heard all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel His people” signifies a deep perception of those things performed for those who belong to the Lord’s **spiritual kingdom** <note>The "spiritual kingdom" refers to a state of being where people are led primarily by the truths they have learned from the Word.</note>; “in that Jehovah had brought forth Israel out of Egypt” signifies that they had been set free by the Lord from **infestations** <note>In this context, "infestations" refers to the constant pressure and spiritual harassment caused by false ideas and negative influences.</note>; “and Jethro Moses’ father-in-law took Zipporah, Moses’ wife” signifies good from the Divine joined with Divine truth; “after he had sent her away” signifies the separation that had existed up to this point relative to the state of those in the spiritual church; “and her two sons” signifies the **goods of truth** <note>The "goods of truth" are the practical, good actions and intentions that grow out of a person’s understanding of spiritual truth.</note>; “of which the name of the one was Gershom, for he said I have been a sojourner in a strange land” signifies the specific quality of the good of truth for those who are outside the church; “and the name of the other was Eliezer” signifies the quality of the good of truth for those who are within the church; “because the God of my father was my help” signifies the Lord’s mercy and presence within the church; “and liberated me from the sword of Pharaoh” signifies being set free from the false ideas of those who harassed them; “and Jethro Moses’ father-in-law came” signifies Divine good; “and his sons” signifies the goods of truth; “and his wife” signifies good joined with Divine truth; “unto Moses unto the wilderness” signifies a state of connection occurring before **regeneration** <note>Regeneration is the spiritual process of being "born again" or reformed by God into a more loving and truthful person.</note> when a person still faces trials and temptations; “where he was encamped at the mount of God” signifies being near the good of truth.

**8643.** *And Jethro the priest of Midian.* This signifies Divine good. This is clear from the symbolic representation of Jethro, the priest of Midian, as the "good of the church" found among those who live in simple goodness (see section n. 7015). However, in this specific context, Jethro represents **Divine good**. The reason for this shift is that Moses—to whom Jethro was a father-in-law—represents Divine truth. In the symbolic language of the Bible, when a son-in-law represents truth, the father-in-law represents good in a higher degree, because he is the "father" or source of the truth’s "wife" (the accompanying good).

The reason Divine good is represented by Jethro here is that this chapter describes the "setting in order" of truths for a person in the spiritual church. This organization is carried out by Divine good acting through Divine truth; for all spiritual ordering

### EXODUS [N. 8643]

...setting in order is by **good** through **truth**. This setting in order is effected with the person of the **spiritual church** <note>In this context, the "spiritual church" refers to individuals who are led toward heaven primarily through their understanding of spiritual truths and the Bible.</note> when they begin to act no longer from duty or truth, but from **good** <note>That is, acting out of love and a willing heart rather than just following rules.</note>; for this state is their second state, which arises after they have undergone **temptations**. For when someone acts from truth, then they are tempted, to the intent that the truths within them may be confirmed; and when these have been confirmed, then they are reduced by the Lord into order; and when they have been reduced into order, then they enter the second state, which consists in willing truths and doing them, whereby they become part of the person's life, and are called **goods**. This setting in order is treated of below.

**8644.** *Moses' father-in-law.* That this signifies the source from which comes **good** conjoined with **truth Divine**, is evident from the signification of "*father-in-law*," as being the good from which originates the good conjoined with truth (see n. 6827); and from the representation of **Moses**, as being **truth Divine** <note>Swedenborg uses "Truth Divine" to describe God's wisdom as it is expressed and understood by people.</note> (n. 6752, 6771, 7010, 7014, 7382). The reason why "a *father-in-law*" signifies good from which is good conjoined with truth, is that "a *wife*" signifies good when "the *man*" signifies truth (n. 2517, 4510, 4823). 

As the following text discusses the conjunction of **Divine good** with **Divine truth**, whereby a setting in order may be effected in the person of the church, let it be known that between Divine good and Divine truth there is this distinction—that **Divine good** is *in* the Lord, and **Divine truth** is *from* the Lord. It is as with the fire of the sun and the light which comes from it; the fire is in the sun, and the light is from the sun; in the light there is not fire, but heat. 

[2] Moreover, in the other life, the Lord is the **Sun**, and is also the **light**. In the Sun there, which is Himself, is **Divine fire**, which is the **Divine good** of the **Divine love**. From that Sun is **Divine light**, which is **Divine truth** from Divine good. In this Divine truth there is also Divine good, but not in the same intensity as it is in the Sun, it being **accommodated** to reception in heaven; for unless it were accommodated to reception, heaven could not have come into existence, because no angel can bear the flame of the Divine love. He would be consumed in a moment, just as a person would be if the flame of the sun of this world should blow directly upon them. 

[3] But how the Divine good of the Lord's Divine love is accommodated to reception cannot be known by anyone, not even...

...even by the angels in heaven, because it is an accommodation of the **Infinite** <note>The "Infinite" refers to the unlimited nature of God, which is too vast for any created being to fully grasp.</note> to the **finite**; and the **Infinite** is such as to transcend all the understanding of the **finite**, insomuch that when the understanding of the **finite** desires to look in that direction, it falls as into the depth of the sea and perishes. (That the Lord is the **Sun** in heaven, and that the **Sun** there is the **Divine good** of His **Divine love**, and that the light therefrom is **Divine truth**, from which is intelligence, see n. 1053, 1521–1533, 1619–1632, 2776, 3094, 3138, 3190, 3195, 3222, 3223, 3225, 3339, 3341, 3636, 3643, 3993, 4180, 4302, 4408, 4409, 4415, 4523, 4533, 4696, 7083, 7171, 7174, 7270, 8197.)

**8645.** *Heard all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel His people.* That this signifies the **perception** <note>In this context, "perception" means a deep, intuitive understanding or inner hearing of spiritual realities.</note> of those things which had been done for those who are of the Lord’s **spiritual kingdom**, is evident from the signification of “*hearing*,” namely, all that God had done, as being **perception** (see n. 5017, 8361); from the signification of “*all that God had done*,” as being the things that had been done by the **Divine**; and from the representation of **Israel**, who here is **Moses** and the people for whom the things were done, as being those who are of the Lord’s **spiritual kingdom** <note>The "spiritual kingdom" consists of those who are led by God through their conscience and their understanding of what is true and right.</note> (n. 6426, 6637, 6862, 6868, 7035, 7062, 7198, 7201, 7215, 7223); for **Moses** together with the people represents this kingdom—**Moses** as the head, and the people as the things that are subject to the head; thus also **Moses** represents the Lord as to **Divine truth**, for from this is the spiritual kingdom.

**8646.** *In that Jehovah had brought forth Israel out of Egypt.* That this signifies that they had been liberated by the Lord from **infestations** <note>The term "infestations" refers to spiritual trials or pressures where a person's faith is tested by negative or false thoughts.</note>, is evident from the signification of “*bringing forth*,” as being to liberate; from the representation of **Israel**, as being those who are of the spiritual kingdom (see above, n. 8645); and from the signification of “**Egypt**,” as being **infestations** by **falsities** <note>Symbolically, Egypt represents a state of being trapped by worldly logic or false ideas that cloud spiritual clarity.</note> (n. 7278). That “**Egypt**” signifies **infestations**, is because by “the **Egyptians**” and “**Pharaoh**” are signified those who by means of **falsities** infested in the other life those who were of the spiritual church (n. 7097, 7107, 7110, 7126, 7142, 7220, 7228, 7317, 8148).

...with **Divine truth**, is evident from the **representation** <note>In this work, a "representation" refers to a person or object in the Bible symbolizing a deeper spiritual reality.</note> of **Jethro**, Moses’ father-in-law, as being the **Divine good** from which comes the good joined with truth—in this case, joined with the **Divine truth** represented by **Moses** (as discussed above, n. 8643, 8644). It is also evident from the **representation** of **Zipporah**, Moses’ wife, as being **Divine good**. For marriages represent the **conjunction** <note>A "conjunction" is the spiritual union or marriage between two complementary forces, like love and wisdom.</note> of **good** and **truth**. In the **celestial church** <note>The "celestial church" refers to a state of being where a person is led primarily by love and the will.</note> the husband represents **good** and the wife represents the resulting **truth**; but in the **spiritual church** <note>The "spiritual church" refers to a state of being where a person is led primarily by intellectual truth and a sense of duty.</note> the man represents **truth** and the wife represents **good**. Here, Moses’ wife represents **good**, because the **spiritual kingdom** is being discussed (n. 2517, 4510, 4823, 7022).

**8648.** *After he had sent her away.* That this signifies **separation** up to this point in relation to the state of those who belong to the **spiritual church**, is evident from the meaning of “sending away,” which is **separation**. The reason this relates to the state of those in the **spiritual church** is that, in the first state of those in that church, **good** does not yet appear—only **truth** is visible. How this works can be seen from what has already been shown regarding the two states of those in the **spiritual church**: namely, that in the first state they act from **truth** and not yet from **good**, but in the second state they act from **good**. In the first state, when they act from truth and not from good, **good** is as if it were absent; it is like a wife who has been sent away. But in the second state, when they act from good, then **good** is present, and is like a wife who is joined with her husband. This is what is meant in the **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" is the hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note> by the phrase “after he had sent her away.”

[2] Furthermore, it should be known that this is from the perspective of those who belong to the **spiritual church**. The **truth** that proceeds from the Lord is always joined with its own **good**; but in the first state, which is before **regeneration** <term>Regeneration: The process of spiritual rebirth where a person's inner motivations are transformed from self-centeredness to love for God and others.</term>, **good** is not received—only **truth** is accepted, even though both flow in from the Lord through heaven. In the second state, however, which is after **regeneration**, **good** is received joined with **truth**. What actually takes place within a person is **predicated** <note>To "predicate" is to assert or attribute a quality to a subject. Here, it means that human experiences are often described in the Bible as if they are God's actions.</note> as taking place with the Lord, because that is how it appears to the person. This is the case in many other instances; for example, when the Bible says the Lord does evil, punishes, or casts into hell. These things are **predicated** of the Lord because it appears so, when in fact all evil that happens to a person is done by the

There are very many such things in the **Word** <note>Swedenborg uses the "Word" to refer to the Bible, emphasizing its character as a vessel for divine revelation.</note>, which however are plain to him who searches the **Scriptures** from the affection of truth, and for the sake of the good of life, because he is enlightened by the **Lord**.

**8649.** *And her two sons.* That this signifies the **goods of truth**, is evident from the meaning of "sons" as being **truths** (see n. 489, 491, 533, 1147, 2159, 2623, 3704, 4257). In this case, it refers specifically to the **goods of truth**, because they are called "sons of the wife," as is plain from the original language <note>Referring to the Hebrew text of Exodus.</note>, just as in the sixth verse following. Consequently, as the "wife" signifies **good** conjoined with **truth** (n. 8647), the "sons" here signify the **goods of truth**. The **goods of truth** are truths that have become part of a person's will and consequently their life; these constitute the **new will** <note>The "new will" is a concept in Swedenborgian theology describing a conscience and desire for good that the Lord creates within a person's intellect.</note> in those who belong to the **spiritual church**.

**8650.** *Of which the name of the one was Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a strange land.* That this signifies the quality of the **good of truth** of those who are outside the church, is evident from the meaning of "name" and "calling the name," which signifies **quality** or character (see n. 144, 145, 1754, 1896, 2009, 2724, 3006, 3421, 6674). This quality is described by the words Moses then spoke: "I have been a **sojourner** in a **strange land**." The reason these words signify the good of truth of those outside the church is that a "sojourner" <note>A "sojourner" traditionally refers to a resident alien; spiritually, it represents one who is not yet fully "at home" in the church but is learning its truths.</note> signifies those born outside the church who were nonetheless being instructed in the church's teachings. A "strange land" signifies a place where the church does not exist. (For the meaning of "sojourner" as those outside the church being instructed, see n. 1463, 4444, 7908, 8007, 8013.) That a "strange land" denotes a place where the genuine church is not found is because "land" signifies the **church** (n. 662, 1067, 1262, 1733, 1850, 2117, 2118, 2928, 3355, 4447, 4535, 5577), and "strange" denotes the absence of what is genuine. Indeed, the Lord’s church is scattered throughout the entire world, including among the **Gentiles** <note>Swedenborg often uses "Gentiles" to refer to people of all nations who live well according to their own religious light, even if they aren't part of the formal Christian church.</note> (n. 2049, 2284, 2589-2604). Furthermore, when **Gershom** was born, **Moses** was outside his own church and was living among those in the good of simple truth, who are represented by the **Midianites** (see n. 6793-6796).

**8651.** *And the name of the other was Eliezer.* That this signifies the quality of the **good of truth** <note>The "good of truth" refers to the practice of doing what is right because one's understanding has been enlightened by spiritual truth.</note> of those who are within the church, is evident from the meaning of "name" and "calling a name," as being the **quality** or character of a thing (see above, n. 8650). It denotes the quality of the **good of truth** because the "two sons" represent different types of spiritual goodness (see n. 8649). That this specific quality belongs to those who are *within* the church is clear from the words Moses spoke when this son was born: "because the God of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh." This contrasts with the first son, **Gershom**, whose name represents the state of those *outside* the church (n. 8650).

**8652.** *Because the God of my father was my help.* That this signifies the **Lord's mercy** and presence in the church, is evident from the meaning of "father," as representing the church in regard to its goodness (see n. 5581), and specifically the **Ancient Church** <note>The "Ancient Church" is a term used to describe a historical spiritual state where people understood the deep symbolic connection between the natural and spiritual worlds.</note> (n. 6050, 6075, 6846). The phrase "the God of my father" refers to the **Divine** aspect of that Ancient Church, which was the **Lord** (n. 6846, 6876, 6884). Furthermore, "help," when said of the Lord, signifies **mercy**; for all help from Him is an act of mercy. It also implies **presence**, because wherever mercy is received, the Lord is present. This is especially true within the church, where the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures, viewed as a direct link between humanity and the Divine.</note> exists, for the Lord is present through the Word.

**8653.** *And liberated me from the sword of Pharaoh.* That this signifies liberation from the **falsity** <note>In this context, "falsity" means deceptive or harmful ideas that lead one away from spiritual truth.</note> of those who **infested** <note>To "infest" in a spiritual sense means to harass or attack someone's mind with doubts and false arguments.</note>, is evident from the meaning of "a sword," which represents truth, or in the opposite sense, **falsity** that fights and **vastates** <note>To "vastate" means to systematically strip away a person's truths or goodness, often as a form of spiritual trial.</note> (see n. 2799, 4499, 6353, 7102, 8294). This is also clear from the representation of **Pharaoh**, who represents those who harass the upright in the **other life** <note>The "other life" refers to the spiritual world or the state of existence after the death of the physical body.</note> by using false ideas (n. 7107, 7110, 7126, 7142, 7220, 7228, 7317).

**8654.** *And Jethro Moses' father-in-law came.* That this signifies **Divine good**, is evident from the representation of **Jethro** as Divine good and **Moses** as Divine truth, and from the meaning of "father-in-law," which denotes the connection between these two (as discussed above, n. 8643, 8644).

**8655.** *And his sons*, signifies the **goods of truth** <note>The "goods of truth" are the practical, good actions a person does because they have learned and understood spiritual truths.</note> (see above, n. 8649).

**8657.** *Unto Moses unto the wilderness.* That this signifies **conjunction** <note>In this context, conjunction refers to the spiritual "linking" or marriage between the heart's goodness and the mind's understanding of truth.</note> in the state before **regeneration** <note>Regeneration is the spiritual process of being "born again," moving from a life focused on oneself to a life focused on God and others.</note> when there are **temptations**, is evident from the signification of "coming unto Moses," as being conjunction—namely, of the **Divine good** (represented by Jethro) with the **Divine truth** (represented by Moses); and from the signification of "the wilderness," as being a state of undergoing temptations (see n. 6828, 8098), and thus the state before regeneration. 

There are two states which those enter into who are being regenerated and are becoming a **spiritual church** <note>A "spiritual church" describes a community or individual state where people are led primarily by their conscience and their understanding of what is true, rather than by direct, intuitive love.</note>.
