This first state is described by the journey of the sons of Israel in the wilderness, and the second state is described by their life in the land of Canaan under Joshua.

**8658.** *Where he was encamped at the mount of God.* That this signifies being near to the **good of truth**, is evident from the signification of "being encamped," as being the setting in order of the truth and good which belong to the church within a person (see n. 8103, 8130, 8131, 8155); and from the signification of "the mount of God," as being the **good of love** (see n. 795, 796, 2722, 4210, 6435, 8327). 

In this specific passage, it refers to the "good of truth," because the subject is the goodness of those who belong to the spiritual church, represented by the sons of Israel. The good they possess is the good of truth (this is also called the **good of charity** <note>The "good of charity" is the love of serving one's neighbor based on spiritual principles.</note>). It is called "the mount of **God**" because the name "God" is used in scripture where truth is the subject, whereas "**Jehovah**" is used where good is the subject (n. 2586, 2769, 2807, 2822, 3921, 4295, 4402, 7268, 7873). 

From all this it is evident that the phrase "he was encamped at the mount of God" signifies the organizing of the church’s good and truth in a state near to the "good of truth." **8675.** *Who hath rescued you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh.* That this signifies liberation from the <term>reviling</term> <note>The original text uses "reviling" to describe the spiritual assault and mockery directed at one's faith by those who oppose it.</note> of those who infested, is evident from what has been unfolded above (n. 8671, 8673).

**8676.** *Who hath rescued His people from under the hand of the Egyptians.* That this signifies mercy toward those who were in the <term>good of truth</term> <note>This refers to a state where a person does what is right because they understand it to be true.</note> and <term>truth of good</term> <note>This refers to the intellectual understanding that grows out of a heart that is already focused on doing good.</note>, is evident from the signification of "rescuing," as being liberation (as just above, n. 8675); from the signification of "the Egyptians," as being those who infested by falsities (n. 8668); and from the representation of Israel, who are here "the people of Jehovah," as being those who are of the <term>spiritual church</term> <note>The "spiritual church" describes people who are guided by their conscience and learned truths rather than by direct, celestial perception.</note> (n. 8645), thus who are in the good of truth and truth of good (n. 7957, 8234). That it is of the Lord's mercy is because it is said, "blessed be Jehovah who hath rescued," and by "blessed be Jehovah" is signified that from Him is all good from His Divine love (n. 8674). The Divine love from which good comes to man who is in a state of misery, because of himself he is wholly in evil and in hell, is <term>mercy</term>.

**8677.** *Now I know that Jehovah is great above all gods.* That this signifies the Lord, that there is no God besides Him, is evident from what has been said and shown above (n. 7401, 7444, 7544, 7598, 7636, 8274).

The love of self, which is pride, is of such a quality that so far as the rein is given it, it rushes on, growing step by step to the utmost of the ability that is granted to it, until at last it lifts itself to the very throne of God with the desire to be in His stead. Such are all who are in hell. That they are such is perceived from their endeavor from there, and also from their dangerous hatreds and direful revenges one against another for the sake of rule. ...that you may offer your burnt-offerings—both the meat and the blood—upon the altar of the Lord your God. The blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out upon the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall eat the meat (Deuteronomy 12:27);

The reason why these two things were represented by the burnt-offerings and the sacrifices was that they represented the entirety of the worship of God in a general sense (see n. 923, 6905). All true worship of God is founded upon love and faith; without these, worship is not truly alive—it is merely a <term>rite</term> <note>A "rite" here refers to an outward ritual or ceremony that lacks the internal spirit or heart-felt conviction that makes it spiritually meaningful.</note>, like the actions of an <term>external man</term> <note>The "external man" refers to our outward behaviors and sensory experiences, while the "internal man" refers to our deeper intentions, thoughts, and spiritual life.</note> without the internal, and is therefore devoid of spiritual life.

**8681.** *And Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel.* This signifies the foundational elements of the church. This is evident from the symbolic meaning of *Aaron*, who represents the truth of doctrine (see n. 6998, 7009, 7089, 7382); and from the *elders of Israel*, who represent the primary truths of the church that are in harmony with <term>good</term> <note>In this context, "good" refers to the selfless motivation of love. "Truths in agreement with good" are ideas and principles that are put into practice through kind and loving actions.</note> (n. 6524, 8578, 8585). "Israel" here signifies the church itself (n. 8645).

**8682.** *To eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.* This signifies the <term>appropriation</term> <note>To "appropriate" something in a spiritual sense means to take a quality—like love or truth—and make it a permanent part of your own character and life.</note> of these spiritual qualities through the power of Divine good. This is clear from the meaning of "eating," which signifies appropriation (see n. 3168, 3513, 3596, 3832, 4745); and from the meaning of "bread," which signifies the good of love (n. 2165, 2177, 3464, 3735, 4211, 4217, 4735, 5915). That this stems from Divine good is shown by the phrase "eating the bread before God."

In this context, "bread" refers to all the food used in those times, especially the meat from the sacrifices; for when sacrifices were offered, the meat was eaten beside the altar. (That "bread" signifies all worship in general, see n. 2165.) [2] The reason the meat of the sacrifices was eaten was to represent the appropriation of <term>celestial good</term> <note>"Celestial good" is the highest form of love, characterized by a direct, heart-felt connection to the Divine without the need for complex reasoning.</note> and the joining together of people through love. Because the meat of the sacrifice signified the "good of love," eating it together was considered a holy feast. (That "meat" or "flesh" signifies the good of love, see n. 7850.) 

From this, we can see what the Lord meant when He said that people should "eat His flesh" (*Gospel of John* 6:53–56), and also why, when He instituted the Holy Supper, He said the bread was "His body" (*Gospel of Matthew* 26:26). No one can truly understand the meaning of...

...one cannot understand these things unless he knows that there is an **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" refers to the hidden, spiritual meaning within the literal words of the Bible, which focuses on the soul’s journey and divine reality rather than historical events.</note>, and that in this sense, celestial and spiritual things are understood in place of natural things; and that the natural things <term>correspond</term> <note>"Correspondences" is the concept that every physical object or action in the world reflects a deeper spiritual reality. **8684.** *And it was on the morrow.* That this signifies what is eternal, is evident from the meaning of "to-morrow," or "the morrow," as being what is eternal <note>In the spiritual sense, time does not exist as it does in our world. Concepts like "tomorrow" refer to a state of being that is perpetual or eternal.</note> (see number 3998).

**8685.** *And Moses sat to judge the people.* That this signifies the arranging of <term>Divine truth</term> <note>"Divine truth" refers to the light of wisdom and laws of order that flow from God to guide the human mind.</note> with those who were of the spiritual church in the state before it was motivated by "good," is evident from the representation of **Moses**, as being the Divine truth that proceeds immediately from the Lord (see numbers 7010, 7382); and from the meaning of "judging," as being an arrangement or a "disposing." 

The reason "judging" here denotes an arrangement is because Divine truth does not "judge" anyone in the sense of condemnation; rather, it flows in and arranges the mind so that truth may be received. According to how a person receives this truth, a "judgment" occurs naturally according to the laws of order. This is what is meant by the "judgment of the Lord" in the Gospels <note>original: "Matt. xxv. 31 to end, John v. 22, 26, 27, 30; ix. 39"</note>. This is clear from the Lord's own words where He says that He "judges no man" <note>original: "John iii. 17-21; viii. 15; xii. 47, 48"</note>. 

Furthermore, from the representation of Israel, who is here called "the people," as being those who belong to the spiritual church (see above, number 8645). From all this, it is clear that "Moses sat to judge the people" signifies the arrangement of Divine truth, which proceeds immediately from the Lord, among those who are of the spiritual church. 

[2] That it denotes a state "before it is from good," is evident from what follows. For a person who is being <term>regenerated</term> <note>"Regeneration" is the spiritual process of being reborn or transformed from a person focused on self to a person focused on love and faith.</note> and becoming a church goes through two states: in the first state, he acts from a sense of "truth" (duty and rules); in the second state, he acts from "good" (love and affection). In both states, the person is led by the Lord; however, in the first state, he is led by <term>immediate influx</term> <note>"Influx" is the spiritual energy or thought-flow from God into the human soul. "Immediate influx" is a direct connection from God to the individual.</note>, and in the second, by influx that is both immediate and <term>mediate</term> <note>"Mediate influx" is God's guidance flowing through secondary means, such as other people, angels, or the structures of the church.</note>. 

Direct (immediate) influx is represented by **Moses** judging the people alone; but influx that is both direct and indirect (mediate) is represented by the choosing of "princes of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens" to judge smaller matters while referring great matters to Moses. However, these are <term>mysteries</term> <note>original: "arcana"</note> which scarcely anyone can understand, except one who is in a state of enlightenment from the Lord...

(That these times correspond to changes of state in the afterlife, see sections 5672, 5962, 6110, 8426). The reason these are "interior" and "exterior" is that in the other life, the angels are interiorly in a state of good and truth when it is "morning" there—that is, in a state of spiritual delight—but they are exteriorly in good and truth when it is "evening" there, which is a state of natural delight (see n. 8431, 8452).

**8688.** *And Moses' father-in-law saw all that he did to the people.* That this signifies the <term>omniscience</term> <note>Omniscience refers to God's all-knowing nature.</note> of Divine Good, is evident from the meaning of "seeing all that he did," when said of the Divine Good (represented here by **Jethro**, Moses' father-in-law). In the internal sense, "to see" denotes to understand and perceive (see 2150, 2325, 2807, 3764, 4403–4421, 5400); but in the supreme sense, where the Lord is the subject, it denotes foresight and <term>providence</term> <note>Providence is God's constant care and government over the universe and individual lives.</note> (n.

**8689.** *And he said, Why sittest thou alone?* That this signifies that there was no <term>influx</term> <note>The author uses this term to describe the way spiritual life and wisdom flow from God into the human mind.</note> of truth from good from any other source, is evident from the meaning of "sitting alone." When this is said of <term>Truth Divine</term> <note>In this context, this refers to the laws and wisdom of God as they are expressed to humanity.</note> proceeding immediately from the Lord (represented here by **Moses**), it refers to an influence coming from Him alone, and not from any other source at the same time. (The details of how this works can be seen in the previous section, n. 8685.)

**8690.** *And all the people standing over thee from the morning until the evening.* That this signifies that, at that time, this was the source of everything of the will for those who were of the <term>spiritual church</term> <note>A term describing people who are led by their understanding of what is true, acting from a sense of duty or obedience to God's laws.</note>, in every state, is evident from:
*   The representation of **Israel**, who is called "the people" here, as those belonging to the spiritual church; 
*   The meaning of "standing over" Moses as being obedience in harmony with Truth Divine; 
*   The fact that obedience belongs to the **will**—specifically the will to do what is true because it is commanded, rather than because one feels a natural desire or affection for it;
*   And the meaning of "from the morning until the evening" as being in every state, whether internal or external.

This section describes the "first state" a person experiences before <term>regeneration</term> <note>The spiritual process of being "born again" or reformed by God into a more heavenly person.</note>. In this stage, a person does what is good out of obedience to rules, not yet out of a heart-felt love. This kind of "good" is actually just "truth" being put into action because it is commanded. Therefore, it is done out of a sense of necessity or compulsion, not yet from true freedom. 

A person only acts from freedom when they act from affection—for anything that flows from the love in one's heart is experienced as free. In this first state, the Lord flows into the person and leads them directly. However, this direct influence is not felt by the person because it happens in their <term>inmosts</term> <note>The deepest, most hidden parts of the human soul.</note>. Later, when the Lord’s influence is both direct and indirect (mediate), the person begins to feel it as a new affection or desire. This happens because the influence reaches not just the soul's depths, but also its <term>mediates</term> <note>The intermediate levels of the mind, such as our conscious thoughts.</note> and <term>outmosts</term> <note>The outer layers of the mind and the physical actions of the body.</note>. This more advanced state is discussed later in the chapter, while these verses focus on the earlier stage where Moses (Truth) judged alone.

**8691.** *And Moses said to his father-in-law.* This signifies the <term>reciprocity</term> <note>A mutual exchange or back-and-forth action; in this context, the way human understanding responds to divine influence.</note> found in a response. This is evident because Moses is providing an answer to his father-in-law. Reciprocity is implied here because **Moses** represents <term>Divine Truth</term> <note>The laws and wisdom of God as they are communicated to humanity.</note> conjoined and united to <term>Divine Good</term> <note>The pure love and intent of God.</note>. When there is such a union, there is a back-and-forth relationship: Good acts and Truth reacts. This reaction is the "reciprocity" found in the answer. This same principle applies generally to the relationship between "good" and "truth" within any individual in whom these two qualities have been united.

**8692.** *Because the people cometh unto me to inquire of God.* This signifies that they do not desire or act from any other source than the fact that the **Word** <note>The sacred scriptures or divine revelation.</note> has said to do so. This is clear from the representation of **Moses** as Divine Truth, and therefore as the Word itself. The "people coming to him to inquire of God" symbolizes consulting what the Divine dictates to determine what they should intend and what they should do.

**8693.** *When they have a word.* This signifies in every single thing that happens. A "word" here refers to an event or circumstance that befalls someone. The phrase "in everything" is implied because the people came to Moses alone, signifying that Divine Truth must be consulted in every matter.

**8694.** *It cometh unto me, and I judge between a man and his companion.* This signifies that, at this time, their lives are arranged in agreement with revealed truth. "Coming unto him" (referring to the Divine Truth represented by **Moses**) means consulting the Divine about what must be willed and done. "Judging between a man and his companion" refers to the process of arranging or "disposing" various truths in the mind. (To "judge" signifies to arrange or dispose). This arrangement is in conformity with revealed truth because the text mentions that the people "inquire of God" and that Moses "makes known to them the laws of God."

Consequently, as everything that is according to Divine truth is according to order, it is possible; and as everything that is contrary to Divine truth is contrary to order, it is impossible. 

That this is the case may appear more evident from examples. It is according to order that they who have lived well shall be saved, and that they who have lived ill shall be condemned. Hence it is impossible that they who have lived well should be sent into hell, and that they who have lived ill should be raised into heaven. Consequently it is impossible that they who are in hell can, by the Lord’s pure mercy, be brought out from there into heaven and be saved; for it is the reception of the Lord’s mercy while they lived in the world through which every one is saved. They who receive it then are in the other life in the Lord’s mercy, for they are then in the capacity of receiving it there. To give it to others, and in general to every one at pleasure—provided they have faith, and thus believe that they are cleansed from sins—is impossible, because it is contrary to order, that is, contrary to the <term>Divine</term> <note>The Divine nature or the Lord Himself.</note> which is order.

# [N. 8701] CHAPTER XVIII. VERSES 17-23

...source, is evident from the meaning of "doing it alone," when applied to the **Divine Truth** represented by Moses. This refers to the flow of truth coming from that source alone, and not simultaneously from another source. The nature of this situation can be understood from what was discussed previously <note>original: "n. 8685"</note> regarding the **immediate influx** <term>Influx: The spiritual process by which life, thought, and love flow from the Divine into the human mind.</term> of Divine Truth, as well as its **mediate** <term>Mediate: Indirect; in this context, influence that reaches a person through intermediate stages, such as through other people, angels, or the physical senses.</term> flow.

Specifically, the flow of Divine Truth is **immediate** during the first stage of a person's spiritual rebirth <note>original: "regenerated"</note>. However, this flow becomes both immediate and mediate during the second stage—that is, once the person has been fully reborn. 

When the influence is immediate, the Lord does indeed flow in with both **good** and **truth**, yet at that stage, the person does not perceive the "good," only the "truth." Therefore, the person is led by means of truth rather than by good. But when the influence is also mediate, then "good" is perceived; this is because this indirect influence reaches into a person's external senses. Because of this, the person is then led by the Lord by means of **good**. 

In general, it should be known that a person has not been fully reborn until they act from an **affection for good** <note>This "affection" is a heartfelt love or inclination toward doing what is right because it is good, rather than just following rules.</note>; for at that point, they will what is good, and find it delightful and a blessing to do it. When someone is in this state, their life is a life of good, and they are already in heaven, for good is what reigns universally in heaven. 

The truth belonging to faith, however, leads a person toward good—and thus toward heaven—but it does not, by itself, place them in heaven. The reason for this is that in the afterlife, everyone is grouped together according to the life of their **will**, not according to the life of their **understanding**. This is because wherever the will is, the understanding follows, but the reverse is not true. This law applies both in heaven and in hell. 

Those who are evil are not sent to hell until they are fully settled in the evil of their life; for when they are in this state, they are also in the falsehood that springs from that evil. In the same way, those who are in a state of "good" are in heaven, living in the "truth" that springs from their good. In the afterlife, everyone is brought to a state of having a "single mind"—meaning that whatever they will, they also think, and they do not think anything different from what they will. 

In the physical world, however, it is different. In the world, a person can think and even understand differently from what they actually will. This is allowed so that a person may be reformed; they can understand what is good even if they currently desire <note>original: "wills"</note> what is evil, and thus be led by their understanding to eventually desire what is good. But in the afterlife, every person is led according to the will they acquired while living in the world.

***

# EXODUS [NUMBER 8702]

**8702.** *Now hear my voice.* That this signifies agreement from the union, is evident from the meaning <note>original: "signification"</note> of "hearing a voice" as being obedience—but here it means agreement, because it is said by Jethro. Jethro represents the **Divine good** united to the **Divine truth** (which is represented by Moses). For their union, see the earlier discussion <note>original: "n. 8666"</note>. Consequently, "hear my voice" signifies agreement arising from this union. 

It should be understood that when good and truth have been joined together, there is agreement in each and every thing—that is, of good with truth and of truth with good. The reason is that good belongs to truth and truth belongs to good, and thus these two are one. For whatever good wills, truth confirms; and whatever truth perceives as truth, good wills; and both act together. The case is similar with good and truth as it is with the **will** and the **understanding**: what the will desires and loves, the understanding thinks and confirms, and *vice versa* <note>original: "and the other way around"</note>. These two are alike because "good" belongs to the will, and "truth" belongs to the understanding. Such is the state of those who are led by the Lord by means of good (as mentioned just above <note>original: "n. 8701"</note>).

**8703.** *I will counsel thee, and God shall be with thee.* That this signifies that it is from the Divine, is evident from the meaning of "to counsel." When spoken by the Divine good (represented by Jethro), it signifies what is determined by the Divine, and thus what is *from* the Divine. It is also evident from the meaning of "God shall be with thee," which likewise means something is from the Divine. However, "from the Divine" as signified by "to counsel" relates to the **Divine good** (represented by Jethro); whereas "from the Divine" as signified by "God shall be with thee" relates to the **Divine truth** (represented by Moses).

**8704.** *Be thou for the people with God.* That this signifies the truth proceeding immediately from the Lord, is evident from the meaning of "being for the people with God" when said of the **Divine truth** represented by Moses. This means being closest to the Lord, because it proceeds **immediately** <term>Immediate: Direct; in this context, spiritual influence that flows directly from God into the inner soul without passing through intermediate stages like angels or external teachings.</term> from Him. The implications of these things will become clear from what follows.

For this reason the Lord, in His <term>Divine Human</term> <note>The concept that God is not an abstract force but exists in a perfectly divine human form, allowing for a personal relationship with humanity</note> state, is called a **“Mediator”** and an **“Intercessor,”** but He mediates and intercedes with Himself. This is how the angels in heaven think of the Divine, and how the wise people of ancient times thought. To them, when the Divine appeared, it appeared as a **Divine Man**, for the Divine energy passing through heaven takes on a human quality. The reason for this is that heaven itself is a **Grand Man** <note>original: *Maximus Homo*; the teaching that the entire collective of heaven is organized in the form of a single human being, reflecting God’s image</note>, as has been shown at the end of many chapters. 

From all this, it is clear what distinguishes the "intelligent" of the world from the "intelligent" of heaven. The intelligent of the world remove the idea of the human from God, leaving their minds without a bridge to the Divine, which results in thick darkness. However, the intelligent of heaven perceive the Divine in the Human; thus, the Lord serves as their mediator, and their minds are filled with light.

# EXODUS [N. 8715]

(That "a hundred" and also "ten" signify a great amount, see previous notes, n. 3107, 4400, 4638).

**8716.** *And let them judge the people in every time.* This signifies that this arrangement or <term>disposing</term> <note>In this context, "disposing" refers to the orderly arrangement or management of spiritual truths within a person's mind.</note> of truths is perpetual. This is clear from the meaning of "judging" as the arrangement of truths (mentioned above in n. 8685), and from the meaning of "in every time" as being something that happens perpetually.

**8717.** *And it shall be, every great word let them bring unto thee.* This signifies that everything originates from the truth that comes directly from the Divine. This is evident from the representation of **Moses**, who symbolizes truth coming immediately from the Divine (see n. 7010, 7382). The phrase "every great word let them bring to him" signifies that all things come from this source. 

In the literal sense of the text, it looks as though everything is being brought *toward* Divine truth; however, because everything actually originates from the Lord through the truth that flows out from Him—since all life comes from Him—the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The "internal sense" is the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and words.</note> indicates that things flow *from* this truth rather than toward it. This follows the principle of <term>influx</term> <note>Influx is the spiritual law that life and influence flow from the interior (the soul or God) to the exterior (the body or the world), and never the other way around.</note> (as shown in n. 3721, 5119, 5259, 5779, 6322). Influx does not move from the outside in, but from the inside out. This is because all external things are formed to serve internal things, just as a tool serves the person using it; without the inner cause, the outer tool has no power of its own. We should keep in mind that the internal sense of the Word describes things as they truly are in themselves, not just how they appear on the surface.

[2] In reality, the Lord uses the truth that proceeds from Himself to direct all things, down to the <term>veriest singulars</term> <note>This refers to the most minute, tiny details of existence.</note>. He does not act like a king in our world, but as God in heaven and the universe. A human king only looks after the kingdom as a whole, leaving specific details to his princes and officers. It is different with God. God sees and knows all things from eternity, provides for all things to eternity, and maintains everything in its proper order by His own power. 

From this, it is clear that the Lord does not just care for the "whole," but also has a specific and individual care for every single thing, unlike any earthly ruler. His management is "immediate" (direct) through the Divine truth coming from Himself, and it is also "mediate" (indirect) through heaven. Yet, even this indirect management through heaven is, in a sense, direct.

When things turn out well, they may say it is "of God," and even admit that nothing exists apart from Him; but few, if any, believe this in their hearts.

Therefore, when they see many wicked people possessing these things while the good do not, they reject and deny Divine Providence in individual matters. They do not consider that the true **Divine Blessing** is to be happy for eternity. The Lord views the things of this world, which last for only a short time, merely as means to reach eternal ends. Therefore, for the sake of their eternal life, the Lord provides the good—those who receive His mercy in time—with whatever contributes to their happiness: riches and honors for those who will not be spiritually harmed by them, and no riches or honors for those who would be harmed. Nevertheless, to these latter individuals, He gives a sense of gladness with the few things they have, making them more content than the wealthy and the honored.

The reason why **"land"** in its highest spiritual sense signifies the **Divine** is because Jethro represented Divine Good—which is the Divine Itself. Therefore, Jethro's return to "his own land" can only be expressed in the historical narrative as a return to the Divine. In the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, symbolic meanings <term>significatives</term> <note>Terms or objects in the Bible that represent deeper spiritual realities.</note> adapt themselves to the subject being described, even while the basic meaning of the word remains. 

For example, the word **"land"** properly signifies the church. This is because those in heaven do not think of physical soil when they read the Word; instead, they think of the spiritual state of the people living there—their religion. Consequently, when they read about a "land" where the church exists, they perceive the church; from the idea of the church, they perceive the Lord's kingdom; from that, they perceive heaven; and finally, they perceive the Divine presence there. However, when the context involves other holy themes like love, charity, or faith, the word "land" can be understood as those specific qualities. Nevertheless, the underlying connection to the "church" remains, as these qualities are what essentially define a church.

Under threat of punishment, they command their servants—whom they keep in great numbers—to call them "lords." They likewise forbid these servants from adoring the Lord of the universe, saying that they themselves are the Lord's mediators, and that they will bring the servants' prayers to the Lord of the universe. The Lord of the universe (who is our Lord), they do not call "the One Only Lord," as the rest of the inhabitants do, but "the Supreme Lord," specifically because they also call themselves "lords."

**8736.** These "saints," who are addressed as lords by their servants, call the sun "the face of the Supreme Lord" and believe His home to be there; for this reason, they also adore the sun. The rest of the inhabitants hold them in aversion and will not have any interaction with them, both because they adore the sun and because they call themselves "lords" and are worshiped by their servants as **mediatory gods**.

# EXODUS

**8737.** The **instructing and chastising spirits** <note>In the author's system, these are specific spirits who visit individuals on other planets to provide guidance or correction for faults.</note> (spoken of above in sections 7802–7812) do not come to these people as they do to others on that planet. This is because these individuals do not allow themselves to be taught, nor are they improved by discipline. They are stubborn because they act from the **love of self**. The spirits say that they can tell who they are by their coldness; when they notice this coldness, they depart from them.

**8738.** I was shown by the spirits the head-covering of those who call themselves "saints": it was a very tall hat of a darkish color.

**8739.** In the **afterlife** <note>The original text uses "the other life" to refer to the spiritual world after death.</note>, such people appear on the right, toward the back, at some height. There they sit like statues <note>The original uses the word "idols."</note> and are initially worshiped by their servants who had been with them; however, they are later held in derision by those same servants. What surprised me was that their faces shine there as if from fire. This is because they believed they were saints and were in the likeness of the Lord, who is in the sun of heaven. But despite this fiery appearance of their faces, they are actually cold and have an intense desire to be made warm. From this, it is plain that the fire with which they shine is merely a **will-o'-the-wisp** <term>ignis fatuus</term> <note>original: "ignis fatuus"; a deceptive light seen over marshes that provides no heat, symbolizing a false or hollow spiritual glow.</note>.

**8740.** In order to make themselves warm, these same people seem to themselves to be **cutting wood**. While they are cutting, something resembling a man appears underneath the wood, whom they attempt to strike at the same time. This happens because they attribute **merit** <note>In this theological context, "merit" refers to the prideful belief that one's own good deeds deserve a reward from God, rather than acknowledging that all good comes from the Divine.</note> to themselves; and as they claim holiness, they also credit themselves with righteousness. Those who do this in the world seem to themselves to be cutting wood in the afterlife. This is also the case with some from our own earth, as mentioned previously from experience, which may be quoted here for the sake of illustrating the subject (from section 4943):

> “In the **lower earth** <note>A region in the spiritual world where certain souls undergo a process of transition or purification.</note>, under the soles of the feet, are also those who have placed merit in good deeds and in works. Some of them appear to themselves to be cutting wood. The place where they are is rather cold, and they seem to themselves to acquire warmth by their labor. I spoke with these people as well; and I was allowed to ask them whether they wished to come out of that place. They replied that they had not yet 'earned' it by their labor. But when this state has been passed through...”

# CHAPTER THE NINETEENTH.

## THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY.

**8742.** Every person has an **internal man** and an **external man**. The internal man is what we call the **spiritual man**, and the external man is what we call the **natural man**. For a person to be fully **regenerated** <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth where a person's priorities shift from selfish desires to divine love.</note>, both of these parts must be transformed.

**8743.** In a person who has not been regenerated, the external or natural man is in command, while the internal or spiritual man serves. But in a person who has been regenerated, this is reversed: the internal or spiritual man commands, and the external or natural man serves. This **inversion** <note>The turning "upside down" of a person's original, selfish nature so that spiritual values take the lead.</note> can only happen through regeneration by the Lord.

**8744.** As long as the external man remains unregenerated, he believes that "good" consists only in physical pleasure, financial gain, and pride; he burns with hatred and a desire for revenge against anyone who stands in his way. In this state, the internal man does more than just agree—it actually provides the logic and reasons to justify and encourage these behaviors. Thus, the internal man is enslaved to the commands of the external man.

<summary>This page describes the spiritual state of Jupiter's "merit-seekers" and introduces the core concept of regeneration, which requires the spiritual internal man to take lead over the natural external man.</summary>
<keywords>Jupiter, merit, salvation, woodcutters, internal man, external man, regeneration, spiritual vs natural, Exodus 19, Doctrine of Charity</keywords>

--- Page 378 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion on the transformation of the human spirit, moving from the description of spirits from Jupiter to the practical application of spiritual growth (regeneration) and the biblical narrative of the Israelites reaching Mount Sinai.</meta>

**8745.** However, once a person’s **external self** has been **regenerated** <note>Regeneration refers to the spiritual rebirth or transformation of a person's character from being self-centered to being God-centered.</note>, the **internal self** makes all goodness consist in thinking and wishing well for one's neighbor. Meanwhile, the external self focuses that goodness on speaking and acting kindly toward them. Ultimately, both parts aim to love their neighbor and the Lord, rather than focusing on themselves or the world as they did before. In this state, the external or "natural" self serves, while the internal or "spiritual" self leads.

**8746.** The Lord first transforms the internal self, and then the external self by means of the internal. The internal self is transformed by contemplating and desiring the truths of faith, while the external self is transformed by living according to those truths. To live out one's faith is what we call **charity** <term>Charity: In this context, it refers to active love and goodwill toward others, rather than just donating money.</term>.

**8747.** A person who has undergone this transformation is already in heaven within their internal self. They are an angel among angels, joining them fully after death. At that point, they can truly live the heavenly life: loving the Lord and their neighbor, understanding truth, delighting in what is good, and feeling the resulting joy. These experiences constitute the happiness of eternal life.

**8749.** "**the third month,**" signifies fulness of state; "**of the going forth of the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt,**" signifies after those who were of the spiritual church <note>The "spiritual church" refers to people who are guided by an intellectual understanding of truth and a conscience of what is right, rather than by direct intuitive love.</note> had been liberated from infestations <note>In this context, "infestations" are spiritual trials or "attacks" by negative influences that cloud a person's thinking and test their resolve.</note>; "**in this day,**" signifies that it was then; "**they came into the wilderness of Sinai,**" signifies a state of good in which truths of faith were to be implanted; "**and they journeyed from Rephidim,**" signifies continuity of life from the former state; "**and came into the wilderness of Sinai,**" signifies to a state of good in which truths were to be implanted; "**and encamped in the wilderness,**" signifies the arrangement in this state; "**and Israel encamped close to the mountain,**" signifies the arrangement by Divine celestial good with those who are of the spiritual church.

**8750.** ***In the third month.*** That this signifies fulness of state, is evident from the signification of "**month**," as being **state** <term>State: In the spiritual world, space and time do not exist as they do here. Instead, "state" refers to a person's internal condition—their thoughts and feelings. Changes in "state" are the spiritual equivalent of moving through time or location.</term>; for all periods of time, as "**days**," "**weeks**," "**months**," and "**years**," signify states (see n. 2788); and from the signification of "**three**" and "**third**," as being what is complete (n. 1825, 2788, 4495, 5159); consequently "**in the third month**" denotes in fulness of state. 

[2] What fulness of state is, shall be briefly told. Every state has its beginning, its progression, and its end. When a state arrives at its end, it is then full, and is called "**fulness**." In the other life all things are measured by progressions of state and their successive changes from beginning to end, as in the world by times. That this is so is because in heaven there are no times, but states in their stead. The reason is that the sun in the other life, which is the Lord, remains constantly in its place, and does not, as in the world, by apparent daily progressions distinguish the day into morning, noon, evening, and night; nor by apparent annual progressions distinguish the year into spring, summer, autumn, and winter. From this it is that in heaven there are no times, but states in their stead. But as in the inmost sphere of heaven there is a certain progression according to the Divine heavenly form, which comes to the perception of no one, and as according to this progression the states of all in heaven undergo changes, the angels there are by turns in the good of love, in the truth of faith, and in obscurity as to the one and the other. From this it is that there is a **correspondence** <term>Correspondence: The relationship between a natural object or event and the spiritual reality it represents. For example, "light" in the world corresponds to "truth" in the mind.</term> of the states...

In the **internal sense** <term>Internal sense: The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and history.</term> it signifies the truth of faith from good—here the truth of faith that is to be implanted in good, because the law had not yet been proclaimed from it. 

“Mount Sinai” has these significations because the law was proclaimed by the Lord from there, and “the law” denotes Divine truth from Divine good, and also the truth of faith from good (sections 6752, 7463, 8695). For this reason the sons of Israel encamped in the wilderness near that mountain, for from it were proclaimed not only the ten commandments, which are “the law” in a strict sense, but also all the statutes of the church, which contained in themselves—because they represented—the spiritual and celestial truths and goods of the Lord’s kingdom. That the law was proclaimed from there is evident from the following chapter, and that the statutes of the church were also proclaimed from there is evident from the succeeding chapters, and also from *Leviticus*.

Whereas those who at the same time believe that such things are to be attended to, but that the essential of worship is the "life of faith"—that is, **charity** toward the neighbor and love to the Lord—these are of the internal church. vi. 1, 2). [6] In the **internal sense** <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note>, "wings" represent spiritual truths—specifically the truths of faith. This is clearly shown in the book of *Ezekiel*:

> Thus said the Lord Jehovah: A great eagle, with large wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took a small branch of a cedar tree. He carried it to a land of trade and placed it in a city of merchants. He then took some seed from the land and planted it in fertile soil; he set it beside abundant waters, where it sprouted and became a spreading vine. And there was another great eagle with large wings and many feathers. The vine stretched its roots toward this eagle and sent out its branches to be watered from the ground where it was planted. It was planted in good soil beside many waters to produce branches and bear fruit, so that it might become a magnificent vine. (*Ezekiel xvii.* 3-8).

This prophecy describes how the Lord establishes a **spiritual church** <note>A community or individual state defined by a love for truth and neighborly charity.</note> once again. In this context, the "eagle" represents faith. Having "large wings and long pinions" signifies the various truths that make up that faith. The "embroidery" or "many colors" represents <term>memory-knowledge<note>original: "scientifica"; refers to the raw facts and information stored in the mind that serve as the foundation for spiritual understanding.</note></term>.

The growth of this church is described by the "small branch of the cedar," the "land of trade," and the "seed in a field of sowing." The church itself, growing from these origins, is called "the vine." (To understand why "a vine" represents the spiritual church, see references n. 1069, 5113; and for the external church, n. 6375). The "magnificent vine" produced by the second eagle represents the **internal church** <note>The deeper, more heartfelt spiritual life of the church, as opposed to its outer rituals or literal doctrines.</note> (n. 6376). The prophet uses two different eagles to distinguish between the church’s outer appearance and its inner spirit. Later in the same chapter, the prophet describes how the ancient church was eventually corrupted.

[7] Similarly, "wings" signify the truth of faith in the book of *Psalms*:

> Though you lie among the sheepfolds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold. (*Psalm lxviii.* 13);

Here, the "wings of a dove" represent the truths of faith (for the "dove" itself represents faith; see n. 870). These wings are said to be "covered with silver" because silver symbolizes **truth derived from good** <note>Truth that is not just intellectual, but motivated by a kind and loving heart.</note> (n. 1551, 2954, 5658, 6914, 7999).

[8] That "wings" represent Divine truth is also clear from these passages:

> Those who wait for Jehovah shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles. (*Isaiah xl.* 31).
> God rode upon a cherub and flew; He was seen upon the wings of the wind. (*Psalm xviii.* 10; *civ.* 3).

In this passage, "wings" represent falsities that fight against the truth. This is because a "locust" signifies <term>falsity in the extremes<note>original: "falsum in extremis"; this refers to errors or lies that exist at the most superficial, sensory level of human thinking.</note></term> (see section 7643).

**8765.** *And brought you unto Me.*

In this specific context, it refers to that Divine Good as it is manifested in heaven (section 8761).

These current words, "I brought you unto Me," signify the Divine Good of love in heaven. This is because it is through the truths of faith that a person is led toward "good"—meaning toward a life of love—and thus into heaven and into the presence of the Lord. A person is not truly in heaven, nor with the Lord, until they live in a state of "good," which is the sincere affection of charity. 

[2] Those who believe that salvation comes through **faith alone** <note>A theological position suggesting that intellectual belief or trust in God is sufficient for salvation, regardless of one's actions or character.</note>, and not through a life of faith (which is a life of charity), assume that anyone can enter heaven and reach the Lord regardless of how they have lived. They do not understand the nature of a person’s "life." Because they lack this understanding, they suppose that a person's actual way of living is irrelevant. These primary truths are:
*   That there is one God.
*   That the Lord was born as a man so that He might save the human race.
*   That there is a heaven and there is a hell.
*   That those who have lived well go to heaven, and those who have lived poorly go to hell.
*   That love for God and love toward one's neighbor are the commandments on which everything else depends.
*   That this love is impossible except through faith.

These and similar principles are the first things instilled by the Lord into the "good" of the person being regenerated. When these truths have been instilled and have become truths rooted in goodness, then all other specific truths are introduced. These are organized within and under those general or primary truths according to a heavenly pattern. Conjunction: A spiritual connection or "joining together" between the human and the Divine.</term>. This is shown by the meaning of "reporting words to Jehovah" as the establishment of harmony and the resulting connection. The subject here is the **covenant** <note>In a spiritual sense, a covenant is not just a legal contract, but a living union between God and humanity based on mutual love and truth.</note> that was to be made with the people. Because covenants are made by mutual consent, a symbolic process is described here: Jehovah proposes, and the people answer through Moses. 

Moses here represents truth that comes from the Divine, which is joined with the Divine Truth in heaven (see n. 8760), acting as a mediator. However, a spiritual covenant is only possible when a person receives the flow of truth from the Divine and acts in harmony with it (correspondence). When higher spiritual forces flow into lower human states, they can only be received through this process of alignment. [2] The nature of correspondence and how it enables this reception can be seen in the explanations provided at the end of many previous chapters.

By this light the understanding is enlightened no otherwise than is the external sight, which is of the eye, by the light which is from the sun of the world. When the understanding is enlightened by that Divine light, it then perceives that to be true which is true, it acknowledges it inwardly in itself, and as it were sees it. Such is the revelation of those who are in the affection of truth from good when they are reading the Word.

**8788. *And sanctify them to-day and to-morrow.*** This signifies the veiling over of the interiors <note>In this theological context, "interiors" refers to a person’s inner thoughts, motives, and spiritual state.</note> so that they may appear in the holiness of faith both now and afterward. This is evident from the meaning of "sanctifying," which is to arrange things so that they appear to be holy in their external form. Because this appearance is created by veiling over the inner state of the people, "sanctifying" here refers to that veiling. It is also clear that "to-day and to-morrow" refers to "now and afterward."

The following brief explanation clarifies this situation: The church established among the Jews was not a true church in terms of their actual spiritual state, but was only the **representative** of a church. For a real church to exist, the person must have faith in the Lord, love for Him, and love toward their neighbor. These qualities are what constitute a church. However, these qualities did not exist within the people called "Jacob" <note>The name "Jacob" is often used here to represent the natural or external side of the church, or the Jewish people in their external worship.</note>, for they did not acknowledge the Lord and were unwilling to hear about faith in Him, much less about love toward Him or their neighbor. Instead, they were governed by self-love and love of the world—motives that are completely opposite to heavenly love. This disposition was deeply rooted in that people from their earliest ancestors. For this reason, a true church could not be established among them, but only a representation of the spiritual things belonging to a church.

[2] A church is "representative" when a person’s worship consists of external rituals that correspond to heavenly things. In such a case, the internal spiritual realities are represented by the outward actions; these internal things are "open" in heaven, allowing for a connection with the Divine. Therefore, in order for the Israelitish people to serve as a representation—even though their inner lives lacked faith and love and were full of selfishness—those interiors had to be **veiled over**. 

By veiling the interior state, their external rituals could be communicated to spirits and, through them, to angels, without being contaminated by their actual inner thoughts. If their inner state had not been veiled, it would have been exposed; the representation would have been destroyed because "unclean" spiritual influences would have burst forth and caused contamination. The Israelitish people were more capable of being veiled in this way than others because they, more than any other people, adored external rituals and placed the essence of holiness in them.

<summary>This page explains that the Israelitish church was "representative," meaning its outward rituals symbolized spiritual truths even though the people themselves lacked internal faith and love. To maintain a connection with heaven, their selfish inner motives had to be "veiled" during worship.</summary>

**8794.** *And thou shalt set bounds to the people round about.* That this signifies extension into heaven no further than to the spiritual spheres of good, is evident from the signification of "setting bounds round about," as being the extension of the sphere into heaven to certain limits, which are determined by the good of each person; and from the representation of the sons of Israel, who are "the people" here spoken of, as being those who are in the spiritual good in which truth is to be implanted; for this state of the good of those who are of the spiritual church is described in this and the following chapters (see n. 8753). Hence it is that by "thou shalt set bounds to the people round about" is signified an extension into heaven no further than to the spiritual spheres of good. 

[2] What is meant by "extension into heaven to the spiritual spheres of good" cannot be known to any one except by revelation. The case herein is this. All the good which is given to man through <term>regeneration<gloss>The spiritual process of being "born again" or reformed by God into a more heavenly person.</gloss></term> from the Lord has extension to societies in heaven. This extension differs as to amount and quality with each person; as to amount when to more remote limits; as to quality, when to the interiors or more to the exteriors of heaven. Good itself with man flows in from the Lord through the societies of heaven which are round about; good without <term>influx<gloss>The concept that spiritual life and thoughts "flow in" to humans from the divine or the spiritual world.</gloss></term>...

...through societies not being possible. The societies of heaven are in continuous connection round about, and nowhere is there seen a discontinuity. It is the same with each and all things that pertain to **good**, and constitute its quality. Wherefore during a person’s <term>regeneration<gloss>The process of spiritual rebirth where a person is gradually changed from being self-centered to being led by God.</gloss></term>, the enriching of **good** is nothing else than an introduction into <term>angelic societies<gloss>Groups of angels in the afterlife who are joined together by shared values and mutual love.</gloss></term>, and thus a conjunction with them (see also n. 4067, 4073, 4077, 6598—6613). <note>These numbers refer to other sections in Swedenborg’s multi-volume work, "Arcana Coelestia."</note>

[3] This has also been frequently shown by living experience; for sometimes the communications with certain societies have been taken away, and then only so much of life and such a quality of life remained as was the degree and quality of extension into the remaining societies; and when more societies were taken away, then the life labored, and began as it were to be extinguished. Every angel, spirit, and person has a <term>spiritual sphere<gloss>An invisible aura or field of influence that radiates from every person, reflecting their true inner character.</gloss></term>, and this exists according to his extension into societies. This extension is not into the societies themselves, but into the spheres of their **good**.

These are secrets which are unknown to people today, but in the other life are very well known. The reason why they are unknown to man is that at this day he believes that he has life in himself, and consequently that he lives without connection with spirits and angels, thus without conjunction with heaven; but in this he is quite mistaken, for all the life of man is from the Lord through societies.

[4] Be it further known that the extension of the life of those who are of the <term>spiritual church<gloss>A group of people whose spiritual life is characterized by obedience to truth and the use of the intellect.</gloss></term> is to the angelic spheres in the second heaven, which is called the *spiritual heaven*; but not to the third heaven where the <term>celestial<gloss>The highest level of angels, who live from a state of pure, intuitive love rather than intellectual reasoning.</gloss></term> are. The reason is that the members of the spiritual church cannot receive the Divine such as it is in the inmost or third heaven where the celestial are, except so generally that it does not at all come to their perception; because the spiritual cannot come even to the first threshold of the **good** in which the celestial are (n. 2718, 3833, 6500, 8521).

From all this it is evident what is meant by extension into heaven no further than to the spiritual spheres of **good**, which is signified by, “*thou shalt set bounds to the people round about;*” also what is meant by what follows.

[5] Be it also known that as they who are in **good** have extension into angelic societies according to the quality and amount of their **good**, so they who are in evil have extension into infernal societies according to the quality and amount of their **evil**; and their extension is into the spheres of those societies. There is a continuous connection in the opposite direction, also, in order that all things may be held together.

**8795.** *Saying, Take heed to yourselves, that ye go not up into the mountain.* This signifies that there is no possible extension or entry into the <term>celestial societies<gloss>The highest groups of angels in heaven, who live in a state of pure love for God.</gloss></term> for those in a different spiritual state. This is clear from the meaning of "going up," which refers to moving toward the Divine presence in a higher heaven; and from the meaning of "the mountain," which symbolizes the **good of love** found there (see previous explanations in sections 4210, 6435, 8327, 8758). The reality of this situation is explained in the section just above (n. 8794).

**8796.** *Or touch the extremity of it.* This signifies that they cannot even reach the intermediate or "border" areas. This is evident from the meaning of "extremity" as those intermediate things. The Lord's **celestial kingdom**, which exists in the innermost or third heaven, is separated from the **spiritual kingdom** (the second or middle heaven) by intermediate states. Through these, the celestial kingdom flows into the spiritual kingdom, but never the other way around. All <term>influx<gloss>The flow of life, heat, and light from God through the inner levels of heaven down to the outer levels.</gloss></term> moves from the interior to the exterior, never from the exterior to the interior (see n. 5259, 5779). From this, it is plain that these "extremities" are the borders, and those of the spiritual kingdom cannot reach even the first boundaries of the celestial kingdom’s love (n. 2718, 3833, 6500, 8521). Thus, the command "do not touch the edge of the mountain" means there is no way for those in the lower heaven to reach into the celestial societies or even their borders.

**8797.** *Every one that toucheth the mountain, dying he shall die.* This signifies that any member of the <term>spiritual church<gloss>Those whose spiritual life is based on truth and neighborly charity rather than the direct, pure love characteristic of the 'celestial' state.</gloss></term> who tries to force their way into the celestial societies will perish. This is clear from the symbolism of "the mountain" as the good of love (as seen in n. 8795)—specifically here, the Divine Good of Divine Love in the highest heaven. This is because the people standing below represent the Lord's spiritual kingdom (the middle heaven). The act of "touching" represents attempting to penetrate or insert oneself into that state.

## CHAPTER XIX. VERSES 10-13
### Section 8797

(of which we will speak shortly); and from the meaning of the phrase "dying he shall die," which signifies to perish spiritually. 

[2] The situation is as follows: those who belong to the Lord's <term>spiritual kingdom<gloss>The middle or second heaven, where the primary focus is on living according to truths and neighborly love.</gloss></term> cannot flow into the <term>celestial kingdom<gloss>The highest or third heaven, where the primary focus is a direct, intuitive love for the Lord.</gloss></term>. This is because the celestial kingdom is higher or more "interior," while the spiritual is lower or more "exterior." According to spiritual laws, what is lower or more outward cannot flow into what is higher or more inward (see sections 5259, 5779). 

Yet, it sometimes happens that those in a lower heaven attempt to ascend into a higher one. This stems from a misguided desire rooted in pride, a craving for power, or envy. When someone makes this attempt out of such a desire, they are permitted to enter; however, they immediately suffer hardships. They are seized with intense anxiety, followed by pain and even spiritual blindness, causing them to lose both their intelligence and their happiness. Consequently, they throw themselves down from that height as if they were dying, and they do not recover their vital spirit until they have returned to their proper level below heaven. 

[3] Such is the fate of those who, driven by the greed of pride, dominion, or envy, try to force themselves into a higher heaven. The reason is that, compared to their own state, the **good of love** in the higher heaven acts like a consuming fire, and the **truth of faith** there acts like a blinding, scorching light to their sight. This is the <term>internal sense<gloss>The deeper spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and words.</gloss></term> behind the command that the people of Israel should not touch Mount Sinai, where Jehovah was present. 

The same would happen to those in the celestial kingdom if they attempted to ascend directly to the Divine itself, and likewise to those beneath heaven if they tried to force their way into heaven. (For more on the hardships these individuals suffer, see sections 4225, 4226, 4299, 5057, 5058.)

### Section 8798

**No hand shall touch it.** This signifies that this applies to those who try to insert themselves through **self-confidence**. This is evident from the meaning of "touching" (specifically the mountain) as attempting to enter into Divine celestial good (as explained above in section 8797). It is also shown by the meaning of "hand" as **power** (sections 4931–4937, 5327, 5328, 6292, 6947, 7188, 7189, 7518, 7673, 8050, 8153, 8281); and consequently, it represents self-confidence (sections 878, 5544). <note>In the symbolic language of the Bible, the "hand" represents the agency or power of the self.</note>

**8800.** *Or shooting, he shall be shot.* This signifies that <term>spiritual good<gloss>The quality of goodness derived from following religious or moral truths.</gloss></term> will also perish. This is clear from the meaning of "being shot" (as by an arrow) as perishing in regard to spiritual good. In the internal sense of the Word, an "archer" represents a <term>spiritual man<gloss>Someone whose spiritual life is primarily guided by truth and the intellect.</gloss></term> (see sections 2686, 2709, 6422).

**8801.** *Whether beast or man, he shall not live.* This signifies that both good and truth will lose their spiritual life. This is evident from the meaning of:
*   "A beast," which represents the affection or desire for good (see sections 45, 46, 142, 143, 246, 714, 715, 776, 2179, 2180, 3218, 3519, 5198, 7523).
*   "A man," which represents truth (sections 3134, 3459, 7716).
*   "Living," which refers to spiritual life (section 5890). 

Consequently, "not to live" means to lose that vital spiritual life. Goodness and truth lose their life when a person no longer perceives the inflow <note>The "influx" or constant spiritual energy flowing from God into the soul.</note> from the Lord, for this is the source of their life. In such a state, the person's goodness and truth might still look like the real thing on the outside, but they are like a painting—it has the appearance of a person, but it possesses no life of its own.

**8802.** *When the jobel* <note>original: "jobel" — The Hebrew word *yobel* refers to a ram's horn or the sound of a trumpet blast.</note> *is drawn out.* This signifies a state for those who have a general perception of <term>celestial good<gloss>The highest form of goodness, rooted in a direct, heart-centered love for the Lord.</gloss></term>. This is evident from the meaning of the phrase "when the *jobel* is drawn out"—or simply, when the trumpet sound is heard—as a general perception of celestial good. To "hear" signifies perception (sections 5017, 8361), and the *jobel* or "sound of the trumpet" signifies celestial good. 

The reason celestial good is represented by the sound of a trumpet or the *jobel* is based on the spiritual correspondence of musical instruments. Different instruments correspond to different types of feelings or "affections": 
*   **Stringed instruments** correspond to the affections for truth.
*   **Wind instruments** correspond to the affections for good (sections 418–420, 4138, 8337). 

The <margin>The Hebrew word *jobel*, used here by Swedenborg, specifically denotes the sound of the trumpet blast that announced the Jubilee year.</margin>

Those who belong to the spiritual church and live a life of truth (and, from that, a life of goodness) are held back from evils and kept in good by the Lord. The good that comes from the Lord is what is holy within them. 

Consequently, they are holy to the extent that they receive good from the Lord. They are considered holy insofar as they live a life of goodness according to the genuine truths of faith, while simultaneously believing that all the good they think and do comes from the Lord. When this happens, the evils within them are separated so as not to appear at all—especially those they have inherited from their parents. These <term>hereditary<gloss>Inclinations and tendencies toward selfishness or evil that are passed down through generations.</gloss></term> evils are "filthy" because they have been building up over many generations and are concentrated in the child. These are the "interiors" which, for those in the spiritual church, are hidden away and, as it were, veiled over (n. 966, 1667, 2307, 2308, 3701, 4317, 8550). Because of this, the entire <term>hereditary will<gloss>The natural inclinations toward self-interest inherited from ancestors.</gloss></term> they possess is destroyed. For this reason, a new <term>will<gloss>The faculty of the mind that chooses and desires.</gloss></term> is formed in their intellectual part by means of the truths of faith from the Lord. **8809.** *Come not near unto a woman.* That this signifies the purification of the <term>good of faith<gloss>The practical, lived expression of one's beliefs; doing what is right because one believes it is true.</gloss></term>, is evident from the fact that the marriages with the Israelitish nation were <term>impure<gloss>Meaning they were focused on external or physical laws rather than a spiritual union of souls.</gloss></term>, because their <term>interiors<gloss>The internal aspects of the mind and spirit.</gloss></term> were filthy; for <term>conjugial love<gloss>A specialized term for the spiritual, eternal love between a husband and wife, reflecting the union of Divine Good and Divine Truth.</gloss></term> descends from the marriage of good and truth; and therefore those who as to the interiors are not in good and truth cannot be in pure marriage; and they who as to the interiors are in evil and falsity, as was that nation, are in impure marriage. Hence it is that "not to come near unto a woman" denotes to abstain from what is impure. (That conjugial love descends from the heavenly marriage, which is that of good and truth, see n. 2727-2759, 2803, 3132, 4434, 4835; and that with the people descended from Jacob there was not anything conjugial, and therefore it was permitted them to have more than one wife, n. 3246.) 

But as regards those who are of the spiritual church and are here represented by the sons of Israel, neither are they in anything conjugial until with them truth has been implanted in good. Before this is the case, there is indeed marriage, but not pure marriage, for in the interiors there is not before this a marriage of good and truth. Hence it is that by "not to come near unto a woman" is signified in the internal sense to be purified as to the good of faith; for in this chapter the good in which truth has not yet been implanted is treated of, and in the following chapters the implanting.

**8812.** **When it was morning.** That this signifies a state when they were in <term>good<gloss>In this context, "good" refers to a state of being where a person's motives are rooted in love and kindness.</gloss></term>, is evident from the signification of “morning,” as being a state of the <term>good of love<gloss>The specific type of "good" that comes from loving others and the Divine.</gloss></term> (see section 8426). From what is here said, that Jehovah, that is, the Lord, descended upon Mount Sinai on the third day, and also on the morning of that day, it is very manifest that this was representative of some Divine thing in heaven. This cannot be made known to any one except from the <term>correspondence<gloss>The concept that every natural object or event reflects a deeper, spiritual reality.</gloss></term> of such things as come forth in the natural world with things that are in the spiritual world, and from the consequent signification; as in the present case what “morning” signifies, and what “the third day.” 

That “the third day” denotes the end of a former state, is because by “three” is signified what is full from beginning to end (see section 8790). That “morning” denotes a state of the good of love, is because the sun which in the other life gives light to the angels and to the universal heaven, is the Lord. The fire there is His Divine love, which gives the heat of life to every living being, and the light there is the Divine truth which enlightens all who receive it. This is quite different from the sun of this world, the fire of which is <note>original: "ignis"</note> fire and not love, and the light from which is light and not truth. 

[2] From all this it can be seen what are the effects of the fire and also of the light from the sun of the world, and what are the effects of the fire and light from the sun of heaven—namely, that from the former, the heat and light are devoid of life, but from the latter, the heat and light are attended with life. These latter, namely, those which come forth from the sun of heaven, are therefore called “spiritual,” because they have life in them; and the former, which are from the sun of the world, are called “natural,” and have no life in them. 

The life which in living beings is noticed in heat and from heat, is not from the heat of the sun of the world, but is from the heat of the sun of heaven. When this heat flows into the heat of the world, it produces that effect, and is felt in the body as elementary heat; but there is in it <term>vital heat<gloss>The actual "spark" or warmth of life that makes a person a living being, rather than just a physical object.</gloss></term> that has its origin from the love which is heat from the sun of heaven. That the origin of the heat of life is from some other source, and that it is in love and is according to the measure and the quality of the love, every one can know provided he is

...anyone willing to reflect correctly can see this, except for those who refuse to acknowledge anything internal within a human being and instead credit everything to nature. [3] Since the heat from the sun of heaven—which is the Lord—is the **good of love**, and the light from that sun is the **truth of faith**, we can see what is meant in the <term>afterlife<gloss>original: "in the other life"</gloss></term> by "morning," "noon," "evening," and "night." These terms describe different states of goodness and truth, or love and faith. "Morning" represents a state of the **good of love**; "noon" represents a state of the **truth of faith**; while "evening" and "night" represent the <term>lack<gloss>original: "privation"</gloss></term> of these states. This results in ignorance and blindness regarding the things of faith, as well as a spiritual <term>sluggishness<gloss>original: "torpor"</gloss></term> and coldness toward heavenly love. 

[4] Furthermore, the sun of heaven works much like the sun of our physical world. The sun itself is fixed; it does not create these different states by <term>moving around<gloss>original: "circumgyration"</gloss></term>. Instead, these changes are caused by the bodies surrounding it, such as the earth revolving around the sun while simultaneously spinning on its own axis. This creates the appearance that these changes come from the sun, when in fact they come from the world revolving around it. It is the same in heaven. The changes of state there—which correspond to morning, noon, evening, and night—do not come from the spiritual sun. That sun is always radiating heat and light (meaning the **good of love** and the **truth of faith**). Rather, these changes occur within those who receive that light—the angels and spirits. According to the patterns of their own lives, they experience regular cycles: sometimes they are in "morning" (the **good of love**), sometimes in "noon" (the **truth of faith**), and sometimes in "evening" and "night" (a state of spiritual shadow and sluggishness regarding love and faith). 

[5] The reason the physical world is so similar to heaven—with the difference being that the world experiences cycles of *time* while heaven experiences cycles of *life*—is that everything in the physical world was created in the image of things in heaven. Natural things <term>emerge<gloss>original: "come forth"</gloss></term> from spiritual things, much like an effect follows its cause. Because of this, there is a <term>correspondence<gloss>A meaningful link where physical objects reflect spiritual realities.</gloss></term> between everything in the world and everything in heaven. Consequently, the whole of nature is a theater that <term>represents<gloss>Acts as a symbolic mirror or stage.</gloss></term> the Lord’s kingdom (see sections 3483, 4939, 8211).

# EXODUS

**8814.** Since this people was in great darkness regarding Divine truths, it is therefore called “a heavy cloud,” and previously in verse 9, “the density of a cloud,” and later in verse 18, “smoke of fire like the smoke of a furnace.” Just how deep their darkness was can be seen from what was discussed earlier regarding that nation (see note 8788), and from the fact that things belonging to the <term>internal man<gloss>the inner spiritual self that connects with God</gloss></term> were not revealed to them. Only things belonging to the <term>external man<gloss>the outer self focused on the physical world and rituals</gloss></term> were shown to them. 

They did not understand internal, spiritual matters, nor did they want to understand them. This is because such truths were contrary to their own desires—namely, their wish to be the most powerful and wealthy people in the world, viewing all other nations as nothing. Where these selfish loves rule, heavenly loves cannot be received; they are extinguished and suffocated by worldly desires. This is why Jehovah—that is, the Lord—appeared to them in a dense and heavy cloud. This reflects what happens in the <term>other life<gloss>the spiritual world or afterlife</gloss></term>: those who are in <term>falsities<gloss>spiritual errors or distorted beliefs</gloss></term> born from evil are surrounded by a dense, black cloud that matches the nature and intensity of their errors. This cloud is visible to everyone there, even though the spiritual sun is actually shining all the time. (For more on this, see notes 6832, 8137, and 8138). Generally speaking, in the spiritual world, the Divine appears to each person according to the specific quality of their faith and love.

**8815.** *And the voice of a trumpet exceeding strong.* This signifies a celestial state that was all around. This is clear from the meaning of “the voice,” or sound, “of a trumpet” as the truth of <term>celestial good<gloss>the highest form of goodness, which flows from love for the Lord</gloss></term>. In this context, a “voice” represents truth, while a “trumpet” represents celestial good (as mentioned in note 8802). 

This represents a celestial state that was “round about” because the Divine in heaven is in the very center or inmost part—that is, in the highest position. However, from the perspective of the angels, heaven is "around" or "outside" of them, which is to say it is "beneath" them. This is because what is around is also outside, and what is outside is also beneath. <term>Truth Divine<gloss>original: "veritas Divina"; truth that proceeds directly from God</gloss></term> itself is symbolized in heaven by “voices” and “lightnings.” However, the celestial or angelic truth that is joined to the Divine—and which exists "beneath" or "around" it—is symbolized by “the voice of a trumpet.” We see this same usage in the book of *Zechariah*:

> Jehovah shall appear over them, and His arrow shall go forth like lightning; and the Lord Jehovih shall sound with the trumpet, and shall advance in the whirlwinds of the south (ix. 14).

The reason why the trumpets produced this effect was that they represented the Divine truth moving through the heavens, which is such that it perfects the good, but destroys the evil. The reason why it perfects the good is that they receive the Divine good which is within the truth; but it destroys the evil because they do not receive the Divine good within it. The "walls of Jericho" signified the <term>falsities<gloss>incorrect or distorted spiritual beliefs</gloss></term> which defended evils; and "Midian, Amalek, and the sons of the east," round about whose camp the three hundred men of Gideon sounded the trumpets, signified those who were in evils and in the resulting falsities.
