By the greatest obscurity, which is signified by "Mount Sinai smoked, the whole of it," and by what is said just below, that "the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace," is meant that obscurity in which was the Israelitish nation, before whom the appearing took place; for Jehovah or the Lord appears to every one according to his quality (see n. 8788, 8814), thus as love and as the light of truth to those who are in good, but as an enemy and avenger to those who are in evil. That so did He appear to the Israelitish people, is also evident from other passages in Moses:—

->### CHAPTER XIX. VERSES 20-25<-

->**[N. 8827]**<-

...because the head of the mountain is its highest point, and "the highest" signifies the <term>inmost<gloss>the deepest or most central level of spiritual reality</gloss></term> (see notes 1735, 2148, 4210, 4599, 8153). There are three heavens: the lowest, which is called the first; the middle, which is called the second; and the inmost, which is called the third. In this third heaven, the Divine presence is felt more fully than in the two lower heavens. Those who dwell there are under the immediate view of the Lord because they live in a state of love to the Lord, and consequently enjoy a level of peace and innocence above all others. 

The angels who dwell there are called <term>celestial angels<gloss>beings who live in a state of pure love and direct perception of truth</gloss></term>, and the angels in the second heaven are called <term>spiritual angels<gloss>beings who live in a state of faith and intellectual understanding</gloss></term>. Consequently, the Divine presence in the one heaven is called "the Divine celestial," and in the other, "the Divine spiritual." From all this, it can be seen what is meant by the phrase, **"Jehovah came down upon the head of the mountain."**

->**[N. 8828]**<-

**And Jehovah called Moses unto the head of the mountain, and Moses went up.** This signifies the <term>conjunction<gloss>a spiritual union or connection between the human soul and the Divine</gloss></term> of truth from the Divine at that level. This is evident from the explanations provided earlier (n. 8760, 8761) regarding similar wording. In this specific context, it signifies a union with the <term>Divine celestial<gloss>the highest level of the Divine presence, characterized by love</gloss></term>—that is, with the Divine as it exists in the inmost heaven.

->**[N. 8829]**<-

**And Jehovah said unto Moses.** This signifies <term>exhortation<gloss>a strong warning or encouragement</gloss></term> from the Divine. This meaning is drawn from the word "saying," which introduces the instructions that follow. These instructions concern the warning that the people must not break through the boundaries that have been set around the mountain.

->**[N. 8830]**<-

**Go down, charge the people, lest perchance they break through unto Jehovah to see.** This signifies a warning that those who belong to the <term>spiritual church<gloss>a state of spiritual life based on faith and truth, distinct from the higher state of pure love</gloss></term> should not desire to ascend into the heaven where the Divine celestial resides. 

This interpretation is based on several factors:
*   **"To charge"** signifies a Divine exhortation or warning.
*   **"The people"** (the sons of Israel) represent those belonging to the spiritual church.
*   **"Breaking through"** the bounds signifies the desire to ascend into a higher heaven than one's own state allows.
*   **"To see Jehovah"** signifies perceiving the Divine. 

Because **"Jehovah on the head of the mountain"** represents the Divine in the inmost heaven (the celestial heaven, see n. 8827), the act of "seeing" represents the act of <term>perception<gloss>the internal ability to see and understand spiritual truth</gloss></term> (see n. 2150, 3764, 4567, 4723, 5400).

# EXODUS [Section 8831]

**8831.** ***And many of them fall.*** This signifies that, in such a state, they would perish <note>original: "perituros"</note>. This meaning is clear enough without further explanation.

**8832.** ***And the priests also, who come near unto Jehovah, shall sanctify themselves.*** This signifies that those who are in a state of <term>spiritual good<gloss>a state where goodness is achieved through the understanding and practice of truth</gloss></term>—a state in which the Divine is present—must be covered over or protected. This is evident from several spiritual associations:
*   **"Priests"** represent goodness (see sections 1728, 2015, 6148). In this specific case, it refers to spiritual good because the "sons of Israel" represent the spiritual church—those who live in goodness by means of truth (see sections 7957, 8234).
*   **"Coming near unto Jehovah,"** when spoken of priests, signifies a state of goodness that contains the Divine.
*   **"Being sanctified"** signifies being "covered over" in one's internal spirit to prevent destruction by the Divine light (see sections 8788, 8806).

**8833.** ***Lest perchance Jehovah make a breach in them.*** This signifies a separation from goodness. This is evident from the meaning of **"making a breach,"** which refers to the separation of truth from goodness (see section 4926). Here, it specifically refers to separation from goodness because it is spoken in reference to the priests, who represent that good.

**8834.** ***And Moses said unto Jehovah.*** This signifies the thought of truth that originates from the Divine. In the spiritual sense, **"saying"** often signifies "thought" (see also sections 3395, 7107, 7244, 7937), especially when represented by Moses, who stands for "truth from the Divine." 

It is described as "the thought of truth from the Divine" to indicate the thought processes of someone who represents such truth. This is because, in a deep spiritual sense, it is the truth within a person that "thinks," and the person thinks by means of that truth. The Lord flows into a person through goodness and into truth, giving that person life. Although this life feels like the person's own, it actually belongs to the Lord, residing in the truth-from-goodness within them. This is the nature of <term>angelic speech<gloss>a higher form of communication that focuses on abstract spiritual realities rather than individual persons</gloss></term>; angels attribute thought to truth and goodness itself, recognizing the true source of wisdom.

**8835.** ***The people cannot come up unto Mount Sinai.*** This signifies that they are unable to raise themselves to the <term>celestial kingdom<gloss>the highest level of heaven, defined by direct love for the Lord rather than just obedience to truth</gloss></term>. This is evident from the representation of "the people" (the sons of Israel) as those belonging to the spiritual church, who reside on a different level of awareness than those in the celestial kingdom.

By being "veiled," they are kept safe from the Divine; if they were not veiled, the intensity of the Divine presence would penetrate and destroy them, for to those who are unprepared, the Divine presence is like a consuming fire. This is the reason even the angels are said to be veiled with a cloud (see section 6849). From this, we can understand what it means to be "veiled over." This is described as being "sanctified" because when a person is thus protected, they appear holy; only then can the Divine flow in and create a state of goodness and a form of truth, which cannot happen without such a protective covering.

**8839.** ***And Jehovah said unto him.*** This signifies a further warning <note>original: "admonitio"</note>. This is evident from the meaning of "saying"—when the Lord <note>original: "Jehovah"</note> speaks to Moses (who represents the truth that comes from the Divine) telling him to warn the people not to "break through to see"—as a spiritual admonition. It is a "further" warning because Moses had just pointed out that they had already been cautioned about this matter.

**8840.** ***Go, get thee down.*** This signifies <term>influx<gloss>the spiritual process where life, heat, and light flow from God into the souls of people</gloss></term>. This is evident from the meaning of "going down to the people and warning them." When this is commanded by the Divine through the Truth-from-the-Divine (represented by Moses), it represents the flow or influx of the Divine through that truth.

### [Section 8847] SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF JUPITER

He appeared at my left side under the elbow and spoke with what seemed to be a broken voice, a sound that could move a listener to pity. But I could only reply that I could give him no help, as such aid comes from the Lord alone. I explained that I could not intercede for him because I did not know whether it would be spiritually beneficial, but I told him that if he were worthy, he might have hope. 

He was then sent back among the upright spirits from his own world; however, they stated that he could not remain in their company because his character did not match theirs. Yet, because he importuned with intense longing to be admitted into heaven, he was sent into a society of upright spirits from our own Earth. They also concluded that he could not stay with them. 

In the light of heaven, he appeared to be of a black color, but he himself claimed he was not black, but of a <term>murrhine<gloss>original: "murrhinus"; a variegated or iridescent color similar to fluorite or fine porcelain</gloss></term> color. I was told that spirits who are later received into the province of the <term>seminal vesicles<gloss>the glands that store and prepare seminal fluid</gloss></term> appear this way at first. In these vesicles, the semen is collected and protected by a suitable material to prevent it from being lost, and this outer layer is eventually shed in the neck of the womb so that the internal substance may serve for conception—that is, the impregnation of the <term>ovulum<gloss>the egg cell</gloss></term>. 

Consequently, within this seminal matter, there is an inherent effort—an almost burning desire—to cast off its outer layer and leave the semen to perform its vital use. A similar quality was visible in this spirit. He returned to me wearing humble clothing and again said he was burning with a desire to enter heaven, perceiving now that he was fit for it. I was moved to tell him that perhaps this feeling was an indication that he would soon be received. The angels then told him to cast off his garment; in his longing, he threw it off so quickly that nothing could be faster. This act represented the nature of the ardent desires felt by those in the spiritual province corresponding to the <term>seminal vesicles</term>.

**8848.** It was said that when such spirits have been prepared for heaven, they are stripped of their old garments and clothed in new, shining ones, and they become angels. The angels likened these spirits to caterpillars which, having moved past their lowly state, are changed into <term>chrysalides<gloss>the pupa or cocoon stage of a butterfly</gloss></term>, and finally into butterflies. At that stage, they are given new clothing and wings of blue, yellow, silver, or gold, along with the freedom to fly in the open air as if in their own heaven.

...in their heaven, to enter into marriages, lay eggs, and ensure the continuation of their species. They are also provided with sweet, pleasant nourishment from the nectar and scents of various flowers. <note>In the internal spiritual sense, these descriptions of birds and flowers represent the growth of new ideas and the delights of spiritual learning.</note>

**8849.** A spirit from that world approached me, explaining that he was searching for the **One Only Lord** <note>original: "Unicum Dominum"; Swedenborg notes that the inhabitants of Jupiter worship the Lord as the sole God of the universe</note> and desired to enter heaven. However, he felt he could not because of a wrong he committed during his physical life. When I asked what he had done, he confessed to taking something of very little value from a companion, mistakenly believing it was a gift. This small act weighed heavily on his conscience. This interaction shows the moral character of those on that planet; they are deeply troubled by even the slightest harm done to others, as this spirit carried the guilt with him from his world into the afterlife.

**8850.** I was shown the top of a bald head, where only the bone was visible. I was told that this sign appears to those who will die within a year, serving as a signal for them to prepare themselves. On that planet, they do not fear death, except for the sadness of leaving their spouse, children, or parents. They understand that life continues after death and that they are not truly "dying" but are becoming **heaven-made.** <note>original: "coelo facti"; a term used by these spirits to describe the transition to the afterlife</note> Those who lived happily in <term>conjugial love<gloss>a term for the spiritual and eternal marriage bond between two souls</gloss></term> and fulfilled their duties as parents do not die from illness. Instead, they pass away peacefully, as if falling asleep, and transition from this world into heaven.

**8851.** Most inhabitants live to be about thirty years old, according to the years of our Earth. Those who live longer are considered "unteachable," and therefore the spirits who guide and correct them no longer visit. Their short lifespan is a result of Divine Providence, ensuring the population does not exceed what the planet can support. They also reach maturity much faster than people on Earth, marrying in the first flower of their youth. Their greatest joys are found in loving their spouse and caring for their children; they consider all other pleasures to be relatively external or secondary.

**8852.** At the conclusion of the next chapter, I will provide an account of the spirits and inhabitants of the planet Saturn.

429 [N. 8853] THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY

## CHAPTER THE TWENTIETH.

->THE DOCTRINE OF CHARITY.<-

**8853.** Every man has something of his own which he loves above all things. This is called that which rules, or if you will, that which <term>reigns universally<gloss>a technical term describing a dominant principle that influences every single thought and action, even when not consciously focused upon</gloss></term> with him. This is constantly present in his thought, and also in his will, and makes his veriest life. <note>original: "ipsissima vita"; Swedenborg suggests that our primary love is not just a part of us, but the very essence of our being.</note>

**8854.** As for example, he who loves wealth above all things, whether money or possessions, is continually revolving in his mind how he may procure it; he inmostly rejoices when he acquires it; he inmostly grieves when he loses it; his heart is in it. He who loves himself above all things is mindful of himself in everything, thinks of himself, speaks of himself, acts for the sake of himself; for his life is a life of self.

**8855.** A man has as the <term>end<gloss>the ultimate purpose or motivation behind an action</gloss></term> that which he loves above all things; in each and all things he has regard to this; it is in his will like the hidden current of a river which draws and bears him away, even when he is doing something else, for it is what animates him. It is this which one man searches out in another, and also sees, and according to it either leads him, or acts with him.

**8856.** When a man is being <term>regenerated<gloss>the process of spiritual rebirth where a person's old selfish nature is replaced by a new spiritual nature</gloss></term>, charity is implanted by means of faith, even until it becomes that which rules; and when charity has become this, he has a new life, for it is then continually present in his thought, and continually in his will, nay, in every single thing of them, even when he is meditating about other things, and when he is engaged in business. <note>This indicates that a spiritual person does not need to be constantly thinking about God to be led by Him; their underlying love of doing good directs them automatically.</note>

**8857.** The case is the same with love to the Lord. When this love is that which rules, it is present in every single thing of the man's life; as for instance with him who loves his king, or his parent, his love toward them shines forth in their presence from every feature of his face, it is heard in every expression of his speech, and is seen in his every gesture. This is meant by having God continually before the eyes, and by loving Him above all things, with all the soul and with all the heart.

<summary>This page introduces the concept of the "ruling love," explaining that whatever a person loves most forms the hidden current of their life and dictates all their actions. It describes how, during spiritual rebirth, charity becomes this dominant force, shaping a person's character even in their daily business and interactions.</summary>

<keywords>ruling love, reigning universally, charity, regeneration, motivation, love of self, love of wealth, love to the Lord, spiritual psychology</keywords>

430 [N. 8858]

**8858.** A person is entirely defined by the ruling principle of their life; it is by this that they are distinguished from all others. It is according to this principle that their heaven is formed if they are good, and their hell if they are evil; for this principle is their <term>veriest will<gloss>the most fundamental level of human intention and desire</gloss></term> <note>original: "ipsissima voluntas"</note>, and thus the very being of their life, which cannot be changed after death. From all this it is evident what the nature of life is for one who is <term>regenerate<gloss>a person undergoing spiritual rebirth or transformation</gloss></term>, and what the nature of life is for one who is not.

## CHAPTER XX.

->**THE TEN COMMANDMENTS**<-
<note>Chapter 20 of Exodus contains the Decalogue, which Swedenborg views not just as civil laws, but as the fundamental laws of spiritual life and the "ruling principles" discussed in the previous section.</note>

1. And God spake all these words, saying,
2. I am Jehovah thy God, who brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of servants.
3. Thou shalt have no other gods before My faces. <note>original: "coram faciebus meis"; a literal translation of the Hebrew, suggesting that nothing should come before God’s direct presence or sight.</note>
4. Thou shalt not make unto thee a graven image, nor any likeness, of that which is in the heavens above, or that which is in the earth beneath, or that which is in the waters under the earth:
5. Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them; for I Jehovah thy God am a zealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the sons, upon the thirds and upon the fourths <note>referring to the third and fourth generations</note> of them that hate Me:
6. And doing mercy to thousands of them that love Me and keep My commandments.
7. Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain; for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that taketh His name in vain.
8. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
9. Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work:
10. And the seventh day is the sabbath to Jehovah thy God; thou shalt not do any work, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, thy manservant, and thy maidservant, and thy beast, and thy <term>sojourner<gloss>a resident alien or guest living within the community</gloss></term> who is in thy gates:
11. For in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested in the seventh day; wherefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.
12. Honor thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be prolonged upon the land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee.

### THE CONTENTS.

**8859.** In this chapter, the subject addressed in the <term>internal sense<gloss>the deeper, spiritual meaning hidden behind the literal words of scripture</gloss></term> is the divine truths that are to be implanted in the hearts of those who belong to the Lord’s spiritual church. The Ten Commandments of the <term>Decalogue<gloss>From the Greek "deka logoi," meaning "ten words"</gloss></term> represent these truths. The laws concerning sacrifices and the altar that follow in this chapter represent the external truths associated with outward worship.

### THE INTERNAL SENSE.

**8860.** Verse 1. *And God spoke all these words, saying*, signifies divine truths for those in the heavens and for those on earth.

**8861.** *And God spoke all these words, saying*. That this signifies divine truths for those in the heavens and for those on earth is evident from the meaning of "the words which God spoke" as being divine truths, for the things which God speaks are nothing else than truths. For this reason, Divine Truth is also called "the Word." This "Word" is the Lord, according to *John 1:1* <note>original: "In principio erat Verbum," meaning "In the beginning was the Word."</note>, because when the Lord was in the world, He was Divine Truth itself; afterward, when He was glorified, He became Divine Good, and from then on, all divine truth proceeds from Him. This divine truth is light to the angels, and this same light illuminates our internal sight, which is the sight of the understanding. 

[2] As this inner sight does not see natural things, but spiritual things, its objects in the spiritual understanding are the truths called "the truths of faith." However, in the "natural understanding," its objects are the truths of the civil state (relating to what is just), truths of the moral state (relating to what is honorable), and lastly, natural truths (which are conclusions drawn from the objects of the external senses, especially sight). From all this, one can see the order in which truths follow one another, and that every single one has its origin in divine truths, which are the internal beginnings of all things. Moreover, the forms...

**8862.** The reason that “the words which God spoke” refers to Divine Truths intended for both those in the heavens and those on earth, is because the Ten Commandments (known as the <term>Decalogue<gloss>From the Greek "deka logoi," meaning "ten words"</gloss></term>) and the subsequent laws given from Mount Sinai are truths meant for more than just those living in the physical world; they are also for those in the spiritual heavens. All words—that is, all truths—that come from the Lord are for both angels and humans simultaneously, because they originate in the Divine, pass through the heavens, and only then reach the earth. 

However, these truths do not "sound" or appear the same in the heavens as they do on earth. In the heavens, they exist in a **spiritual form**, while on earth they appear in a **natural form**. The difference between these two forms is revealed through the study of the <term>internal sense<gloss>The deeper, spiritual meaning of scripture</gloss></term> versus the <term>external sense<gloss>The literal, historical, or physical meaning of the text</gloss></term> of the Word. The internal sense is spiritual and is adapted for angels in the heavens, while the external sense (the literal text) is natural and has been adapted for people on earth.

[2] This is because the Word has been sent from the Divine itself, passing through the heavens on its way to the earth. When it reaches the earth, it is truth <term>accommodated<gloss>Adapted or adjusted to fit the limited understanding of the recipient</gloss></term> to the human race, which is focused on earthly and physical things. In the heavens, it is adapted for angels, who focus on spiritual and heavenly things. Because of this dual nature, the Word is inherently holy; it contains within itself everything that is heavenly and Divine. 

This can be clearly seen in the Ten Commandments. Anyone can see that these laws are globally recognized—such as the laws to honor parents, and the prohibitions against murder, adultery, theft, and lying. In fact, the <term>Israelite nation<gloss>The ancient Hebrew people to whom the Law was first given</gloss></term> could have known these laws through <term>natural light<gloss>Human reason and common sense without the help of divine revelation</gloss></term> alone; for what nation exists that does not already know...

**8864.** **I am Jehovah thy God.** That this signifies the Lord as to the **Divine Human** universally reigning in each and all things of good and truth, is evident from the fact that in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture.</note> no one other than the Lord is meant by "Jehovah" (see sections 1343, 1736, 2921, 3023, 3035, 3448, 5663, 6280, 6281, 6303, 8274), and in the same way by "**Jehovah of Hosts**" <note>original: *Jehovah Zebaoth*</note>, by "**the Lord God**" <note>original: *Lord Jehovih*</note>, and by "**Jehovah God**" (sections 2921, 3023, 3448, 6303). The Lord is called "Jehovah" from the Divine good, which is the Divine **Being** <note>original: *Esse*. In this philosophy, *Esse* refers to the underlying, essential core of existence.</note>, but He is called "God" from the Divine truth, which is the Divine **Coming-forth** <note>original: *Existere*. This refers to the way the inner essence manifests or becomes visible.</note> (section 6905, also 709, 732, 1096, 2586, 2769, 2807, 2822, 3921, 4402). 

That it is the **Divine Human** of the Lord which is meant here by "Jehovah God," is because the Lord, in respect to this Human, is meant in the Word by both "Jehovah" and "God"—He is "Jehovah" because of the Divine good, which He is even in His Human form; and He is "God" because of the Divine truth, which He is because it proceeds from Him. <margin>[2]</margin> The reason the <term>Divine Human<gloss>The concept that the Lord took on a human form that became fully divine, making the infinite God visible and accessible to finite beings</gloss></term> of the Lord is meant by "Jehovah God," is because the Divine nature itself, as it is in the Lord, cannot be seen in heaven, nor even perceived; therefore, it cannot be received in faith and love. Only the Divine Human can be so perceived. It is well known that the Divine itself cannot be communicated to the angels in heaven, and still less to men on earth, except through the Divine Human.

The things following in this chapter are the commandments of the <term>decalogue<gloss>The Ten Commandments</gloss></term>, which are internal truths, followed by the statutes, which are external truths. In both of these, the Lord must reign as the Divine Human, for they come from Him and are Him. This is because all truths that are truly truths proceed from Him, and what proceeds from Him is Himself. It is also known in the churches that the Lord, as the Divine Human, must reign in every single aspect of faith; for it is taught there that without the Lord there is no salvation, and that all the truth and good of faith come from Him. **8865.** What is meant by "universally reigning" can be seen from what has been shown before (see sections 8853–8858). When the Lord universally reigns with a member of the church, as He does with the angels of heaven, then the Lord is present in all the truths and goods of faith within that person, just as the heart is present in all the blood vessels—because the vessels derive their origin and the blood (which is their life) from the heart.

A person does not usually perceive that this is the source, because they do not realize that their life flows in from the spiritual world, nor that this "universal ruler" of their mind makes up their life. **8871.** *Of that which is in the heavens above, or that which is in the earth beneath.* That this signifies of those things which are in <term>spiritual light<gloss>In this context, the clarity and understanding that comes from divine truth and love, which illuminates the soul</gloss></term>, or of those which are in <term>natural light<gloss>Knowledge and perception derived from the physical world and human reasoning</gloss></term>, is evident from the signification of “a likeness of those things which are in the heavens above,” as being those things which appear and are seen in spiritual light, all of which bear relation to the good and truth which are of faith, of charity toward the neighbor, and of love to the Lord—to counterfeit and make a pretense of these things is to “make a likeness of those things which are in the heavens above;” and from the signification of “a likeness of those things which are in the earth beneath,” as being those things which appear and are seen in natural light, which are such as bear relation to civil and moral good and truth—to counterfeit and make a pretense of these things is to make a likeness of those things which are in the earth beneath. 

In the sense of the letter are meant such things as appear in heaven, as the sun, the moon, the stars; and such things as appear on the earth, as animals of various kinds, both flying, walking, and creeping; but in the internal sense are meant such things as are signified by these, all of which bear relation to good and truth, as was said above. [2] These things are further described in <note>Moses was the traditional author of the first five books of the Bible, including Deuteronomy.</note> **Moses**, in these words:—

> Lest ye make you a graven image in the shape of any likeness, the figure of male or of female, the figure of any beast that is on the earth, the figure of any winged bird that flieth under heaven, the figure of any thing that creepeth on the earth, of a fish that is in the waters under the earth: and lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and look at the sun, and the moon, and the stars, all the army of the heavens, and thou be impelled, and bow thyself to them, and serve them. Jehovah shall scatter you among the peoples, where ye shall serve gods, the work of a man’s hands, wood and stone (**Deuteronomy iv. 16–19; 23–28**).

They provoked Him to <term>zeal<gloss>In biblical language, this word often fluctuates between "zeal" and "jealousy," describing a passionate intensity</gloss></term> with strange gods; with <term>abominations<gloss>Actions or idols that are spiritually repulsive</gloss></term> they rendered Him angry. However, in a sense that is not genuine—appearing as it does to those who are in evils and <term>falsities<gloss>Untrue beliefs or distorted perceptions of reality</gloss></term>—anger and <term>vastation<gloss>A spiritual process of being emptied or stripped of the old self</gloss></term> are signified. 

Be it known that Jehovah—that is, the Lord—is especially called “zealous,” or “an avenger,” when that is corrupted which ought to reign universally within a person of the church: namely, the Divine. This Divine must be loved, thought of, or feared above all things. When this has been corrupted or destroyed, then instead of heavenly light, mere thick darkness takes its place. This happens because there is no longer any influx <note>original: "influxus"</note> of this light from the Divine, because there is no longer a way to receive it. 

For this reason it is said, “I am Jehovah thy God, a zealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the sons, upon the third and upon the fourth generations of them that hate Me.” This refers to cases where people worshiped other gods or made for themselves a <term>graven image<gloss>An idol carved from wood or stone, representing a man-made concept of God</gloss></term> or likenesses; for these things corrupt the Divine truth which should hold the central place in the heart. [9] Therefore it is declared in a similar way elsewhere in the books of <term>Moses<gloss>Specifically referring to the Torah or the first five books of the Bible</gloss></term>:—

> Take heed lest you make for yourselves a graven image of any figure, for Jehovah God is a devouring fire, a zealous God (*Deuteronomy 4:23, 24*).

# CHAPTER XX. VERSES 2-7

> You shall not worship another God; for Jehovah, whose name is <term>Zealous<gloss>Meaning a passionate, intense protection of what is holy and true</gloss></term>, is a zealous God (*Exodus 34:14*).

**8875.** This was so severely forbidden to the people of Israel because the worship of other gods, carved figures, and images destroyed every <term>representative<gloss>Physical objects or rituals that serve as symbols for spiritual realities</gloss></term> of the church among them. In heaven, Jehovah—that is, the Lord—is the one who rules over everything. His Divine presence fills all things there and provides life to everyone. If anything had been worshiped in place of the Divine, every spiritual symbol would have lost its meaning, and the communication with heaven would have been cut off.

**8876.** *Visiting the <term>iniquity<gloss>A word for deep-seated wickedness or sin</gloss></term> of the fathers upon the sons.* That this signifies the resulting <term>prolification<gloss>The rapid multiplication or spreading of something</gloss></term> of false ideas derived from evil, is clear from the meaning of "visiting the iniquity of the fathers." In this context, "visiting" refers to the way evil spreads and multiplies. This describes the state of those who utterly reject the Divine; they no longer receive what is good, but only what is evil. In such people, evil increases continually, which is what is meant by "prolification." <note>In the symbolic language of the Bible, "father" refers to good, or in the opposite sense, to evil (see entries 3703, 5902, 6050, 7833, 7834).</note>

This is also clear from the meaning of "sons" as truths, or in the opposite sense, <term>falsities<gloss>Wrong or distorted ideas that arise from a bad heart or bad intentions</gloss></term>. In the literal sense, "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the sons" does not mean that children are punished for the sins of their parents, for that would be against Divine law (*Deuteronomy 24:16*). Instead, it means that evil increases in the parents and is then carried over into the children through <term>heredity<gloss>The passing on of physical or mental characteristics genetically from one generation to another</gloss></term>. This results in a continuous buildup of evil over time. However, in the <term>spiritual sense<gloss>The deeper, symbolic meaning that lies beneath the literal text</gloss></term>, "fathers" do not mean human parents but the evils themselves, and "sons" do not mean children but the false ideas produced by those evils. Therefore, these words signify how false ideas are continually generated from underlying evil.

**8877.** *Upon the <term>thirds and upon the fourths<gloss>A biblical idiom indicating a complete or long-lasting series</gloss></term>.* That this signifies a long sequence and the way these things are joined together is evident from the meaning of the number "three." In the Bible, "three" represents something that is full or complete from beginning to end. Therefore, "the third generation of sons" refers to a long series of false ideas. <note>As noted above, "sons" represent these false ideas.</note>

# EXODUS [N. 8879]

...ness; and from the signification of "a thousand," as being very much, and when it is said of the Divine mercy, as being forever (see numbers 2575, 8715).

**8880.** *Of them that love Me.* That this signifies those who receive the good of love, is evident from the meaning of "those who love Jehovah"—that is, the Lord—as being to receive the good of love. For those who love the Lord do not love from themselves, but from the Lord; for all good <term>flows in<gloss>The process of "influx," where spiritual life and qualities move from the Divine into the human mind, like light flowing into a room</gloss></term> from Him. Those who love are those who stop doing evil, because evil stands in the way and rejects the <term>influx<gloss>The constant spiritual energy or "flow" from the Lord into the soul</gloss></term> of good from the Lord. Therefore, when evil has been removed, good is received, which is continually present from the Lord and constantly endeavoring to enter.

**8881.** *And keep My commandments.* That this signifies those who receive the truths of faith, is evident from the meaning of "commandments," as being the truths of faith (see numbers 3382, 8362). That "to keep" these denotes to receive them is because, in order for the truths which are called the "truths of faith" to actually be of faith and to be living within a person, these also must flow in from the Lord. They are indeed learned by the person and stored up in the memory, but so long as the person does not will them, and consequently does not do them, they do not become living. But when they are brought forth from the memory and are introduced through the <term>intellectual<gloss>The part of the mind that handles thought, reasoning, and understanding</gloss></term> into the <term>will<gloss>The part of the mind where our intentions, desires, and love reside</gloss></term>—that is, through the thought into the affection, and then into action—they then become living and are truly "truths of faith." This is accomplished by the Lord when the person stops committing evils (as was said just above in number 8880).

**8882.** *Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain* <note>Original Latin: "in vanum." This phrase can mean "for nothing," "uselessly," or "falsely."</note>. That this signifies <term>profanations<gloss>The act of treating something sacred with irreverence or mixing spiritual truths with worldly evils</gloss></term> and blasphemings of the truth and good of faith, is evident from the meaning of "the name of God," as being all things in their entirety by which the Lord is worshiped, and thus all the truth and good of faith (see numbers 2724, 3006, 6674); and from the meaning of "taking in vain," as being to profane and blaspheme. By "taking the name of God in vain" is properly signified to turn truth into evil—that is, to believe that something is truth and yet to live in evil; and it also denotes to turn good into falsity—that is, to live a holy outward life and yet not to believe. Both are <term>profanations<gloss>The spiritual damage caused when a person knows the truth but lives against it, essentially "taking the name in vain."</gloss></term>.

# EXODUS [N. 8882]

...[prof]anation (number 4601), for believing belongs to the understanding, and living belongs to the will; <note>In this theological framework, the "understanding" is the part of the mind that processes logic and faith, while the "will" is the seat of a person's actual intentions and love.</note> and therefore in those who believe one way but live another, the thought and the will are divided. But as the will continually flows into the understanding—for the understanding is the form <gloss>the outward expression or structure</gloss> of the will, where the will manifests itself in light—it follows that when a person believes one way and lives in another, truth is joined with evil, or good is joined with falsity. In this state, the things of heaven are tangled with the things of hell within the person. This conjunction cannot be dissolved, and the person cannot be healed, except by a "pulling asunder" <note>A term describing a traumatic spiritual separation where the conflicting parts of a person's character are torn apart, often resulting in the loss of spiritual identity.</note> which carries away everything of spiritual life; therefore, such individuals are sent into the most grievous hell of all, where they are direfully tormented. [2] This is what is meant by the words of the Lord in *Matthew*:

> All sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy of the spirit shall not be forgiven unto men. If any one shall say a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him; but he who shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in that which is to come (chapter 12, verses 31, 32).

Also by these words in *Luke*:

> When the unclean spirit hath gone out of a man, he goeth through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he saith, I will return into my house whence I came out. And if on coming he findeth it swept and garnished, he goeth away and taketh seven other spirits worse than himself: and they enter in and dwell there; and the man’s last things become worse than the first (chapter 11, verses 24–26).

[3] These words describe the <term>profanation<gloss>The act of acknowledging a spiritual truth and then living a life that contradicts it, effectively "polluting" what is holy.</gloss></term> of truth from the Lord. The "unclean spirit going out" refers to a person first acknowledging and having faith in the truth; the "house swept" refers to a life lived contrary to those truths; and the "return with seven other spirits" refers to a state of profanation. These are the things signified by "taking the name of God in vain." That such a state cannot be healed—and thus cannot be forgiven—is signified also by the words that immediately follow: "Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that taketh His name in vain," which means it cannot be forgiven. (For further information about the nature of profanation and those who are guilty of it, see numbers 593, 1003, 1008, 1010, 1059.)

# CHAPTER XX. VERSES 2–7

(Cross-references: 1327, 1328, 2051, 2426, 3398, 3399, 3402, 3489, 6348, 6595, 6959, 6963, 6971, 8394.) [4] By “taking the name of God in vain,” the text also signifies **blasphemy**. This occurs when holy things are treated with contempt, or are dragged down to the level of unclean, worldly interests and thus defiled (see numbers 4050, 5390). However, in relation specifically to the ancient Israelite nation—who did not truly recognize the internal goodness or truth of faith (which are what is meant by “the name of God”)—the phrase refers to something else. For them, it meant applying the name of **Jehovah**, <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, often translated as "The LORD."</note> as well as the commandments and laws given to them, to the worship of idols. This is exactly what they did in the wilderness with the worship of the golden calf. They not only offered burnt-offerings and sacrifices to it and ate the food sanctified by those rites, but they even called the day of its celebration “a feast to Jehovah,” as we read in the writings of *Moses*:

> Aaron made of the gold a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it, and made proclamation, and said, To-morrow is a feast to Jehovah. And therefore they rose up in the morning of the next day, and offered burnt-offerings, and brought things eucharistic <note>original: "sacra eucharistica." In this context, these are "peace offerings" or "thank-offerings" expressing gratitude, though the term later became associated specifically with the Christian Lord's Supper.</note> (*Exodus* 32:4–6).

[5] It is clear that those who took the name of Jehovah God in vain in this way could not be forgiven (signified by the statement that they would “not be held guiltless”). This is evident from the words Jehovah spoke to Moses at that time regarding the people:

> Him that hath sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book. Nevertheless go, lead this people in unto the place of which I have spoken unto thee; but in the day of My visitation <note>A biblical term for a time of divine judgment or accounting, where the consequences of one's actions are finally met.</note> I will visit their sin upon them (verses 33 and 34).

**8883.** *For Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that taketh His name in vain.* That this signifies that these things cannot be forgiven is evident from the explanation provided just above (number 8882).

# EXODUS [Number 8884]

...who is in your gates. *For in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; wherefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath day and hallowed it.* "**Remember**" signifies what is perpetual in the thought; "**the sabbath day**" signifies, in the supreme sense, the union of the **Divine Itself** <note>The infinite, unknowable essence of God.</note> and the **Divine Human** <note>God as He is manifested and made perceivable to humanity, specifically in the person of the Lord.</note> of the Lord; in the internal sense, it signifies the conjunction of the Divine Human with the heavens—thus heaven itself—and the marriage of good and truth there. "**To keep it holy**" signifies that it must not be violated in any manner. "**Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work**" signifies the combat <note>Spiritual struggle or temptation.</note> which precedes and prepares a person for this marriage; "**and the seventh day is the sabbath to Jehovah thy God**" signifies good implanted and thus the marriage is achieved. "**Thou shalt not do any work, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, thy manservant, and thy maidservant, and thy beast, and thy sojourner who is in thy gates**" signifies that, in this case, heaven and blessedness are present in each and all things in the **internal and the external of man** <term>Internal and external: The distinction between a person's inner spiritual world and their outer worldly life.</term>. "**For in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea**" signifies the **regeneration** <note>The process of spiritual rebirth.</note> and **vivification** <note>The act of being given spiritual life.</note> of those things which are in the internal and the external man; "**and all that is in them**" signifies all things therein; "**and rested on the seventh day**" signifies that then there is peace and the good of love; "**wherefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath* day**" signifies that then there is the heavenly marriage from the Lord; "**and hallowed it**" signifies that it cannot in any wise be violated.

8885. **Remember.** That this signifies what is perpetual in the thought is evident from the meaning of "remembering" when said of something that must not in any way be forgotten, as being what is perpetual in the thought. That is "perpetual in the thought" which universally reigns there; and that universally reigns with a person which is perpetually in their thought, even when they are meditating on other things or are engaged in business affairs. The thought of a human being involves many things together, for it is the form of many things which have entered the mind successively. When this is the case, love or affection flows from the will into the intellectual ideas also, and by a certain kind of inspiration **vivifies** <note>original: "vivificat" — to give life to or animate.</note> and moves them.

[4] With the good these intellectual ideas make a "one" with the affections which are of the will; but it is otherwise with the evil, for with these the thought and the will do indeed inmostly agree, because the evil which the will wills, the understanding thinks, as **falsity** that is in agreement with this evil; but this agreement does not appear before men in the world, because from their infancy the evil learn to speak differently from what they think, and to act differently from what they will; in a word, they learn to separate their **interior man from their exterior** <term>Interior and exterior man: The distinction between a person's hidden spiritual intentions (interior) and their public, outward behavior (exterior).</term>, and in this latter to form another will and...

### [Number 8885] CHAPTER 20: VERSES 8–11

...also another thought besides that which is in their **interior man** <note>The inner, spiritual part of a person's mind that is open to heaven.</note>, and thus by the **exterior man** <note>The outer, natural part of the mind used for interacting with the world.</note> to counterfeit good that is quite contrary to the interior man—which at the same instant wills evil and also imperceptibly thinks it. But in the other life <note>The spiritual world or the afterlife.</note>, the quality of the interior will and thought is manifest as in clear light, for in that life external things are removed, and internal things are laid bare.

**8886.** *The sabbath day.* That this signifies in the **supreme sense** <note>The highest level of spiritual meaning, relating specifically to the Lord.</note> the union of the **Divine Itself** <term>Divine Itself: The infinite, unmanifested essence of God (traditionally called the Father).</term> and the **Divine Human** <term>Divine Human: The Lord’s glorified humanity, which is the accessible and visible aspect of God.</term> of the Lord; in the internal sense, the conjunction of the Divine Human with the heavens—thus heaven itself—and so the **marriage of good and truth** <term>Marriage of good and truth: The perfect spiritual harmony where what a person understands (truth) is fully united with what they love (good).</term> there, is evident from what was shown before (n. 8495). As such things are signified by "the sabbath," therefore in the **representative church** <note>A religious system, such as that of the ancient Israelites, where physical rituals and objects were designed to mirror and "represent" spiritual realities in heaven.</note> it was most holy, and was that which was to be perpetually in the thought—that is, which was to **reign universally** <note>To be the dominant or underlying influence in all of one’s thoughts and motivations.</note>. (That this makes the life of man, see n. 8853–8858, 8885.) The Israelitish nation did not indeed think about the union of the Divine and the Divine Human of the Lord, nor about His union with heaven, nor about the conjunction of good and truth in heaven, which things were signified by "the sabbath," because they were altogether in **externals without an internal** <note>Focusing entirely on the outward performance of a ritual without any inner spiritual understanding or genuine love.</note>. But they were enjoined to hold the sabbath as most holy, in order that these Divine and heavenly things might be represented in heaven. How the case herein was with them, is plain from what was shown above concerning that nation and the representative of a church therewith (n. 3147, 3479, 3480, 3881, 4208, 4281, 4288, 4289, 4293, 4307, 4444, 4580, 4680, 4825, 4844, 4847, 4899, 4912, 6304, 6306, 7048, 7051, 8301).

**8887.** *To keep it holy.* That this signifies no violation in any manner, is evident from what was commanded concerning the sabbath, as before shown (n. 8495), and from what here follows concerning the **sanctification** <note>The process of making something holy or set apart for God.</note> of the sabbath, namely, "Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work; and the seventh day is the sabbath to **Jehovah** <note>The Hebrew name for God, used here to emphasize His Divine being.</note> thy God; thou shalt not do any work, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy sojourner that is within thy gates; for in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested in the seventh day; wherefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath..."

### [Number 8887] CHAPTER 20: VERSES 8–11

"...day and hallowed it." From these words it is evident that by "keeping the sabbath holy" is signified not to violate it in any manner; but in the **internal sense** <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that relates to the soul and the Lord, rather than just historical facts.</note> that those things which are signified by "the sabbath" are not to be violated in any manner. Specifically, this refers to the union of the **Divine essence** <term>Divine essence: The infinite, innermost nature of God.</term> of the Lord with His **Human essence** <term>Human essence: The human nature the Lord took on in the world, which He eventually made Divine.</term>, as well as the union of this with the heavens, and the resulting conjunction of good and truth within them (see n. 8886). If these things are violated, spiritual life perishes within that person, and their life becomes merely **natural** <note>A state focused only on the physical world and self-interest.</note> and afterward **sensuous** <note>A state where a person believes only what they can see and touch, often leading to a rejection of spiritual truth.</note>; then, falsity is easily learned instead of truth, and evil instead of good, because falsity and evil then hold total power over them.

**8888.** *Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work.* That this signifies the combat which precedes and prepares for this marriage, is evident from the signification of "six days," as being states of combat (that "six" denotes combat, see n. 720, 737, 900; and that "days" denote states, see n. 23, 487, 488, 493, 2788, 4850, 5672, 5962, 6110, 8426); and from the signification of "laboring and doing one's work," as being to do those things which are necessary to life—in this context, those which are necessary to spiritual life, which is the life in heaven. 

[2] Furthermore, by the combat which precedes and prepares for the **heavenly marriage** <term>Heavenly marriage: The state of harmony where a person’s will (love) and understanding (truth) act as one.</term>, is meant spiritual combat or **temptation** <note>Inner struggles where a person's old selfish habits fight against new spiritual values.</note>. Before a person enters into the heavenly marriage—that is, before they are **regenerated** <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or made new by the Lord.</note>—they are in a state of combat against the evils and falsities within themselves. These must be removed before the truth and good that come from the Lord can be received. These evils and falsities are removed by using the truths of faith; through these truths, a person not only learns what "good" actually is, but is also led toward that good. 

This first stage is the state of a person being regenerated, and it is called the state that precedes and prepares for the heavenly marriage. But when the person is finally "in good" <note>Meaning they act from a love for what is right, rather than just following rules.</note> and is led by the Lord through that good, they are then in the heavenly marriage—and thus in heaven, for the heavenly marriage is heaven itself. The first state is what is signified by the "six days" which come before the seventh, and the second state is signified by the "seventh day" (regarding these two states in man, see n. 7923, 8505, 8506, 8510, 8512, 8516, 8539, 8643, 8648, 8658, 8685, 8690, 8701, 8722). 

[3] As by "the sabbath" is signified the heavenly...

...marriage, that is, heaven. Therefore, the Lord’s kingdom in the heavens is called a perpetual Sabbath, signifying a state of unending rest and peace; in that state, the "six days of labor" <note>Symbolizing the period of spiritual struggle and conflict during a person's regeneration.</note> no longer exist.

**8889.** *And the seventh day is the sabbath to Jehovah thy God.* This signifies that goodness has been rooted in the person, resulting in the "marriage." This is evident from the meaning of the **Sabbath** as the **heavenly marriage** <term>Heavenly marriage: The internal union of love (good) and wisdom (truth) within a person, which creates heaven in the soul.</term> (see n. 8886). This represents goodness that is first planted through the learning of truths and is afterward shaped by them. Within a person, "good" does not become truly spiritual until it has been given form by truths. When this formation is complete, the heavenly marriage occurs; this is the conjunction of good and truth, and it is the very essence of heaven within a human being. Because of this, the "seventh day" signifies a holy state. (That a "day" signifies a state of being, see n. 8888; and that the number "seven" signifies what is holy, see n. 395, 433, 716, 881, 5265.)

**8890.** *Thou shalt not do any work, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, thy manservant, and thy maidservant, and thy beast, and thy sojourner who is within thy gates.* This signifies that in this state, heaven and blessedness are present in each and every part of the person—both in their **internal** and **external** <note>The "internal man" refers to the higher, spiritual mind; the "external man" refers to the natural mind and physical life.</note>. This is clear from the meaning of "not doing any work" as rest and peace, which is the state of heaven. When a person is in heaven, they are free from all worry, unrest, and anxiety; in this freedom, they experience true blessedness.

The various members of the household signify all the specific parts of a person's inner and outer life:
*   **"Thou"** signifies the person themselves.
*   **"Son"** signifies the **intellectual** <term>Intellectual: The faculty of the mind that understands and perceives truth.</term> part of the internal man.
*   **"Daughter"** signifies the **will** <term>Will: The faculty of the mind that loves and intends goodness.</term> of the internal man.
*   **"Manservant"** signifies the natural mind in relation to truth.
*   **"Maidservant"** signifies the natural mind in relation to good.
*   **"Beast"** signifies general affection or emotion.

They believe that there were six literal days during which the sky, the earth, the sea, and all living things were created, and finally man in the likeness of God. 

But who, if they take the time to consider the details of the description, cannot see that the creation of the physical universe is not what is meant there? For the things described there are of a nature that can be recognized through common sense as having a deeper meaning.

**8897.** *Honor thy father and thy mother.* That this signifies love for what is **good** <term>Good: In this context, "good" refers to the intentions and desires of the heart that seek the well-being of others.</term> and **truth** <term>Truth: The intellectual concepts or principles that guide a person to do what is good.</term>—and in the highest spiritual sense, love for the Lord and for His kingdom—is clear from the meaning of "honoring." This is because, in the spiritual world, the Lord as Divine Good appears as a Sun, while as Divine Truth He appears as light. This Divine light from the Lord—acting as the Sun—is what enlightens the minds of angels, filling them with intelligence and wisdom, and making them "angels of light." Divine Good is contained within Divine Truth just as heat from the sun is contained within the light during the spring and summer.

**8902.** *You shall not kill.* That this signifies not to take away spiritual life from anyone, and also not to extinguish faith and charity, as well as not to hold the neighbor in hatred, is evident from the meaning of "killing" as being to deprive someone of spiritual life <term>spiritual life: The inner life of the soul, which the author defines as being composed of faith in God and love (charity) toward others.</term>. The reason "killing" means this in the internal sense <term>internal sense: The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that the author believes lies beneath the literal words of the text.</term> is because this sense deals with the life of heaven within a person; and the life of heaven in man is the life of faith and of charity. Therefore, by "not to kill" is also signified not to destroy faith and charity in anyone. 

The reason "not to kill" also means, in the internal sense, not to hold the neighbor in hatred, is that anyone who holds another in hatred continually wishes to kill them. Such a person would indeed kill them in outward act if they were not prevented by the fear of legal penalties, the loss of their own life, the loss of reputation, or similar restraints. For hatred belongs to evil, is the opposite of charity, and breathes nothing but the murder of the one it hates: in this world, the murder of the body; in the other life, the murder of the soul. This is what the Lord meant by these words in *Matthew*:

> You have heard that it was said to those of old time, "You shall not kill; and whoever shall kill shall be in danger of judgment"; but I say to you, that whoever is angry with his brother without cause shall be in danger of judgment; and whoever shall say to his brother, "You worthless one" <note>original: "Raca", an Aramaic term of contempt</note>, shall be in danger of the council; and whoever shall say, "You fool," shall be in danger of the hell <note>original: "Gehenna"</note> of fire (chapter 5, verses 21, 22).

Hatred against the neighbor is meant here by "being angry with the brother without cause," and the degrees of its increase are described by saying "worthless one" and by calling him "a fool." (For more on how anger is a turning away from charity and stems from evil—and thus is hatred—see entries 357, 4164, 5034, 5798, 5887, 5888).

The Law stated:

> They were to measure the distance to the surrounding cities from the person lying pierced in the field. The elders of the nearest city were to take a young cow—a heifer—that had never been worked and had never worn a yoke. They were to bring her down to a valley with a rapid stream, and there the priests, the sons of Levi, were to break the heifer's neck. Then the elders of that city were to wash their hands over the heifer and declare that their hands had not shed that blood and their eyes had not seen the deed, so that the blood might be forgiven (*Deuteronomy xxi. 1–8*).

Who would ever understand why such a procedure was required for someone found killed in a field, unless they understood the **internal sense** <term>Internal sense: The hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal story or "letter" of the text.</term>? One must know what is meant by “one pierced in a field,” the “nearest city,” a “heifer,” a “rapid stream,” and the “washing of hands.” 

In this deeper meaning, “one pierced in the field” signifies that truth and good have been extinguished (n. 4503); the “field” signifies the church itself (n. 2971, 3310, 3766); the “city” signifies the system of teachings or doctrine of truth (n. 402, 2449, 2943, 3216, 4492, 4493); and the “elders of the city” signify truths that are in harmony with what is good (n. 6524, 6525, 8578, 8585).

## 8904.

*Thou shalt not commit adultery.* That this signifies that those things which are of the **doctrine of faith and of charity** <note>This refers to the organized system of religious beliefs (faith) and the active practice of love toward others (charity).</note> are not to be perverted—meaning that the Word is not to be applied to confirm falsities and evils, and that the laws of order are not to be upset—is evident from the **signification** <note>The specific symbolic meaning within the author’s system of interpretation.</note> of “committing adultery,” “debauching,” and “whoredom.” In the spiritual or internal sense, these terms mean to pervert the goods and falsify the truths which belong to the doctrine of faith and charity. 

Because these things are signified by “committing adultery,” it also means to use the Word of God to justify evil actions or false ideas. The Word is the very foundation of faith and charity, and to pervert its truth and goodness is to misapply it to what is false or evil. 

That these things are signified by “committing adultery” and “debauching” in the spiritual sense is known to almost no one today. This is because, within the church, few now understand what the “spiritual” is, or how it differs from the “natural.” Scarcely anyone knows that there is a **correspondence** <note>original: *correspondentia*. A central concept in this text where every natural object or action has a matching spiritual reality or "soul."</note> between the two. This relationship is so close that the image of the spiritual is presented in the natural; the spiritual is like a soul, and the natural is like its body. Through a process called **influx** <note>The flow of spiritual energy or life from the Divine through the spiritual world into the natural world.</note> and their resulting conjunction, they act as one, much like a **regenerate man** <note>A person who has undergone a spiritual rebirth or transformation.</note> whose **internal man** (the spiritual side) and **external man** (the natural side) work together. 

[2] Since these concepts are unknown today, people cannot understand that “committing adultery” means anything more than an unlawful physical union. However, because these deeper meanings are currently a secret, we must explain why “committing adultery” in the spiritual sense signifies the perversion of faith and charity—that is, the adulteration of what is good and the falsification of what is true. 

The reason is that **conjugial love** <term>A specific term (derived from the Latin *conjugialis*) used by the author to describe the holy, spiritual love between spouses that reflects the union of Divine Goodness and Divine Truth.</term> descends from the marriage of good and truth, which is called the **“heavenly marriage.”** <note>The spiritual union where goodness and truth are perfectly joined together.</note> The love that flows in from the Lord, which exists between goodness and truth in heaven, is transformed into marriage love on earth through the law of correspondence. Because of this connection, the falsification of truth is called “whoredom,” and the perversion of good is called “adultera-

Jehovah spoke to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms; because the land is committing great whoredom by turning away from Jehovah" (*Hosea* 1:2). <note>original: "quia scortando scortatur terra de post Jehovam." Woe to the city of bloods! <note>The "city of bloods" refers to a state of mind or a religious community that destroys spiritual life by twisting the Word of God.</note> Because of the many whoredoms of the attractive harlot, the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her whoredoms, and families through her sorceries (*Nahum* 3:1, 4).

[11] Since the falsification of truth and the corruption of good corresponded to "whoredoms" on the earth, the penalty of death was decreed for adulterers (*Leviticus* 20:10). If the daughter of a priest profaned herself by committing whoredom, she was to be burned with fire (*Leviticus* 21:9). Also, no daughter in Israel was to be exposed to whoredom (*Leviticus* 19:29). Likewise, a person of illegitimate birth <note>original: "bastardus." In this spiritual context, it refers to those born of a "marriage" between false principles and evil desires.</note> was not to enter the congregation of Jehovah, not even to the tenth generation (*Deuteronomy* 23:2); and the pay of a harlot was not to be brought into the house of Jehovah, because it is an abomination (*Deuteronomy* 23:18).

[12] From these passages it can now be fully seen what is signified by **"committing adultery."** Specifically:
*   In the **external sense**, it is to commit physical acts of adultery.
*   In the **internal representative sense**, it is to worship idols and other gods by using things that belong to the church; consequently, it refers to both external and internal idolatry.
*   In the **internal spiritual sense**, it signifies the corruption of what is good and the perversion of what is true. 

From all this, it is plainly evident why adultery is considered so wicked and is called an "abomination." It is because it corresponds to the marriage of falsity and evil, which is the **infernal marriage**. On the other hand, genuine marriages are holy because they correspond to the marriage of good and truth, which is the **heavenly marriage**. Indeed, genuine <term>conjugial love</term> <note>From the Latin *amor conjugialis*. A technical term used by Swedenborg to describe a spiritual, holy love between spouses that is distinct from natural or worldly marriage love.</note> descends from the marriage of good and truth, and thus out of heaven—that is, through heaven from the Lord. Conversely, the love of adultery comes from the marriage of falsity and evil—that is, from hell, or the devil.

**8906.** **Thou shalt not steal.** <note>In the numbering system used here, following the Augustinian tradition, "Thou shalt not steal" is considered the seventh commandment, found in Verse 13 of Exodus 20. In many modern Bibles, this is Verse 15.</note> This signifies that no one’s spiritual goods must be taken away from them, and that those things which belong to the Lord must not be claimed as one's own. This is evident from the spiritual meaning of "stealing," which is to take away spiritual goods from anyone. In a spiritual sense, "riches" and "wealth" are the knowledge of what is good and true—specifically, everything belonging to faith and charity <note>In this context, "charity" refers to the active love for one's neighbor, while "faith" is the internal acknowledgement of truth.</note> that constitutes a person's spiritual life. 

Therefore, to take these things away from someone is "to steal" in the spiritual sense. Furthermore, because all spiritual goods—everything of faith and love—come from the Lord alone and not at all from man, "stealing" also refers to the act of a person claiming for themselves what actually belongs to the Lord. Those who do this are called "thieves and robbers" in the Gospel of *John*:

> Truly I say to you, he that enters not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber; but he that enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. I am the door; by Me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out, and find pasture. The thief comes only to steal, and slay, and destroy; I came that they may have life, and may have abundance (John 10:1, 2, 9, 10).

"Entering by the door into the sheepfold" signifies approaching through the Lord, for the Lord is the "door," as He Himself says. The "sheep" represent those who live in love and, consequently, in faith. These people enter through the Lord when they acknowledge that everything regarding faith and love flows from Him. But to attribute these qualities to others, and especially to oneself, is to take them away—to "slay and to destroy." 

Those who claim for themselves what is the Lord’s also believe they earn heaven through their own merit <term>merit in works: the mistaken belief that one's own actions, rather than divine grace, are the cause of salvation</term> and view themselves as the source of their own righteousness (see references n. 1110, 1877, 2027, 2273, 2340, 2373, 2400, 3816, 4007, 4174, 4943, 6388–6390, 6392, 6393, 6478). This, then, is what "stealing" means in the spiritual sense. When a person reads about "stealing" in the Word of God, this is how the angels in heaven understand it, for they perceive the Word only in its spiritual essence. [2] A similar meaning is given to "stealing" in the book of *Hosea*:

### N. 8910] CHAPTER XX. VERSE 14 489

...neighbor’s. This signifies that one must beware of the love of self and of the world, and thus take care lest the evils contained in the preceding commandments become part of the **will** and so come forth into action. This is evident from the meaning of “coveting” (*<term>concupiscere</term>* <note>original: "concupiscere"; a Latin term for strong desire or longing, often used in a theological sense to describe the stirrings of the lower nature.</note>), which is to **will** from an evil love. 

The reason “coveting” has this meaning is because all **concupiscence** <note>The state of desiring or lusting after something; the "breath" of one's underlying love.</note> is a product of some kind of love; for nothing is ever coveted (*<term>concupiscitur</term>* <note>original: "concupiscitur"; the passive form meaning "is coveted."</note>) unless it is first loved. Therefore, concupiscence (or “coveting”) is the continuous extension of love—in this case, of the love of self or of the world—and is, as it were, the very breath of its life. For that which an evil love breathes is called “concupiscence,” but that which a good love breathes is called “desire.” 

Love itself belongs to the other part of the mind, which is called the **will**, for whatever a man loves he wills; but concupiscence belongs to both the **will** and the **understanding**, though it is properly rooted in the **will** as it manifests in the **understanding**. From all this, it is evident why the words, “thou shalt not covet the things that are thy neighbor’s,” signify that one must beware lest these desires become part of the **will**; for the things which become part of the **will** are **appropriated** <note>In this context, to 'appropriate' means that a thought or desire is no longer just passing through the mind, but has been adopted and made a permanent part of the person’s spiritual identity.</note> to the man, because the **will** is the man himself. 

[2] It is believed in the world that **thought** is what makes the man; but there are actually two things which constitute the life of man: the **understanding** and the **will**. To the **understanding** belongs **thought**, and to the **will** belongs the **affection** which comes from love. Thought without the affection of love does not constitute any part of a man’s actual life; rather, it is thought that springs from affection—thus, the **understanding** acting from the **will**. 

That these two are distinct from each other is plain to every one who reflects on the fact that a man can **understand** and perceive something to be evil even while he **wills** it, and can perceive something to be good which he either **wills** or does not **will**. From this it is clear that the **will** is the man himself, but not the **thought**, except in so far as something from the **will** passes into it. Hence it is that the things which enter into the thought of man, but do not pass through the thought into the **will**, do not **defile** <note>To 'defile' here means to spiritually corrupt or stain the person's character and eternal state.</note> him; only the things which enter through the thought into the **will** do so. These things defile him because they are then **appropriated** to him and become his own; for the **will**, as already said, is the man himself. The things which become part of the **will** are said to “enter into his heart” and to come...

It distinguishes between the understanding (thought) and the will (affection), arguing that a person is defined spiritually by what they will rather than what they merely think.</summary>

[3] From these words, as from all His other words, it can be seen of what nature was the Lord's speech, namely, that internal and spiritual things were meant, but that they were expressed by external or natural things, and this according to <term>correspondences</term> <note>A spiritual law where natural things in the world or the body represent and mirror deeper realities of the mind or soul.</note>; for the mouth corresponds to the thought, as also all things that belong to the mouth, as the lips, the tongue, the throat; and the heart corresponds to the affection which is of love, thus to the **will** (that there is a correspondence of the heart with these, see n. 2930, 3313, 3883–3896, 7542).

From this it is plain what is signified by, “whatsoever entereth into the mouth goeth into the belly and is cast out into the draught,” namely, that evil and falsity are injected into the thought of man from hell, and are sent back again thither. 

These things cannot defile the man, because they are sent back; for a man cannot stand apart from thinking evil, but from doing it. But so soon as he receives evil from the thought into the **will**, it then does not go out of him, but enters into him, and this is called “coming forth out of the heart.” The things which come forth thence defile him, because what a man **wills** goes forth into speech and into act, in so far as external bonds, which are fear of the law, of the loss of reputation, of honor, of gain, and of life, do not forbid. From all this it is now evident that by “thou shalt not covet” is signified—

That by "not coveting those things which are the neighbor's" is signified that one must beware of the love of self and of the world, is because all the evils of concupiscence spring from these loves as from their fountains (see n. 2045, 7178, 7255, 7366–7377, 7488, 8318, 8678).

**8911.** From what has been thus far said it can be seen how the case is with man and his life, namely, that man is such as his will is, and that he remains such after death, because death is not the end of life, but its continuation. As therefore man is such as his will is, because, as before said, the will is the man himself, therefore "to be judged according to his deeds" signifies to be judged according to his will, for will and deed are not at variance, the deed being in the will and the will in the deed, provided external bonds do not hinder, such as fears of the law, of the loss of honor, of gain, of reputation, and of life. This is circumstanced like <term>endeavor</term> <note>original: *conatus*. In 18th-century physics, this refers to the internal force or pressure that exists before actual movement occurs.</note> and <term>motion</term> <note>original: *motus*. The outward physical movement resulting from an internal force.</note>. Motion is nothing else than continuous endeavor; for when endeavor ceases, motion ceases, and therefore there is nothing essential in motion except endeavor. The learned know this, for it is an acknowledged and confirmed <term>theorem</term> <note>A reference to the principles of mechanics where action is viewed as the result of a continuous internal pressure or potential.</note>. Endeavor in man is will, and motion in him is action; they are so called in man because in him endeavor and motion are living. To be judged according to the will is the same thing as to be judged according to the love, and also the same as to be judged according to...
