**8911.** <term>the ends of life</term> <note>The "ends" of life refer to the ultimate purposes or motives that drive a person’s behavior; in this theology, your primary motivation determines your spiritual destination.</note>, likewise to be judged according to the life, for the will of man is his <term>love</term>, and is his <term>end of life</term>, and is his very life itself. That this is the case is evident from the words of the Lord quoted above, that “whoever looketh on a strange woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart” (*Matthew 5:27, 28*); also that “to kill” a man is not only to do so in act, but also to will to do it, which is signified by “being angry” with him and treating him with insult (*Matthew 5:21*). Moreover man is judged according to his deeds, but no further than in so far and in such a manner as his <term>deeds</term> have proceeded from his will.

**8912.** It must also be explained briefly what is meant in the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The "internal sense" refers to the spiritual or symbolic meaning that the author believes lies beneath the literal text of the Bible.</note> by the things here mentioned, namely, “<term>house</term>,” “<term>wife</term>,” “<term>manservant</term>,” “<term>maidservant</term>,” “<term>ox</term>,” and “<term>ass</term>,” which are not to be coveted. They are all the <term>goods</term> and <term>truths of faith</term> in one complex, which are not to be taken away from any one, and to which no injury is to be done; and they are the same things which in the <term>internal sense</term> are signified by “keeping the <term>sabbath day</term> holy,” “<term>honoring father and mother</term>,” “<term>not killing</term>,” “<term>not committing adultery</term>,” “<term>not stealing</term>,” “<term>not bearing false witness</term>,” all which things have been shown above to be in the <term>internal sense</term> such as are of <term>love</term> and <term>faith</term>. 

By “house” is meant all good in general; by “wife,” all <term>truth</term> in general; by “manservant,” the <term>affection of spiritual truth</term>; by “maidservant,” the <term>affection of spiritual good</term>; by “ox,” the <term>affection of natural good</term>; and by “ass,” the <term>affection of natural truth</term>. <note>In this system of "correspondences," natural objects represent spiritual states: for example, a "manservant" represents a part of the mind that serves higher spiritual truths, while an "ox" represents good intentions in our everyday, natural life.</note> These are the things which are “not to be coveted,” that is, which are not to be taken away from any one, or to which harm must not be done. That these things are meant in the <term>internal sense</term>, is because the Word <note>The "Word" is a common term for the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> in this sense is for those who are in <term>heaven</term>, for those who are there do not perceive the Word naturally, but spiritually, thus not house, nor wife, nor manservant, nor maidservant, nor ox, nor ass, but the spiritual things that correspond to them, which are the goods of love and the truths of faith. In a word, the external sense or the sense of the letter is for those who are in the <term>world</term>, but the internal sense is for those who are in heaven, and also for those who are in the world, yet in so far as they are at the same time in <term>charity</term> and faith.

**8913.** **Verses 15–17.** *And all the people saw the voices, and the torches, and the voice of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and the people saw, and they quaked, and stood afar off. “And all the people saw the voices, and the torches,” signifies the perception of <term>truths Divine</term> <note>In this context, "Divine truths" are the laws and realities of the spiritual world as communicated by God.</note> from <term>good</term> <note>In Swedenborg's writing, "good" refers to the impulse of love and charity that gives life to truth.</note>; “and the voice of the trumpet,” signifies the same things through heaven; “and the mountain smoking,” signifies the good itself of truth not perceptible except in its external form; “and the people saw, and they quaked,” signifies the tremor <note>A spiritual shaking or profound awe.</note> which occurs when these things are received; “and they stood afar off,” signifies being remote from internal things; “and they said unto Moses,” signifies a complaint; “Speak thou with us,” signifies the reception of truth in an <term>accommodated form</term> <note>An "accommodated form" is a version of truth that is "stepped down" or simplified so that human beings can understand and accept it without being overwhelmed by its pure brilliance.</note>, which they would then be able to obey; “and let not God speak with us,” signifies truth in a form that is not accommodated; “lest perchance we die,” signifies that in such a case, the life of heaven within them would perish; “and Moses said unto the people,” signifies information; “Fear not, because God has come to tempt you,” signifies that the life of heaven will not perish, but rather this experience occurs so that it may be known that this life exists, and what its quality is; “and that the fear of Him may be before your faces, that ye sin not,” signifies a holy fear of the Divine arising from this, and the resulting preservation of spiritual life.

**8914.** *And all the people saw the voices, and the torches.* That this signifies the perception of truths Divine from good, is evident from the signification of “seeing,” as being to understand and perceive (see section numbers 2150, 2325, 2807, 3764, 3863, 3869, 4403–4421, 4567, 4723, 5400); from the signification of “voices” <note>original: "voces," often used in the Latin Bible to denote thunderings.</note> or thunderings, as being truths Divine (n. 7573, 8813); and from the signification of “torches” <note>original: "lampades," referring here to the flashes of lightning accompanying the thunder.</note> or lightnings, as being the brightness which truths have from the good of love, and which strike through and penetrate the mind (see n. 8813). [2] By "truths Divine from good" are here meant all the commandments of the <term>decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, which were pronounced from Mount Sinai out of the midst of thunderings and lightnings; these being then displayed as the people watched.

For a person's internal self is in the light of heaven, and their external self is in the light of the world; or what is the same, a person's soul or spirit is in heaven, but their body is in the world. Heaven is closer to the Divine than the world is, because in heaven the Divine of the Lord reigns and is the all in all. Regarding the meaning of "afar off," it should be known that in the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>A way of interpreting reality where physical concepts like time and space represent internal states of mind and spirit.</note>, "afar off" has no reference to physical space, but rather to the Divine—thus, to what is good and true. The <term>good</term> <note>In this context, "good" refers to the selfless love and benevolence that flows from God.</note> itself which proceeds from the <term>Divine</term> <note>The nature or essence of God.</note>, causes the appearance of distance in heaven. The angelic societies there appear distinct and even remote from one another; but as already said this idea of space comes from distance from the good and truth which are from the Divine of the Lord. This must needs appear a paradox, nay, absurd, to many in the world. The reason is that the thoughts and their ideas with man are founded upon spaces and times, insomuch that man cannot think without them. 

Consequently if you abstract times and spaces from a man’s thought, he scarcely perceives anything. Nevertheless the angels in heaven think absolutely without any idea of time and space, and with such fulness that in intelligence and wisdom their thoughts surpass the thoughts of man thousands, nay, myriads of times; and, wonderful to say, if there occurs to them an idea derived from time and space, shade and thick darkness at once come to their minds, because they then fall from the light of heaven into the light of nature, which to them is thick darkness.

By "Abraham" is not meant the historical figure of Abraham, for he is not known individually in heaven; rather, in the highest sense, he represents the **Lord** <note>In this text, "the Lord" specifically refers to God as the Divine Human.</note>, and in a relative sense, he represents those in heaven who live in the <term>good of love</term> <note>Actions and intentions motivated by selfless love.</note> and faith in the Lord (references: n. 1834, 1876, 1965, 1989, 2011, 3245, 3305, 6098, 6185, 6276, 6894). 

Those who are in hell are said to "see those in heaven from afar," because they exist in a state most distant from what is good and true. The "**great gulf**" described between them signifies this very distance from goodness, which creates the spiritual appearance of a dividing chasm. 

[4] People who think only in terms of physical space—as everyone does while living in the world—perceive hell and heaven as being physically distant from humanity. But the reality is different. Hell and heaven are near to us—in fact, they are *within* us: hell is within an evil person, and heaven is within a good person. Furthermore, after death, every person enters that hell or heaven in which they have already lived while in the world. However, their state then changes; the hell that was not felt in the world becomes perceptible, and the heaven that was not felt in the world becomes perceptible. One becomes a heaven full of all happiness, and the other a hell of all unhappiness. That heaven is within us is what the Lord teaches in the Gospel of *Luke*:

> The kingdom of God is within you (xvii. 21).

The concept of being "afar off" <note>original: "a longinquo"</note> as a symbol of spiritual distance is also seen in the following passages:

> They come from a land afar off, from the extremity of the heavens (*Isaiah* xiii. 5; also *Jeremiah* v. 15).
> 
> Hear, you that are far off, what I have done; and you that are near, acknowledge My might (*Isaiah* xxxiii. 13).
> 
> I will say to the north, Give; and to the south, Keep not back; bring My sons from far, and My daughters from the extremity of the earth. Bring forth the blind people that have eyes, and the deaf that have ears (*Isaiah* xliii. 6, 8; also xlix. 12).
> 
> Attend, O isles <note>In biblical symbolism, "isles" often refer to people who are far from the central teachings of the church but are still open to truth.</note>, unto Me; hearken, you peoples, from far (*Isaiah* xlix. 1; also *Jeremiah* xxxi. 10).
> 
> The voice of the cry of the daughter of My people from a land afar off: Is not Jehovah in Zion? Is not her King in her? (*Jeremiah* viii. 19).
> 
> Jehovah, Thou hast planted them, and they have also taken root. But Thou art near in their mouth, but far off from their <term>reins</term> <note>The "reins" or kidneys were anciently believed to be the seat of the deepest emotions and secret intentions; thus, being "far from the reins" means God is not in their true intentions.</note> (*Jeremiah* xii. 2).
> 
> Am I a God near, and not a God afar off? (*Jeremiah* xxiii. 23).

In all these passages, being "afar off" signifies a spiritual remoteness from what is good.

# CHAPTER XX. VERS. 15-17
<note>While the header indicates verses 15-17, the commentary here specifically addresses verse 19: "And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die."</note>

**8920.** *Speak thou with us, and we will hear.* This signifies the reception of truth in an **accommodated form** <note>Truth that has been "stepped down" or modified so that it can be grasped by a finite mind without causing spiritual overwhelm.</note> which the people could then obey. This is evident from the symbolic meaning of "speaking," which represents <term>influx</term> <note>The process of spiritual energy, life, or thought flowing from a higher level (the Divine) to a lower level (the human mind).</note> and communication (references: n. 2951, 3060, 4131, 5481, 5797, 6228, 7270, 8128). Consequently, it also represents "reception," for that which flows in and is communicated must be received.

This is further shown by the role of **Moses**, who was to speak. In this context, Moses represents truth from the Divine as it exists beneath heaven, joined with the <term>Divine Truth</term> that is within heaven. He acts as a mediator between the Lord and the people (references: n. 8760, 8787, 8805). Therefore, "Moses" here specifically denotes truth presented in an **accommodated form**.

[2] Regarding **truth in an accommodated form**, it must be understood that when Divine Truth descends through the heavens to humanity—as <term>the Word</term> <note>Referring here to the Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> has descended—it is adapted along the way for everyone, both for those in the heavens and those on the earth. However, Divine Truth exists in a completely different form in the heavens than it does in the world. In the heavens, it exists as the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Word that exists beneath the literal stories and history.</note> of the Word; in the world, it exists as the sense of the letter.

Indeed, even within the heavens themselves, it takes diverse forms: one form in the inmost (third) heaven, another in the middle (second) heaven, and still another in the lowest (ultimate) heaven. The form of Divine Truth—that is, the way it is perceived, thought about, and spoken—in the third heaven is so high that it cannot even be understood in the second heaven. It is so Divine and exalted that it contains countless things that cannot be expressed in the middle heaven; it consists purely of changes in state regarding the **affections of love**. 

In the same way, the form of Divine Truth in the middle heaven transcends the form in the lowest heaven, and it transcends the form of Divine Truth in our world even more significantly. This is why the things spoken in those higher heavens are such as "no human mind has ever perceived, nor any ear heard," as those who have been raised into heaven know from their own experience.

[3] Those who are unaware of this believe that people in the heavens think and speak no differently than they do on earth. They believe this only because they do not realize that the internal parts of a human being are in a much more exalted state than the external parts. The thought and speech of those in the heavens is **celestial** and **spirit-**

**8921.** *And let not God speak with us.* That this signifies truth in a form not accommodated, is evident from what precedes; for by “Moses” is signified truth Divine beneath heaven conjoined with truth Divine in heaven, thus mediating between the Lord and the people, consequently truth Divine in an **accommodated form** (as just shown above, n. 8920). 

Consequently by “Let not God speak with us,” is signified truth Divine in a form not accommodated; for by “God” is here meant the Lord as to **Divine truth** in heaven (n. 8805), consequently the Divine truth itself; which is also the reason why it is said “God,” and not “Jehovah;” for in the Word where “God” <note>original: "Deus"</note> is named, the Lord as to **Divine truth** is meant; but where “Jehovah” is named the Lord as to <term>Divine good</term> <note>The aspect of the Divine that relates to love, mercy, and the will, whereas "Truth" relates to wisdom and the intellect.</note> is meant (references: n. 2586, 2769, 2807, 2822, 3921, 4295, 4402, 7091, 7268, 7873, 8301, 8867).

# CHAPTER XX. VERS. 15-17
<note>While the header lists verses 15-17, the text here continues the explanation of verse 19 and begins explaining verse 20: "And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you."</note>

**8922.** The meaning of “dying” is to die spiritually <note>original: "mori"</note> (see n. 6119), which is to perish in regard to the life of heaven. It is clear from what was shown just above (n. 8920) that Divine Truth has this effect when it is not "accommodated" <note>By "accommodated," the author means Divine Truth that has been "stepped down" or simplified so that human beings can understand it without being overwhelmed by its pure, brilliant intensity.</note>. This is because Truth in its unadapted form—as it exists in heaven—is far beyond human understanding. Anything that transcends our reach cannot be received; what is not received cannot flow into our faith or our living; and without faith and a life guided by it, the "life of heaven" cannot exist within us. A person is "regenerated"—meaning they receive this heavenly life—through the Divine Truth that belongs to faith (n. 2046, 2063, 2189, 2979, 3155, 3876, 3877, 5893, 5912, 6247, 8635–8640, 8772).

**8923.** **And Moses said unto the people.** This signifies information being provided. This is evident from the meaning of "saying" in this context. When Moses speaks to the people here, he is providing information to address their complaints and fears. Similarly, in other parts of the Scripture, "saying" signifies the act of informing when it answers a specific inquiry (see n. 7769, 7793, 7825, 8041).

**8924.** **Fear not, because God is come to tempt you.** This signifies that the life of heaven will not perish. Rather, this experience happens so that the people may recognize that heavenly life exists and understand its nature. We know this because "not fearing" (specifically, not fearing they would die) means they will not perish in regard to the life of heaven (see n. 8922). 

Furthermore, "to tempt you" <note>In this context, the word "tempt" does not mean to entice someone to do evil, but rather to "test" or "prove" them, much like a metal is tested in a fire.</note> signifies teaching about the existence and quality of heavenly life. This is the purpose of <term>spiritual temptation</term> <note>These are internal struggles or trials where a person's faith is tested by difficult circumstances or doubts, leading to a deeper, more rooted spiritual life.</note>: it teaches and confirms these spiritual realities within a person. Temptations are intended to plant and root the faith and affection for truth—and eventually the affection for what is good—so that the person may receive new life. 

[2] In essence, temptations are battles against evils and falsities. When a person overcomes these, they are strengthened, because they have fought using truths to defend what is right. At the moment of the struggle, a person might not feel they are using "truths," because those truths are tucked away in the deeper parts of the mind <note>original: "interiora"</note> and are not immediately obvious to the outward senses; but the fact that they are fighting for what is right proves those truths are present.

<summary>This page explains that spiritual "death" occurs when Divine Truth is not adapted to human understanding and defines "temptation" as a necessary spiritual trial that strengthens faith rather than a threat to heavenly life.</summary>

<keywords>spiritual death, Divine Truth, accommodation, Moses, spiritual temptation, trials, regeneration, faith, Exodus 20:20</keywords>

**"And the people stood afar off"** signifies a state of being distant from internal truths <note>Internal truths refer to the deeper spiritual meanings that lie beneath the literal surface of the scriptures.</note>; **"and Moses came near unto the thick darkness where God was"** signifies the ongoing connection between the truth of spiritual good and Divine truth; **"and Jehovah said unto Moses"** signifies further instruction; **"Thus shalt thou say unto the sons of Israel"** signifies those who belong to the spiritual church <note>The "spiritual church" refers to people who are guided primarily by their conscience and their understanding of what is true and right.</note>; **"Ye have seen that I have spoken with you from heaven"** signifies that everything in the Word <note>The Word refers here to the Holy Scriptures as a vehicle for Divine communication.</note> comes by means of influx <note>Influx is the spiritual process where life and wisdom flow from the Divine into the human mind.</note> from the Divine through heaven; **"ye shall not make with Me gods of silver and gods of gold"** signifies that they should completely stay away from things that look true and good on the outside but are actually false and evil on the inside; **"ye shall not make unto you"** signifies that they must be carefully on their guard.

**8927.** *And the people stood afar off.* That this signifies a distance from internal truths is evident from the meaning of "standing afar off," which represents being remote from internal things (as discussed previously in section 8918).

**8928.** *And Moses came near unto the thick darkness where God was.* That this signifies the ongoing connection of the truth of spiritual good with Divine truth is evident from the representation of Moses. This is essentially the "truth of spiritual good," because this is the level of Divine truth where the spiritual church—represented by the sons of Israel—exists. Moses represents this truth as the leader of that church (section 7041). This is also evident from the meaning of "coming near," which signifies conjunction <note>Conjunction refers to a spiritual bonding or connection.</note>, for to draw near to the Divine is to be joined with it.

### EXODUS

**8928.** <note>original: "n. 8928"</note> ...therewith; and from the signification of **"thick darkness,"** as being Divine truth <term>Divine truth: In this context, the wisdom and laws originating from God.</term> relative to those who belong to the spiritual church, and also relative to that people whom Moses led. 

The reason that Divine truth appears as **thick darkness** to that church and those people is because they do not possess internal light regarding spiritual matters. 

[2] To begin with, those belonging to the spiritual church believe they are in the light; however, they are actually in obscurity—even in thick darkness—regarding Divine truth. This is evident because they do not recognize truth through any <term>internal perception: A direct, intuitive awareness of spiritual truth granted to the heart and mind.</term>. Instead, they simply believe what the church teaches because the church says it is so. They confirm these teachings to themselves regardless of whether they are actually true or false. Anyone who lacks this internal perception of Divine truth is in "thick darkness," or, to put it another way, Divine truth remains a mystery—darkness—to them. 

For example, those in the spiritual church do not know, nor do they care to know, that the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> has an internal, spiritual sense. Even if they did believe it, that belief would come from being persuaded by others, rather than from their own internal sight.

[3] To take another example: those in the spiritual church often claim that faith is the only requirement for salvation, even without <term>charity: Active love and good-heartedness toward others.</term> and its good works. They believe this simply because it is the church’s doctrine. They do not reach a state of perception clear enough to see that faith cannot exist without charity, and that the two belong together like a **consort to a consort** <note>Meaning a husband and wife; a balanced partnership where one cannot function without the other.</note>. Consequently, they fail to see that charity is the essential heart of the church because it is rooted in what is "good." 

From this, it is clear how much obscurity, or **thick darkness**, the spiritual church resides in. Because they are in this darkness, they divide the church into as many different "churches" as there are different opinions on the "truths of faith." They would not do this if they were in the light. 

Anyone who is in the light never doubts—much less denies—that love for the Lord and charity toward one’s neighbor are the essentials of the church. All the truths of the Word, and therefore all the truths of faith, are based upon these two principles. The same applies to all other truths that depend on these. 

(These points have been explained more fully in other sections: 2708, 2715, 2831, 2849, 2935, 2937, 3241, 3246, 6289, 6427, 6865, 6945, 7233.)

...those of the spiritual church do not reach even the first threshold of wisdom, or the first ray of light, which is enjoyed by those in the celestial church <term>celestial church: A state of the church or an individual where faith is grounded in direct love for the Lord and intuitive perception of truth.</term> <note>original: "see n. 2718, 3833, 6500"</note>.

This is why, to them, the Divine appeared as **thick darkness**. 

It is well known that the Divine is never in darkness, but in light—for the Divine is light itself. Therefore, when God is called "**thick darkness**," it is only in relation to those who possess no spiritual light. To such people, Divine truths appear as darkness because they do not believe them and even deny them. The Divine appears to every person according to the quality of their life and faith; it appears as light to those in the light, and as **thick darkness** to those in **thick darkness**.

# EXODUS

...of Israel <note>see paragraph number 8930</note>, as being Divine Truth, or the Word from the Divine through heaven; for that which Jehovah speaks is Divine Truth, and thus constitutes the Word which exists in the church; and what He speaks passes through heaven. 

[2] It should be understood that heaven is not located in any specific or fixed place—it is not "on high" in the way people commonly think. Instead, heaven exists wherever the Divine is. It is present with every person and within every person who lives in **charity** and **faith**; for these two qualities *are* heaven, because they come from the Divine, and that is where the angels dwell. That heaven is where the Divine is (that is, where the Lord is) can be seen from the fact that Mount Sinai, from which the Lord spoke, is called "heaven" here. This is also why "Mount Sinai" symbolizes the heaven from which Divine Truth originates <note>see n. 8805</note>. 

[3] The reason why "all things of the Word" are signified here is that Jehovah (the Lord) then began to reveal the Word which would provide the human race with doctrine and a way of life—first through Moses, and later through the prophets. In order for people to know that the Word came from the Divine through heaven, the Lord Himself chose to descend and, with a living voice, proclaim the **ten commandments**. In doing so, He showed that everything that follows in the law—that is, in the Word—likewise comes by means of <term>influx: The spiritual process of life or truth flowing from a higher, Divine source into a lower, worldly one.</term> from the Divine through heaven.

**8932.** *Ye shall not make with Me gods of silver and gods of gold.* 

This signifies that they should wholly abstain from things that appear to be true and good in their external form, but are actually false and evil in their internal form. This is evident from:
*   The meaning of "making gods," which is to worship (since someone only makes gods for the sake of worship).
*   The meaning of "silver," which represents truth, and in its opposite sense, falsehood.
*   The meaning of "gold," which represents goodness, and in its opposite sense, evil <note>original references: "see n. 113, 1551, 1552, 2954, 5658, 6914, 6917, 7999"</note>.

The reason this refers to things that *appear* true and good externally but are false and evil internally is because the text says, "Ye shall not make them **with Me**"—that is, alongside Jehovah God. Divine Truth itself and Divine Good itself exist within the "internals" (the inner spirit) and also within the "externals" (the outer form). However, in the external form, Divine Truth and Good are presented as <term>representative types: Objects or actions in the physical world that serve as symbols for spiritual realities.</term>; for these external things in a "type" point toward and represent...

# CHAPTER XX. VERSES 18-20

...internal things. External things are false and evil whenever they are separated from internal things yet still treated as holy or worshiped. Even so, they may still look like things that are true and good because they <term>represent: To serve as an outward, physical sign or symbol of a deeper spiritual reality.</term> what is truly good and true. These concepts are signified by the phrase "making with Jehovah God gods of silver and gods of gold." 

[2] This commandment follows immediately after the ten commandments for the reason that the Israelitish and Jewish people were of such a character that they viewed external rituals as holy—and worshiped them as entirely Divine—while those rituals were separated from any internal meaning <note>The author provides numerous cross-references to earlier parts of this work (n. 3479, 3769, 4281, 4293, 4307, 4314, 4316, 4433, 4680, 4825, 4832, 4844, 4847, 4865, 4903, 6304, 6832, 8814, 8819) to illustrate the spiritual state of the ancient Israelites.</note>. 

To better understand the nature of things that appear true and good on the outside but are false and evil on the inside, let us look at the rituals of the Jewish Church as an example—such as sacrifices, the burning of incense, ceremonial washings, and many others. In their outward form, these were true and good, not because of the physical acts themselves, but because they were <term>types: Historical or physical symbols that point toward a future or spiritual reality.</term> that referred to internal truths and goods, which are matters of love and faith in the Lord. When such things were regarded as holy only for their outward form, and especially when they were worshiped—as they were by the Jews and Israelites when they turned to <term>idolatry: The worship of physical objects or images as gods.</term> and applied these rituals to the worship of foreign gods—they no longer contained any of the spiritual truth or goodness they were meant to represent. Only the appearance remained, because internally they had become falsities and evils. 

[3] The situation was the same for all the other things that served as symbolic representations of heavenly and Divine things for that people. As soon as those external things were used to worship other gods, they became idols or "gods of silver and of gold" which they made alongside Jehovah God; for at that point, they looked true and good on the outside, but were false and evil on the inside. 

[4] In a general sense, "gods of silver and of gold" denote all the false ideas and the resulting evils of worship that are made to look like truth and goodness through the wrong application and interpretation of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or Divine revelation.</note>, and through reasoning based on one's own intelligence. These things are signified by "the gods of silver and of gold" in the following passages. In *Isaiah:*—

# EXODUS

### [Section 8932 continued]

> In that day a man shall cast forth his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made for themselves to bow down to, to the moles and to the bats; to enter into the clefts of the rocks, and into the clefts of the crags (Isaiah 2:20, 21);

In this passage, "moles and bats" signify those who live in spiritual darkness—that is, those who dwell in false beliefs and the harmful behaviors that result from them. 

[5] Again in the book of *Isaiah*: —

> In that day they shall cast away every man his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your hands have made for you, a sin (Isaiah 31:7);

The phrase "which the hands have made" refers to things that originate from <term>self-intelligence: The human tendency to rely on one's own ego and limited reasoning rather than divine revelation.</term>. Again: —

> The craftsman casteth a graven image, and the caster overlayeth it with gold, and casteth silver chains (*Isaiah 40:19*);

"Graven images" symbolize things that come from a person's <term>own: Known in the original Latin as "proprium," referring to the self-centered nature of a human being.</term> (see section 8869). "To overlay with gold" means to give these self-made ideas an appearance of being "good" in their outward form. "Casting silver chains" means making these ideas stick together so they seem logically connected to truths. (Recall that "gold" symbolizes spiritual good, and "silver" symbolizes spiritual truth, as noted in previous citations.) 

[6] In a similar way, it is written in *Jeremiah*: —

> The statutes of the nations are vanity: surely he cutteth out wood from the forest, the work of the hands of the workman. He decketh it with gold and with silver; they fasten them with nails and with hammers, that it sway not to and fro (Jeremiah 10:3, 4).

And in *Hosea*: —

> The Ephraimites sin more and more, and make them a molten image of silver, idols in their intelligence, all the work of the craftsmen (Hosea 13:2);

In the spiritual language of the Bible, "Ephraim" represents the <term>intellectual of the church: The faculty within the church or the individual that understands and processes spiritual truth.</term> (see sections 5354, 6222, 6234, 6238, 6267). A "molten image of silver" represents a falsehood that is made to look like the truth, which is why the text specifies it is made "in their intelligence." The phrase "all the work of the craftsmen" signifies that these beliefs are entirely constructed through reasoning based on the self. 

[7] In *Habakkuk*: —

> Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, This shall teach. Behold this is fixed with gold and silver, but there is no breath in the midst of it (Habakkuk 2:19);

Here, "wood" symbolizes evil and "stone" symbolizes falsity. To be "fixed with gold and silver" means these errors are given an appearance of being good and true by misapplying religious concepts. 

Finally, in *Daniel*: —

It is inwardly profane due to self-love but outwardly holy because it uses the Word to justify its actions.

The second religiosity is one where the <term>light of nature: Human reason and sensory evidence relied upon without spiritual insight</term> is everything. People in this group do not acknowledge anything as truth unless they can understand it through their own intellect. Some in this group may accept the Word, but they only use it for confirmation, making it a "servant" to their own ideas. Others reject the Word entirely; they believe the Divine is simply nature itself. Because their "light" is only natural, it remains trapped in nature and cannot be enlightened by the light of heaven, as they reject the Word—the only source of such enlightenment. In these passages, "hewn stone" denotes those matters of faith that are derived from self-intelligence. 

**[5]** Because "hewn stone" carries this meaning, the altar first built in the land of Canaan by the sons of Israel after they had passed over the Jordan was built of unhewn stones. This is because the passage over the Jordan River represented the transition into the kingdom of the Lord, a transition that is achieved through the genuine truths of faith. Regarding this altar, it is written in the book of *Joshua*:

> Joshua built an altar unto Jehovah the God of Israel in Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded the sons of Israel, an altar of whole stones, upon which no man had moved iron (*Joshua 8:30, 31; also Deuteronomy 27:1–8*).

**[6]** In a similar way, the temple of Jerusalem was built of whole, unhewn stones, as described in the first book of *Kings*:

> As to the house itself, when it was in building, it was built of whole stone, as it was brought; for there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tools of iron heard in the house, while it was in building (*1 Kings 6:7*).

This is because the temple of the Lord represented the Lord in His aspect as Divine Truth. That the Lord was represented by the temple...

### [N. 8949] THE SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF SATURN

**8949.** In worship they are very humble; for therein they account themselves as nothing. They worship our Lord, and acknowledge Him as the One Only God. For the Lord sometimes appears to those who are on that earth in an angelic form, and thus as a man; and then the **Divine** <term>Divine: The essential nature of God, characterized by infinite love and wisdom, which radiates as spiritual light.</term> beams forth from the face and affects their mind. Moreover when the inhabitants become of age, they speak with spirits, by whom they are instructed concerning the Lord, and how He is to be worshiped, also how they ought to live.

**8950.** When any wish to lead astray the spirits of that earth, and draw them away from faith in the Lord, or from humility toward Him, and from uprightness of life, they say that they wish to die. Then little knives are seen in their hands, by which they seem to wish to pierce their breasts. When they are asked why they do so, they say that they would rather die than be led away from the Lord. Sometimes the spirits of our earth <note>The author frequently contrasts spirits from different planets; those from Earth are often described as being more attached to physical sciences and external reasoning compared to the more internal focus of Saturnian spirits.</note> laugh at these things, and infest them with questionings why they do so. But they answer that they know very well that they are not going to kill themselves, and that this is only an **appearance** <term>appearance: In the spiritual world, thoughts and intentions are often visibly represented by symbolic objects or actions.</term> proceeding from the will of their mind, showing that they would rather die than be drawn away from the worship of the Lord.

**8951.** There are some also on that earth who call their light at night, which is great, the Lord; but these are separated from the rest, and are not tolerated among them. This nocturnal light is shed from the great belt which encompasses that earth at a distance, and from the moons which are called the satellites of Saturn.

**8952.** They were asked about that great belt <note>This refers to the rings of Saturn, which were a subject of great scientific and theological interest during the 18th century.</note>, which appears from our earth to be elevated above the horizon of that planet, and to vary its positions. <header>EXODUS [N. 8953]</header>

Whatever is of the **spiritual sense** <term>spiritual sense: The inner, heavenly meaning of sacred texts or reality that relates to the soul and the afterlife.</term> is in heaven; but whatever is of the **natural sense** <term>natural sense: The literal or physical meaning of things as perceived by the five senses on earth.</term> is beneath heaven.

**8954.** There are no cities there, nor kingdoms, but they live distinguished into families, each family apart from others; thus, husband and wife together with their children. **8955.** Everyone on that earth, unlike those on ours, knows that they shall live after death; and therefore they make no account of their bodies, except in so far as may be necessary for life—which they say is to remain and serve the Lord. For this reason, they do not bury the bodies of the dead, but cast them forth and cover them with branches of trees from the forest.

**8956.** They also have little concern about food and clothing. They live on fruits and vegetables of various kinds which their earth produces. And they are but scantily clothed, for they are encompassed with a thick skin or coat <note>original: "pelle crassiori seu tunica". The author clarifies that their own natural skin is so thick that they require very little additional clothing. See *Spiritual Diary*, n. 1522, 3.</note> which wards off the cold.

**8957.** A continuation about the spirits and inhabitants of the earth Saturn will be found at the end of the following chapter.

**8958.** They who are being **regenerated** <term>regenerated: The process of being spiritually reborn or made new by God, moving from a selfish life to a life of love and faith.</term> undergo **Temptations** <term>Temptations: In this context, these are not just urges to do wrong, but intense spiritual struggles where a person's inner faith and character are tested.</term>.

**8961.** That which is dealt with in **Temptations** <term>Temptations: Not merely the urge to sin, but intense internal spiritual struggles or "combats" where a person’s faith and character are tested and strengthened.</term> relates to the dominion of the evil that is with the man from hell, and of the good that is with him from the Lord. The evil that wishes to have dominion is in the **natural or external man** <term>natural man: The part of the human personality focused on the physical world, self-interest, and the five senses.</term>, but the good is in the **spiritual or internal man** <term>spiritual man: The inner part of the human soul that is open to heaven and capable of selfless love and divine truth.</term>; hence it is that in Temptations that which is dealt with also relates to the dominion of the one over the other; if evil conquers, the natural man has dominion over the spiritual; if good conquers, the spiritual man has dominion over the natural.

**8962.** These combats are carried on by means of **truths of faith** which are from the **Word** <term>The Word: A term for the Sacred Scriptures, understood here as a reservoir of divine power and truth used to resist spiritual trials.</term>. The man must fight against evils and falsities from these; if he fights from anything else, he does not conquer, because the Lord is not in anything else.

**8963.** As the combat is carried on by means of truths of faith which are from the Word, the man is not admitted into combat until he is in the knowledges of truth and of good, and has obtained therefrom some spiritual life; and therefore these combats do not arise with man until he has come to years of maturity.

**8964.** He who has not with him truths of faith from the Word by which he may fight, thus who has not any spiritual life in himself from these, is not admitted into any combat, because he yields; and if a man yields, his state after Temptation becomes worse than his state before Temptation, for evil has then acquired to itself power over good, and falsity over truth.

**8965.** As at this day faith is rare, for the church is at its end <note>The author frequently suggests that the historical era of the Christian church had reached a point of spiritual decline or "consummation," requiring a renewal of faith.</note>, therefore at this day few undergo any spiritual Temptations. Hence it is that it is scarcely known what they are, and to what they conduce.

**8966.** Temptations conduce to the confirmation of the truths of faith, also to the implantation of them, and the insinuation of them into the will, that they may become **goods of charity** <term>charity: In this sense, charity is not just giving to the poor, but the active life of doing what is good and just from a love for one's neighbor.</term>. For, as before said, man fights from the truths of faith against evils and falsities; and because his mind is then in truths, when he conquers he confirms himself in them and implants them; and also accounts as an enemy, and rejects from him—

**8970.** In this chapter, in the <term>internal sense</term> <note>The "internal sense" refers to the hidden, spiritual meaning that Swedenborg believed existed within the literal words of the Bible.</note>, the subject treated of is those who injure or destroy, in themselves or in others, the truth of faith or the good of charity; what is the penalty; and what the restoration. Such things are here involved in the judgments or laws relating to servants, to the death or injury occasioned to companions or to servants, also relating to oxen that strike with the horn, and to a pit.

# EXODUS [N. 8971]

Those who do not live according to the truths of faith and a life based on them do not acknowledge—and even less do they perceive—anything of holiness in the **Word** <note>original: "Verbum." Swedenborg uses this term to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible as a living Divine communication.</note>. When these persons read the Word, they do not see anything higher in it than in any other writing. In fact, those who in their hearts deny the holiness of the Word also say to themselves while reading it that the writings of men are more elegant, because the literal sense of the Bible is not always composed in a "fine" or polished style.

This has been shown to me by living experience regarding those in the other life who, in their hearts, had denied that the Word was inspired by the Divine. When they were told that the Word is holy and Divine down to every "jot and smallest point" <note>A reference to Matthew 5:18, emphasizing that even the tiniest stroke of a pen in the original text has meaning.</note> within it, they stood amazed and marveled at how this could be. 

When they were told further—and shown through actual experience—that all things in the Word contain a **spiritual sense** <note>The internal or symbolic meaning that refers to the soul, heaven, and the Lord, rather than physical objects.</note> which does not appear in the letter, and that this sense of the Word is present with the angels in heaven when the Word is being read by man, they then acknowledged it because it was demonstrated to them. However, they argued that they did not know this while they were in the world, and because of this ignorance, they believed they should be free from blame. 

But when these same persons were examined, it was observed that they had lived just as they liked, without any restraints from **conscience** <note>An inner moral and spiritual compass formed by religious truths.</note>. They had, at heart, denied the Divine, heaven and hell, the life after death, and all other matters of faith. It was this internal state—not a lack of information—that was the true cause of their not having acknowledged the holiness of the Word. 

It was further shown that all those who have lived in the truths of faith and in a life according to them have held the Word to be holy; while reading it, they have also perceived this holiness within themselves. This convinced the observers that the cause of the disbelief was not in the Word itself, but in the readers. For those who are in a "life of good," their **interiors** <note>The inner levels of the human mind and spirit that connect to the spiritual world.</note> are open into heaven, allowing the holiness of the Word to flow in from the angels. In contrast, for those who are in a life of evil, these interiors are closed toward heaven but are open into hell, from which the opposite influence flows in.

[2] Take for example the judgments or laws in this chapter about **menservants, maidservants, and oxen**. Those who deny the holiness of the Word because they are in a life of evil will say that in these judgments or laws they do not see anything <note>The text concludes mid-sentence, implying that such readers see only mundane civil laws where there is actually deep spiritual wisdom.</note>

From this every one can see how holy in themselves these judgments are, however little they appear so in the letter.

# EXODUS [N. 8972]

...be in the civil state where there is a **representative church** <note>A "representative church" refers to a religious system, like that of the ancient Israelites, where outward rituals and laws were designed to physically act out or symbolize deeper spiritual realities.</note>, and which flow from the **internal truths** which are of order in the heavens. That these things are signified by “the judgments which were to be set before the sons of Israel” is evident from the signification of “judgments,” as being truths (see *n.* 2235, 6397, 7206, 8685, 8695). The reason why “judgments” denote truths is that all judgment is effected by means of truths; consequently by “doing judgment” in the **Word** <note>original: "Verbum"; referring to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> is signified doing truth, that is, judging according to truths. But by “judgments,” in the plural, are signified civil laws, thus exterior truths such as are in the civil state. It is said “where there is a representative church,” for the reason that interiorly they contain and involve in them those truths which are of order in the heavens, as can be seen from their **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" is the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and laws.</note>.

[2] The laws which were enacted and commanded the sons of Israel by the Lord were distinguished into “commandments,” “judgments,” and “statutes.” 

*   Those were called **“commandments”** which belonged to life; 
*   those **“judgments”** which belonged to the civil state; 
*   and those **“statutes”** which belonged to worship. 

As regards “judgments” *specifically*, they are such things as are contained in this chapter, and also in several chapters that follow. They served for laws in a church wherein the **internal things** which are of heaven and the church were represented by **external things**. 

But they do not serve for laws in a church wherein **internal things** are no longer represented by **external**, as in the **Christian Church**. The reason is that to the man of this Church **internal things** have been revealed, and therefore communication with heaven is effected by means of **internal things**, and not by means of **external things**, as before. This is the reason why the man of the Christian Church is not bound to observe in their **external form** <note>The literal, physical practice of the law.</note> those things which are called “judgments” and “statutes,” but in their **internal form**. Nevertheless holiness abides in them, because they contain holy things within them, as do also all and each of the things commanded in the Word about sacrifices. Although these things have been abrogated <note>Abolished or no longer legally binding.</note>, they nevertheless are holy things of the Word by reason of the Divine things which are in them, and which they **represented**. For when they are read by a Christian man, the Divine things that are within them, and...

> Now, therefore, O Israel, hear the **statutes** and the **judgments** which I will teach you, that ye may do them. What great nation is there that hath **statutes** and **judgments** so just as all this law, which I will give before you this day? (*Deuteronomy 4:1, 8; 5:1*).

> Jerusalem hath changed My **judgments** into wickedness more than the nations, and My **statutes** more than the lands that are round about her; for they have rejected My **judgments**, and have not walked in My **statutes** (*Ezekiel 5:6, 7*).

**“When thou shalt buy a Hebrew servant,”** signifies those within the church who possess the truths of doctrine but are not yet living in the **good** <note>In this context, "good" refers to the practice of love and charity that should accompany religious knowledge.</note> that aligns with those truths; **“if his master shall give him a woman,”** signifies **good** from the spiritual realm <note>A higher level of goodness that flows from the spiritual realm into a person's life during trials.</note> joined to truth while one is in combat; **“and she bear him sons or daughters,”** signifies the secondary truths and goods that are derived from that union; **“the woman and her children shall be his master's,”** signifies that the good joined to truth by a higher spiritual influence, along with its results, cannot be claimed as the person's own property; **“and he shall go out in his body,”** signifies the state after the struggle, which consists simply of truth that has been confirmed and implanted; **“and if saying the servant shall say,”** signifies a thought arising from that newly implanted truth; **“I love my master, my woman, and my children,”** signifies the joy found in remembering spiritual goods; **“I will not go out free,”** signifies the delight found in **obedience**; **“then his master shall bring him unto God,”** <note>original: "ad Deum"; **“and shall bring him to the door, or unto the door-post,”** signifies a state where the confirmed and implanted truth is connected to spiritual good <note>The "door" or "door-post" represents the entrance or introduction to a new state of being.</note>; **“and his master shall bore through his ear with his awl,”** signifies a representative act of **obedience** <note>In ancient times, piercing the ear was a ritual symbol showing that a servant had heard and accepted the master's will, choosing to stay forever.</note>; **“and he shall serve him forever,”** signifies service into **eternity**.

# N. 8974] CHAPTER XXI. VERS. 2-6

8974. **When thou shalt buy a Hebrew servant.** That this signifies those within the church who are in the truths of doctrine and not in good according to them, is evident from the signification of **“buying,”** as being to procure and appropriate to one’s self (see n. 4397, 5374, 5397, 5406, 5410, 5426, 7999); and from the signification of **“a Hebrew servant,”** as being those within the church who are in the truths of doctrine and not in **good of life** <note>The practice of love and charity that should accompany religious knowledge.</note> according to them; for **“servant”** is predicated of those who are in truth and not in the corresponding good, and in general, of truth relatively to good (n. 3409), and **“Hebrew”** is predicated of those things which are of the church, and of those things which are of some service (that it is predicated of those things which are of the church, see n. 5136, 5236, 6675, 6684; also that it is predicated of those things which are of some service, n. 1703, 1741, 5013). 

As in what now follows, the menservants and maidservants of the sons of Israel are treated of, it must be told what the statutes concerning them involve in the **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal words.</note>. Every one can see that the statutes contain within them **secret things of heaven** <note>original: "arcana coeli"</note>, because they were spoken and commanded orally by **Jehovah** <note>A primary name for God in the Old Testament, signifying the Divine Being.</note> to Moses on Mount Sinai, and because they follow immediately after the words of the **decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>. What and of what quality these secret things are, will be plain in the following explication of each particular.

# EXODUS

**8977.** *If he comes in by himself* <note>The Latin "in corpore suo" literally means "in his body," but here it refers to a servant entering service alone, without a wife.</note>. That this signifies truth without delight is evident from the meaning of the "body," which represents truth alone—that is, truth without its accompanying joy. In this context, "body" refers to the manservant without a woman. Thus, it signifies a state without delight, for the "woman" of a manservant represents delight joined with truth, as will be explained in what follows. 

Regarding this spiritual secret, the situation is as follows: The members of the **external church** <note>Those who focus on the outward rules and literal teachings of religion rather than inner spiritual motivations.</note>, who were represented by the Hebrew servants, are those who learn truth not because of any inner joy, but solely because it is the teaching of the church. They believe they can be saved through this knowledge, and this sense of necessity is what drives them to learn and know it. In the **internal sense** <note>The deeper spiritual meaning of the Scripture that lies beneath the literal historical narrative.</note>, these are the people meant by "manservants who come in their body and go out in their body." For these individuals, truth is merely something confirmed in the mind but not felt in the heart. 

In the afterlife, such persons are at the entrance to heaven, not in heaven itself. They are called the **"cuticulars"** <note>From the Latin word for skin; these are spirits who perform a protective, outer function in the spiritual world.</note> because in the **Grand Man** <note>The concept that the entirety of heaven is organized like a single human body, where every person or group performs a function corresponding to a specific organ or part.</note> they correspond to the skin (see sections 5553–5559). 

[2] However, those who possess truth to which delight is joined are represented here by the manservants who come with a woman. In this symbolism, "woman" signifies **good** <note>Spiritual "good" refers to the motivation of love, kindness, and charity.</note> when "man" signifies truth. But in this specific case, "woman" signifies **delight**, because for a person of the external church, delight takes the place of true spiritual good. 

The good that such a person possesses does not have a spiritual origin, but a **natural origin** <note>Something originating from worldly habits, personality, or self-interest rather than from Divine love.</note>. It draws its flavor from the delight of living and teaching the truth for the sake of profit or honor—and consequently, for the sake of self. This is why it is called "delight" and not "good." On the outside, it may appear to be good, but because it originates from the world and not from heaven, it is specifically termed delight. 

[3] On the other hand, good from a **spiritual origin** <note>Goodness that is motivated by a genuine love for God and the neighbor, regardless of personal reward.</note> is meant in the internal sense by the woman whom the master gives to his servant. However, this kind of good cannot be fully joined to the servant's state. Therefore, it was decreed that when the manservant left his service, the woman (and her sons and daughters) would remain with the master. This is because spiritual good is not performed for the sake of profit or honor, but for the sake of the church and the salvation of the neighbor. Such good cannot be truly united with those who are only in the ex- <note>The text cuts off mid-word, likely "external," continuing the thought that spiritual motivations cannot be fully integrated by those who only act out of external duty or self-interest.</note>

# EXODUS [Section 8979]

By the phrase a woman’s “man,” **truth** is represented. (That truth is represented by a “male servant,” see section 8974; it is also represented by the word “man,” see sections 3134, 3309, 3459, 7716.) The reason a “woman” refers to **delight** <note>Spiritual "delight" is the joy or pleasure found in living according to what is good and true.</note> is because, in the **internal sense** <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning hidden within the literal words of the Bible.</note>, a man's wife represents **good** <note>In this context, "good" refers to the practice of love and kindness.</note> (sections 915, 2517, 4823, 6014, 8337). 

However, a male servant from the people of Israel represents a person of the **external church** <note>A person who focuses on the outward rules and rituals of faith rather than the inner spirit of love.</note>. Such a person possesses the truths of religious doctrine but lacks the corresponding inner goodness (section 8974). This is because they do not act for the sake of truth or goodness itself, but rather so that they may be **recompensed** <note>Rewarded or paid back.</note>. Therefore, in the truth and goodness they practice, there is an underlying focus on the self. In a spiritual sense, this is not considered "good" but rather a form of "delight." In the spiritual sense, nothing is called "good" unless it belongs to love for the Lord and love for one's neighbor. While this goodness may also appear as a natural pleasure to the **natural man** <note>The part of the human personality focused on the physical world and self-interest.</note>, it is the spiritual quality within it that makes it truly good. 

[2] To understand this more clearly, keep in mind that a person of the **internal church** <note>One who acts from a heart transformed by divine love.</note> acts from **charity**—that is, from an affection rooted in love for their neighbor. In contrast, a person of the external church does not act from the goodness of charity, but from the **truth of faith**. They do not act from an affection for their neighbor, but from **obedience**, simply because it has been commanded. 

This results in the internal person being free, while the external person is, by comparison, a servant. Whoever acts from the affection of love acts from **freedom** (sections 2870–2893); but whoever acts only from obedience does not act from freedom, for mere obeying is not the same as being free. This is why a person who acts from the goodness of charity is a true member of the **spiritual church**, and is therefore represented in the **Word** <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> by **Israel**. Conversely, the person who does not act from charity, but only from the truth of faith, is not a true member of the spiritual church but is relatively its servant. For this reason, he was represented by the male servant called a “Hebrew servant,” because he was purchased from the children of Israel.

But these people are of as many types and varieties as there are skins or membranes in the body. There are those that wrap the whole body, those that wrap the internal regions in general—such as the **peritoneum** <note>The lining of the abdominal cavity.</note>, the **pleura** <note>The lining around the lungs.</note>, and the **pericardium** <note>The sac surrounding the heart.</note>—and there are those that specifically wrap each individual internal organ.

## [N. 8981] CHAPTER XXI. VERS. 2-6

...whom it is revealed what the secret <note>original: "arcanum"; a hidden spiritual truth or mystery.</note> herein is (for it is a secret), it shall be briefly explained. They who from infancy have thought little about **eternal life**, thus about the salvation of their soul, but only of worldly life and its prosperity, and yet have lived a good moral life, and have also believed in the truths of the doctrine of their church, when they come to more adult age, cannot be reformed otherwise than by the adjoining of **spiritual good** when they are in **combat** <note>Spiritual combat refers to the internal struggle or temptation a person feels when trying to live according to their conscience.</note>; but still they do not retain this good, but only confirm the truths of their doctrine by means of it. 

The reason why they are of this character is that in their past life they have indulged worldly loves; and when these loves have been rooted in, they do not suffer spiritual good to be conjoined with truth, because these loves are altogether repugnant to that good. Nevertheless spiritual good can take possession of the thought when these loves become inactive, as is the case when they are in anxiety, in misfortunes, and in sicknesses, and the like. Then the affection of welldoing from **charity** <note>original: "caritas"; the active practice of love and kindness toward others.</note> flows in, but this affection serves only for confirming and rooting in more deeply the truths of doctrine; but it cannot be conjoined with truth. 

The reason is that this influent affection of charity fills only the **intellectual part** <note>The part of the mind that understands and thinks about concepts.</note> of the mind, but does not enter into its **will part** <note>The part of the mind where our actual desires and intentions reside; the seat of character.</note>, and that which does not enter into the will part is not appropriated—thus is not conjoined—because the conjunction of good and truth with man is effected when truth enters the will; consequently when the man wills truth, and from willing does it. Then for the first time truth becomes good, or what is the same, faith becomes charity.

[4] This cannot be effected with those who from infancy have indulged the loves of the world, and yet are in the truth of the doctrine of their church; for their will part is possessed by these loves, which are wholly in opposition to and reject spiritual good. They merely admit this into the intellectual part of the mind, that is, into the thought, when these loves are dormant, which is the case, as said above, in a state of sickness or of misfortune, or in anxiety, consequently in labor, and in some combat. 

This is the secret which lies hidden in this **statute**. In the sense of the letter this does not savor of anything Divine; nevertheless it is most Divine; but this does not appear except through the <term>internal sense<note>The underlying spiritual message of the Bible that the author believe is intended for the soul and for angels, rather than the literal historical or legal meaning.</note></term>. Thus do the angels perceive these things who are with a man who is reading this word. For the angels do not think of a door or of a door-post, nor of an ear and its boring, nor even of a manservant; but instead thereof they think of the aforesaid communication and conjunction. Communications of truth with good are there presented to view by means of doors, and conjunctions by means of door-posts, and other things by the rooms themselves, by the courts, by the windows, and the various adornments.

### [No. 8989] CHAPTER 21, VERSES 2–6

“Shall He accept you favorably?” says the <term>Lord of Hosts<note>Translated from the Hebrew *Jehovah Zebaoth*, a title for God emphasizing His command over the heavenly "hosts" or spiritual armies.</note></term>. “Who is there even among you that would rather shut the doors, and not kindle a light upon My altar in vain?” (*Malachi* 1:9, 10);

> I have chosen to stand at the door in the house of my God, rather than dwell in the tents of wickedness (*Psalm* 84:10);

> Lift up your heads, O ye gates; be ye lifted up, ye eternal doors; that the King of glory may come in (*Psalm* 24:7, 9);

“The eternal doors being lifted up” signifies the opening and elevation of hearts to the Lord, who is the “King of glory,” so as to allow communication—that is, so that He may flow in with the good of charity and the truth of faith. Because of this, even in regard to His Humanity, He is called “God,” and here, “the God of Israel.”

> Behold, I have set before thee an open door, which no one can shut; for thou hast a little power, and hast kept My word (*Revelation* 3:8);

# EXODUS [N. 8990]

[5] The inner meaning of many expressions has flowed from the spiritual world by virtue of **correspondences** <term>correspondences<note>The symbolic relationship between spiritual realities and natural objects or words; for example, "light" in nature corresponds to "truth" in the mind.</note></term>. This is similar to how we speak of “spiritual light,” and the resulting “sight,” to signify the things of faith; or “spiritual fire,” and the resulting “life,” to signify the things of love. The reason the boring through of the ear was performed with an **awl** was because an “awl” signifies the same thing as a “peg” or a “nail”—namely, an attachment or a joining together. In a spiritual sense, it represents being assigned to something. However, because the awl was a tool used by a servant, it represents an assignment to perpetual obedience on the part of the servant. That “pegs” or “nails” signify an attachment or joining is clear from several passages where they are mentioned, such as: 

*Isaiah* 22:23, 33:20, 41:7, 54:2; *Jeremiah* 10:4; *Exodus* 27:19, 38:31; and *Numbers* 3:37, 4:32.

### 8991. *And he shall serve him forever.* 
This signifies that this state continues into eternity. This is evident from the meaning of “serving,” which is to obey—for servants are those who obey, and masters are those who command. As established previously, the men-servants represent those who have done good out of a sense of obedience, rather than from the inner motivation of **charity** <term>charity<note>In this work, "charity" refers to a selfless, internal love for one’s neighbor, as opposed to "faith" or "obedience," which may be driven by duty or intellectual belief.</note></term>. 

In the literal sense, “forever” here means service to a master until the end of the servant's physical life. However, in the internal or spiritual sense, it signifies what is eternal, as it refers to the state of the soul after death. It is described as being “to eternity” because those who do good merely out of the obedience of faith—and not from the heart’s affection—can never be brought to a state of acting purely from "good" in the afterlife. 

This is because a person’s inner life remains the same after death. As a person is when they die, so they remain; according to the common saying, “as the tree falls, so it lies.” This does not refer to a person’s state in the final hours of death, but rather the character formed by the entire course of their life. Therefore, those who have spent their lives habituated to doing good only out of duty or obedience, rather than love, remain in that state for eternity. While they may be perfected in their ability to obey, they do not reach the higher state of acting from love.

<summary>This page explains that symbols like the awl represent a permanent spiritual commitment to obedience. It concludes that a person's fundamental motivation—whether duty-bound obedience or heartfelt love—remains their permanent state after death.</summary>

**8992.** Verses 7–11. *And when a man shall sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out according to the going out of the menservants. If she be evil in the eyes of her master, so that he will not betroth her, then he shall let her be redeemed: to sell her to a strange people he shall have no power, in his acting treacherously against her. “And when a man shall sell his daughter to be a maidservant,” signifies the **affection of truth** <term>affection of truth<note>A person’s internal desire or love for understanding what is true, specifically for the sake of living a better life.</note></term> from **natural delight** <term>natural delight<note>The pleasure or satisfaction found in worldly or sensory experiences; here, it refers to an early stage of spiritual development where a person is drawn to truth because it feels good or useful on a natural level.</note></term>; “she shall not go out according to the going out of the menservants,” signifies a state not like truth without affection; “if she be evil in the eyes of her master,” signifies if the affection of truth from natural delight does not agree with **spiritual truth** <term>spiritual truth<note>Truth that is understood through internal enlightenment and a love for God, rather than just through memory or logical reasoning.</note></term>; “so that he will not betroth her,” signifies so that it cannot be conjoined <note>original: "conjungi," meaning to be spiritually joined or married.</note>; “then he shall let her be redeemed,” signifies alienation from these truths; “and if he shall betroth her to his son,” signifies if it agrees with any derived truth so that it can be conjoined therewith; “he shall do to her according to the judgment of daughters,” signifies that it shall be as is the genuine affection of truth; “if he shall take him another,” signifies conjunction with the affection of truth from another stock; “her food, her clothing, and her **conjugial due** <term>conjugial due<note>Based on the Latin "conjugialis," this refers to the spiritual and physical rights and duties within a marriage, representing the deep union between goodness and truth.</note></term> he shall not diminish,” signifies no deprivation of the interior life which is “food,” nor of the exterior life which is “clothing,” thus no deprivation of conjunction which is the “conjugial due;” “and if he shall not do these three to her,” signifies the deprivation of these; “she shall go out free with no silver,” signifies alienation therefrom without truth conjoined with it.

[3] Keep in mind that a **genuine affection for truth** is a person’s willingness and longing to know the truest teachings of faith for the purpose of being useful and for the sake of their life. On the other hand, an affection for truth that is *not* genuine is a desire for truths for the sake of oneself—to seek honors and hunt for profits. Those whose affection for truth comes from this source do not care whether the truths they know are genuine, as long as they are the kind of things they can pass off as truths; therefore, they stick stubbornly to confirming the specific teachings of the church they happened to be born into, whether those teachings are actually true or not. They are also in darkness regarding the truths themselves because worldly goals (profits) and bodily goals (honors) completely blindfold them. 

[4] But those who have a **genuine affection for truth**—that is, who long to know truths for the sake of doing good and for the sake of their life—continue in the teachings of their church until they reach an age where they begin to think for themselves. # N. 8994] CHAPTER XXI. VERS. 7-11

In the **representative sense** <note>The symbolic meaning where physical people or objects in the Bible represent spiritual or mental states.</note>, those who are “menservants,” or “men,” are not moved by truth and good themselves, but only by the **knowledges** <term>knowledges<note>From the Latin *scientifica*; refers to facts, information, or external data about spiritual things rather than the internal experience of them.</note></term> of them; consequently, they find delight in truths for the sake of knowing. But they who are in the **affection of truth and of good** <note>A heartfelt love for what is true and good for its own sake.</note>, and who in the representative sense are “maidservants,” or “women,” are not moved by mere knowledge, but by the truths and goods themselves when they hear them and perceive them in others. Such affection is common with good women, whereas the affection for the knowledge of truth is more common with men.

[4] From this it is that those who possess **spiritual perception** <note>An internal "gut feeling" or intuitive sight into the quality of truth.</note> love women who are moved by truths, but do not love women who are only interested in knowledges; for it is according to Divine order that men should be centered in knowledges, but women solely in affections; and thus that women should not love themselves for their own knowledge, but should love men; from this comes **the conjugal** <term>the conjugal<note>A term describing the spiritual principle of marriage—the union of a husband’s intellect (truth) and a wife’s heart (goodness/affection).</note></term>. From this also it is that it was said by the ancients that women should be silent in the church. This being the case, knowledges are represented by men, but affections by women; here, the affections of truth which spring from the delights of natural loves are represented by the maidservants. As these are of a totally different nature from those who are moved by knowledges, the case with maidservants is quite different from what it is with menservants. This then is what is signified by the statute that “the maidservant shall not go out according to the going out of the menservants.” 

But be it known that the case is so with those who belong to the Lord’s **spiritual kingdom** <term>spiritual kingdom<note>One of the two broad divisions of heaven; here, people are governed by truth and the intellect.</note></term>; but it is the other way around with those who belong to His **celestial kingdom** <term>celestial kingdom<note>The higher division of heaven; here, people are governed by love and the will.</note></term>. In the latter kingdom, husbands are in affection, but wives are in the knowledges of good and truth. From this comes the conjugal bond with them.
