# EXODUS [N. 8995]

...of the **"master,"** as representing spiritual truth (see n. 8981). [2] We must explain how this situation should be understood. It was stated above (n. 8993, 8994) that a **"maidservant"** represents the affection for truth that comes from the pleasures of self-love or love of the world. The reason this affection can be joined with spiritual truth is that the affection for spiritual truth is an internal affection—located in the **interior man**—whereas the affection for truth stemming from natural pleasure is in the **external man**. 

The internal affection belonging to the **spiritual man** <term>spiritual man<note>The part of a person's mind and character that is focused on heaven, eternal values, and selfless love.</note></term> is constantly joined with the external affection of the **natural man** <term>natural man<note>The part of a person's mind focused on the physical world, personal biological needs, and social status.</note></term>. However, this must happen in such a way that the internal affection for truth is the ruling power, and the external affection is its servant. This is because **Divine order** requires the spiritual part of a person to rule over the natural part (n. 8961, 8967). Furthermore, when the spiritual man rules, the person looks upward—represented by having one's "head in heaven." But when the natural man rules, the person looks downward—represented by having one's "head in hell."

[3] To shed more light on this subject, we should say more. Most people, through the truths they learn and the good things they do, do indeed think about the resulting benefits or the honor they might receive in their country. If these worldly benefits are seen as the **end** <note>In this context, the "end" refers to the ultimate goal or primary motivation for an action.</note>, then the natural man is ruling and the spiritual is serving. If, however, they are not seen as the ultimate goal, but only as **means** to an end, then the spiritual man rules and the natural man serves, as has been said before (n. 7819, 7820). 

When profit or honor is viewed as a means to an end rather than the goal itself, the person is not actually focused on the profit or honor, but on the goal, which is **use** <term>use<note>A central concept in this philosophy: the practical benefit or service one provides to others, society, or the Lord's kingdom.</note></term>. For example, a person who desires and acquires wealth for the sake of a specific "use" (which they love above all else) does not take delight in riches for the sake of riches, but for the sake of those uses. In fact, it is these very **uses** that constitute a person's spiritual life; riches merely serve as the tools or means (see n. 6933–6938). 

From this, we can see what the quality of the natural man must be for it to be joined with the spiritual: it must view profit and honor—and thus wealth and status—as means, and not as the ultimate goal. Whatever a person regards as their goal constitutes their **very life**, because they love it above all things; for whatever is loved is viewed as the end goal. [4]

# EXODUS 21:7–11 [N. 8995]

Anyone who does not realize that the **goal** <term>end<note>original: "finis." In this context, the "end" refers to the ultimate purpose or intention behind an action—the "why" that drives a person.</note></term>—or what is the same thing, the **love**—is what creates a person’s spiritual life, cannot understand how this works. Consequently, a person is essentially located where their love is: in heaven if their love is heavenly, and in hell if their love is infernal. Such a person might assume that the delights of natural loves—specifically the love of self and the love of the world—cannot be reconciled with spiritual truth and goodness. This is because they do not know that during the process of **regeneration** <term>regeneration<note>The spiritual process of being "born again" or rebuilt by God, where a person’s priorities shift from selfish desires to heavenly love.</note></term>, a person must be completely turned around, or "inverted." When a person has been inverted, their "head" is in heaven; but before this change, their "head" is in hell.

A person’s head is in hell when they treat the pleasures of self-love or love of the world as their ultimate goal. But their head is in heaven when these same pleasures are used merely as **means** to a higher goal. This is because the goal—which is the love—is the only thing in a person that is truly alive. The means used to reach that goal have no life in themselves; they only receive life from the goal they serve. 

Consequently, the steps taken toward an ultimate goal are called "intermediate goals." To the extent that they point toward the final, primary goal, they are filled with life. Because of this, once a person has been regenerated and makes loving their neighbor and the Lord their ultimate goal, they then use self-love and worldly love as tools or "means." When someone reaches this state and looks toward the Lord, they view themselves and the world as nothing by comparison; and if they do regard themselves as anything, it is only so that they may be able to serve the Lord. Previously, however, the opposite was true: when such a person looked to themselves, they viewed the Lord as nothing—or if they did value Him, it was only so they could gain personal profit and honor.

[5] From all this, we can see the secret meaning hidden within these laws concerning **maidservants** <term>maidservant<note>In this symbolic context, a "maidservant" represents a lower or "natural" level of affection that serves a higher spiritual purpose.</note></term> from the daughters of Israel. Even though they were servants, if they were good, they were betrothed to the master who bought them, or to his son. But if they were "evil" <note>In a symbolic sense, "evil" here refers to an affection that cannot be joined to spiritual truth because it remains focused purely on the self rather than service.</note>, they were not betrothed, but were either redeemed or sold, as described in these verses. 

Furthermore, betrothing maidservants or taking them as secondary wives was permitted in the **representative church** <term>representative church<note>A historical form of worship (like that of the ancient Israelites) where physical actions and laws were designed to mirror and represent deeper spiritual realities.</note></term>, particularly the Jewish and Israelite church. This was because a wife represented the affection for spiritual truth, while a maidservant represented the affection for...

But when the internal things of the church had been opened by the Lord, the representations of internal things by external ceased, because it was then internal things—which are those of faith and love—with which the man of the church was to be imbued, and by means of which he was to worship the Lord; and therefore it was then no longer permissible to have more wives than one, nor to have concubines for wives (n. 865, 2727–2759, 3246, 4837).

**9003. *Her food, her raiment, and her conjugial due, he shall not diminish.*** That this signifies no deprivation of the **interior life** which is "food," nor of the **exterior life** which is "clothing," thus no deprivation of conjunction which is the "**conjugial due**," is evident from:
*   The signification of **"food,"** as being the sustenance of the interior life. In the spiritual sense, "food" (or meat and drink) denotes the knowledges of good and truth: "meat" refers to the knowledges of good (n. 5147), and "drink" to the knowledges of truth (n. 3168, 3772). Therefore, "food" denotes the things which nourish the spiritual life of man (n. 5293, 5576, 5579, 5915, 8562).
*   The signification of **"covering"** or **"raiment,"** as being the sustenance of the exterior life. In the spiritual sense, "covering" or "clothing" denotes lower **memory-knowledges** <term>memory-knowledges<note>Basic facts and information stored in the external memory; these provide the "clothing" or structure for our outer life in the world.</note></term>, because these are what sustain the external life of man (n. 5248, 6918).
*   The signification of the **"conjugial due"** <term>conjugial due<note>From the Latin 'conjugialis,' referring specifically to the spiritual union in marriage. Here it signifies the actual joining together of the soul's affection with truth.</note></term>, as being conjunction or union.
*   The signification of **"not to diminish,"** as being not to deprive of. 

[2] The case herein is that natural affection conjoined with spiritual truth—which is signified by "a maid-servant betrothed to a son"—requires continual sustenance of life from the spiritual truth with which it has been conjoined.

**9007.** *He that smiteth a man, and he die.* That this signifies the injuring of the <term>truth of faith<note>The specific ideas and concepts that allow a person to understand spiritual reality.</note></term> and the consequent loss of spiritual life, is evident from the signification of “smiting,” as being to injure by falsity (see n. 7136, 7146); from the signification of “a man,” <note>original: "vir"</note> as being the truth of faith (of which below); and from the signification of “dying,” as being the loss of spiritual life (n. 5407, 6119, 7494). In the <term>internal sense<note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and laws.</note></term>, no other life is meant, though in the <term>external sense<note>The literal or historical meaning of the text.</note></term>, natural life is meant. 

The reason why spiritual life perishes by the injuring of the truth of faith is that good united to truth constitutes that life; and therefore when truth is stolen away, good—and thus spiritual life—falls to the ground. That “a man” denotes the truth of faith is because in heaven no attention is paid to person, or to anything of person, but to things abstracted from person (n. 4380, 8343, 8985). Consequently, where “a man” is mentioned in the Word, the angels do not perceive a person, because a person is a physical individual; instead, they perceive that faculty of his by virtue of which he is a man, namely, the <term>intellectual faculty<note>The part of the mind that thinks, reasons, and understands truth.</note></term>. When they perceive this faculty, they perceive the truth of faith, because the truth of faith belongs to it, and not only enlightens it, but also forms it. 

And as by “man” <note>original: "vir"</note> there is perceived in heaven the intellectual side of man, so by “human” <note>original: "homo"</note> there is perceived his will; because a human is a human from the will, but is a man from the understanding. And as the will is the man himself, therefore the good of love is the human, for this belongs to the will, and perfects and makes it. (That “man” <note>original: "vir"</note> denotes the intellectual, and therefore the truth of faith, see n. 158, 265, 749, 1007, 2517, 3134, 3309, 3459, 4823, 7716; and that “human” <note>original: "homo"</note> denotes the good of love, n. 768, 4287, 7523, 8547, 8988.)

# EXODUS [N. 9008

Because these are the opposites of the truths and goods that make up life, they are therefore the cause of death—but specifically spiritual death, which is <term>damnation<note>A state of being spiritually "dead" or completely separated from divine goodness and truth.</note></term>, hell, and eternal unhappiness. The reason that people who are in evils and falsities (or who are in hell) are nevertheless "alive" is because they were born as human beings, and therefore they were born with the capacity to receive life from the Lord. They also receive just enough life from the Lord to be able to think, reason, and speak, which allows them to make the evil in themselves appear as good and the falsity appear as truth; thus, they live as mere semblances of life.

9009. ***And he that hath not lain in wait.*** That this signifies when an action was not done with <term>foresight<note>The act of looking ahead and planning an outcome before acting.</note></term> from the will, is evident from the meaning of "**lying in wait**." To lie in wait means to act with deliberation, and thus with foresight; for anyone who lies in wait foresees in their mind the evil they are about to commit. Because they do such evil with foresight, they also do it from the **will**, for the action proceeds from there. There are evils which proceed from the will of man but are not planned with foresight; and there are evils which proceed from the will and *are* planned with foresight. Those which proceed from both the will and from foresight are much worse than those which are not from foresight. This is because the person sees that they are evils and could therefore stop, but they are not willing to do so. In this way, they confirm these evils within themselves. Evils that are "confirmed" become part of one's nature, so that afterward they can scarcely be <term>extirpated<note>To pull up by the roots; to completely remove.</note></term>; for in such a case, the person summons spirits from hell who do not easily leave afterward. 

[2] Evils which proceed from one part of the mind and not at the same time from the other—such as those which come from the **intellectual part** but not at the same time from the **will part**—are not rooted in and <term>appropriated<note>The process by which a thought or action becomes a permanent part of a person’s spiritual character or identity.</note></term> to the person. Only what passes from the intellectual part into the will part is rooted in them. Or, what is the same: only what passes from a **thought** (which belongs to the understanding) into an **affection** (which belongs to the will), and from there into an **act**, becomes part of the person. Those things which enter into the will are what are said to "enter into the heart." 

[3] But evils which proceed solely from the will, and thus without premeditation, are those which a person is inclined toward hereditarily...

### N. 9009] CHAPTER XXI. VERS. 12-15

These are not <term>imputed<note>In a legal or spiritual sense, to "impute" something is to formally assign responsibility or guilt to someone.</note></term> to a person unless they have confirmed them in their <term>intellectual part<note>The faculty of the mind associated with reasoning, logic, and understanding, as distinct from the will or emotions.</note></term> (see n. 966, 2308, 8806 <note>These numbers refer to specific sections in Swedenborg's larger theological works for further reading.</note>); but when they have been confirmed in this part, they have then been inscribed on the person and become their own, and are imputed to them.

**9010.** *But God caused it to happen to his hand.* That this signifies what appears to be chance is evident from how the ancients viewed the world. Their idea of chance was that it happened from God; therefore, they expressed the concept of an accident by saying, “God caused it to happen to the hand.” 

Those who belonged to the ancient churches knew that the <term>Providence<note>The constant care and guidance provided by God over the universe and human life.</note></term> of the Lord is in each and every thing. They understood that things which happen—that is, things which *appear* to be chance—were actually part of Providence. Because of this, the "simple" (those who could not distinguish between things God *permits* to happen and things He *wills* to happen) attributed both good and evil to the Lord. They attributed good to Him because they knew all good comes from Him; they attributed evil to Him because of how things appeared. 

For when a person does evil and turns away from the Lord, it appears as if the Lord is the one turning away; in that state, the Lord appears to be behind the person, not in front of them. It is for this reason that if anyone struck another by chance—without planning it beforehand—it was described with the words, “God caused it to happen to the hand.” 

(That the Providence of the Lord is in each and all things has been already shown, see n. 1919, 4329, 5122, 5155, 5195, 5894, 6058, 6481–6487, 6489, 6491, 7004, 7007, 8478, 8717; also that things which happen, or are matters of chance, are of Providence, n. 5508, 6493, 6494; and that evil is attributed to the Lord, even though it actually comes from man, n. 2447, 5798, 6071, 6832, 6991, 6997, 7533, 7877, 7926, 8197, 8227, 8228, 8282, 8284, 8483, 8632.)

# EXODUS [N. 9011]

...a <term>forest<note>In this symbolic system, a forest represents a state of mind focused on gathering many external facts or "knowledges."</note></term> represents <term>knowledge<note>Translated from the Latin *scientia*, referring to factual or external information.</note></term>, a “garden” represents <term>intelligence<note>The ability to see how various truths relate to one another.</note></term>, and a “paradise” represents <term>wisdom<note>The highest state, where truth is lived and loved, not just understood.</note></term> (see section n. 3220). > The light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for flame. He shall cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a magnificent one (*Isaiah 10:17–19, 34*);

In this passage, “the forest” signifies the church in terms of its knowledge of truth; “Carmel” signifies the church in terms of its knowledge of good; and “Lebanon” and “Hermon” are used in a similar way. The “trees of the forest” refer to these specific pieces of knowledge, as mentioned above. The phrase “a number that a child may describe” means that they are very few. The “thickets of the forest” signify <term>memory-knowledges<note>General facts or raw information stored in the mind, which have not yet been applied to life.</note></term> (n. 2831).

> I will visit upon you according to the fruit of your works, and I will kindle a fire in her forest (*Jeremiah 21:14*).
> Prophesy against the forest of the field unto the south; and say to the forest of the south, Behold I will kindle a fire in thee, and it shall devour every tree (*Ezekiel 20:46, 47*).
> Feed Thy people with Thy rod, the flock of Thine heritage who dwell alone in the forest in the midst of Carmel (*Micah 7:14*).

## 9012. 
***And when a man shall act of set purpose against his companion.*** 

That this signifies premeditation from a <term>depraved will<note>A will that is turned away from what is good and toward what is selfish or harmful.</note></term> is evident from the significance of “acting of set purpose,” which means to act with premeditation. Whoever proposes evil to themselves does so with premeditation; and because it is evil and they carry it out, it originates in the will, for the doing of evil begins there. However, the <term>falsity<note>Incorrect or distorted ideas used to justify bad behavior.</note></term> by which that evil is affirmed, defended, and promoted belongs to the thought—thus it comes from a depraved or inverted understanding. (That a person is guilty when they do evil from both the understanding and the will may be seen above, in section n. 9009.)

## 9013. 
***To kill him with deceit.*** 

That this signifies the resulting malice of depriving the neighbor of eternal life is evident from the significance of “to kill,” which means to take away faith and charity from the neighbor, and thus to deprive them of spiritual life, which is eternal life (see sections nn. 6767, 8902). It is also evident from the significance of “deceit,” which is malice from the will combined with forethought or premeditation—thus, from a set purpose. 

Evils are committed either from enmity, hatred, or revenge, and either with deceit or without it. But evils done with <term>deceit<note>Translated from the Latin *dolus*, meaning calculated trickery or hidden malice.</note></term> are the worst, because deceit is like a poison that infects and destroys with infernal venom; it penetrates the entire mind, reaching even its innermost parts. The reason is that one who acts with deceit meditates on evil, feeds their understanding with it, and takes delight in it. In doing so, they destroy everything within themselves that makes them truly human—that is, the life that comes from the good of faith and charity. [2] Those who, while in the world, have ensnared their neighbor with deceit regarding worldly and earthly things, will ensnare their neighbor in the next life with...

### [NUMBER 9013] CHAPTER XXI. VERSES 12-15

When seen by the angels in the light of heaven, these individuals appear like serpents and vipers who hide their wickedness under the cover of truths; that is, they deceitfully twist truths to justify doing evil. These people hide their poison as if under their teeth, and in this way, they kill. [5] But those who live in the <term>faith of truth<note>A belief system grounded in genuine spiritual truths rather than mere personal opinion.</note></term> and in a life of goodness from the Lord cannot be harmed by such poisons. This is because they live in light from the Lord, a light in which the deceitful appear plainly as serpents and their tricks as poison. The fact that these people are kept safe by the Lord is expressed in His words to the disciples:

> Behold, I give you the power to tread upon serpents and scorpions (*Luke 10:19*).

[6] Those who have been inwardly infected with spiritual deceit—that is, with hypocrisy—are the ones meant by those who speak against the <term>Holy Spirit<note>In this context, the divine truth proceeding from the Lord; to speak against it is to knowingly reject or corrupt the very core of spiritual reality.</note></term>, for whom there is no forgiveness. As stated in *Matthew*:

> I say to you, every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven; but the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven. Indeed, if anyone says a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the one to come. Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad. O offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak what is good! (*Matthew 12:31–34*).

To "speak a word against the Holy Spirit" means to speak well while thinking evil, and to act well while willing evil, regarding the things of the Lord, His kingdom, His church, and His <term>Word<note>The Holy Scriptures.</note></term>. In such people, falsehood lies hidden inside the truths they speak, and evil—which is a hidden poison—lies within the good deeds they do; consequently, they are called an "offspring of vipers." 

[7] In the afterlife, an evil person is permitted to speak evil and falsehood, but they are not allowed to speak good or truth. This is because there, everyone is compelled to speak from the heart and is not permitted to have a <term>divided mind<note>A state of hypocrisy where the outward speech does not match the inner intention or "will."</note></term>. Those who attempt to act otherwise are separated from everyone else and are hidden in hells from which they cannot possibly escape. This is what is meant by those who "say a word..."

# EXODUS [NUMBER 9013]

"...against the Holy Spirit" is evident from the Lord’s words: "Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; how can you, being evil, speak what is good?" The <term>Holy Spirit<note>In this theology, the Holy Spirit is specifically defined as the Divine Truth that radiates from the Lord into the human mind.</note></term> denotes this Divine Truth, which is the very essence of holiness. To blaspheme it is to inwardly reject and profane the core of spiritual reality. 

[8] The reason such a state will not be forgiven is that hypocrisy or deceit regarding sacred things infects the <term>interiors<note>The inner levels of the human mind and spirit where true character resides, hidden behind the outward persona.</note></term> of a person. This infection destroys everything of spiritual life within them, as previously stated, until eventually no part of their character remains healthy. Since the <term>forgiveness of sins<note>Defined here not as a simple legal pardon, but as the actual process of separating evil from good and moving evil to the "sides" of one's life (see reference n. 8393).</note></term> involves the separation of evil from good, it cannot occur in someone whose "good" has been entirely destroyed. Therefore, it is said, "It shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in that which is to come." This describes the same character as the man who "had not on a wedding garment," who was bound and cast into outer darkness (*Matthew 22:11–13*; see reference n. 2132). 

[9] That "deceit" in the Word <note>The "Word" is a traditional term for the Holy Scriptures.</note> signifies hypocrisy is clear from the following passages:

> Beware every man of his companion, and put no trust in any brother; for every brother acts as a supplanter. They mock one another and do not speak the truth; they have taught their tongue to speak lies. Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they have refused to know Me, says Jehovah (*Jeremiah 9:4–6*).

> You shall destroy those who speak lies; Jehovah abhors the man of blood and deceit (*Psalm 5:6*).

> Blessed is the man to whom Jehovah does not attribute iniquity, provided there is no deceit in his spirit (*Psalm 32:2*).

> Deliver my soul from lying lips, from a tongue of deceit (*Psalm 120:2*).

The same meaning is found in *Psalm 52:4* and *Psalm 109:2*.

**9014.** *Thou shalt take him from Mine altar, that he may die.* 

This signifies <term>damnation<note>A state of spiritual death or separation from the Divine life.</note></term>, even if the person flees to the worship of the Lord, begs for forgiveness, and promises to repent. This is evident from the meaning of the "altar of Jehovah" as the primary symbol for the worship of the Lord (see references n. 921, 2777, 2811, 4541, 8935, 8940). Because the altar represented worship, "to flee to the altar" means to seek the Lord’s protection, to pray for forgiveness, and to promise repentance; for one naturally follows the other.

[2] How this works can be seen from what was explained in the paragraph above (n. 9013), namely, that in spiritual matters, deceit—which is **hypocrisy**—cannot be forgiven. The reason is that deceit acts like a poison; it penetrates even to the <term>interiors<note>The "interiors" are the deeper levels of the human mind and soul where a person's true intentions and love reside.</note></term>, killing everything of faith and charity. It also destroys the <term>remains<note>A technical term in this theology referring to the storehouse of innocent goods and truths—like childhood wonder or moments of kindness—that the Lord preserves in a person’s inner mind to serve as a foundation for spiritual life.</note></term>, which are the truths and goods of faith and charity stored up by the Lord in the inner reaches of a person. When these are destroyed, nothing of spiritual life can survive. (Regarding "remains," see references n. 468, 530, 560–563, 660, 661, 798, 1050, 1738, 1906, 2284, 5135, 5342, 5344, 5897, 5898, 6156, 7560, 7564.) 

Therefore, when such people pray to the Lord for forgiveness and promise to repent—which is signified by <note>original: "ad altare confugere"</note> **“fleeing to the altar,”**—they do not pray or promise anything from the heart, but only from the lips. Because of this, they are not heard; for the Lord looks at the heart, and not at words that are detached and estranged from the heart. Consequently, for such people there is no forgiveness, because no genuine repentance is possible for them.

[3] Many people within the church believe that the **forgiveness of sins** is a "wiping out" or "washing away" of wrongs, similar to washing away dirt with water, and that after being forgiven, they go on their way clean and pure. This opinion is especially common among those who believe that salvation comes through **faith alone** <note>A theological doctrine suggesting that belief in God is the sole requirement for salvation, regardless of one's actions or character development.</note>. 

But let it be known that the reality of the forgiveness of sins is quite different. The Lord forgives everyone their sins because He is mercy itself. Nevertheless, they are not actually forgiven unless the person performs serious **repentance**, stops doing evil things, and afterward lives a life of faith and charity—and continues this until the end of their life. When this is done, the person receives spiritual life from the Lord, which is called **new life**. 

When a person views the evils of their former life from the perspective of this new life, turning away from them and regarding them with horror, only then are the evils truly "forgiven." At that point, the person is held in truths and goodness by the Lord and is kept away from evils. From this, it is clear what the forgiveness of sins actually is: it cannot be granted in a single hour, nor even within a year. The church acknowledges this truth, for it is said to those who come to the <term>Holy Supper<note>The ritual of Holy Communion or the Eucharist, involving bread and wine as symbols of Divine love and truth.</note></term> that their sins are forgiven if they begin a new life by...

In this context, “one that hath an issue” signifies the **profanation** <note>The act of taking something sacred and treating it with contempt or mixing it with worldly evils.</note> of the good of love; “one that is a leper” signifies the profanation of the truth of faith (number 6963); “one that leaneth on a staff,” or one who is lame, signifies those in whom all sense of "good" has been destroyed (numbers 4302, 4314); “one that falleth by the sword” signifies those who are continually dying spiritually because of false beliefs (numbers 4499, 6353, 7102, 8294); and “one that lacketh bread” signifies those who are destitute of all spiritual life, for “bread” represents the nourishment of the spirit through goodness (numbers 6118, 8410). Because Joab represented these qualities, he was eventually executed at the altar where he had fled for safety, by the command of Solomon (1 *Kings* 2:28–32).

**9015.** *And he that smiteth his father and his mother.* This signifies the **blaspheming** of the Lord and of His kingdom. This is clear from the meaning of “smiting,” which is to cause injury through false ideas (see numbers 7136, 7146, 9007); when this is said in relation to the Lord and His kingdom, it means to blaspheme. It is also clear from the meaning of “father,” which represents the Lord, and “mother,” which represents His kingdom. This was explained in the discussion of the Fourth Commandment (the Decalogue), where it was shown that the **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" is the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and laws.</note> of “honoring father and mother” is to love the Lord and His kingdom—and thus, in a general sense, to love what is good and true. Therefore, "to smite father and mother" means, in a general sense, to blaspheme the goodness and truth of the church.

**9016.** **Dying he shall die.** That this signifies damnation is evident from the meaning of "dying," which refers to spiritual damnation (see section 9008 <note>Swedenborg uses these numbers to refer back to previous points in his extensive commentary, *Arcana Coelestia*.</note>).

**9017.** **Verses 16, 17. And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, and if he shall be found in his hand, dying he shall die. And he that curseth his father and his mother, dying he shall die.** 

"And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him," signifies taking a truth of faith and applying it to something evil, thereby turning away from it; "and if he shall be found in his hand," signifies that the person nevertheless acknowledges that truth; "dying he shall die," signifies damnation; "and he that curseth his father and his mother," signifies the total denial of the Lord and of His kingdom by those who belong to the church, which results in the **profanation** <term>profanation<note>The spiritual crime of acknowledging a truth as holy and then intentionally living in a way that contradicts or mocks it, which "mixes" the sacred with the corrupt.</note></term> of the church's good and truth; "dying he shall die," signifies damnation.

**9018.** **And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him.** That this signifies the application of the **truth of faith** <term>truth of faith<note>Specific spiritual concepts or teachings that a person believes to be true regarding God and the spiritual life.</note></term> to evil, and its alienation, is evident from the meaning of "stealing a man." In this context, "a man"—specifically a man of the sons of Israel—represents the truth of faith (as seen in sections 5414, 5879, 5951, 7957, 9007); "stealing" represents applying that truth to evil (section 5135); and "selling" represents **alienation** <note>The act of distancing oneself from a spiritual truth or losing ownership of it in one's heart.</note> (sections 4098, 4752, 4758, 5886).

**9019.** **And if he shall be found in his hand.** That this signifies that the person nevertheless acknowledges the truth of faith is evident from the meaning of being "found in the hand." When speaking of a truth of faith, this means acknowledgment; for when a truth is acknowledged with any degree of faith, it is said to be "found" with that person, and "in his hand" means it remains with them.

**9020.** **Dying he shall die.** That this signifies damnation, see above (section 9008). The reason those who apply the truths of faith to evils—and thus distance themselves from those truths—are damned, is that they had previously acknowledged them. When a truth of faith that was once acknowledged is later used to justify evil, it becomes mixed with the falsehood that comes from that evil. ### CHAPTER XXI. VERSES 16, 17

**9021.** ...representative of a church was at that time being instituted, and by whom therefore the church was signified <note>The author refers to the ancient Israelites as a "representative" church, meaning their outward actions and laws were designed to mirror deeper spiritual realities.</note> (n. 6426, 6637, 6862, 6868, 7035, 7062, 7198, 7201, 7215, 7223, 7957, 8234, 8805). Therefore also by “cursing father and mother” is signified **profanation** <term>profanation<note>In this context, profanation is the act of someone who has known and acknowledged spiritual truths later turning against them or treating them with contempt.</note></term>, for those within the church who wholly deny the Lord and the things which are of His kingdom and church, profane them. **9022.** *Dying he shall die* <note>original Latin: *moriendo morietur*, a Hebrew idiom emphasizing the certainty of the outcome.</note>, signifies **damnation** (as above, n. 9008, 9016, 9020).—How the particulars in the **internal sense** <term>internal sense<note>The hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and laws.</term></note> cohere together, is evident from what has been said and shown. For the internal sense treats in a series of the denial, blaspheming, and profanation of the truth and good which are from the Lord. But in the **external sense** <term>external sense<note>The literal, historical, or legal meaning of the text as it appears on the surface.</note></term> no such series appears, for in this sense various things are treated of; as those who smite a man so that he dies; those who kill a companion with deceit; those who smite father and mother; those who steal a man and sell him; and those who curse father and mother. Such is the Word in its particulars, namely, that in the internal sense things follow in order and as it were in a chain; although in the external sense, that is, in the sense of the letter, they are scattered, and in many places disconnected.

**9024.** **And when men shall dispute.** That this signifies contention among themselves about truths, is evident from the meaning of "disputing," as being to contend; and from the meaning of "men" <note>original Latin: *viri*. This specific term for "men" usually implies those who are intelligent or possessors of truth.</note>, as being those who are intelligent and who are in truths, and in the abstract sense, things of the intellect and truths; consequently "the disputing of men" signifies contention about truths among those who are of the church, and in the abstract sense, about truths among themselves. 

For in the **spiritual sense** <term>spiritual sense<note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that describes the development of the human soul and the nature of heaven.</note></term> "to dispute" denotes to contend about such things as are of the church, and consequently such as are of faith. Nothing else is meant in the Word <note>The "Word" is a term used here to refer to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> by "disputing," for the Word is spiritual and treats of spiritual things—that is, of those things which belong to the Lord, His kingdom in heaven, and His kingdom on the earth, which is the church. That in the Word "to dispute" signifies contention about truths, and in general in favor of truths against falsities, and likewise defense and liberation from falsities, is plain from the following passages:

> A tumult is come even to the end of the earth; for Jehovah hath a **dispute** against the nations, He will enter into judgment with all flesh; He will deliver the wicked to the sword. Behold evil shall go forth from nation to nation, and a great tempest shall be raised up from the sides of the earth (Jeremiah 25:31, 32);

These are factual pieces of information from the Bible stored in the memory before they are fully understood or applied to life.</note></term>, and differ from the truths of faith which are of the **doctrine of the church**. Hence also it is that in very many cases the doctrines of the church depart from the **literal sense** of the Word.

[3] Among priests, and among the men of the church, there are those who teach and who learn the truths of the church from the <term>literal sense</term> of the Word; and there are those who teach and those who learn from doctrine drawn from the Word, which is called the **doctrine of faith** of the church. The latter differ very much from the former in perception, but they cannot be distinguished by the common people, because they both speak from the Word nearly alike. 

But those who teach and who learn only the <term>literal sense</term> of the Word without the doctrine of the church as a guide, apprehend only those things which belong to the **natural or external man**; whereas those who teach and who learn from true doctrine drawn from the Word, understand also things which are of the **spiritual or internal man**. The reason is that the Word in the external or **literal sense** is natural, but in the <term>internal sense</term> it is spiritual. The former sense is called in the Word a **“cloud,”** but the latter sense is called the **“glory”** in the cloud (n. 5922, 6343, 6752, 8106, 8781). 

[4] From all this it can now be seen what is meant by **“contention among themselves about truths,”** and by the **“invalidating of some one [truth of the church] by means of some memory or general truth.”** As before said, **memory or general truth** is truth from the <term>literal sense</term> of the Word. And as this varies, and as it were contradicts itself, according to the appearance, it must needs sometimes invalidate the spiritual truths which are of the doctrine of the church. These are invalidated when the thought comes into doubt from passages in the Word that are seemingly contradictory.

**9026.** *And he does not die.* That this signifies that it is not extinguished is evident from the meaning of "dying," which is to cease to be such as one was before (see numbers 494, 6587, 6593); consequently, "to die" means to be extinguished, and here "not to die" means not to be extinguished. 

Since the <term>internal sense</term> here deals with the agreement of the <term>truths of faith</term> with the truths of the <term>literal sense</term> of the Word, and since the truths of the literal sense cannot be extinguished—as they are truths in the <term>ultimate of order</term><note>The "ultimate of order" refers to the most basic, physical level of reality or the literal words of Scripture, which serve as a foundation for higher spiritual truths.</note>—the text does not discuss a blow that causes death. Instead, it speaks only of a blow from which a person does not die. This is because the truths of the literal sense of the Word can indeed be invalidated or weakened, but they cannot be completely destroyed. Furthermore, after they have been invalidated, they can be set aside; yet, by an unfolding of their true meaning, they can be restored. These concepts are symbolized by the laws decreed about a man who is struck by his companion but rises again and walks upon his staff.

[2] Anyone who investigates the deeper contents of the Word can see that there is a secret reason why the Lord decreed that the one who struck the blow should be guiltless if the victim recovered and walked abroad with a staff. This reason does not become clear to the understanding unless it is enlightened by the light of heaven. It is especially mysterious that the Lord decreed that a master who strikes his servant should not be punished if the servant survives for a day or two, "because he is his silver" <note>Original Latin: *quia argentum ejus est*. In this spiritual system, "silver" symbolizes truth or knowledge purchased for the mind.</note>. On the surface, this seems to be the taking of a human life, for a servant is a man even though he is in service. 

But the secret reason why this was decreed by the Lord does not appear except through the <term>internal sense</term>. This sense deals with the truths of the church derived from the Word. The situation is similar when the text speaks of "a man disputing and striking his neighbor," and "a man striking his male or female servant." In the spiritual sense, these scenarios correspond to specific internal realities, which are now being explained. Among the Israelite nation, a <term>representative church</term><note>A form of worship where physical objects and outward actions symbolize deep spiritual and heavenly realities.</note> was established—that is, a church in which the internal things of heaven and the church were represented by external things. ### N. 9031] CHAPTER XXI. VERS. 18-21

He is called the “Sunrise,” or “East,” <note>original: "Oriens." In Swedenborg's Latin, this term refers both to the direction of the rising sun and to the Lord as the source of all spiritual light.</note> and He is never in any setting; nor does He turn Himself away from man, but man turns himself away from Him. From this arises the appearance that the Lord turns away His face and also brings evil; and therefore it is also so said in the Word. This likewise is the truth, but **apparent truth**, thus it is not in conflict with the former. From all this it can now be seen what is meant in the <term>internal sense<note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the surface-level stories and laws.</note></term> by “healing he shall heal,” namely, the restoration of **spiritual truth**, which is effected by means of a right interpretation of the <term>memory-truth<note>Information or facts stored in the mind (scientificum) that have not yet been fully lived or understood spiritually.</note></term>, or that of the <term>literal sense<note>The plain, surface-level meaning of the words in the Bible.</note></term> of the Word. 

[2] The case is similar with every truth of the **literal sense**, for in the <term>natural light<note>The intellectual perspective of the physical world and the five senses.</note></term>, which is that of the <term>sensuous man<note>A person who judges reality solely based on what they can see, touch, and feel in the physical world.</note></term>, this appears just as it is expressed in the Word, because the **literal sense** is natural, and is for the **sensuous man**. But when the same is presented in the light of heaven, it then appears according to the **internal sense**; for this sense is spiritual, and is for the <term>heavenly man<note>A person whose mind is open to spiritual wisdom and divine love.</note></term>, because those things which are of **natural light** vanish away in the light of heaven; for **natural light** is like shade or cloud, and heavenly light is like the glory and the brightness when the cloud is taken away. And therefore also the **literal sense** of the Word is called “a cloud,” and the **internal sense** “glory” (see the preface to *Genesis* xviii., and n. 4391, 5922, 6343, 8106, 8443, 8781). 

[3] By “healing he shall heal” is signified in the spiritual sense to restore, because disease and sickness signify the infirmity of the internal man, which infirmity exists when he is sick in respect to his life, which is the spiritual life; thus when he turns aside from truth to falsity, and from good to evil. When this is the case, the spiritual life sickens; and when he wholly turns himself away from truth and good, it dies; but this death is called “**spiritual death**,” which is damnation. As this is the case with the life of the internal man, therefore such things as relate to diseases and death in the natural world are said in the Word of the diseases of the spiritual life, and of its death. So also the cures of diseases, or healings, as in *Isaiah*:—

> Jehovah smiteth Egypt, smiting and healing; whence he turneth himself unto Jehovah, and He shall be entreated for them, and shall heal them (xix. 22).

### 9032. 

In the last two verses the subject treated of is **spiritual truth**, which is the truth of the doctrine of faith from the Word, invalidated by means of **memory-truth** <term>Latin: *scientificum veri*; facts or verses held in the memory from the literal text of the Bible</term>, which is the truth of the literal sense of the Word. But as it is commonly believed that the truth of the doctrine of faith of the church is one and the same thing with the truth of the literal sense of the Word, the subject may be illustrated by an example. 

The genuine truth of the doctrine of the church is that **charity toward the neighbor** and **love to the Lord** make the church with man, and that these loves are insinuated by the Lord through faith, that is, by means of the truths of faith which are from the Word, consequently that faith alone does not make the church with man. <note>Swedenborg argues against "faith alone," suggesting that belief without active love (charity) is spiritually incomplete.</note> He who is in this truth, and consults the Word, is everywhere confirmed therein. But when he meets with words about faith, and no mention is made at the same time of love, he hesitates, and begins to revolve doubts with respect to the truth of the doctrine of his faith. Consequently this truth is for the time invalidated, and is separated from the other truths which are of undoubted faith.

But when this **memory-truth**, that is, truth of the literal sense of the Word, is viewed interiorly, it is plain that it nevertheless does agree with the truth of doctrine; for in the **internal sense** <term>the deeper, spiritual meaning of Scripture intended for the soul</term> by "being baptized" is signified to be **regenerated** <term>the process of being spiritually reborn and transformed by God</term> (see n. 4255, 5120), and to be regenerated is to be led into the good of love and charity by means of the truths of faith (n. 8548—8553, 8635—8640, 8742—8747). <meta>This page continues the commentary on Exodus 21:18-19, concluding the discussion on how spiritual truth is invalidated and restored. # EXODUS

...the reason why it is said that "**he that believeth not shall be condemned**" <note>Mark 16:16</note> is that such a person cannot be "**baptized**"—that is, **regenerated** <term>the process of spiritual rebirth and personal transformation</term>—and thus cannot be introduced into the church, much less become a church themselves. For baptism is a symbol of regeneration and of being brought into the church, which happens when one is led into a life of goodness through the truths found in the Word.

[3] From all this, it is now clear what is meant in the **internal sense** <term>the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal words</term> by the law that if a man strikes his companion with a stone or his fist, and the man does not die but is bedridden, then rises to walk with his staff, the one who struck him shall be guiltless, but "he should pay for his loss of time, and should heal him." In the internal sense, this means that if a truth of the church’s faith is weakened by a **memory-truth** <term>Latin: *scientificum veri*; factual knowledge or verses from the literal text of the Bible stored in the memory</term> taken from the literal sense of the Word, but is not completely destroyed, it shall be repaired and restored. This restoration is achieved through a correct interpretation.

### 9033.

The weakening of spiritual truth—the actual genuine faith of the church—was the subject of the previous two verses. In the two verses that follow, the subject is the weakening of **memory-truth**, which is the truth found in the literal sense of the Word. This literal truth appears to be the same as spiritual truth, but it is not. To make this clear, consider this example:

It is a **spiritual truth**, a genuine truth of the church's faith, that the Lord punishes no one. Because He is mercy itself, everything He does is done from mercy, and never from anger or a desire for revenge. And yet, the Lord says in *Matthew*:

> Be ye not afraid of those who are able to kill the body, but rather fear Him who is able to destroy both body and soul in **Gehenna** <note>Matthew 10:28. "Gehenna" (Greek/Hebrew origin) refers here to a state of spiritual destruction or hell.</note> (x. 28);

In this passage, it is said that God is "to be feared" because He "is able to destroy body and soul in Gehenna," even though He actually destroys no one. Nevertheless, this is a truth, and therefore it must not be "extinguished"—that is, denied. For if the literal Word is denied, faith in the Word perishes; and if faith perishes, a person cannot live spiritually, because spiritual life comes through faith derived from the Word.

[2] The reality of the matter is this: it is a law of **Divine order** that goodness should have its own reward—and thus heaven—within itself. Because of this same order, evil has its own punishment within itself...

To do so would extinguish the faith of those who are **simple** <note>people who believe the Bible's literal stories with a sincere heart but do not yet grasp deeper spiritual complexities</note>, for whom this faith is intended (see n. 2447, 6071, 6991, 6997, 7533, 7632, 7643, 7679, 7710, 7877, 7926, 8197, 8227, 8228, 8282, 8483, 8631, 8632, 9010).

### 9034.

**"And when a man shall smite his manservant, or his maidservant, with a rod."** That this signifies if any one within the church ill-treats the **memory-truth** <term>Latin: *scientificum veri*; factual knowledge or literal verses from the Word stored in the memory</term>, or the affection for it, from his own power, is evident from the following:
* **"Smiting"** signifies to ill-treat, for "smiting" is used to describe any kind of injury whatsoever.
* **"A man"** (*vir*) <note>Latin: *vir*, referring specifically to a man who possesses spiritual truth or belongs to the church</note>, here meaning one of the sons of Israel, signifies someone who is of the church and who is consequently in spiritual truth (which is the truth of the church's doctrine from the Word).
* **"A manservant"** signifies memory-truth, which is the truth of the Word, specifically in its literal sense (as discussed below).
* **"A maidservant"** signifies natural affection—the desire for memory-knowledges—because these reside in the **natural** <term>the outer level of the mind that deals with the physical world</term>.
* **"A rod"** signifies natural power, and in this case, one's own power (the ego), because the manservant in question was "bought" (indicating ownership).

From this it is plain that by the words, "if a man shall smite his manservant, or his maidservant," it is signified that someone within the church is damaging the literal truths of the Word or the affection felt for them.

[2] The reason why a "manservant" denotes the truth of the literal sense of the Word is that a "servant" in general signifies lower or exterior things, because these serve higher or interior things. Consequently, a "servant" signifies the **natural**, because the natural serves the **spiritual**; and therefore it signifies memory-truth, which belongs...

# EXODUS [N. 9034]

...to the **literal sense** <term>the plain, historical meaning of the biblical text</term> of the Word, for this serves **spiritual truth** <note>truth that relates to the inner life and heaven</note>, which belongs to the **internal sense** <term>the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible</term>. The truth of the internal sense of the Word is the same as the genuine truth of the doctrine of faith of the church. 

[3] How the truth of the literal sense of the Word serves spiritual truth shall be briefly told. The person of the church first learns truth from the literal sense of the Word, which is **general truth** <note>broad, simplified concepts suited for beginners</note> accommodated to the understanding of the **external man** <term>the part of our personality that interacts with the physical world</term>, who exists in **natural light** <note>intellectual light derived from the world and the senses</note>. This truth is received by an external way—that is, by hearing—and is stored up in the memory of the external man, where there are also various **memory-knowledges** <term>Latin: *scientifica*; factual data or information gathered from the world</term> (see n. 2469–2494). 

Afterward, the things stored up in this memory are subjected to the sight or view of the **internal man** <term>the higher, spiritual part of the mind</term>, who sees from the light of heaven. The internal man selects from that memory the truths which agree with the **good** <note>love, kindness, and divine order</note> which flows in from the Lord by way of the soul, and which the person had received. There, the Lord conjoins these truths with good. The truths which are thus joined together in the internal man are called "spiritual truths," and the good with which the truths are joined is called "spiritual good." This good, formed by means of truths, is what makes the spiritual life of man. The truths themselves there are called "the truths of faith," and the good is called "the good of charity." The good in which truths have thus been implanted is what constitutes the church within a person. 

[4] From this it is plain in what manner the truths of the literal sense of the Word serve for the formation of spiritual truths—and in general for the formation of faith and of charity, which make the spiritual life. This life consists in being moved by truths for the sake of good, and in being moved by good because of truths, and finally in being moved by truths because they come from good.

For by the **"hand"** is signified the power which belongs to spiritual truth (n. 5327, 5328, 7011); thus, that which belongs to the "view" or "notice," for this notice is achieved by the power of this truth. **9038.** *He shall not be avenged.* That this signifies no punishment of death, is evident from the signification of “vengeance being taken,” as being the punishment of death (see above, n. 9036).

That is called “truth acquired by one’s own” which, by induction from principles conceived from one’s own <term>Latin: *proprium*; the self-centered part of human nature</term>, is believed to be truth, and yet is not truth. <meta>This page continues the commentary on Exodus 21:21, specifically examining the phrase "he shall not be avenged" and what it means to take a "full view" of a spiritual truth before rejecting or confirming it.</meta>

# EXODUS [N. 9039]

...full view, there is **damnation** <term>the state of being cut off from divine life</term>, because there is a rejection of the truth of faith itself. For that which has been made of any one’s faith, even if it is not true, ought not to be rejected, except after taking a full view; if it is rejected sooner, the first beginning of the man’s spiritual life is plucked up by the roots; and therefore the **Lord** never breaks such truth with a man, but as far as possible bends it. 

Let an example serve for illustration. [2] He who believes that the glory and therefore the joy of heaven consist in rule over many, and from this conceived principle explains the Lord’s words concerning the servants who gained ten pounds and five pounds, that they should have power over ten cities and over five cities (*Luke* 19:11); and also the Lord’s words to the disciples, that they should sit upon thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel (*Luke* 22:30); if before taking a full view he extinguishes his faith—which is a faith of truth from the **literal sense** <note>the surface-level or historical meaning of the scripture</note> of the **Word** <note>the Holy Scripture or Divine Revelation</note>—he occasions the loss of his spiritual life. 

But if after taking a full view, he interprets these words of the Lord from His other words—that “whosoever will be greatest must be the least,” and “whosoever would be the first must be the servant of all” (*Matthew* 20:26-28; *Mark* 10:42-45; *Luke* 22:24-27); if he then extinguishes his faith as regards heavenly glory and joy from rule over many, he does not occasion the loss of his spiritual life; for by the “cities” over which those were to have power who gained the pounds are signified the **truths of faith** (n. 2268, 2449, 2712, 2943, 3216), and the derivative intelligence and wisdom; in like manner by the “thrones” upon which the disciples were to sit (n. 2129, 6937).

[3] Those in heaven who are pre-eminently in intelligence and wisdom from the truths of faith, are in such **humiliation** <note>a state of self-acknowledgment that all good comes from the Divine</note> that they attribute everything of power to the Lord, and nothing to themselves; and therefore they do not make anything of glory and joy to consist in ruling, but in serving; and when they are in this state, they are in rule, and also in glory and joy, above others; yet not as before said from the love of rule, but from the affection of love and **charity** <note>the desire to do good for others without thought of reward</note>, which is that of serving others. For the Lord flows with power into those who are humble; but not into those who are puffed up, because the former receive **influx** <term>the continuous flow of life and light from the Divine into the human mind</term>, but the latter reject it (n. 7489-7492).

# CHAPTER XXI. VERSES 22–27

**9040.** **Verses 22–27.** *And when men shall quarrel, and shall strike a pregnant woman, and her births go forth, and harm is not done, with fining he shall be fined, as the woman's master shall lay upon him; and he shall give according to the judges. And if harm is done, then thou shalt give soul for soul, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burning for burning, wound for wound, blow for blow. And when a man shall smite the eye of his manservant, or the eye of his maidservant, and shall destroy it; he shall let him go free for his eye. And if he shall knock out his manservant's tooth, or his maidservant's tooth; he shall let him go free for his tooth.*

“And when men shall quarrel,” signifies a severe conflict or contention between different truths; “and shall strike a pregnant woman,” signifies the harming of the good <note>original: *bonum*, the inherent goodness or spiritual potential</note> which arises from truth; “and her births go forth,” signifies if the truth or state of life is nonetheless confirmed and takes root in the natural mind; “and harm is not done,” signifies that no spiritual injury occurred there; “with fining he shall be fined,” signifies a process of amendment or correction; “as the woman's master shall lay upon him,” signifies until the situation agrees with the truth of good; “and he shall give according to the judges,” signifies according to what is equitable and fair. 

“And if harm is done,” signifies a spiritual injury; “then thou shalt give **soul for soul**,” signifies the **law of order** <term>lex talionis: the law of spiritual reciprocity where one's actions toward others inevitably shape one's own spiritual state</term> which dictates that you should do to your neighbor as you would have them do to you—consequently, what you do to another shall be done to yourself; the “soul” here denotes the spiritual life. 

“Eye for eye,” signifies if anything is injured in the **interior intellectual** <note>the deeper capacity for spiritual understanding</note>; “tooth for tooth,” signifies if anything is injured in the **exterior intellectual** <note>the surface-level or sensory understanding</note>; “hand for hand,” signifies an injury to the power of spiritual truth; “foot for foot,” signifies an injury to the power of natural truth; “burning for burning,” signifies an injury to the affection of love which resides deep within the will; “wound for wound,” signifies an injury to the affection of love that exists in the outer will; “blow for blow,” signifies an injury to the affection within the intellect—that is to say, if any of these spiritual faculties are extinguished or damaged. 

“And when a man shall smite the eye of his manservant,” signifies if the **internal man** <note>the higher, spiritual part of the human being</note> should injure the truth of faith in the **external or natural man** <note>the lower, worldly part of the human being</note>; “or the eye of his maidservant,” signifies the injury of the affection for truth in that natural man; “and shall destroy it,” signifies if he shall completely extinguish that truth; “he shall let...”

<summary>This page provides a spiritual interpretation of the biblical laws of "an eye for an eye," explaining how physical injuries represent damage to specific levels of human understanding and the spiritual will.</summary>

For when a person is born anew <note>Refers to the process of spiritual awakening and character transformation.</note>, they are first conceived, then carried as if in a womb, and finally born. Because regeneration, or the generation of spiritual life, is the joining together of truth and good (that is, of faith and charity), "carrying in the womb" signifies the first introduction of truth into good. 

From this it is plain what is signified by "a pregnant woman," namely, the state where spiritual "good" is being formed out of "truths." (That "the womb" denotes where truth and good lie conceived, see n. 4918, 6433; and that "to be in the womb," and "to come forth from the womb" denote the process of being regenerated, n. 4904, 8043; also that "generations" and "births" denote the developments of faith and charity, n. 613, 1145, 1255, 2020, 2584, 6239.)

Until there is agreement,” signifies restoration for the injury caused by an untimely birth. **9047.** *And he shall give according to the judges.* This signifies that the restoration must be according to what is equitable. If the amount is too much or too little, the judges ensure it is made equal.

**9048.** *And if harm is done.* This signifies injury, which is clear without further explanation.

**9049.** *Then thou shalt give soul for soul.* This signifies the law of order: that you should do to your neighbor as you would have another do to you. Consequently, whatever you do to another will be done to you. This is evident because the phrase “to give soul for soul, eye for eye, tooth for tooth,” and so on, means that your actions toward others will return to you. 

The reason this law was given to the children of Israel is that it is the actual law of the spiritual world. In that world, anyone who does good to another from their heart receives that same good back. Conversely, anyone who does evil to another from their heart receives that same evil back. This is because good from the heart is naturally joined to its reward, and evil from the heart is naturally joined to its punishment; this is why heaven exists for the good and hell for the evil. 

I have been allowed to know that this is true through much personal experience. The situation is this: for a person who does good from the heart, goodness flows into their heart and soul from heaven from every side. This inflow inspires them and, at the same time, increases their affection of love for the neighbor to whom they are doing the good.

## [N. 9050 Continued]

"To draw out thy soul to the hungry" <note>This quote is from Isaiah 58:10.</note> denotes a desire to instruct others in the truths of faith; and "to sate the afflicted soul" denotes to instruct others in the good of faith. [8] In *Jeremiah*:—

> Though thou clothest thyself with double-dyed <note>Referring to scarlet or crimson fabrics, often symbolizing outward appearances or intellectual pride.</note>, though thou deckest thee with ornament of gold, though thou rendest thine eyes with antimony <note>A dark mineral used as eye makeup in antiquity, here symbolizing an attempt to make false doctrines appear beautiful.</note>, in vain shalt thou make thyself beauteous; thy lovers will abhor thee, they will seek thy soul (iv. 30);

here "soul" denotes the life of faith, and consequently faith itself in man, because this constitutes his spiritual life. That faith is meant by "soul" is plain from the specific details in this verse. In the same prophet:—

> They shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow together unto the good of Jehovah, to the wheat, and to the new wine, and to the oil, and to the sons of the flock and of the herd; and their soul shall become as a watered garden; I will water the weary soul, and every sorrowful soul (xxxi. 12, 25);

"the soul" denotes the life of faith in the person of the church, who is said "to become as a garden," because by "a garden" is signified the <term>intelligence</term> <note>The ability to perceive and understand spiritual truths.</note> which comes from the truths of faith (see references n. 100, 108, 2702); and the soul is said to be "watered," because by "being watered" is signified to be instructed. [9] In the same prophet:—

> We bring our bread with the peril of our souls, because of the sword of the wilderness (*Lamentations v. 9*);

"the peril of souls" denotes the danger of losing one's faith and consequently one's spiritual life; for "the sword of the wilderness" denotes <term>falsity</term> <note>Spiritual error or incorrect beliefs that attack true faith.</note> fighting against the truths of faith (n. 2799, 4499, 6353, 7102, 8294). In *Ezekiel*:—

> Javan, Tubal, and Meshech <note>Ancient names used here to represent specific types of spiritual or intellectual groups.</note>, these were thy traders, with the soul of man, and with vessels of brass, they furnished thy trading (xxvii. 13);

"the soul of man" denotes the interior truth of faith derived from what is good; "vessels of brass" denote exterior truths of faith from good; "vessels" denoting exterior truths or <term>memory-truths</term> <note>Facts and information stored in the mind, which serve as the "containers" for deeper spiritual understanding.</note> (see n. 3068, 3079), and "brass" denoting the good of the natural man (n. 425, 1551). Unless it were known that "the soul of man" denotes faith, it could not be understood what is signified by "trading with the soul of man, and with vessels of brass." [10] In the same:—

## [N. 9050 Continued]

> Every living soul that creepeth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live; whence there is exceeding much fish; because these waters are come hither, and are healed (Ezekiel xlvii. 9);

In this passage, the prophet is speaking of the new temple, which represents a new spiritual church established by the Lord. Here, "the living soul that creepeth" refers to <term>memory-truths</term> <note>These are basic truths of faith stored in the memory before they are fully lived or understood.</note> that belong to faith. The "much fish" mentioned signifies <term>memory-knowledges</term> <note>original: "scientifica"; these are factual pieces of information or external data about spiritual things.</note> (see references n. 40, 991). The "rivers" signify things belonging to intelligence, which flow from the truths of faith (n. 2702, 3051). Without understanding the internal spiritual sense, it would be impossible to know why "much fish" results from the arrival of these rivers. Again, we read:

> Save me, O God, for the waters are come even unto my soul (Psalm lxix. 1).
> The waters compassed me about, even to my soul (Jonah ii. 5).

In these passages, "waters" represent falsities, and they also signify the spiritual trials or temptations caused when such falsities are injected into a person's mind (n. 705, 739, 756, 790, 8137, 8138, 8368). [11] In the book of *Jeremiah*:

> Jehovah said, Shall not My soul be avenged on such a nation as this? (v. 9, 29).
> Admit chastisement, O Jerusalem, lest My soul be turned away from thee, and I make thee a waste (vi. 8).

When the term "the soul" is predicated of the Lord <note>That is, when the Bible speaks of God having a "soul."</note>, it signifies Divine truth. In the book of *John*:

> The second angel poured out his vial into the sea, and it became blood as of a dead man, whence every living soul died in the sea (Revelation xvi. 3);

In this context, "the sea" signifies the entire complex of memory-knowledges (n. 28). "Blood" represents the truths of faith originating from good, but in the opposite sense—as used here—it represents those truths when they have been falsified and profaned (n. 4735, 6978, 7317, 7326). Consequently, the "living soul" here refers to the spiritual life that is derived from faith. [12] In *Matthew*:

> Be not anxious for your soul, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink (vi. 25);

Here, "soul" signifies the truths of faith, while "eating" and "drinking" signify being instructed in the "good" and "truth" of faith. In the internal sense, this passage is dealing with spiritual life and how it is nourished. Again:

> Whoever will find his soul shall lose it, and whoever shall lose his soul for My sake shall find it (Matthew x. 39);

...predicated of the Lord, it represents Divine Truth. Thus,] “the soul” denotes the life of faith such as it is with those who believe, and in the opposite sense the life not of faith such as it is with those who do not believe. In the Gospel of *Luke*:

> In your patience possess ye your souls (xxi. 19);

To “possess the souls” denotes those things which belong to faith and, consequently, to spiritual life. The meaning is similar in very many other passages.

**9051.** **Eye for eye.** That this signifies if they shall injure anything in the <term>interior intellectual</term> <note>This refers to the inner capacity of the human mind to grasp spiritual truths, as opposed to mere worldly facts.</note>, is evident from the signification of “the eye,” which represents the understanding. In this specific context, it refers to the interior understanding, the life of which is the life of faith. 

Man possesses both an exterior understanding and an interior understanding. The **exterior understanding** is where the thought is that we are consciously aware of; however, the **interior understanding** is where the thought is that we do not perceive—though it is perceived by angels. This latter understanding is what the Lord enlightens when a person receives faith, for it exists in the light of heaven. Within it resides the spiritual life of man, which is not fully manifest to him while he is in the world, but becomes clear in the afterlife when he becomes an angel among the angels in heaven. 

Meanwhile, this inner life lies hidden within the thoughts of the exterior understanding, where it produces a holy and reverent feeling for the Lord, for love and faith in Him, for the Word, and for all other matters of the church. The reason why “the eye” signifies the understanding is because the eye corresponds to the understanding; the understanding sees by virtue of the light of heaven, while the eye sees by virtue of the light of the world. Those things which the former eye—the understanding—sees are spiritual, and the field of its view consists of <term>memory-knowledges</term> <note>original: "scientifica"; these are the facts and data stored in a person's memory which serve as the foundation for deeper thought.</note> in the human memory. But the things which the external eye sees are earthly, and the field of its view includes everything that appears in the physical world. 

In the spiritual sense, “the eye” denotes the understanding and also faith, because faith constitutes the life of the interior understanding (see n. 2701, 4403–4421, 4523–4534). [2] Anyone who does not know that the understanding is meant in the Word by “the eye” cannot know what is signified by the words the Lord spoke concerning the eye in the Gospels, such as these:

## CHAPTER XXI. VERSES 22–27 [N. 9051 Continued]

...for truth and for the Word, even when the person is not consciously thinking about it.

"If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out; it is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into the <term>Gehenna</term> <note>original: "Gehennam"; This refers to a state of spiritual suffering or "hell," traditionally associated with a valley near Jerusalem used for burning waste.</note> of fire" (*Mark 9:47; Matthew 5:29*). Everyone knows that a physical eye is not literally to be plucked out, even if it causes one to stumble, and that no one actually enters the kingdom of God with only one eye. Rather, by “the right eye,” the scripture signifies a **falsity of faith** regarding the Lord; it is this mistaken belief that must be removed. Again:

> The light of the body is the eye; if therefore your eye be simple, your whole body shall be full of light. But if your eye be evil, your whole body shall be darkened. If therefore the light that is in you be darkness, how great is that darkness! (*Matthew 6:22, 23; Luke 11:34*).

In this passage, "eye" does not refer to the physical organ, but to the **understanding of the truth of faith**. This is why the eye is called “the light of the body,” and why it is said, “if the light that is in you be darkness, how great is the darkness.” In the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that relates to the soul and the afterlife.</note>, “darkness” represents the falsities of faith (refer to notes 1839, 1860, 4418, 4531, 7688, 7711). 

[3] And again:

> Why do you look at the mote that is in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam that is in your own eye? (*Matthew 7:3–5*).

To “behold a mote in the eye of a brother” signifies noticing something erroneous regarding the understanding of truth; whereas “the beam in one’s own eye” signifies a massive evil of falsity. This is because, in the internal sense, “wood” signifies good, and in the opposite sense, evil (notes 643, 2784, 2812, 3720, 8354). Furthermore, in the <term>other life</term> <note>The spiritual world or afterlife.</note>, "good" is represented by a beam; consequently, those who pretend to have goodness in themselves appear to carry a beam, and thus walk about in a state of false security. Without this symbolic meaning of “the eye” and “a beam,” what could be meant by “seeing a beam in the eye”? 

If one does not know that in the Word of God “the eye” signifies the understanding of truth (which is faith), then one cannot understand the deeper meaning of the Lord's actions when He healed a blind man—specifically, when “He spat on the ground and made clay of the spittle, and said to him, 'Wash yourself in the pool of Siloam'” (*John 9:6, 7*). Just as the Lord’s miracles, like all Divine miracles, involved realities concerning the Lord’s kingdom and the church (notes 7337, 8364), so does this specific act.

# EXODUS
### [Number 9052]

“A tooth” signifies the outer intellectual capacity, which is **natural truth**, for this is what constitutes the life of this level of understanding. The reason “teeth” have this symbolic meaning is that they grind like a mill, and in doing so, they prepare the food which is to nourish the body; in this context, they prepare the food which is to nourish the soul. 

The food that nourishes the soul is **intelligence and wisdom**. This is first received, ground, and prepared by means of knowledge and goodness in the <term>natural</term> <note>The "natural" refers to the lowest level of the human mind, which deals with the physical world and literal facts.</note>. (Regarding how intelligence and wisdom are called “spiritual and heavenly food,” see notes 56–58, 680, 1480, 4792, 5147, 5293, 5340, 5342, 5576, 5579, 5915, 8562, and 9003.) From this, it is clear why “the teeth” signify the outer understanding. What the outer understanding is can be seen from what was shown just above (in note 9051) concerning the inner understanding.

[2] That “the teeth” signify natural truth, which belongs to the outer understanding—and, in the opposite sense, the falsity which destroys this truth—is evident from the following passages in the <term>Word</term> <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>. To show that they signify natural truth, we look to the books of *Moses*:

> His eyes shall be redder than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk (*Genesis 49:12*);

Here, both “eyes” and “teeth” are mentioned together. The subject being discussed is Judah, by whom is meant the Lord in regards to the **Divine heavenly** <note>original: "coeleste"; the highest level of divine love.</note> (see note 6363); “the eyes” signify the Lord’s Divine understanding (note 6379); and “the teeth” signify His **Divine natural** (note 6380), and thus also the Divine truth in the natural world.

[3] In the book of *Amos*:

> I have given you emptiness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places (*Amos 4:6*);

In this verse, “emptiness of teeth” denotes a scarcity of truth, and “lack of bread” denotes a scarcity of good. From all this, it is evident what is meant by the “gnashing of teeth” among those who are in hell (*Matthew 8:12; 13:42, 50; 22:13; 25:30; Luke 13:28*), namely, the collision of false ideas with the truths of faith. For as previously stated, “the teeth,” when used in the opposite sense, signify the falsity which destroys truth; as seen in the Psalms of *David*:

> Arise, O Lord <note>original: "Jehovah"</note>; save me, O my God; for You will strike all my enemies on the jaw; You will break the teeth of the wicked (*Psalm 3:7*);
