To “break the teeth of the wicked” means to shatter the <term>falsities</term> <note>In this context, "falsities" refers to distorted or deceptive ideas that specifically target and erode spiritual truths.</note> that they use to destroy what is true. Similarly, in the Psalms:

> My soul lies in the midst of lions; their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword (*Psalm 57:4*);

The “teeth of lions” represent the lies that ruin truths; here, “lions” represent those lies fueled by evil that possess a certain power (see notes 6367, 6369).

->[4] In the same book:<-

> O God, shatter the teeth in their mouths; tear out the grinders of the young lions (*Psalm 58:6*).

->In the Book of Joel:<-

> A nation has invaded My land, powerful and beyond counting; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the grinders of a great lion. It has reduced My vine to a wasteland and turned My fig tree into splinters (Joel 1:6, 7);

In this passage, “teeth” and “grinders” represent the lies that destroy the core truths of the church. The “vine” symbolizes the <term>spiritual church</term> <note>The "spiritual church" refers to a community or state of mind governed by intellectual truth and charity.</note> (notes 1069, 5113, 6376), while the “fig tree” represents its <term>natural good</term> <note>The "natural good" refers to the basic, practical kindness and morality found in everyday life.</note> (notes 217, 4231, 5113). It is clear that “teeth” carry this meaning because they are attributed to a nation that brings total destruction.

->In the Book of John:<-

> The shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for battle; they had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like the teeth of lions (Revelation 9:7, 8);

“Locusts” represent those who are caught up in external or superficial lies (note 7643). This further demonstrates that “teeth” symbolize the deceptive ideas that consume and destroy truths.

**9053.** **Hand for hand.** This signifies that a part of the power of **spiritual truth** was either damaged or destroyed by them. This is evident from the symbolic meaning of the “hand,” which represents the power that comes from truth (see notes 3091, 3387, 4931–4937, 6292, 6947, 7188, 7189, 7518, 7673, 8050, 8153, 8281). Specifically, it refers to the power originating from spiritual truth (see notes 5327, 5328, 7011).

**9054.** **Foot for foot.** This signifies a loss or injury to the power of **natural truth**. This is shown by the symbolic meaning of the “foot,” which represents the <term>natural</term> <note>The "natural" level of the mind is the part of us that interacts with the physical world and literal facts.</note> (see notes 2162, 3147, 3761, 3986, 4280, 4938–4952). Specifically, it represents the power inherent in natural truth (see notes 5327, 5328).

<meta>This page continues the line-by-line spiritual interpretation of Exodus 21. While the previous page focused on "teeth" and "eyes" as symbols of the understanding, this section moves to the "will," explaining how "burning" symbolizes damage to a person’s inner motivations and loves.</meta>

## [Number 9055]

**9055.** *Burning for burning.* This signifies the potential injury or extinction of the deep-seated affections of love within the <term>will</term> <note>In this theological framework, the "will" is the part of the mind that drives our desires and intentions, as opposed to the "understanding," which handles thoughts and logic.</note>. This meaning is derived from "burning," which symbolizes the damaging or smothering of the "good" that arises from love. 

It is specified as being "in the will" because the good associated with love belongs to the will, whereas the truths associated with faith belong to the understanding (as discussed in notes 9050 and 9051). The reason "burning" refers specifically to the *interior* or inner will is that a "wound" (which is discussed later) represents injury to the *exterior* or outer will. 

As established in the preceding sections, this text describes injuries occurring in both the "internal man" and the "external man" <note>The "internal man" refers to our higher spiritual self, while the "external man" refers to our natural, worldly self.</note>. To summarize the map of the human spirit provided so far:
*   **The Eye:** Injury to the inner understanding.
*   **The Tooth:** Injury to the outer understanding.
*   **The Hand:** Injury to the power of truth in the inner self.
*   **The Foot:** Injury to the power of truth in the outer self.

Following this pattern, **burning** represents injury to the will of the inner self, and a **wound** represents injury to the will of the outer self.

[2] Just as a person has an inner and outer understanding, they also have an inner and outer will. These must work in harmony. The inner will resides where the inner understanding is, and the outer will resides where the outer understanding is. They are designed to be joined together because wherever truth exists, there must also be "good" (the practical application or essence of that truth). Truth without good is not truly truth, and good without truth is not truly good; good is the very <term>being</term> <note>original: "esse"</note> of truth, and truth is the <term>coming-forth</term> <note>original: "existere"; this refers to how a hidden essence becomes visible or active in the world.</note> of good. 

The same applies to the human mind: the understanding is designed to receive truth, and the will is designed to receive good. From this, it is clear that when a person is being <term>regenerated</term> <note>Regeneration is the process of spiritual rebirth or character transformation.</note>, the Lord provides them with a new understanding through the truths of faith and a new will through the good of charity. Both are necessary and must be united for a person to be spiritually renewed.

[3] The reason "burning" specifically represents the injury of love’s "good" is that "fire" symbolizes love in a spiritual sense (see notes 934, 2446, 4906, 5071, 5215, 6314, 6832, 6834, 6849, 7324, 7575, 7852). Consequently, the damage to that love is called <term>concupiscence</term> <note>Concupiscence refers to intense, selfish desires or "cravings" that stem from self-love rather than love for others.</note>. This "burning" of selfish desire is also mentioned in the Book of Isaiah:—

# CHAPTER XXI. VERSES 22-27

> Instead of spice there shall be rottenness; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of curls baldness; and instead of a gown a girding of sackcloth; **burning instead of beauty** (Isaiah 3:24);

[4] This passage speaks of the "daughter of Zion," by whom is signified the <term>celestial church</term> <note>The "celestial church" refers to a state of being or a group of people whose primary motivation is pure love for the Lord, rather than just obedience to rules.</note>—that is, the church which lives in love to the Lord. In this context, "burning" denotes the evil of <term>concupiscence</term> <note>original: "concupiscence" — here meaning an intense, burning desire for selfish or worldly things that consumes the soul's better nature.</note> arising from self-love. 

Anyone who does not know that there is an **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" is the idea that the Bible contains a hidden, spiritual meaning beneath the literal stories and descriptions.</note> in the Word might believe that the "proud ornaments" of the daughters of Zion mentioned in that chapter (Isaiah 3:16–24) refer only to physical jewelry and clothing. Such a person would believe that the Jewish and Israelite people were punished and fell by the sword simply because of their fashion choices, as suggested in verses 25 and 26. 

However, the reality is quite different. Those ornaments actually represent the spiritual and heavenly qualities belonging to that church. Every reader who carefully considers the prophetic passages where "Zion" or the "daughter of Zion" is mentioned will see that these terms do not refer to a literal young woman, but rather signify the church itself.

**9056. *Wound for wound.*** This signifies that if any part of the "affection of love" which resides in the **exterior will** is injured, a corresponding spiritual consequence follows. This is evident from the meaning of a "wound," which symbolizes an injury to the affections—and because affection is a matter of love, it belongs to the <term>will</term> <note>The faculty of the mind responsible for our desires, choices, and loves.</note>. 

The reason this refers specifically to the **exterior** (outer) will is that "burning" (discussed in number 9055) signifies an injury to the affection within the **interior** (inner) will. In the Word, a clear distinction is made between a "wound" and a "blow":
*   **Wound:** Refers to the destruction or injury of **good** (love and motivation).
*   **Blow:** Refers to the destruction or injury of **truth** (thought and faith).

This distinction is seen in *Isaiah*:

> From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but **wound**, and bruise, and fresh **blow**; they have not been pressed out, nor bound up, nor mollified with oil (Isaiah 1:6);

In this verse, "wound" refers to the loss of "good," while "blow" refers to the loss of "truth."

**9057. *Blow for blow.*** This signifies that if any part of the affection in the **intellectual** <note>The "intellectual" part of the mind refers to the understanding or the faculty of thought.</note> is extinguished or injured, there is a spiritual penalty. This is clear from the symbolic meaning of a "blow" as the harming of the affection associated with the understanding—that is, the...

# EXODUS

[N. 9057]

...affection of truth. In the original tongue <note>original: Hebrew "chabburah," referring to a bruise or weal.</note> "blow" is expressed by a term which signifies the black and blue from a collection of blood or of bloody matter, and in the **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" is the idea that the Bible contains a hidden, spiritual meaning beneath the literal stories and descriptions.</note> "blood" denotes the truth of faith from the good of love, and in the opposite sense, truth falsified and profaned (see n. 4735, 6978, 7317, 7326); consequently "blow for blow" denotes truth injured or extinguished. 

This is also signified by the "blows" (or "plagues") in the *Revelation* ix. 20; xi. 6; xv. 1, 6, 8; xvi. 21; xviii. 8; also in *Jeremiah* xxx. 12, 14, 17; l. 13; in *Zechariah* xiv. 12–15; in *David*, *Ps*. xxxviii. 5; and in *Luke* x. 30–35, in the parable of him that fell among thieves, who inflicted blows on him and left him half dead; and it is said that a Samaritan "bound up his blows," pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn. 

[2] He who understands the **internal sense** of the Word is able to know why it was said by the Lord that the Samaritan "bound up the blows, poured in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast." For by "the Samaritan" in the internal sense is meant one who is in the **affection of truth** <note>A "desire for truth," or a state of mind where one loves to learn what is true for the sake of living rightly.</note>, by "binding up the blows" is signified the healing of this affection when injured, by "pouring in oil and wine" is signified the <term>good of love</term> <note>Love in action; the warmth and kindness that flows from the heart.</note> and the <term>good of faith</term> <note>The clarity and conviction of knowing what is true.</note>, and by "setting him on his own beast" is signified uplifting him by virtue of his own **intellectual** <note>original: "intellectuale" — here referring to the mind’s capacity to understand and process information.</note>. 

Thus by these words is described <term>charity toward the neighbor</term>; naturally for man in the world, and spiritually for the angels in heaven; naturally in the sense of the letter, and spiritually in the internal sense. The reason why a "Samaritan" denotes one who is in the affection of truth, is that "Samaria" in the Word signifies this affection (that "oil" denotes the good of love, see n. 886, 3728, 4582; also that "wine" denotes the good of faith, n. 1798, 6377; and that a "beast of burden" denotes the intellectual, n. 2761, 2762, 2781, 3217, 5321, 5741, 6125, 6401, 6534, 7024, 8146, 8148). In this manner spake the Lord; but few apprehend this, for they believe that such things were said merely for the sake of giving the parable the connection of a narrative; but in this case they would not be words from the Divine. All words from the Divine have within them such things as belong to the Lord, heaven, and the church, and this is the case in every <term>jot</term> <note>original: "iota" — referring to the smallest letter or stroke of a pen, signifying that every tiny detail of the Word has a spiritual purpose.</note> (see above, n. 9049).

# EXODUS

### CHAPTER XXI. VERSES 22–27

**9058.** *And when a man shall smite the eye of his manservant.* This signifies a situation where the **internal man** <note>The "internal man" is the higher, spiritual part of the human mind that is open to heaven.</note> causes injury to the **truth of faith** in the **external man** <note>The "external man" is the lower, natural part of the mind that deals with the physical world and memory.</note>. This is evident from the meaning of “smiting,” which signifies causing injury; and from the meaning of “man” <note>original: Latin "vir"</note>—specifically a man from the children of Israel—which signifies someone belonging to the church who possesses spiritual truth (which is the truth of faith). 

In this context, the “man” represents the **internal man** because the life of that higher mind is formed by the truth of faith. We call it the “internal man” here because of its relationship to the “manservant,” who represents the **external man**. Furthermore, the “eye” signifies the interior understanding and thus the truth of faith; while the “manservant” signifies **memory-truth** <note>Knowledge stored in the mind that has not yet been fully integrated into one's spiritual life.</note> located in the external man. 

In the literal sense of the Bible, the text speaks of a “man” and his “servant” as two separate people. However, in the **internal sense** <note>The "internal sense" refers to the deeper spiritual meaning hidden beneath the literal stories of the Bible.</note>, where “man” is the internal mind and “servant” is the external mind, they both exist within a single person. This is because the spiritual meaning focuses on principles and states of being rather than individual people.

**9059.** *Or the eye of his maidservant.* This signifies a situation where he injures the **affection for truth** <note>The desire or emotional love for learning what is true.</note> in that same part of the mind. This is clear from the meaning of the “eye” as the understanding (as mentioned above), and from the meaning of a “maidservant” as the affection or love for natural truth.

**9060.** *And shall destroy it.* This signifies that he injures it so severely that he extinguishes it. When the Bible speaks of “destroying” in relation to the truth of faith (represented by the eye), it means to completely blot out that understanding.

**9061.** *He shall let him go free for his eye.* This signifies that the external man can no longer serve the internal man. This is evident from the meaning of “letting go free,” which is to release from service, and from the meaning of “for his eye,” which refers to the fact that the truth of faith has been extinguished in the external or natural man. In this state, the eye—the capacity for understanding—has been lost.

<summary>This page provides a spiritual interpretation of Exodus 21:26, explaining that "man," "servant," and "eye" symbolize the interaction between the internal spiritual mind and the external natural mind. It describes how damaging one's understanding of truth disrupts the proper relationship between these two levels of the self.</summary>

**9074.** *The ox shall be stoned.* That this signifies the penalty of destroyed truth, is evident (as above, n. 9067).

**9075.** *And his master also shall die.* That this signifies the damnation of the internal man, is evident from the meaning of "the master of the ox," as being the internal man <note>The "internal man" refers to the higher, spiritual part of a person that is open to heaven, while the "external man" is the part focused on the physical world.</note> (see n. 9069); and from the meaning of "dying," as being damnation (of which above, n. 9008). That the ox was to be stoned and his master was to die if he had known that the ox was prone to strike with the horn and he had not watched him, is because the spiritual meaning of this judgment or law is that the person who knows a thing to be evil, and does not repress it, is guilty; for he approves it, and thus extinguishes the light of truth, and together with it the faith of truth in its beginning stages. When this light is extinguished, goodness from the Lord is not received. Consequently, the internal man cannot be opened, and therefore spiritual life—which is the life of the truth and the good of faith—cannot be given to him. When a person is in such a state, he then lives a natural life, which belongs to the external man. But without spiritual life this life is dead; consequently there is damnation (see n. 7494).

**9076.** *If expiation be laid on him.* That this signifies that he may be free from damnation, is evident from the meaning of "expiation," as being that he may be free from damnation. For expiations were laid upon those who did evil not by deliberate purpose, or with deceit; and they were various, and were in such cases called "redemptions of the soul," for by them the life was redeemed <note>In ancient law, a "redemption" was a payment made to avoid a death penalty. Spiritually, this represents the process of inner change that saves a person from the "death" of their spiritual character.</note>. But these external things signified internal things; namely, "expiation" signified liberation from damnation, and consequently "redemption" signified the improvement of spiritual life through actual repentance. As "expiation" signified liberation from damnation, it consequently also signified the pardon of sins and the resulting cleansing of the spirit.

**9077.** *Then he shall give the redemption of his soul.* That this signifies the difficult and painful aspects of repentance, is evident...

## [N. 9084

**9084.** *And when a man shall open a pit.* That this signifies if any one shall receive falsity from another, is evident from the signification of “a pit,” as being falsity <note>original: "falsum," which in this context refers to a specific incorrect concept or a general state of intellectual error</note> (see n. 4728, 4744, 5038); and from the signification of “opening,” when said of falsity, as being to receive, here from another, because the words follow, “or when a man shall dig a pit,” the meaning of which is, to receive, or to devise of one’s self.

**9085.** *Or when a man shall dig a pit.* That this signifies or if he himself has devised falsity, is evident from the signification of “a pit,” as being falsity; and from the signification of “digging,” as being to receive from one’s self, or to devise (of which just above, n. 9084).

**9086.** *And an ox or an ass shall fall in there.* That this signifies which perverts good or truth in the natural <term>natural: in this system of thought, the "natural" (Latin: "naturale") refers to the outer level of the human mind that interacts with the physical world and thinks in literal terms</term>, is evident from the signification of “to fall,” as being to pervert (of which below); from the signification of “an ox,” as being the affection of evil in the natural, thus evil therein (of which above, n. 9065); and from the signification of “an ass,” as being truth in the natural (n. 2781, 5492, 5741, 7024, 8078). That “to fall into a pit,” when said of good and truth in the natural, which are signified by “ox and ass,” denotes to pervert, is plain from what is contained in the following verse, where amendment by means of truth is treated of, which can be effected with perverted goods and truths, but not with those that have been extinguished; for when good or truth is perverted, it still remains, although explained in a perverted manner. [2] “To fall” also denotes to fall by mischance. Because this was signified by “falling into a pit,” therefore it was said by the Lord:—

> Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fall into a well, and will not straightway draw him out on the Sabbath day? (*Luke* xiv. 5);

this was said by the Lord when He healed on the Sabbath day the man who had the dropsy <note>dropsy: an archaic medical term for edema or swelling; here interpreted spiritually as a condition where the mind is "swollen" with distorted or misunderstood truths</note>. In that church, the Sabbath day was most holy because it signified the heavenly marriage, which is the conjunction of good and truth from the Lord (n. 8495, 8510); consequently healings were performed by the Lord on the Sabbath day, because “healing” involved the healing of the spiritual life; and the disease of dropsy the perversion of truth and good; thus “healing” involved the amendment <note>amendment: here used in the legal and spiritual sense of "setting right" or correcting a fault</note> of those things.

### 9094. *And the dead one also they shall divide.* 

That this signifies that the injuring affection shall also be dissipated, is evident from the meaning of what is "**dead**," which represents evil and falsity (as mentioned above, n. 9008). It is also evident from the meaning of "**to divide**," which signifies to dissipate (n. 9093). 

How the specific details contained in this verse function in their internal sense can only be explained to human understanding with great difficulty. These are matters that can be fully grasped by the angels, but only in a limited way by human beings. This is because angels perceive the **<term>arcana</term>** <note>original: "arcana"; hidden spiritual secrets or inner mysteries of the Divine.</note> of the Word in the light that comes from the Lord. In that light, countless things are visible that cannot be expressed in human speech or even captured by human thought as long as we live in the physical body. 

The reason for this is that, in humans, the light of heaven flows into the light of the world. In doing so, it encounters things in the world that either extinguish, reject, or darken it, making it "dead" to our perception. The cares of the world and the body are such obstacles, especially those arising from the **<term>love of self and the world</term>** <note>The selfish desire for power or material gain that blocks spiritual insight.</note>. Because of this, the things belonging to angelic wisdom are mostly unutterable and incomprehensible to us now. [2] Nevertheless, a person enters into such wisdom after laying aside the body—that is, after death—provided they have received the life of faith while living in the world.

In the spiritual sense, **bonds** are nothing else than the **<term>affections</term>** <note>In this context, "affections" refers to the deep-seated loves or desires that motivate a person's thoughts and actions.</note> of love, for these are what lead a person and what restrain them. If the affections of evil lead them, there must be affections of truth from good to restrain them. Internal bonds in a person are affections for truth and for good. These are also called the “bonds of conscience.” 

But external bonds are the affections of the love of self and the love of the world, for these lead a person in outward matters. If these outward affections come from internal bonds (which are the love of truth and good), they are good; in that case, the person loves themselves and the world not for their own sake, but for the sake of being useful to others (see sections 7819, 7820, 8995). 

But if the affections of the love of self and the world do not come from these internal bonds, the affections are evil and are called **<term>cupidities</term>** <note>Selfish cravings or lusts that focus entirely on one's own desires at the expense of others.</note>; for then the person loves themselves only for their own sake, and the world only for the sake of the world. 

[2] From all this, one can understand what is meant by internal bonds and external bonds, which have been mentioned often. But what we call "bonds" are only truly felt as such when compared to their opposites. Someone who acts from a love for what is good acts from **freedom**; however, someone who acts from a love for what is evil may *seem* to themselves to act from freedom, but they do not. This is because they are acting from selfish cravings that originate from hell. Only those who are in the affection of good are truly free, because they are led by the Lord. This is what the Lord teaches in the Gospel of *John*:

> If you abide in My word, you are truly My disciples; and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. Every one that commits sin is the servant of sin. If the Son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed (*Chapter 8, verses 31, 32, 34, 36*).

To be led by the Lord is freedom, while being led by the cravings of hell is servitude (see sections 892, 905, 2870–2893, 6205, 6477, 8209); for the Lord plants a love for good and a dislike for evil. From this, a person gains freedom in doing good and finds themselves in total servitude when doing evil. Anyone who believes that Christian liberty allows for more than this is greatly mistaken.

### CHAPTER XXI. VERSE 37

The **meaning** <note>The original text uses "signification," a technical term in this system for the spiritual concept represented by a physical word.</note> of the number “five” is that it can represent both a small amount (see sections 4638, 5291) and a large amount (sections 5708, 5956). The term “repaying” signifies making an amendment (section 9087) or a restoration (section 9097). It also signifies a penalty, because when a person's inner “good” has been distanced or alienated, they must undergo hardships to restore it. In this state, a person is either left to face the consequences of their own choices—since evil always carries its own inherent punishment (section 8214)—or they are led into **temptations** <note>In this context, "temptations" refer to internal spiritual struggles or trials that test a person's character.</note> where that evil is conquered and removed. These struggles are the “penalty” signified here by “repaying.” The reason this is a "corresponding" penalty is that the pain of the punishment matches the nature of the original fault (see sections 1857, 6559, 8214).

**9103.** *And four of the flock for one of the flock.* This signifies a corresponding penalty that is complete or "to the full." This is evident from the meaning of the number “four,” which signifies conjunction or connection. “Four” carries a similar meaning to “two,” as it is simply two doubled (for "two" as connection, see sections 5194, 8423; and for "four," see sections 1686, 8877). From this, it follows that these numbers also represent something being "full" or complete, as things that are fully joined together are complete. Furthermore, the phrase “one of the flock” refers to **interior good** <note>Interior good refers to the spiritual motives and love for others that reside in the deeper parts of the soul, rather than just outward behavior.</note> (see section 9099).

The corresponding penalty is signified by “repaying”—specifically, four sheep for one sheep (section 9102). “Interior good” is the quality of **charity** <note>Here, "charity" does not just mean giving to the poor, but a general love for one's neighbor that motivates all actions.</note> as it exists in a person's inner spirit, while “exterior good” is charity as it is expressed in their outward life. This outward good must draw its life from the inner good; for the charity in the inner spirit is the essence of one's spiritual life, and the charity in the outward life is the essence of one's **natural** <note>The "natural life" refers to our everyday existence, emotions, and interactions with the physical world.</note> life. 

This outward good is experienced by a person as a feeling of delight or pleasure. However, the inner good is not felt as a physical sensation; instead, it is experienced as a **perception** <note>Perception is a form of intuitive "seeing" or an inner conviction of truth and rightness.</note> that "this is how things ought to be," which produces a peaceful and contented mind. In the life after death, this spiritual good is also experienced as a tangible sensation.

[2] No one can understand why five oxen were to be repaid for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep, unless they understand the **spiritual sense** <note>The "spiritual sense" is the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that deals with the growth of the soul, hidden beneath the literal laws and stories.</note> of "theft," as well as what is meant by "ox" and "flock." As explained, these terms represent the taking away or distancing of a person's internal and external "good." This loss occurs through the influence of evil and results in spiritual alienation.

<summary>This page explains the symbolic legal requirements for restitution in Exodus, showing how the numbers four and five represent degrees of spiritual restoration and the difference between inner peace and outer pleasure.</summary>

falsity; consequently the penalty and restoration thereof are signified by “five” and “four.” That all numbers in the **Word** <note>The author uses "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible, which he believes contains a hidden, spiritual meaning.</note> signify things, see sections 575, 647, 648, 755, 813, 1963, 1988, 2075, 2252, 3252, 4264, 4495, 4670, 5265, 6175; here the things which involve restoration, namely, the number “five” the restoration of <term>exterior good</term> <note>The outward habits, behaviors, and natural affections of a person.</note> to much; and the number “four” the restoration of <term>interior good</term> <note>The deeper, spiritual motivations and love within a person.</note> to the full. Interior good is to be restored to the full, because this good makes the spiritual life of man, and unless spiritual life is restored to the full, the exterior good which makes the natural life cannot be restored, for the latter life is restored by means of the former, as can be seen from the <term>regeneration</term> <note>The process of being "born again" or spiritually rebuilt by God.</note> of man. (That the external man is regenerated by means of the internal, see n. 9043, 9046, 9061.) But good in the external or natural man cannot be restored to the full, because the injury remains there as a scar which is grown callous. These are the things which these numbers involve. 

[3] A few words more however shall be said about the restoration of exterior good, which makes the natural life of man, from interior good which makes his spiritual life. The <term>natural</term> <note>The part of the human mind focused on the physical world and sensory experience.</note> of man sees things in the light of the world, which light is called **natural light**. Man procures for himself this light by means of the objects which enter through the sight and hearing, thus by means of objects which are of the world. Thus man sees those things within himself, almost as the eye sees them. The objects which enter by these senses appear to him at first as pleasure and delight. Afterward the infant man distinguishes between the different delights, from which he learns to discriminate, and by degrees to do so more perfectly. When light from heaven flows into these things, the man begins to see them spiritually, and first to discriminate between the useful and the non-useful. From this he begins to have an insight as to what is true; for that which is useful to him is to him true, and that which is useless is not true. This insight increases according to the influx of the light of heaven, until at last he discriminates not only between truths, but also between truths within these truths; and he does this with greater clearness in proportion as the communication is better opened between the internal and external man; for the light of heaven inflows from the Lord through the internal man into the external man.

has perception; but still it is not yet <term>spiritual perception</term> <note>A deeper, intuitive understanding of spiritual realities that goes beyond mere logic.</note>. This perception does not arise from natural truths, but from spiritual truths. Spiritual truths are those which are called the truths of faith. The reason why spiritual perception arises from these truths is that the <term>light of heaven</term> <note>Swedenborg describes spiritual light as a literal radiation of Divine Truth that illuminates the mind, just as the sun illuminates the world.</note> is Divine truth proceeding from the Lord, and this shines as light before the eyes of the angels, and also shines in their understandings, and gives them intelligence and wisdom; but with variety according to the reception of it in <term>good</term> <note>In this context, "good" refers to the person’s underlying motive of love or kindness.</note>. 

Wherefore the knowledges of spiritual things must be with man in his <term>natural</term> <note>The "natural" refers to the natural mind—the part of us that deals with the physical world and memory.</note> in order that there may be spiritual perception; and knowledges of spiritual things must be from <term>revelation</term> <note>Information that cannot be discovered by human science or logic alone, but must be provided by God (e.g., through the Bible).</note>. When the light of heaven flows into these knowledges, it flows into its own, for, as before said, this light is the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord (n. 1053, 1521–1533, 1619–1632, 2776, 3138, 3167, 3195, 3222, 3223, 3341, 3636, 3643, 4180, 4302, 4408, 4415, 4527, 5400, 6032, 6313, 6608 <note>These numbers refer to specific sections in Swedenborg's multi-volume work, *Arcana Coelestia* (Heavenly Secrets), where these topics are explained in greater detail.</note>). From this the man has intelligence and wisdom in such things as are of eternal life, and these increase according to the reception of that light, that is, of the truths of faith in good. Good is <term>charity</term> <note>A selfless love and desire to do what is right for the sake of others.</note>. 

[5] That the <term>natural or external man</term> <note>Our outward personality and physical life.</note> is <term>regenerated</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or restructured by God.</note>, and also amended and restored, through the <term>internal man</term> <note>The inner, spiritual self that is capable of direct connection with the Divine.</note>, can be seen from what has now been said. For the things which are in the external or natural man live from the light of heaven, for this light is living light, because it proceeds from the Lord, who is life itself; but they do not live from natural light, for in itself this light is dead. 

In order therefore that those things which are in natural light may live, there must be an <term>influx</term> <note>A spiritual "flowing in" of life and truth from God through the inner mind into the outer mind.</note> of living light through the internal man from the Lord. This influx accommodates itself according to the knowledges of truth <term>analogous and corresponding</term> <note>Swedenborg uses the "Law of Correspondences" to explain how physical things represent spiritual things; the influx "fits" into the mind's existing concepts that mirror higher truths.</note> in the natural, and according to the compliance there. From this it is evident that the external or natural of man must be regenerated through his internal. In the same way must the good in the natural that has been taken away and alienated, be amended and restored.

### CONTINUATION ABOUT THE SPIRITS AND INHABITANTS OF THE PLANET SATURN.

**9104.** Some spirits from our Earth traveled to the spirits of the planet Saturn. As mentioned previously, these spirits appear to be at a vast distance, seemingly at the very edge of our solar system. In the <term>other life</term> <note>Swedenborg’s term for the spiritual world or the state after physical death.</note>, such a journey happens in an instant. This is because "distance" in the spiritual world is merely an appearance caused by differences in a person's <term>state of life</term> <note>A person's "state" refers to their current quality of mind, including their thoughts, feelings, and motives. To be "distant" from someone means to be spiritually different from them.</note> (see references n. 2625, 2837, 3356, 3387, 3404, 4321, 4882, 5605, 7381). Connection between spirits is achieved simply by a desire to speak with one another. Because of this, people who were connected in the world through love, friendship, or high respect meet together in the afterlife whenever they wish; however, they eventually part ways based on how much their inner characters differ.

**9105.** After the spirits of Saturn had finished talking with those from our Earth, they communicated with me through <term>intermediate spirits</term> <note>Spirits who act as bridges or "translators" between different groups of spirits who are not in the same spiritual state.</note> from their own location. They expressed surprise that spirits from this Earth visit them so frequently and ask what God they worship. The Saturnians remarked that whenever they notice Earthly spirits making such inquiries, they consider them to be "insane." To them, there is no greater insanity than asking what God someone worships, because there is only one God for everyone in the entire universe. They added that Earthly spirits seem even more irrational because they do not realize that <term>the Lord</term> <note>In Swedenborg's writings, "the Lord" refers specifically to Jesus Christ as the one God of heaven and earth.</note> is the Only God. He rules the entire heaven, and consequently the entire world; for whoever rules heaven also rules the world, since the physical world is governed through the spiritual world of heaven.

**9106.** They further mentioned that another group of spirits, who travel in large companies, often come to them wanting to know everything about their lives. These visiting spirits use various methods to extract information. Regarding this group, the Saturnians said they aren't "insane," except for the fact that they have an overwhelming obsession with knowing things purely for the sake of knowing. I was later informed that these spirits are from the planet Mercury. They find their greatest joy in gathering <term>knowledge</term> and the resulting intelligence, rather than in the <term>uses</term> <note>In this context, "uses" refers to the practical application of knowledge for the benefit of others or for a moral purpose. The Mercury spirits are portrayed as intellectual "collectors" who value information over action.</note> that might come from that knowledge.

<vocab>spirits, Saturn, Mercury, God, Lord, heaven, world, knowledge, intelligence, universe, solar world</vocab>

...unless indeed knowledge is to them for the sake of use <note>Swedenborg emphasizes that for these spirits, gathering information is pointless unless it is applied to a useful, moral, or spiritual purpose.</note> (see references n. 6811, 6815, 6921–6932, 7069–7079, 7170–7177).

**9107.** I have been allowed to learn through direct experience the ways in which the spirits of our Earth and the spirits of the planet Saturn differ. At the same time, I learned how the **spiritual or internal man** and the **natural or external man** <note>The "internal man" refers to the higher, spiritual part of a person that connects with heaven, while the "external man" refers to the lower, worldly mind focused on physical life.</note> fight and clash with each other when the external man lacks faith and charity.

In the <term>Grand Man</term> <note>A central concept in Swedenborg’s writings where the entire spiritual world and the inhabitants of all planets are organized into a single "Universal Human" form. Each group of spirits corresponds to a specific anatomical part or sensory function of this cosmic body.</note>, the spirits of Saturn represent the sense that sits midway between the spiritual and the natural—moving away from the natural world and toward the spiritual (see n. 8953). In contrast, the spirits of our Earth represent the natural and bodily senses. Consequently, our spirits relate to the **external man**, while the spirits of Saturn relate to the **internal man**. The following experience showed just how much opposition and conflict exists between them when the external or natural man does not receive spiritual life through faith in and love for the Lord.

**9108.** The spirits of the planet Saturn appeared from a distance. At that time, many spirits from our Earth were present. Upon seeing those from Saturn, the Earth-spirits became as if they were insane; they began to harass the Saturnians by feeding them unworthy ideas about faith and about the Lord. In their fits of verbal abuse, the Earth-spirits even threw themselves into the middle of the Saturnian group and, in their state of insanity, tried to harm them. 

But the spirits of Saturn were not afraid; they remained safe and in a state of tranquility. Meanwhile, the spirits from our Earth—having forced themselves into the Saturnians' presence—began to breathe with great difficulty and fell into a state of anguish. Eventually, they threw themselves out of the group, scattering in every direction until they disappeared.

**9109.** Those watching this event realized the true nature of the **external or natural man** when he is separated from the **internal man** and enters a spiritual sphere—the environment where the internal man lives. They saw that such a person becomes "insane." This is because every person is surrounded by a <term>sphere</term> <note>In this context, a "sphere" is a spiritual aura or atmosphere that flows out from a person’s inner character and love.</note> that emanates from their very life (see references n. 1048, 1053, 1316, 1504–1512, 4464, 5179, 6206, 7454). When the natural man is separated from the spiritual, his only wisdom comes from the world rather than from heaven. And someone who is wise only in the ways of the world...

...from the world, believes nothing but what the senses apprehend, and what he believes, he believes from the fallacies of the senses, consequently from falsities. From this it is that spiritual things are not anything to him, insomuch that he scarcely endures to hear mention made of the spiritual. From this also it is that he does not apprehend what the **internal man** is, and consequently does not believe that there is an internal man <note>The "internal man" is the higher part of the human mind that is capable of receiving love and wisdom from the Divine, as opposed to the "external man" which deals with the physical world.</note>. Wherefore such are insane when kept in a spiritual sphere. It is otherwise while they are living in the world. They then either think naturally about spiritual things; or turn away the ear, that is, hear and do not attend. **9110.** From the above experience it was also made evident that the **natural man** cannot introduce himself into the spiritual, that is, ascend. But when a man is in faith and consequently in spiritual life, and is thinking, then the spiritual man descends, that is, thinks in the natural. For there is spiritual **influx** <term>influx: the concept that life, thought, and energy flow from a higher, spiritual source into a lower, physical one, similar to how light flows from the sun into an object</term>, that is, influx from the spiritual world into the natural, but not the reverse. (That physical influx <note>original: "influxus physicus" — the mistaken philosophical idea that the physical body or world can produce thoughts or spiritual states.</note> is quite contrary to order, and contrary to nature, thus is impossible, see n. 3721, 5119, 5259, 5779, 6322, 8237.) Wherefore when the natural man that has been separated from the internal, comes into the sphere of spiritual life, he is seized first with blindness, then with insanity, and finally with anguish. It is also for this reason that those who are in hell have no inclination to look toward heaven (n. 4225, 4226, 8137, 8265, 8945, 8946).
